text_mt:
White garments, clear water, a fruit-bearing tree, and a spotless sky.
Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, called 'The Chapter on Dreams', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter:
Omens.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
auṣadhāni ca yuktāni dhānyaṃ kṛṣṇamaśobhanaṃ /
kārpāsaṃ tṛṇaśuṣkañca gomayaṃ vai dhanāni ca //
:p 333
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
औषधानि च युक्तानि धान्यं कृष्णमशोभनं /
कार्पासं तृणशुष्कञ्च गोमयं वै धनानि च //
:प् 333
text_mt:
Puṣkara said: / Medicines properly prepared, and black grain is inauspicious; / cotton, dry grass, cow dung, and riches;
[Page 333]

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgāraṃ guḍasarjau ca(1) muṇḍābhyaktañca nagnakaṃ /
ayaḥ paṅkaṃ carmakeśau unmattañca napuṃsakaṃ //
meaning:
अङ्गारं गुडसर्जौ च(1) मुण्डाभ्यक्तञ्च नग्नकं /
अयः पङ्कं चर्मकेशौ उन्मत्तञ्च नपुंसकं //
text_mt: Charcoal, jaggery and resin, a shaven-headed person anointed with oil, a naked person, / iron, mud, hide, hair, a madman, and a eunuch;

sanskrit_iast:
caṇḍālaśvapacādyāni narā bandhanapālakāḥ /
garbhiṇī strī ca vidhavāḥ piṇyakādīni vai mṛtaṃ //
meaning:
चण्डालश्वपचाद्यानि नरा बन्धनपालकाः /
गर्भिणी स्त्री च विधवाः पिण्यकादीनि वै मृतं //
text_mt: Caṇḍālas, dog-cookers, and the like, men who are prison guards, / a pregnant woman, widows, oil-cake and the like, and a corpse;

sanskrit_iast:
tuṣabhasmakapālāsthibhinnabhāṇḍamaśastakaṃ /
aśasto vādyaśabdaś ca bhinnabhairavajharjharaḥ //
meaning:
तुषभस्मकपालास्थिभिन्नभाण्डमशस्तकं /
अशस्तो वाद्यशब्दश् च भिन्नभैरवझर्झरः //
text_mt: Chaff, ashes, skulls, bones, and broken vessels are inauspicious; / an inauspicious instrumental sound is harsh, fearful, and shrill.

sanskrit_iast:
ehīti purataḥ śabdaḥ śasyate na tu pṛṣṭhataḥ /
gaccheti paścācchabdo 'gryaḥ purastāttu vigarhitaḥ //
meaning:
एहीति पुरतः शब्दः शस्यते न तु पृष्ठतः /
गच्छेति पश्चाच्छब्दो ऽग्र्यः पुरस्तात्तु विगर्हितः //
text_mt: The sound 'Come!' in front is praised, but not behind; / the sound 'Go!' behind is excellent, but censured in front.

sanskrit_iast:
kva yāsi tiṣṭha mā gaccha kinte tatra gatasya ca /
aniṣṭaśabdā mṛtyarthaṃ kravyādaś ca dhvajādigaḥ //
meaning:
क्व यासि तिष्ठ मा गच्छ किन्ते तत्र गतस्य च /
अनिष्टशब्दा मृत्यर्थं क्रव्यादश् च ध्वजादिगः //
text_mt: Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, called 'The Chapter on Auspicious Omens', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.

sanskrit_iast:
skhalanaṃ vāhanānāñca śastrabhaṅgastathaiva ca /
śiroghātaś ca dvārādyaiścchatravāsādipātanaṃ //
meaning:
स्खलनं वाहनानाञ्च शस्त्रभङ्गस्तथैव च /
शिरोघातश् च द्वाराद्यैश्च्छत्रवासादिपातनं //
text_mt: The stumbling of mounts, the breaking of weapons, / striking the head on doors and the like, and the falling of an umbrella, garment, and the like:

sanskrit_iast:
harimabhyarcya saṃstutya syādamaṅgalyanāśanaṃ /
dvitīyantu tato dṛṣṭvā viruddhaṃ praviśedgṛhaṃ //
meaning:
हरिमभ्यर्च्य संस्तुत्य स्यादमङ्गल्यनाशनं /
द्वितीयन्तु ततो दृष्ट्वा विरुद्धं प्रविशेद्गृहं //
text_mt: By worshipping and praising Hari, inauspiciousness is destroyed; / but having seen a second contrary [omen] thereafter, one should enter the house.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetāḥ sumanasaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ pūrṇakumbho mahottamaḥ /
māṃsaṃ matsyā dūraśabdā vṛddha ekaḥ paśustvajaḥ //
meaning:
श्वेताः सुमनसः श्रेष्ठाः पूर्णकुम्भो महोत्तमः /
मांसं मत्स्या दूरशब्दा वृद्ध एकः पशुस्त्वजः //
text_mt: White flowers are best; a full pitcher is most excellent; / meat, fish, sounds from afar, one old animal, namely a goat;

sanskrit_iast:
gāvastaraṅgamā nāgā devaś ca jvalito 'nalaḥ /
dūrvārdragomayaṃ veśyā svarṇarūpyañca ratnakaṃ //
meaning:
गावस्तरङ्गमा नागा देवश् च ज्वलितो ऽनलः /
दूर्वार्द्रगोमयं वेश्या स्वर्णरूप्यञ्च रत्नकं //
text_mt: Cows, horses, elephants, a deity, and a blazing fire; / dūrvā grass, moist cow dung, a courtesan, gold, silver, and jewels;

sanskrit_iast:
vacāsiddhārthakauṣadhyo mudga āyudhakhaḍgakaṃ /
chatraṃ pīṭhaṃ rājaliṅgaṃ śavaṃ ruditavarjitaṃ //
meaning:
वचासिद्धार्थकौषध्यो मुद्ग आयुधखड्गकं /
छत्रं पीठं राजलिङ्गं शवं रुदितवर्जितं //
text_mt: Sweet flag, white mustard, medicinal herbs, kidney beans, weapons, swords, / an umbrella, a throne, a royal insignia, a corpse unaccompanied by weeping;

sanskrit_iast:
phalaṃ ghṛṭaṃ dadhi payo akṣatādarśamākṣikaṃ /
śaṅkhaṃ ikṣuḥ śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bhaktavāditagītakaṃ //
:n
1 guḍasarpau ceti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 334
meaning:
फलं घृटं दधि पयो अक्षतादर्शमाक्षिकं /
शङ्खं इक्षुः शुभं वाक्यं भक्तवादितगीतकं //
:न्
1 गुडसर्पौ चेति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 334

sanskrit_iast:
gambhīrameghastanitaṃ taḍittuṣṭiś ca mānasī /
ekataḥ sarvaliṅgāni manasastuṣṭirekataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe māṅgalyādhyāyo nāma
ekonatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śakunāni
meaning:
गम्भीरमेघस्तनितं तडित्तुष्टिश् च मानसी /
एकतः सर्वलिङ्गानि मनसस्तुष्टिरेकतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे माङ्गल्याध्यायो नाम
एकोनत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
शकुनानि
text_mt:
Deep rumbling of clouds, lightning, and mental satisfaction: / on one side are all signs, and on the other is the satisfaction of the mind.
Thus ends the two hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Chapter on Auspicious Things," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirtieth chapter:
Omens.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
tiṣṭhato gamane praśne puruṣasya śubhāśubhaṃ /
nivedayanti śakunā deśasya nagarasya ca //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
तिष्ठतो गमने प्रश्ने पुरुषस्य शुभाशुभं /
निवेदयन्ति शकुना देशस्य नगरस्य च //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / When a man is staying still, departing, or making an inquiry, omens indicate / the good and evil fortune of a region and a city.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaḥ pāpaphalo dīpto nirdiṣṭo daivacintikaiḥ /
śāntaḥ śubhaphalaś caiva daivajñaiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वः पापफलो दीप्तो निर्दिष्टो दैवचिन्तिकैः /
शान्तः शुभफलश् चैव दैवज्ञैः समुदाहृतः //
text_mt: Every inflamed [omen] is proclaimed by interpreters of fate as yielding evil results; / a tranquil [omen] is declared by astrologers as yielding auspicious results.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭprakārā vinirdiṣṭā śakunānāñca dīptayaḥ /
velādigdeśakaraṇarutajātivibhedataḥ //
meaning:
षट्प्रकारा विनिर्दिष्टा शकुनानाञ्च दीप्तयः /
वेलादिग्देशकरणरुतजातिविभेदतः //
text_mt: The inflamed states of omens are stated to be of six kinds, / differentiated by time, direction, place, action, cry, and species.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvā pūrvā ca vijñeyā sā teṣāṃ balavattarā /
divācaro rātricaras tathā rātrau divācaraḥ //
meaning:
पूर्वा पूर्वा च विज्ञेया सा तेषां बलवत्तरा /
दिवाचरो रात्रिचरस् तथा रात्रौ दिवाचरः //
text_mt: Each preceding one among them is to be known as stronger: / a diurnal creature moving at night, or a nocturnal creature moving by day;

sanskrit_iast:
krūreṣu dīptā vijñeyā ṛkṣalagnagrahādiṣu /
dhūmitā sā tu vijñeyā yāṅgamiṣyati bhāskaraḥ //
meaning:
क्रूरेषु दीप्ता विज्ञेया ऋक्षलग्नग्रहादिषु /
धूमिता सा तु विज्ञेया याङ्गमिष्यति भास्करः //
text_mt: It should be known as inflamed under cruel asterisms, ascendants, planets, and the like. / That direction toward which the sun will proceed is to be known as 'smoky';

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāṃ sthitaḥ sā jvalitā muktā cāṅgāriṇī matā /
etāstisraḥ smṛtā dīptāḥ pañca śāntās tathāparāḥ //
:p 335
meaning:
यस्यां स्थितः सा ज्वलिता मुक्ता चाङ्गारिणी मता /
एतास्तिस्रः स्मृता दीप्ताः पञ्च शान्तास् तथापराः //
:प् 335
text_mt:
The direction in which it stands is 'blazing', and that which it has left is considered 'charcoal-like'. / These three are remembered as inflamed; the other five are tranquil.
[Page 335]

sanskrit_iast:
dīptāyāndiśi digdīptaṃ śakunaṃ parikīrtitaṃ /
grāmo 'raṇyā vane grāmyās tathā ninditapādapaḥ //
meaning:
दीप्तायान्दिशि दिग्दीप्तं शकुनं परिकीर्तितं /
ग्रामो ऽरण्या वने ग्राम्यास् तथा निन्दितपादपः //
text_mt: An omen in an inflamed direction is proclaimed as directionally inflamed. / A wild creature in a village, village creatures in a forest, or an inauspicious tree,

sanskrit_iast:
deśe caivāśubhe jñeyo deśadīpto dvijottamaḥ /
kriyādīpto vinirdiṣṭaḥ svajātyanucitakriyaḥ //
meaning:
देशे चैवाशुभे ज्ञेयो देशदीप्तो द्विजोत्तमः /
क्रियादीप्तो विनिर्दिष्टः स्वजात्यनुचितक्रियः //
text_mt: And in an inauspicious place, O best of the twice-born, it should be known as spatially inflamed; / one performing an action unsuited to its own species is stated to be actionally inflamed;

sanskrit_iast:
rutadīptaś ca kathito bhinnabhairavanisvanaḥ /
jātidīptas tathā jñeyaḥ kevalaṃ māṃsabhojanaḥ //
meaning:
रुतदीप्तश् च कथितो भिन्नभैरवनिस्वनः /
जातिदीप्तस् तथा ज्ञेयः केवलं मांसभोजनः //
text_mt: One having a harsh and frightful sound is called vocally inflamed; / and one feeding exclusively on meat is to be known as specifically inflamed.

sanskrit_iast:
dīptācchānto vinirdiṣṭaḥ sarvair bhedaiḥ prayatnataḥ /
miśrair miśro vinirdiṣṭastasya vācyaṃ phalāphalaṃ //
meaning:
दीप्ताच्छान्तो विनिर्दिष्टः सर्वैर् भेदैः प्रयत्नतः /
मिश्रैर् मिश्रो विनिर्दिष्टस्तस्य वाच्यं फलाफलं //
text_mt: A tranquil [omen] is defined as opposite to an inflamed one by every category, with care; / by mixed categories it is stated to be mixed, and its good or bad fruit should be declared accordingly.

sanskrit_iast:
gośvoṣṭragardabhaśvānaḥ sārikā gṛhagodhikā /
caṭakā bhāsakūrmādyāḥ kathitā grāmavāsinaḥ //
meaning:
गोश्वोष्ट्रगर्दभश्वानः सारिका गृहगोधिका /
चटका भासकूर्माद्याः कथिता ग्रामवासिनः //
text_mt: Cows, horses, camels, donkeys, dogs, mynahs, house lizards, / sparrows, vultures, turtles, and the like are declared village-dwellers.

sanskrit_iast:
ajāviśukanāgendrāḥ kolo mahiṣavāyasau /
grāmyāraṇyā vinirdiṣṭāḥ sarve 'nye vanagocarāḥ(1) //
meaning:
अजाविशुकनागेन्द्राः कोलो महिषवायसौ /
ग्राम्यारण्या विनिर्दिष्टाः सर्वे ऽन्ये वनगोचराः(1) //
text_mt: Goats, sheep, parrots, noble elephants, boars, buffaloes, and crows / are designated as both village and forest dwellers; all others range in the forest.

sanskrit_iast:
mārjārakukkuṭau grāmyau tau caiva vanagocarau /
tayorbhavati vijñānaṃ nityaṃ vai rūpabhedataḥ //
meaning:
मार्जारकुक्कुटौ ग्राम्यौ तौ चैव वनगोचरौ /
तयोर्भवति विज्ञानं नित्यं वै रूपभेदतः //
text_mt: The cat and the rooster are domestic, and they also range in the forest; / the distinction between the two is always made by their difference in appearance.

sanskrit_iast:
gokarṇaśikhicakrāhvakharahārītavāyasāḥ /
kulāhakukkubhaśyenapherukhañjanavānarāḥ //
meaning:
गोकर्णशिखिचक्राह्वखरहारीतवायसाः /
कुलाहकुक्कुभश्येनफेरुखञ्जनवानराः //
text_mt: The gokarṇa antelope, peacock, ruddy shelduck, donkey, green pigeon, crow, / owl, coucal, hawk, jackal, wagtail, monkey,

sanskrit_iast:
śataghnacaṭakaśyāmacāsaśyenakaliñjalāḥ /
tittiraḥ śatapatrañca kapotaś ca tathā trayaḥ //
meaning:
शतघ्नचटकश्यामचासश्येनकलिञ्जलाः /
तित्तिरः शतपत्रञ्च कपोतश् च तथा त्रयः //
text_mt: Woodpecker, sparrow, Indian robin, blue jay, falcon, sparrow, / francolin, hoopoe, and the pigeon—these three—

sanskrit_iast:
khañjarīṭakadātyūhaśukarājīvakukkuṭāḥ /
bhāradvājaś ca sāraṅga iti jñeyā divācarāḥ //
meaning:
खञ्जरीटकदात्यूहशुकराजीवकुक्कुटाः /
भारद्वाजश् च सारङ्ग इति ज्ञेया दिवाचराः //
text_mt: Wagtail, water-hen, parrot, kingfisher, rooster, / skylark, and sāraṅga bird are to be known as diurnal creatures.

sanskrit_iast:
vāguryulūkaśarabhakrauñcāḥ śaśakakacchapāḥ /
lomāsikāḥ piṅgalikāḥ kathitā rātrigocarāḥ //
:n
1 sarve 'nye ca vanecarā iti jha..
:p 336
meaning:
वागुर्युलूकशरभक्रौञ्चाः शशककच्छपाः /
लोमासिकाः पिङ्गलिकाः कथिता रात्रिगोचराः //
:न्
1 सर्वे ऽन्ये च वनेचरा इति झ..
:प् 336
text_mt:
The bat, horned owl, śarabha, crane, hare, turtle, / fox, and spotted owlet are declared nocturnal creatures.
[...]
[Variant reading: 'and all others move in the forest' in manuscript jha. Page 336]

sanskrit_iast:
haṃṣāś ca mṛgamārjāranakularkṣabhujaṅgamāḥ /
vṛkārisiṃhavyāghroṣṭragrāmaśūkaramānuṣāḥ //
meaning:
हंषाश् च मृगमार्जारनकुलर्क्षभुजङ्गमाः /
वृकारिसिंहव्याघ्रोष्ट्रग्रामशूकरमानुषाः //
text_mt: Swans, deer, cats, mongooses, bears, serpents, / wolves, lions, tigers, camels, village boars, men,

sanskrit_iast:
śvāvidvṛṣabhagomāyuvṛkakokilasārasāḥ /
turaṅgakaupīnanarā godhā hy ubhayacāriṇaḥ //
meaning:
श्वाविद्वृषभगोमायुवृककोकिलसारसाः /
तुरङ्गकौपीननरा गोधा ह्य् उभयचारिणः //
text_mt: porcupines, bulls, jackals, wolves, cuckoos, cranes, / horses, men in loincloths, and monitors are land-and-water animals.

sanskrit_iast:
balaprasthānayoḥ sarve purastātsaṅghacāriṇaḥ /
jayāvahā vinirdiṣṭāḥ paścānnidhanakāriṇaḥ //
meaning:
बलप्रस्थानयोः सर्वे पुरस्तात्सङ्घचारिणः /
जयावहा विनिर्दिष्टाः पश्चान्निधनकारिणः //
text_mt: When an army marches, all of them moving together in a flock in front / are declared to bring victory; [if] behind, they cause destruction.

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhādgamya yadā cāso vyāharet purutaḥ sthitaḥ /
nṛpāvamānaṃ vadati vāmaḥ kalahabhojane //
meaning:
गृहाद्गम्य यदा चासो व्याहरेत् पुरुतः स्थितः /
नृपावमानं वदति वामः कलहभोजने //
text_mt: And when having left the house it cries while standing in front, / it indicates insult from the king; on the left, [it indicates] a meal in a quarrel.

sanskrit_iast:
yāne taddarśanaṃ śastaṃ savyamaṅgasya vāpyatha /
caurair moṣamathākhyāti mayūro bhinnanisvanaḥ //
meaning:
याने तद्दर्शनं शस्तं सव्यमङ्गस्य वाप्यथ /
चौरैर् मोषमथाख्याति मयूरो भिन्ननिस्वनः //
text_mt: Upon setting out, the sight of it is praised, or on the left side of the body. / Moreover, a peacock with a broken call announces theft by thieves.

sanskrit_iast:
prayātasyāgrato rāma mṛgaḥ prāṇaharo bhavet /
ṛkṣākhujambukavyāghrasiṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ //
meaning:
प्रयातस्याग्रतो राम मृगः प्राणहरो भवेत् /
ऋक्षाखुजम्बुकव्याघ्रसिंहमार्जारगर्दभाः //
text_mt: A deer in front of one who has set forth, O Rāma, takes away life. / Bears, mice, jackals, tigers, lions, cats, donkeys,

sanskrit_iast:
pratilomās tathā rāma kharaś ca vikṛtrasvanaḥ /
vāmaḥ kapiñjalaḥ śreṣṭhas tathā dakṣiṇasaṃsthitaḥ //
meaning:
प्रतिलोमास् तथा राम खरश् च विकृत्रस्वनः /
वामः कपिञ्जलः श्रेष्ठस् तथा दक्षिणसंस्थितः //
text_mt: going against the wind, O Rāma, and a donkey with an unnatural cry [bring evil]. / A francolin partridge on the left is best, and likewise situated on the right;

sanskrit_iast:
pṛṣṭhato ninditaphalastittiristu na śasyate /
eṇā varāhāḥ pṛṣatā vāmā bhūtvā tu dakṣiṇāḥ //
meaning:
पृष्ठतो निन्दितफलस्तित्तिरिस्तु न शस्यते /
एणा वराहाः पृषता वामा भूत्वा तु दक्षिणाः //
text_mt: behind, its fruit is censured; but a partridge is not commended. / Blackbucks, boars, and spotted deer, being on the left and then on the right,

sanskrit_iast:
bhavantyarthakarā nityaṃ viparītā vigarhitāḥ /
vṛṣāśvajambukavyāghrāḥ siṃhamārjāragardabhāḥ(1) //
meaning:
भवन्त्यर्थकरा नित्यं विपरीता विगर्हिताः /
वृषाश्वजम्बुकव्याघ्राः सिंहमार्जारगर्दभाः(1) //
text_mt: always bring wealth; reversed, they are censured. / Bulls, horses, jackals, tigers, lions, cats, donkeys,

sanskrit_iast:
vāñchitārthakarā jñeyā dakṣiṇādvāmato gatāḥ /
śivā śyāmānanācchūcchūḥ piṅgalā gṛhagodhikā //
meaning:
वाञ्छितार्थकरा ज्ञेया दक्षिणाद्वामतो गताः /
शिवा श्यामाननाच्छूच्छूः पिङ्गला गृहगोधिका //
text_mt: gone from the right to the left, are to be known as fulfilling desired aims. / A female jackal, a dark-faced chūcchū-bird, a screech-owl, a house lizard,

sanskrit_iast:
śūkarī parapuṣṭā ca punnāmānaś ca vāmataḥ /
:n
1 pratilomāstathetyādiḥ, siṃhamārjāragardabhā ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ
ja.. bha.. pustakadvaye nāsti
:p 337
strīsañjñā bhāsakārūṣakapiśrīkarṇaśchitkarāḥ //
meaning:
शूकरी परपुष्टा च पुन्नामानश् च वामतः /
:न्
1 प्रतिलोमास्तथेत्यादिः, सिंहमार्जारगर्दभा इत्य् अन्तः पाठः
ज.. भ.. पुस्तकद्वये नास्ति

a sow, a cuckoo, and [creatures] with masculine names, [are auspicious] on the left.

[Creatures] with feminine names, bhāsas, kārūṣas, monkeys, śrīkarṇas, [and birds that] make a screeching cry,

sanskrit_iast:
kapiśrīkarṇapipyīkā(1) ruruśyenāś ca dakṣiṇāḥ /
jātīkṣāhiśaśakroḍagodhānāṃ kīrtanaṃ śubhaṃ //
meaning:
कपिश्रीकर्णपिप्यीका(1) रुरुश्येनाश् च दक्षिणाः /
जातीक्षाहिशशक्रोडगोधानां कीर्तनं शुभं //
text_mt: monkeys, śrīkarṇas, pipyīkās, ruru deer, and falcons [are auspicious] on the right. / Mentioning a chameleon, a snake, a hare, a boar, or an iguana is auspicious;

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sandarśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ pratīpaṃ vānararkṣayoḥ /
kāryakṛdbalī śakunaḥ prasthitasya hi yo 'nvahaṃ //
meaning:
ततः सन्दर्शनं नेष्टं प्रतीपं वानरर्क्षयोः /
कार्यकृद्बली शकुनः प्रस्थितस्य हि यो ऽन्वहं //
text_mt: the sighting of them afterwards is not desired; [likewise] an monkey or a bear coming from the opposite direction. / An omen that is strong and effective for one who has departed every day,

sanskrit_iast:
bhavettasya phalaṃ vācyaṃ tadeva divasaṃ budhaiḥ /
matā bhakṣyārthino bālā vairasaktāstathaiva ca //
meaning:
भवेत्तस्य फलं वाच्यं तदेव दिवसं बुधैः /
मता भक्ष्यार्थिनो बाला वैरसक्तास्तथैव च //
text_mt: its fruit should be pronounced by the wise on that very day. / Those seeking food, young ones, and those engaged in enmity,

sanskrit_iast:
sīmāntamabhyantaritā vijñeyā niṣphalā dvija /
ekadvitricaturbhistu śivā dhanyā rutair bhavet //
meaning:
सीमान्तमभ्यन्तरिता विज्ञेया निष्फला द्विज /
एकद्वित्रिचतुर्भिस्तु शिवा धन्या रुतैर् भवेत् //
text_mt: and those separated by a boundary are to be known as fruitless, O twice-born. / By one, two, three, or four cries, a female jackal is auspicious;

sanskrit_iast:
pañcabhiś ca tathā ṣaḍbhiradhanyā parikīrtitā /
saptabhiś ca tathā dhanyā niṣphalā parato bhavet //
meaning:
पञ्चभिश् च तथा षड्भिरधन्या परिकीर्तिता /
सप्तभिश् च तथा धन्या निष्फला परतो भवेत् //
text_mt: by five and six cries, she is declared inauspicious; / by seven cries, she is likewise auspicious; beyond that, she becomes fruitless.

sanskrit_iast:
nṛṇāṃ romāñcajananī vāhanānāṃ bhayapradā /
jvālānalā sūryamukhī vijñeyā bhayavardhanī //
meaning:
नृणां रोमाञ्चजननी वाहनानां भयप्रदा /
ज्वालानला सूर्यमुखी विज्ञेया भयवर्धनी //
text_mt: Causing goosebumps to men and causing fear to conveyances, / flaming with fire, facing the sun, she is to be known as increasing fear.

sanskrit_iast:
prathamaṃ sāraṅge dṛṣṭe śubhe deśe śubhaṃ vadet /
saṃvatsaraṃ manuṣyasya aśubhe ca śubhaṃ tathā //
meaning:
प्रथमं सारङ्गे दृष्टे शुभे देशे शुभं वदेत् /
संवत्सरं मनुष्यस्य अशुभे च शुभं तथा //
text_mt: When a deer is first seen in an auspicious region, one should declare good fortune / for a man for a year; and [likewise] what is auspicious in an inauspicious [region].

sanskrit_iast:
tathāvidhannaraḥ paśyetsāraṅgaṃ prathame 'hani /
ātmanaś ca tathātvena jñātavyaṃ vatsaraṃ phalaṃ //

text_mt:
When a man sees a deer of such a kind on the first day, / the fruit of the year for himself is to be known accordingly.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirtieth chapter, named [Omens from] Birds, in the great Agni Purāṇa.

It cannot be emended even with the aid of any one of them; nor are the words found therein attested in dictionaries and the like. Therefore, we desist here. / [Page 338]
Now the two hundred and thirty-first chapter.
Omens from Birds

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
viśanti yena mārgeṇa vāyasā bahavaḥ puraṃ /
tena mārgeṇa ruddhasya purasya grahaṇaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
विशन्ति येन मार्गेण वायसा बहवः पुरं /
तेन मार्गेण रुद्धस्य पुरस्य ग्रहणं भवेत् //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / By whichever road many crows enter a city, / by that road will be the capture of the besieged city.

sanskrit_iast:
senāyāṃ yadi vāsārthe niviṣṭo vāyaso ruvan /
vāmo bhayāturastrasto bhayaṃ vadati dustaraṃ(1) //
meaning:
सेनायां यदि वासार्थे निविष्टो वायसो रुवन् /
वामो भयातुरस्त्रस्तो भयं वदति दुस्तरं(1) //
text_mt: If a crow cawing alights in an army for lodging, / being on the left, distressed by fear, and terrified, it foretells insurmountable fear.

sanskrit_iast:
chāyāṅgavāhanopānacchatravastrādikuṭṭane /
mṛtyustatpūjane pūjā tadiṣṭakaraṇe śubhaṃ //
meaning:
छायाङ्गवाहनोपानच्छत्रवस्त्रादिकुट्टने /
मृत्युस्तत्पूजने पूजा तदिष्टकरणे शुभं //
text_mt: When it pecks at a shadow, a limb, a vehicle, shoes, an umbrella, or garments, / there is death; in revering them, respect; in doing what is pleasing to it, good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
proṣitāgamakṛtkākaḥ kurvan dvāri gatāgataṃ /
raktaṃ dagdhaṃ gṛhe dravyaṃ kṣipanvahnivedakaḥ //
meaning:
प्रोषितागमकृत्काकः कुर्वन् द्वारि गतागतं /
रक्तं दग्धं गृहे द्रव्यं क्षिपन्वह्निवेदकः //
text_mt: A crow going back and forth at the door causes the arrival of a traveller. / Dropping a red or burnt object in the house, it indicates fire.

sanskrit_iast:
nyasedraktaṃ purastācca nivedayati bandhanaṃ /
pītaṃ dravyaṃ tathā rukma rūpyameva tu bhārgava //
meaning:
न्यसेद्रक्तं पुरस्ताच्च निवेदयति बन्धनं /
पीतं द्रव्यं तथा रुक्म रूप्यमेव तु भार्गव //
text_mt: If it should place a red [object] in front, it indicates imprisonment; / likewise a yellow object [indicates] gold, and silver [indicates] silver, O Bhārgava.

sanskrit_iast:
yaccaivopanayed dravyaṃ tasya labdhiṃ vinirdiśet /
dravyaṃ vāpanayedyattu tasya hāniṃ vinirdiśet //
meaning:
यच्चैवोपनयेद् द्रव्यं तस्य लब्धिं विनिर्दिशेत् /
द्रव्यं वापनयेद्यत्तु तस्य हानिं विनिर्दिशेत् //
text_mt: Whatever object it brings, one should predict the acquisition thereof; / or whatever object it carries away, one should predict the loss thereof.

sanskrit_iast:
purato dhanalabdhiḥ syādāmamāṃsasya chardane /
bhūlabdhiḥ syān mṛdaḥ kṣepe rājyaṃ ratnārpaṇe mahat //
meaning:
पुरतो धनलब्धिः स्यादाममांसस्य छर्दने /
भूलब्धिः स्यान् मृदः क्षेपे राज्यं रत्नार्पणे महत् //
text_mt: Upon vomiting raw meat in front, there will be gain of wealth; / upon throwing soil, gain of land; upon offering a jewel, a great kingdom.

sanskrit_iast:
yātuḥ kāko 'nukūlastu kṣemaḥ karmakṣamo bhavet /
na tvarthasādhako jñeyaḥ pratikūlo bhayāvahaḥ //
meaning:
यातुः काको ऽनुकूलस्तु क्षेमः कर्मक्षमो भवेत् /
न त्वर्थसाधको ज्ञेयः प्रतिकूलो भयावहः //
text_mt: A favorable crow brings welfare to a traveler and makes him successful in his endeavor; / but an unfavorable [crow] is to be known as not accomplishing aims and bringing fear.

sanskrit_iast:
sammukhe 'bhyeti viruvan yātrāghātakaro bhavet /
vāmaḥ kākaḥ smṛto dhanyo dakṣiṇo 'rthavināśakṛt(2) //
:n
1 duṣkaramiti kha.. , cha ca
2 dakṣiṇo 'nnavināśakṛditi ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 339
meaning:
सम्मुखे ऽभ्येति विरुवन् यात्राघातकरो भवेत् /
वामः काकः स्मृतो धन्यो दक्षिणो ऽर्थविनाशकृत्(2) //
:न्
1 दुष्करमिति ख.. , छ च
2 दक्षिणो ऽन्नविनाशकृदिति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 339
text_mt:
Coming directly in front while crying out, it causes disruption to the journey. / A crow on the left is remembered as auspicious; on the right, it causes loss of wealth.
[...]
1. Manuscripts kha and cha read "duṣkaram".
2. Manuscripts ga, gha, and ña read "dakṣiṇo 'nnavināśakṛt". / [Page 339]

sanskrit_iast:
vāmo 'nulomagaḥ śreṣṭho madhyamo dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
pratilomagatirvāmo gamanapratiṣedhakṛt //
meaning:
वामो ऽनुलोमगः श्रेष्ठो मध्यमो दक्षिणः स्मृतः /
प्रतिलोमगतिर्वामो गमनप्रतिषेधकृत् //
text_mt: On the left going with the wind is best; on the right is considered middling. / Moving against the wind on the left prohibits traveling.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedayati yātrārthamabhipretaṃ gṛhe gataḥ(1) /
ekākṣaracaraṇastvarkaṃ vīkṣamāṇo bhayāvahaḥ //
meaning:
निवेदयति यात्रार्थमभिप्रेतं गृहे गतः(1) /
एकाक्षरचरणस्त्वर्कं वीक्षमाणो भयावहः //
text_mt: Gone to a house, it indicates the desired purpose for a journey. / But moving with one eye or foot while looking at the sun, it brings fear.

sanskrit_iast:
koṭare vāsamānaś ca mahānarthakaro bhavet /
na śubhastūṣare kākaḥ paṅkāṅkaḥ sa tu śasyate //
meaning:
कोटरे वासमानश् च महानर्थकरो भवेत् /
न शुभस्तूषरे काकः पङ्काङ्कः स तु शस्यते //
text_mt: And dwelling in a hollow, it causes great calamity. / A crow in a barren ground is not auspicious, but smeared with mud it is commended.

sanskrit_iast:
amedhyapūrṇavadanaḥ kākaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ(2) /
jñeyāḥ patatriṇo 'nye 'pi kākavad bhṛgunandana //
meaning:
अमेध्यपूर्णवदनः काकः सर्वार्थसाधकः(2) /
ज्ञेयाः पतत्रिणो ऽन्ये ऽपि काकवद् भृगुनन्दन //
text_mt: A crow whose mouth is full of impure matter accomplishes all ends. / Other birds should also be understood like the crow, O son of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
skandhāvārāpasavyasthāḥ śvāno vipravināśakāḥ /
indrasthāne narendrasya pureśasya tu gopure //
meaning:
स्कन्धावारापसव्यस्थाः श्वानो विप्रविनाशकाः /
इन्द्रस्थाने नरेन्द्रस्य पुरेशस्य तु गोपुरे //
text_mt: Dogs staying to the right of an army camp destroy the Brahmins; / at Indra's station, [they destroy] the king; at the gate, the lord of the city.

sanskrit_iast:
antargṛhe gṛheśasya maraṇāya bhavedbhaṣan /
yasya jighrati vāmāṅgaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye //
meaning:
अन्तर्गृहे गृहेशस्य मरणाय भवेद्भषन् /
यस्य जिघ्रति वामाङ्गं तस्य स्यादर्थसिद्धये //
text_mt: Barking inside the house, it leads to the death of the master of the house. / The one whose left limb it smells will have attainment of wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayāya dakṣiṇaṃ cāṅgaṃ tathā bhujamadakṣiṇaṃ /
yātrāghātakaro yāturbhavet pratimukhāgataḥ //
meaning:
भयाय दक्षिणं चाङ्गं तथा भुजमदक्षिणं /
यात्राघातकरो यातुर्भवेत् प्रतिमुखागतः //
text_mt: The right limb [it smells] leads to fear, and likewise the left arm. / Coming face-to-face, it disrupts the journey of the traveler.

sanskrit_iast:
mārgāvarodhako mārge caurān vadati bhārgava /
alābho 'sthimukhaḥ pāpo rajjucīramukhas tathā //
meaning:
मार्गावरोधको मार्गे चौरान् वदति भार्गव /
अलाभो ऽस्थिमुखः पापो रज्जुचीरमुखस् तथा //
text_mt: Obstructing the path on a road, it announces thieves, O Bhārgava. / With a bone in its mouth it is evil, causing failure; likewise with a rope or rag in its mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
sopānatkamukho dhanyo māṃsapūrṇamukho 'pi ca /
amaṅgalyamukhadravyaṃ keśañcaivāśubhaṃ tathā //
meaning:
सोपानत्कमुखो धन्यो मांसपूर्णमुखो ऽपि च /
अमङ्गल्यमुखद्रव्यं केशञ्चैवाशुभं तथा //
text_mt: With a shoe in its mouth it is auspicious, and also with a mouth full of meat. / An inauspicious substance or hair in its mouth is likewise unfavorable.

sanskrit_iast:
avamūtryāgrato yāti yasya tasya bhayaṃ bhavet /
yasyāvamūtrya vrajati śubhaṃ deśantathā drumaṃ //

The one in front of whom it urinates and walks on will have fear. / An auspicious land or tree upon which it urinates and goes,

sanskrit_iast:
maṅgalañca tathā dravyaṃ tasya syādarthasiddhaye /
śvavacca rāma vijñeyās tathā vai jambukādayaḥ //
meaning:
मङ्गलञ्च तथा द्रव्यं तस्य स्यादर्थसिद्धये /
श्ववच्च राम विज्ञेयास् तथा वै जम्बुकादयः //
text_mt: and likewise an auspicious substance, will lead to his attainment of prosperity. / And jackals and other [animals] are to be known like dogs, O Rāma.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayāya svāmini jñeyamanimittaṃ rutaṅgavāṃ /
niśi caurabhayāya syādvikṛtaṃ mṛtyave tathā //
meaning:
भयाय स्वामिनि ज्ञेयमनिमित्तं रुतङ्गवां /
निशि चौरभयाय स्याद्विकृतं मृत्यवे तथा //
text_mt: A groundless cry of cows is to be known to cause fear to the owner; / at night, it leads to fear of thieves, and unnatural [crying leads] to death.

sanskrit_iast:
śivāya svāmino rātrau balīvardo nadan bhavet /
utsṛṣṭavṛṣabho rājño vijayaṃ samprayacchati //
meaning:
शिवाय स्वामिनो रात्रौ बलीवर्दो नदन् भवेत् /
उत्सृष्टवृषभो राज्ञो विजयं सम्प्रयच्छति //
text_mt: An ox bellowing at night brings welfare to its master. / A bull set free confers victory upon a king.

sanskrit_iast:
abhayaṃ bhakṣayantyaś ca gāvo dattās tathā svakāḥ /
tyaktasnehāḥ svavatseṣu garbhakṣayakarā matāḥ //
meaning:
अभयं भक्षयन्त्यश् च गावो दत्तास् तथा स्वकाः /
त्यक्तस्नेहाः स्ववत्सेषु गर्भक्षयकरा मताः //
text_mt: And cows that eat fearlessly, as well as those given away as one's own, [are auspicious]; / those lacking affection for their calves are considered to cause loss of the womb.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmiṃ pādair vinighnantyo dīnā bhītā bhayāvahāḥ /
ārdrāṅgyo hṛṣṭaromāś ca śṛgalagnamṛdaḥ śubhāḥ //
meaning:
भूमिं पादैर् विनिघ्नन्त्यो दीना भीता भयावहाः /
आर्द्राङ्ग्यो हृष्टरोमाश् च शृगलग्नमृदः शुभाः //
text_mt: Cows striking the ground with their feet, wretched and frightened, bring fear. / Those whose limbs are wet, whose hair stands on end, and who have mud sticking to their horns, are auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣyādiṣu cāpyetat sarvaṃ vācyaṃ vijānatā /
ārohaṇaṃ tathānyena saparyāṇasya(1) vājinaḥ //
meaning:
महिष्यादिषु चाप्येतत् सर्वं वाच्यं विजानता /
आरोहणं तथान्येन सपर्याणस्य(1) वाजिनः //
text_mt: All this should also be declared by a knowledgeable person regarding she-buffaloes and the like. / Likewise, if a horse with a saddle is mounted by another,

sanskrit_iast:
jalopaveśanaṃ neṣṭaṃ bhūmau ca parivartanaṃ /
vipatkaranturaṅgasya suptaṃ vāpyanimittataḥ //
meaning:
जलोपवेशनं नेष्टं भूमौ च परिवर्तनं /
विपत्करन्तुरङ्गस्य सुप्तं वाप्यनिमित्ततः //
text_mt: [or] sitting in water, or rolling on the ground—[these] are not desirable; / or sleeping without cause brings calamity to the horse.

sanskrit_iast:
yavamodakayordveṣastvakasmācca na śasyate /
vadanādrudhirotpattirvepanaṃ na ca śasyate //
meaning:
यवमोदकयोर्द्वेषस्त्वकस्माच्च न शस्यते /
वदनाद्रुधिरोत्पत्तिर्वेपनं न च शस्यते //
text_mt: Sudden aversion to barley and sweets is not praised; / bleeding from the mouth and trembling are not praised.

sanskrit_iast:
krīḍan vaikaḥ kapotaiś ca sārikābhirmṛtiṃ vadet /
sāśrunetro jihvayā ca pādalehī vinaṣṭaye(2) //
meaning:
क्रीडन् वैकः कपोतैश् च सारिकाभिर्मृतिं वदेत् /
साश्रुनेत्रो जिह्वया च पादलेही विनष्टये(2) //
text_mt: Playing alone with pigeons or with mynas indicates death; / with tearful eyes and licking its legs with its tongue, [it leads] to destruction.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmapādena ca tathā vilikhaṃś ca vasundharāṃ /
svapedvā vāmapārśvena divā vā na śubhapradaḥ //
meaning:
वामपादेन च तथा विलिखंश् च वसुन्धरां /
स्वपेद्वा वामपार्श्वेन दिवा वा न शुभप्रदः //
text_mt: And scratching the earth with its left foot, / or sleeping on its left side during the day, does not bestow good fortune.

sanskrit_iast:
bhayāya syāt sakṛnmūtrī tathā nidrāvilānanaḥ /
:n
1 saparyārhasyeti sādhuḥ
2 vināśakṛditi ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 341
ārohaṇaṃ na ceddadyāt pratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet //
meaning:
भयाय स्यात् सकृन्मूत्री तथा निद्राविलाननः /
:न्
1 सपर्यार्हस्येति साधुः
2 विनाशकृदिति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 341
आरोहणं न चेद्दद्यात् प्रतीपं वा गृहं व्रजेत् //
text_mt:
Excreting urine and dung together, or having a face clouded with sleep, brings fear.
[...]
1. "Saparyārhasya" is the correct reading.
2. "Vināśakṛt" in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
Page 341.
If it does not permit mounting, or turns back to the stable,

sanskrit_iast:
yātrāvighātamācaṣṭe vāmapārśvaṃ tathā spṛśan /
heṣamāṇaḥ śatruyodhaṃ pādasparśī jayāvahaḥ //
meaning:
यात्राविघातमाचष्टे वामपार्श्वं तथा स्पृशन् /
हेषमाणः शत्रुयोधं पादस्पर्शी जयावहः //
text_mt: it indicates an obstacle to the expedition; likewise, touching its left flank [is ominous]. / Neighing [and] touching an enemy warrior with its hoof brings victory.

sanskrit_iast:
grāme vrajati nāgaścen maithunaṃ deśahā bhavet /
prasūtā nāgavanitā mattā cāntāya bhūpateḥ //
meaning:
ग्रामे व्रजति नागश्चेन् मैथुनं देशहा भवेत् /
प्रसूता नागवनिता मत्ता चान्ताय भूपतेः //
text_mt: If an elephant enters a village, copulation [there] destroys the country; / a female elephant giving birth or in musth leads to the end of the king.

sanskrit_iast:
ārohaṇaṃ na ceddadyāt pratīpaṃ vā gṛhaṃ vrajet /
madaṃ vā vāraṇo jahyādrājaghātakaro bhavet //
meaning:
आरोहणं न चेद्दद्यात् प्रतीपं वा गृहं व्रजेत् /
मदं वा वारणो जह्याद्राजघातकरो भवेत् //
text_mt: If it does not permit mounting, or turns back to its stable, / or if the elephant sheds its musth, it will cause the death of the king.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmaṃ dakṣiṇapādena pādamākramate śubhaḥ /
dakṣiṇañca tathā dantaṃ parimārṣṭi kareṇa ca //
meaning:
वामं दक्षिणपादेन पादमाक्रमते शुभः /
दक्षिणञ्च तथा दन्तं परिमार्ष्टि करेण च //
text_mt: When it steps over its left foot with its right foot, it is auspicious; / and likewise when it wipes its right tusk with its trunk.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣo 'śvaḥ kuñjaro vāpi ripusainyagato 'śubhaḥ /
khaṇḍameghātivṛṣṭyā tu senā nāśamavāpnuyāt //
meaning:
वृषो ऽश्वः कुञ्जरो वापि रिपुसैन्यगतो ऽशुभः /
खण्डमेघातिवृष्ट्या तु सेना नाशमवाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: A bull, horse, or elephant that goes over to the enemy army is inauspicious. / Through the excessive rain of scattered clouds, an army meets destruction.

sanskrit_iast:
pratikūlagraharkṣāttu tathā sammukhamārutāt(1) /
yātrākāle raṇe vāpi chatrādipatanaṃ bhayaṃ //
meaning:
प्रतिकूलग्रहर्क्षात्तु तथा सम्मुखमारुतात्(1) /
यात्राकाले रणे वापि छत्रादिपतनं भयं //
text_mt: Due to adverse planets and lunar mansions, as well as a headwind, / at the time of an expedition or in battle, the falling of umbrellas and the like brings fear.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛṣṭā narāścānulomā grahā vai jayalakṣaṇaṃ /
kākair yodhābhibhavanaṃ kravyādbhirmaṇḍalakṣayaḥ //
meaning:
हृष्टा नराश्चानुलोमा ग्रहा वै जयलक्षणं /
काकैर् योधाभिभवनं क्रव्याद्भिर्मण्डलक्षयः //
text_mt: Men who are joyous and planets that are favorable are marks of victory; / the overcoming of warriors by crows [is unfavorable], and by carnivorous creatures [indicates] destruction of the realm.

sanskrit_iast:
prācīpaścimakaiśānī śaumyā preṣṭhā śubhā ca dik //

ekatriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||

1 vāmaṃ dakṣiṇetyādiḥ, sammukhamārutādityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ
jha.. pustake nāsti
:p 342

yātrāmaṇḍalacintādiḥ

प्राचीपश्चिमकैशानी शौम्या प्रेष्ठा शुभा च दिक् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शकुनानि नाम
एकत्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्

झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति

:श् अथ द्वात्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
यात्रामण्डलचिन्तादिः
text_mt:
The east, west, northeast, and north are most favored and auspicious directions.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-first chapter, named "Omens", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[...]
1. The text beginning with "vāmaṃ dakṣiṇa-" up to "sammukhamārutāt" is not present in manuscript jha.
Page 342.
Now, the two hundred and thirty-second chapter.
Deliberation on the Circle of Kings for an Expedition, etc.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
sarvayātrāṃ pravakṣyāmi rājadharmasamāśrayāt /
astaṅgate nīcagate vikale ripurāśige //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
सर्वयात्रां प्रवक्ष्यामि राजधर्मसमाश्रयात् /
अस्तङ्गते नीचगते विकले रिपुराशिगे //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / I will explain all expeditions, based upon the duties of kings. / When [a planet] has set, is in its debilitation, is impaired, or is in an enemy sign,

sanskrit_iast:
pratilome ca vidhvaste śukre yātrāṃ visarjayet(1) /
pratilome budhe yātrāṃ dikpatau ca tathā ca grahe //
meaning:
प्रतिलोमे च विध्वस्ते शुक्रे यात्रां विसर्जयेत्(1) /
प्रतिलोमे बुधे यात्रां दिक्पतौ च तथा च ग्रहे //
text_mt: and when Venus is retrograde or afflicted, one should avoid an expedition; / likewise when Mercury is retrograde, and when the planetary regent of the direction is [adverse].

sanskrit_iast:
vaidhṛtau ca vyatīpāte nāge ca śakunau tathā /
catuṣpāde ca kintughne tathā yātrāṃ vivarjayet //
meaning:
वैधृतौ च व्यतीपाते नागे च शकुनौ तथा /
चतुष्पादे च किन्तुघ्ने तथा यात्रां विवर्जयेत् //
text_mt: And during Vaidhṛta, Vyatīpāta, Nāga, Śakuni, / Catuṣpad, and Kiṃtughna, one should likewise avoid an expedition.

sanskrit_iast:
vipattāre naidhane ca pratyarau cātha janmani /
gaṇḍe vivarjayedyātrāṃ riktāyāñca tithāvapi //
meaning:
विपत्तारे नैधने च प्रत्यरौ चाथ जन्मनि /
गण्डे विवर्जयेद्यात्रां रिक्तायाञ्च तिथावपि //
text_mt: Under a star of adversity, of death, of enmity, or the star of birth, / during a gaṇḍa, and also on an empty lunar day, one should avoid an expedition.

sanskrit_iast:
udīcī ca tathā prācī(2) tayoraikyaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
paścimā dakṣiṇā yā dik tayoraikyaṃ tathaiva ca //
meaning:
उदीची च तथा प्राची(2) तयोरैक्यं प्रकीर्तितं /
पश्चिमा दक्षिणा या दिक् तयोरैक्यं तथैव च //
text_mt: The north and the east: their unity is proclaimed; / the west and the south: their unity is likewise stated.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyvagnidiksamudbhūtaṃ parighanna tu laṅghayet /
ādityacandraśaurāstu divasāś ca na śobhanāḥ //
meaning:
वाय्वग्निदिक्समुद्भूतं परिघन्न तु लङ्घयेत् /
आदित्यचन्द्रशौरास्तु दिवसाश् च न शोभनाः //
text_mt: One should not cross the obstacle arising in the direction of the wind (northwest) or fire (southeast). / The days of the Sun, the Moon, and Saturn are not auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛttikādyāni pūrveṇa maghādyāni ca yāmyataḥ /
maitrādyānyapare cātha vāsavādyāni vāpyudak //
meaning:
कृत्तिकाद्यानि पूर्वेण मघाद्यानि च याम्यतः /
मैत्राद्यान्यपरे चाथ वासवाद्यानि वाप्युदक् //
text_mt: [The asterisms] beginning with Kṛttikā belong to the east, those beginning with Maghā to the south, / those beginning with Maitrā (Anurādhā) to the west, and those beginning with Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā) to the north.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvadvārāṇi śastāni chāyāmānaṃ vadāmi te /
āditye viṃśatirjñeyāś candre ṣoḍaśa kīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
सर्वद्वाराणि शस्तानि छायामानं वदामि ते /
आदित्ये विंशतिर्ज्ञेयाश् चन्द्रे षोडश कीर्तिताः //
text_mt: All gates are praised; I shall tell you the measurement of shadows: / on Sunday, twenty [aṅgulas] are known; on Monday, sixteen are proclaimed;

sanskrit_iast:
bhaume pañcadaśaivoktāś caturdaśa tathā budhe /
:n
1 vivarjayet iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
2 dik pūrvā yā tathodīcīti ja..
:p 343
trayodaśa tathā jīye śukre dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
भौमे पञ्चदशैवोक्ताश् चतुर्दश तथा बुधे /
:न्
1 विवर्जयेत् इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
2 दिक् पूर्वा या तथोदीचीति ज..
:प् 343
त्रयोदश तथा जीये शुक्रे द्वादश कीर्तिताः //

sanskrit_iast:
ekādaśa tathā saure sarvakarmasu kīrtitāḥ /
janmalagne śakracāpe sammukhe na vrajennaraḥ //
meaning:
एकादश तथा सौरे सर्वकर्मसु कीर्तिताः /
जन्मलग्ने शक्रचापे सम्मुखे न व्रजेन्नरः //
text_mt: and eleven on Saturday, proclaimed for all undertakings. / A man should not set out during the ascendant of birth, or when Indra's rainbow is in front.

sanskrit_iast:
śakunādau śubhe yāyājjayāya harimāsmaran /
vakṣye maṇḍalacintānte kartavyaṃ rājarakṣaṇaṃ //
meaning:
शकुनादौ शुभे यायाज्जयाय हरिमास्मरन् /
वक्ष्ये मण्डलचिन्तान्ते कर्तव्यं राजरक्षणं //
text_mt: When an omen and the like is auspicious, he should march for victory, remembering Hari. / Following the deliberation on the circle [of kings], I shall speak of the protection of the king that must be performed.

sanskrit_iast:
svāmyamātyaṃ tathā durgaṃ koṣo daṇḍastathaiva ca /
mitrañjanapadaś caiva rājyaṃ saptāṅgamucyate //
meaning:
स्वाम्यमात्यं तथा दुर्गं कोषो दण्डस्तथैव च /
मित्रञ्जनपदश् चैव राज्यं सप्ताङ्गमुच्यते //
text_mt: The lord, the minister, the fortress, the treasury, and the army, / the ally, and the territory: the kingdom is said to have seven limbs.

sanskrit_iast:
saptāṅgasya tu rājyasya vighnakartṝn vināśayet /
maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu vṛddhiḥ kāryā mahīkṣitā //
meaning:
सप्ताङ्गस्य तु राज्यस्य विघ्नकर्तॄन् विनाशयेत् /
मण्डलेषु च सर्वेषु वृद्धिः कार्या महीक्षिता //
text_mt: He should destroy those who create obstacles for the seven-limbed kingdom; / and prosperity must be achieved by the ruler of the earth in all circles [of kings].

sanskrit_iast:
ātmamaṇḍalamevātra prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ bhavet /
sāmantāstasya vijñeyā ripavo maṇḍalasya tu //
meaning:
आत्ममण्डलमेवात्र प्रथमं मण्डलं भवेत् /
सामन्तास्तस्य विज्ञेया रिपवो मण्डलस्य तु //
text_mt: One's own circle here is the first circle; / the adjacent rulers are known as the enemies of that circle.

sanskrit_iast:
upetastu suhṛj jñeyaḥ śatrumitramataḥ paraṃ /
mitramitraṃ tato jñeyaṃ mitramitraripustataḥ //
meaning:
उपेतस्तु सुहृज् ज्ञेयः शत्रुमित्रमतः परं /
मित्रमित्रं ततो ज्ञेयं मित्रमित्ररिपुस्ततः //
text_mt: The one adjoining [the enemy] is known as a friend; beyond that is the enemy's friend; / after that is known the friend's friend; after that is the enemy's friend's friend.

sanskrit_iast:
etatpurastāt kathitaṃ paścādapi nibodha me /
pārṣṇigrāhastataḥ paścāttatastvākranda ucyate(1) //
meaning:
एतत्पुरस्तात् कथितं पश्चादपि निबोध मे /
पार्ष्णिग्राहस्ततः पश्चात्ततस्त्वाक्रन्द उच्यते(1) //
text_mt: This is stated regarding the front; understand from me also what is behind: / the rearward enemy is behind, and after him is called the rearward ally.

sanskrit_iast:
āsārastu tato 'nyaḥ syādākrandāsāra ucyate /
jigīṣoḥ śatruyuktasya vimuktasya tathā dvija //
meaning:
आसारस्तु ततो ऽन्यः स्यादाक्रन्दासार उच्यते /
जिगीषोः शत्रुयुक्तस्य विमुक्तस्य तथा द्विज //
text_mt: The one after him would be the ally of the rearward enemy, and [the next] is called the ally of the rearward ally. / For the conqueror, joined with or freed from an enemy, O twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
nātrāpi niś cayaḥ śakyo vaktuṃ manujapuṅgava /
nigrahānugrahe śakto madhyasthaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
नात्रापि निश् चयः शक्यो वक्तुं मनुजपुङ्गव /
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तो मध्यस्थः परिकीर्तितः //
text_mt: no certainty can be stated here, O best of men! / Capable of punishment and favor, the intermediary is proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
nigrahānugrahe śaktaḥ sarveṣāmapi yo bhavet /
udāsīnaḥ sa kathito balavān pṛthivīpatiḥ //
:n
1 maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu sureśvarasamā hi te ity ardhaśloka
āsārastvityasya pūrvaṃ ṭa.. pustake vartate, parantvasaṃlagnaḥ
:p 344
meaning:
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तः सर्वेषामपि यो भवेत् /
उदासीनः स कथितो बलवान् पृथिवीपतिः //
:न्
1 मण्डलेषु च सर्वेषु सुरेश्वरसमा हि ते इत्य् अर्धश्लोक
आसारस्त्वित्यस्य पूर्वं ट.. पुस्तके वर्तते, परन्त्वसंलग्नः
:प् 344
text_mt:
Whoever is capable of punishment and favor toward all / is called the neutral king, a powerful ruler of the earth.
[...]
1. The half-verse "maṇḍaleṣu ca sarveṣu sureśvarasamā hi te" occurs before "āsārastu" in manuscript ṭa, but it is unconnected.
Page 344.

sanskrit_iast:
na kasyacidripurmitraṅkāraṇācchatrumitrake /
maṇḍalaṃ tava samproktametad dvādaśarājakaṃ //
meaning:
न कस्यचिद्रिपुर्मित्रङ्कारणाच्छत्रुमित्रके /
मण्डलं तव सम्प्रोक्तमेतद् द्वादशराजकं //
text_mt: No one is an enemy or a friend [by nature]; enemies and friends exist due to a cause. / This circle of twelve kings has been declared to you.

sanskrit_iast:
trividhā ripavo jñeyāḥ kulyānantarakṛtrimāḥ /
pūrvapūrvo gurusteṣāṃ duścikitsyatamo mataḥ //
meaning:
त्रिविधा रिपवो ज्ञेयाः कुल्यानन्तरकृत्रिमाः /
पूर्वपूर्वो गुरुस्तेषां दुश्चिकित्स्यतमो मतः //
text_mt: Enemies are known to be of three kinds: born of the same family, neighboring, and fabricated; / each preceding one is considered more formidable and more difficult to cure than the next.

sanskrit_iast:
anantaro 'pi yaḥ śatruḥ so 'pi me kṛtrimo mataḥ /
pārṣṇigrāho bhavecchatrormitrāṇi ripavas tathā //
meaning:
अनन्तरो ऽपि यः शत्रुः सो ऽपि मे कृत्रिमो मतः /
पार्ष्णिग्राहो भवेच्छत्रोर्मित्राणि रिपवस् तथा //
text_mt: Even an immediate neighbor who is an enemy is also considered by me as fabricated. / The rearward enemy belongs to the enemy, and likewise allies [can become] enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
pārṣṇigrāhamupāyaiś ca śamayecca tathā svakaṃ /
mitreṇa śatrorucchedaṃ praśaṃsanti purātanāḥ //
meaning:
पार्ष्णिग्राहमुपायैश् च शमयेच्च तथा स्वकं /
मित्रेण शत्रोरुच्छेदं प्रशंसन्ति पुरातनाः //
text_mt: One should pacify one's own rearward enemy by means of expedients; / the ancients praise the eradication of an enemy by means of an ally.

sanskrit_iast:
mitrañca śatrutāmeti sāmantatvādanantaraṃ /
śatruṃ jigoṣurucchindyāt(1) svayaṃ śaknoti cedyadi //
meaning:
मित्रञ्च शत्रुतामेति सामन्तत्वादनन्तरं /
शत्रुं जिगोषुरुच्छिन्द्यात्(1) स्वयं शक्नोति चेद्यदि //
text_mt: And an ally turns into an enemy due to immediately bordering; / if the would-be conqueror is able himself, he should eradicate the enemy.

sanskrit_iast:
pratāpavṛddhau tenāpi nāmitrājjāyate bhayaṃ /
yathāsya nodvijelloko viśvāsaś ca yathā bhavet //
meaning:
प्रतापवृद्धौ तेनापि नामित्राज्जायते भयं /
यथास्य नोद्विजेल्लोको विश्वासश् च यथा भवेत् //
text_mt: When majesty increases through that, no fear arises even from an enemy; / in such a way that the people do not become agitated and trust is established,

sanskrit_iast:
jigīṣurdharmavijayī tathā lokaṃ vaśannayet /
:e ity āgneye mahāopurāṇe yātrāmaṇḍalacintādirnāma
dvātriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trayastriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ
meaning:
जिगीषुर्धर्मविजयी तथा लोकं वशन्नयेत् /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महाओपुराणे यात्रामण्डलचिन्तादिर्नाम
द्वात्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
षाड्गुण्यं
text_mt:
the would-be conqueror, victorious through righteousness, should bring the world under his sway.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-second chapter, named 'Consideration of Expedition, the Maṇḍala, and Other Matters', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirty-third chapter:
The Six Measures of Policy

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
sāmabhedau mayā proktau dānadaṇḍau tathaiva ca /
daṇḍaḥ svadeśe kathitaḥ paradeśe vravīmi te //
:n
1 śatruṃ jihīrṣurucchindyāditi gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 345
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
सामभेदौ मया प्रोक्तौ दानदण्डौ तथैव च /
दण्डः स्वदेशे कथितः परदेशे व्रवीमि ते //
:न्
1 शत्रुं जिहीर्षुरुच्छिन्द्यादिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 345
text_mt:
Puṣkara said: / Conciliation and sowing dissension have been taught by me, and likewise gift and punishment. / Punishment has been described regarding one's own realm; I shall explain it to you regarding a foreign realm.
[...]
1 'Wishing to take the enemy, he should uproot [him]' in manuscripts gha and ña. / [Page 345]

sanskrit_iast:
prakāśaścāprakāśaś ca dvividho daṇḍa ucyate /
luṇṭhanaṃ grāmaghātaś ca śasyaghāto 'gnidīpanaṃ //
meaning:
प्रकाशश्चाप्रकाशश् च द्विविधो दण्ड उच्यते /
लुण्ठनं ग्रामघातश् च शस्यघातो ऽग्निदीपनं //
text_mt: Punishment is said to be of two kinds: open and secret. / Plundering, devastation of villages, destruction of crops, setting fires,

sanskrit_iast:
prakāśo 'tha viṣaṃ vahnirvividhaiḥ puruṣair badhaḥ /
dūṣaṇañcaiva sādhūnāmudakānāñca dūṣaṇaṃ //
meaning:
प्रकाशो ऽथ विषं वह्निर्विविधैः पुरुषैर् बधः /
दूषणञ्चैव साधूनामुदकानाञ्च दूषणं //
text_mt: are open [punishment]; whereas poison, fire, slaying through various secret agents, / defamation of honest persons, and poisoning of waters,

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍapraṇayaṇaṃ proktamupekṣāṃ śṛṇu bhārgava /
yadā manyate nṛpatī raṇe na mama vigrahaḥ //
meaning:
दण्डप्रणयणं प्रोक्तमुपेक्षां शृणु भार्गव /
यदा मन्यते नृपती रणे न मम विग्रहः //
text_mt: are described as the execution of [covert] punishment. Hear about diplomatic indifference, O descendant of Bhṛgu: / When a king considers, 'War in battle will not [benefit] me,

sanskrit_iast:
anarthāyānubandhaḥ syāt sandhinā ca tathā bhavet /
sāmalabdhāspadañcātra dānañcārthakṣayaṅkaraṃ //
meaning:
अनर्थायानुबन्धः स्यात् सन्धिना च तथा भवेत् /
सामलब्धास्पदञ्चात्र दानञ्चार्थक्षयङ्करं //
text_mt: an escalation would lead to misfortune, and likewise through an alliance; / conciliation finds no ground here, and a gift causes loss of wealth;

sanskrit_iast:
bhedadaṇḍānubandhaḥ syāttadopekṣāṃ samāśrayet /
na cāyaṃ mama śaknoti kiñcit kartumupadravaṃ //
meaning:
भेददण्डानुबन्धः स्यात्तदोपेक्षां समाश्रयेत् /
न चायं मम शक्नोति किञ्चित् कर्तुमुपद्रवं //
text_mt: an escalation of dissension or punishment would occur,' then he should resort to indifference. / [Or if he thinks,] 'This enemy is not able to cause me any injury,

sanskrit_iast:
na cāhamasya śaknomi tatropekṣāṃ samāśrayet /
avajñopahatastatra rājñā kāryo ripurbhavet //
meaning:
न चाहमस्य शक्नोमि तत्रोपेक्षां समाश्रयेत् /
अवज्ञोपहतस्तत्र राज्ञा कार्यो रिपुर्भवेत् //
text_mt: and I am not able [to harm] him,' then he should resort to indifference. / There the enemy should be brought into a condition of being stricken by contempt by the king.

sanskrit_iast:
māyopāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi utpātair anṛtaiś carat /
śatrorudvejanaṃ śatroḥ śivirasthasya pakṣiṇaḥ //
meaning:
मायोपायं प्रवक्ष्यामि उत्पातैर् अनृतैश् चरत् /
शत्रोरुद्वेजनं शत्रोः शिविरस्थस्य पक्षिणः //
text_mt: I shall declare the method of illusion: operating with false portents, / causing terror to the enemy; [for example,] attaching to the tail of a bird,

sanskrit_iast:
sthūlasya tasya pucchasthāṃ kṛtvolkāṃ vipulāṃ dvija /
visṛjecca tataś caivamulkāpātaṃ pradarśayet //
meaning:
स्थूलस्य तस्य पुच्छस्थां कृत्वोल्कां विपुलां द्विज /
विसृजेच्च ततश् चैवमुल्कापातं प्रदर्शयेत् //
text_mt: a large one, that resides in the enemy's camp, a huge firebrand, O twice-born one, / and then releasing it, he should thus display the falling of a meteor.

sanskrit_iast:
evamanye darśanīyā utpātā bahavo 'pi ca /
udvejanaṃ tathā kuryāt kuhakair vividhair dviṣāṃ //
meaning:
एवमन्ये दर्शनीया उत्पाता बहवो ऽपि च /
उद्वेजनं तथा कुर्यात् कुहकैर् विविधैर् द्विषां //
text_mt: In this way many other portents also should be shown. / Likewise he should terrify enemies through diverse illusions.

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃvatsarāstāpasāś ca nāśaṃ brūyuḥ prarasya ca /
jigīṣuḥ pṛthivīṃ rājā tena codvejayet parān //
meaning:
सांवत्सरास्तापसाश् च नाशं ब्रूयुः प्ररस्य च /
जिगीषुः पृथिवीं राजा तेन चोद्वेजयेत् परान् //
text_mt: Astrologers and ascetics should predict the destruction of the adversary; / and by this means the king desiring conquest over the earth should alarm his foes.

sanskrit_iast:
devatānāṃ prasādaś ca kīrtanīyaḥ parasya tu /
āgatanno 'mitrabalaṃ praharadhvamabhītavat //
meaning:
देवतानां प्रसादश् च कीर्तनीयः परस्य तु /
आगतन्नो ऽमित्रबलं प्रहरध्वमभीतवत् //
text_mt: And the favor of deities toward him should be proclaimed to the enemy: / 'Our enemy's army has arrived; strike without fear!'

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ brūyādraṇe prāpte bhagnāḥ sarve pare iti /
:p 346
kṣveḍāḥ kilakilāḥ kāryā vācyaḥ śatrurhatas tathā //
meaning:
एवं ब्रूयाद्रणे प्राप्ते भग्नाः सर्वे परे इति /
:प् 346
क्ष्वेडाः किलकिलाः कार्या वाच्यः शत्रुर्हतस् तथा //
text_mt:
Thus he should proclaim when battle is joined: 'The enemies have all been broken!'
[Page 346]
War cries and shouts of triumph should be raised, and it should be declared: 'The enemy has been slain!'

sanskrit_iast:
devājñāvṛṃhito rājā sannaddhaḥ samaraṃ prati /
indrajālaṃ pravakṣyāmi indraṃ kālena darśayet //
meaning:
देवाज्ञावृंहितो राजा सन्नद्धः समरं प्रति /
इन्द्रजालं प्रवक्ष्यामि इन्द्रं कालेन दर्शयेत् //
text_mt: The king, bolstered by divine command, should be equipped for battle. / I shall explain sorcery: he should display Indra in due time,

sanskrit_iast:
caturaṅgaṃ balaṃ rājā sahāyārthaṃ divaukasāṃ /
balantu darśayet prāptaṃ raktavṛṣṭiñcendrapau //
meaning:
चतुरङ्गं बलं राजा सहायार्थं दिवौकसां /
बलन्तु दर्शयेत् प्राप्तं रक्तवृष्टिञ्चेन्द्रपौ //
text_mt: a fourfold army [descending] to aid the king on behalf of the gods; / he should display an army arrived, and a rain of blood, and royal guardians,

sanskrit_iast:
chinnāni ripuśīrṣāṇi prāsādāgreṣu darśayet(1) /
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ sampravakṣyāmi tadvarau sandhivigrahau //
meaning:
छिन्नानि रिपुशीर्षाणि प्रासादाग्रेषु दर्शयेत्(1) /
षाड्गुण्यं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि तद्वरौ सन्धिविग्रहौ //
text_mt: and severed heads of enemies displayed upon the tops of temples. / I shall declare the sixfold policy, of which alliance and war are the foremost:

sanskrit_iast:
sandhiś ca vigrahaś caiva yānamāsanameva ca /
dvaidhībhāvaḥ saṃśayaś ca ṣaḍguṇāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
सन्धिश् च विग्रहश् चैव यानमासनमेव च /
द्वैधीभावः संशयश् च षड्गुणाः परिकीर्तिताः //
text_mt: Alliance, war, marching, halting, / duplicity, and seeking refuge are declared to be the six measures of policy.

sanskrit_iast:
paṇabandhaḥ smṛtaḥ sandhirapakārastu vigrahaḥ /
jigīṣoḥ śatruviṣaye yānaṃ yātrābhidhīyate //
meaning:
पणबन्धः स्मृतः सन्धिरपकारस्तु विग्रहः /
जिगीषोः शत्रुविषये यानं यात्राभिधीयते //
text_mt: Alliance is traditionally understood as a binding agreement, whereas war is injury. / The movement of one desiring conquest into the enemy's territory is termed marching.

sanskrit_iast:
vigraheṇa svake deśe sthitirāsanamucyate /
balārdhena prayāṇantu dvaidhībhāvaḥ sa ucyate //
meaning:
विग्रहेण स्वके देशे स्थितिरासनमुच्यते /
बलार्धेन प्रयाणन्तु द्वैधीभावः स उच्यते //
text_mt: Remaining in one's own realm while in a state of hostility is called halting. / Setting out with half one's force is called duplicity.

sanskrit_iast:
udāsīno madhyago vā saṃśrayātsaṃśayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
samena sandhiranveṣyo 'hīnena ca balīyasā //
meaning:
उदासीनो मध्यगो वा संश्रयात्संशयः स्मृतः /
समेन सन्धिरन्वेष्यो ऽहीनेन च बलीयसा //
text_mt: Seeking shelter with a neutral or intermediary king is known as seeking refuge. / An alliance should be sought with an equal, not with an inferior, and with one who is stronger.

sanskrit_iast:
hīnena vigrahaḥ kāryaḥ svayaṃ rājñā balīyasā /
tatrāpi śuddhapārṣṇistu balīyāṃsaṃ samāśrayet //
meaning:
हीनेन विग्रहः कार्यः स्वयं राज्ञा बलीयसा /
तत्रापि शुद्धपार्ष्णिस्तु बलीयांसं समाश्रयेत् //
text_mt: War should be waged against an inferior by a stronger king himself; / even then, having secured his rear, he should resort to a stronger ally.

sanskrit_iast:
āsīnaḥ karmavicchedaṃ śaktaḥ kartuṃ riporyadā /
aśuddhapārṣṇiścāsīta vigṛhya vasudhādhipaḥ //
meaning:
आसीनः कर्मविच्छेदं शक्तः कर्तुं रिपोर्यदा /
अशुद्धपार्ष्णिश्चासीत विगृह्य वसुधाधिपः //
text_mt: When, while remaining halted, the ruler of the earth is able to interrupt the enemy's undertakings, / he should remain halted in hostility, even if his rear is not secure.

sanskrit_iast:
aśuddhapārṣṇirbalavān dvaidhībhāvaṃ samāśrayet /
balinā vigṛhītastu(2) yo 'sandehena pārthivaḥ //
meaning:
अशुद्धपार्ष्णिर्बलवान् द्वैधीभावं समाश्रयेत् /
बलिना विगृहीतस्तु(2) यो ऽसन्देहेन पार्थिवः //
text_mt: If powerful but with his rear insecure, he should resort to duplicity. / But that monarch who is undoubtedly assailed by a stronger foe,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃśrayastena vaktavyo guṇānāmadhamo guṇaḥ /
:n
1 prāsādāgre pradarśayediti ṭa..
2 vigṛhītastu iti kha..
:p 347
bahukṣayavyayāyāsaṃ(1) teṣāṃ yānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
meaning:
संश्रयस्तेन वक्तव्यो गुणानामधमो गुणः /
:न्
1 प्रासादाग्रे प्रदर्शयेदिति ट..
2 विगृहीतस्तु इति ख..
:प् 347
बहुक्षयव्ययायासं(1) तेषां यानं प्रकीर्तितं //
text_mt:
should adopt seeking refuge, which is said to be the lowest among the measures of policy.
[...]
1 'should display upon the top of a temple' in manuscript ṭa.
2 'vigṛhītastu' in manuscript kha. / [Page 347]
Marching for them is proclaimed to entail great loss, expense, and effort.

sanskrit_iast:
bahulābhakaraṃ paścāttadā rājā samāśrayet(2) /
sarvaśaktivihīnastu tadā kuryāttu saṃśrayaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe upāyaṣaḍguṇādirnāma
trayastriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catustriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
prātyahikarājakarma
meaning:
बहुलाभकरं पश्चात्तदा राजा समाश्रयेत्(2) /
सर्वशक्तिविहीनस्तु तदा कुर्यात्तु संश्रयं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे उपायषड्गुणादिर्नाम
त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुस्त्रिंशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
प्रात्यहिकराजकर्म
text_mt:
When it brings great gain afterward, only then should the king undertake it. / But one completely bereft of all power should then seek refuge.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-third chapter, named 'Means, the Six Measures of Policy, and Other Matters', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and thirty-fourth chapter:
Daily Duties of the King

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
ajasraṃ karma vakṣyāmi dinaṃ prati yadācaret /
dvimuhūrtāvaśeṣāyāṃ rātrau nidrāntyajennṛpaḥ //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
अजस्रं कर्म वक्ष्यामि दिनं प्रति यदाचरेत् /
द्विमुहूर्तावशेषायां रात्रौ निद्रान्त्यजेन्नृपः //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the perpetual duty which he should perform day by day. / When two muhūrtas remain of the night, the king should abandon sleep.

sanskrit_iast:
vādyavandisvanair gītaiḥ paśyed gūḍhāṃstato narān /
vijñāyate na ye lokāstadīyā iti kenacit //
meaning:
वाद्यवन्दिस्वनैर् गीतैः पश्येद् गूढांस्ततो नरान् /
विज्ञायते न ये लोकास्तदीया इति केनचित् //
text_mt: Awakened by the sounds of musical instruments, bards, and songs, he should then interview secret agents, / men whom no people recognize as belonging to him.

sanskrit_iast:
āyavyayasya śravaṇaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi /
vegotsargaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā rājā snānagṛhaṃ vrajet //
meaning:
आयव्ययस्य श्रवणं ततः कार्यं यथाविधि /
वेगोत्सर्गं ततः कृत्वा राजा स्नानगृहं व्रजेत् //
text_mt: Then hearing the report of income and expenditure should be done according to rule. / Having then relieved himself, the king should go to the bathhouse.

sanskrit_iast:
snānaṃ kuryānnṛpaḥ paścāddantadhāvanapūrvakaṃ /
kṛtvā sandhyāntato japyaṃ vāsudevaṃ prapūjayet //
meaning:
स्नानं कुर्यान्नृपः पश्चाद्दन्तधावनपूर्वकं /
कृत्वा सन्ध्यान्ततो जप्यं वासुदेवं प्रपूजयेत् //
