likewise the Srāvantīya chant is the Śrīsūkta in the Sāmaveda.

sanskrit_iast:
śriyaṃ dhātarmayi dhehi prāktamātharvaṇe tathā /
śrīsūktaṃ yo japedbhaktyā hutvā śrīstasya vai bhavet //
meaning:
श्रियं धातर्मयि धेहि प्राक्तमाथर्वणे तथा /
श्रीसूक्तं यो जपेद्भक्त्या हुत्वा श्रीस्तस्य वै भवेत् //
text_mt:
In the Atharvaveda, it is recited as "śriyaṃ dhātar mayi dhehi".
He who, with devotion, offers fire oblations and recites the Śrīsūkta, prosperity shall be his.

sanskrit_iast:
padmāni cātha vilvāni hutvājyaṃ vā tilān śriyaḥ /
ekantu pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ prativedantu sarvadaṃ //
meaning:
पद्मानि चाथ विल्वानि हुत्वाज्यं वा तिलान् श्रियः /
एकन्तु पौरुषं सूक्तं प्रतिवेदन्तु सर्वदं //
text_mt:
Having offered lotuses, vilva fruits, clarified butter, or sesame seeds of Śrī—
and the single Puruṣasūkta in each Veda bestows all things.

sanskrit_iast:
sūktena ddadyānniṣpāpo hy ekaikayā(1) jalāñjaliṃ /
snāta ekaikayā puṣpaṃ viṣṇordatvāghahā bhavet //
meaning:
सूक्तेन द्दद्यान्निष्पापो ह्य् एकैकया(1) जलाञ्जलिं /
स्नात एकैकया पुष्पं विष्णोर्दत्वाघहा भवेत् //
text_mt:
Freed from sin, one should offer a handful of water with each [verse of the] sūkta;
having bathed, giving a flower to Viṣṇu with each one, he becomes a destroyer of sins.

sanskrit_iast:
snāta ekaikayā datvā phalaṃ syāt sarvakāmabhāk /
mahāpāpopapānto bhavejjaptvā tu pauruṣaṃ //
meaning:
स्नात एकैकया दत्वा फलं स्यात् सर्वकामभाक् /
महापापोपपान्तो भवेज्जप्त्वा तु पौरुषं //
text_mt:
Having bathed, by offering a fruit with each one, he enjoys all desires.
Having recited the Puruṣasūkta, he is freed from mortal sins and minor sins.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛcchrair viśuddho japtvā ca hutvā snātvātha sarvabhāk /
aṣṭādaśabhyaḥ śāntibhyastisro 'nyāḥ śāntayo varāḥ //
meaning:
कृच्छ्रैर् विशुद्धो जप्त्वा च हुत्वा स्नात्वाथ सर्वभाक् /
अष्टादशभ्यः शान्तिभ्यस्तिस्रो ऽन्याः शान्तयो वराः //
text_mt:
Purified by kṛcchra penances, reciting [it], offering fire oblations, and having bathed, he enjoys all.
Out of eighteen pacifications, three other pacifications are the best:

sanskrit_iast:
amṛtā cābhayavā saumyā sarvotpātavimardanāḥ /
amṛtā sarvadavatyā abhayā brahmadaivatā //
meaning:
अमृता चाभयवा सौम्या सर्वोत्पातविमर्दनाः /
अमृता सर्वदवत्या अभया ब्रह्मदैवता //
text_mt:
the Amṛtā, the Abhayā, and the Saumyā, which crush all portents.
The Amṛtā has all deities as its divinity; the Abhayā has Brahmā as its deity;

sanskrit_iast:
saumyā ca sarvadaivatyā ekā syātsarvakāmadā /
:n
1 hy ekaikaśa iti ka.. , gha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 461
abhayāyā maṇiḥ kāryo varuṇasya bhṛgūttama //
meaning:
सौम्या च सर्वदैवत्या एका स्यात्सर्वकामदा /
:न्
1 ह्य् एकैकश इति क.. , घ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 461
अभयाया मणिः कार्यो वरुणस्य भृगूत्तम //
text_mt:
and the Saumyā has all deities as its divinity; each single one grants all desires.
[Footnote]
1. "hy ekaikaśaḥ" thus in manuscripts ka, gha, cha, and ña. / [Page 461]
For the Abhayā, an amulet of Varuṇa should be made, O best of the Bhṛgus;

sanskrit_iast:
śatakāṇḍo 'mṛtāyāś ca saumyāyāḥ śaṅkajo maṇiḥ /
taddaivatyās tathā mantrāḥ siddhau(1) syānmaṇibandhanaṃ //
meaning:
शतकाण्डो ऽमृतायाश् च सौम्यायाः शङ्कजो मणिः /
तद्दैवत्यास् तथा मन्त्राः सिद्धौ(1) स्यान्मणिबन्धनं //
text_mt:
the hundred-knotted [dūrvā] for the Amṛtā, and an amulet made of conch for the Saumyā.
Likewise the mantras belong to those deities; upon accomplishment, tying the amulet should take place.

sanskrit_iast:
divyāntarīkṣabhaumādisamutpātārdanā imāḥ /
divyāntarīkṣabhaumantu adbhutaṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu //
meaning:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमादिसमुत्पातार्दना इमाः /
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमन्तु अद्भुतं त्रिविधं शृणु //
text_mt:
These destroy celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents.
Hear from me about the three kinds of portents—celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial:

sanskrit_iast:
graharkṣavaikṛtaṃ divyamāntarīkṣannibodha me /
ulkāpātaś ca digdāhaḥ pariveśastathaiva ca //
meaning:
ग्रहर्क्षवैकृतं दिव्यमान्तरीक्षन्निबोध मे /
उल्कापातश् च दिग्दाहः परिवेशस्तथैव च //
text_mt:
aberrations of planets and lunar mansions are celestial; know from me the atmospheric:
the fall of meteors, the red glow of the horizon, and likewise halos [around the sun or moon],

sanskrit_iast:
gandharvanagarañcaiva vṛṣṭiś ca vikṛtā ca yā /
carasthirabhavaṃ bhūmau bhūkampamapi bhūmijaṃ //
meaning:
गन्धर्वनगरञ्चैव वृष्टिश् च विकृता च या /
चरस्थिरभवं भूमौ भूकम्पमपि भूमिजं //
text_mt:
and the city of the Gandharvas, and unnatural rainfall.
Whatever occurs among mobile or immobile things on earth, and an earthquake, is born of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
saptāhābhyanatare vṛṣṭāvadbhutaṃ bhayakṛdbhavet /
śāntiṃ vinā tribhirvaṣair adbhutaṃ bhayakṛdbhavet //
meaning:
सप्ताहाभ्यनतरे वृष्टावद्भुतं भयकृद्भवेत् /
शान्तिं विना त्रिभिर्वषैर् अद्भुतं भयकृद्भवेत् //
text_mt:
If rain falls within a week [of it], the portent causes fear;
without pacification, the portent causes fear for three years.

sanskrit_iast:
devatārcāḥ(2) pranṛtyanti vepante prajvalanti ca /
āraṭhanti(3) ca rodanti prasvidyante hasanti ca //
meaning:
देवतार्चाः(2) प्रनृत्यन्ति वेपन्ते प्रज्वलन्ति च /
आरठन्ति(3) च रोदन्ति प्रस्विद्यन्ते हसन्ति च //
text_mt:
If divine images dance, tremble, and blaze,
or wail, weep, perspire, and laugh,

sanskrit_iast:
arcāvikāropaśamo 'bhyarcya hutvā prajāpateḥ /
anagnirdīpyate yatra rāṣṭre ca bhṛśanisvanaṃ //
meaning:
अर्चाविकारोपशमो ऽभ्यर्च्य हुत्वा प्रजापतेः /
अनग्निर्दीप्यते यत्र राष्ट्रे च भृशनिस्वनं //
text_mt:
the pacification of a change in an image is performed after worship and fire oblations to Prajāpati.
Where fire blazes without fuel in a kingdom and makes a loud sound,

sanskrit_iast:
na dīpyate cendhanavāṃstadrāṣṭraṃ pāḍyate nṛpaiḥ /
agnivaikṛtyaśamanamagnimantraiś ca bhārgava //
meaning:
न दीप्यते चेन्धनवांस्तद्राष्ट्रं पाड्यते नृपैः /
अग्निवैकृत्यशमनमग्निमन्त्रैश् च भार्गव //
text_mt:
or does not blaze even when supplied with fuel, that kingdom is oppressed by kings.
The pacification of fire's unnatural state is by means of Agni's mantras, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast:
akāle phalitā vṛkṣāḥ kṣīraṃ raktaṃ sravanti ca /
vṛkṣotpātapraśamanaṃ śivaṃ pūjya ca kārayet //
meaning:
अकाले फलिता वृक्षाः क्षीरं रक्तं स्रवन्ति च /
वृक्षोत्पातप्रशमनं शिवं पूज्य च कारयेत् //
text_mt:
When trees bear fruit out of season, and ooze milk or blood,
one should bring about the pacification of tree portents by worshipping Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
ativṛṣṭiranāvṛṣṭirdurbhikṣāyobhayaṃ mataṃ /
:n
1 siddhyā iti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 devatāśceti kha.. , cha.. ca
3 āvaṭantīti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 462
anṛtau tridinārabdhavṛṣṭirjñeyā bhayāya hi //
meaning:
अतिवृष्टिरनावृष्टिर्दुर्भिक्षायोभयं मतं /
:न्
1 सिद्ध्या इति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 देवताश्चेति ख.. , छ.. च
3 आवटन्तीति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 462
अनृतौ त्रिदिनारब्धवृष्टिर्ज्ञेया भयाय हि //
text_mt:
Excessive rain and drought are both considered to lead to famine.
[Footnote] / 1. "siddhyā" thus in manuscripts gha and ña.
2. "devatāś ca" thus in manuscripts kha and cha.
3. "āvaṭan" thus in manuscripts kha, gha, cha, and ña. / [Page 462]
Rain beginning out of season and lasting three days should be known to cause fear.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣṭivaikṛtyanāśaḥ syātparjaṇyendvarkapūjanāt /
nagarādapasarpante samīpamupayānti ca //
meaning:
वृष्टिवैकृत्यनाशः स्यात्पर्जण्येन्द्वर्कपूजनात् /
नगरादपसर्पन्ते समीपमुपयान्ति च //
text_mt:
The destruction of unnatural rainfall comes from worshipping Parjanya, the Moon, and the Sun.
If rivers, lakes, and springs withdraw from a city,

sanskrit_iast:
nadyo hradapraśravaṇā virasāś ca bhavanti ca /
śalilāśayavaikṛtye japtavyo vāruṇo manuḥ //
meaning:
नद्यो ह्रदप्रश्रवणा विरसाश् च भवन्ति च /
शलिलाशयवैकृत्ये जप्तव्यो वारुणो मनुः //
text_mt:
or draw near it, or become tasteless—
in the case of an unnatural state of bodies of water, the mantra of Varuṇa is to be recited.

sanskrit_iast:
akālaprasavā nāryaḥ kālato vāprajās tathā /
vikṛtaprasavāś caiva yugmaprasavanādikaṃ //
meaning:
अकालप्रसवा नार्यः कालतो वाप्रजास् तथा /
विकृतप्रसवाश् चैव युग्मप्रसवनादिकं //
text_mt:
When women give birth out of season, or produce no offspring in season,
or have unnatural births, twins, and the like,

sanskrit_iast:
strīṇāṃ prasavavaikṛtye strīviprādiṃ prapūjayet /
vaḍavā hastinī gaurvā yadi yugmaṃ prasūyate //
meaning:
स्त्रीणां प्रसववैकृत्ये स्त्रीविप्रादिं प्रपूजयेत् /
वडवा हस्तिनी गौर्वा यदि युग्मं प्रसूयते //
text_mt:
in an unnatural state of women's childbirth, one should worship women, brāhmaṇas, and others.
If a mare, female elephant, or cow gives birth to twins,

sanskrit_iast:
vijātyaṃ vikṛtaṃ vāpi ṣaḍbhirmāsair mriyeta vai /
vikṛtaṃ vā prasūyante paracakrabhayaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
विजात्यं विकृतं वापि षड्भिर्मासैर् म्रियेत वै /
विकृतं वा प्रसूयन्ते परचक्रभयं भवेत् //
text_mt:
or to a different species or a deformed creature, it surely dies in six months;
or if they give birth to monstrosities, there will be danger from an enemy army.

sanskrit_iast:
homaḥ prasūtivaikṛtye japo viprādipūjanaṃ /
yāni yānānyayuktāni yuktāni na vahanti ca //
meaning:
होमः प्रसूतिवैकृत्ये जपो विप्रादिपूजनं /
यानि यानान्ययुक्तानि युक्तानि न वहन्ति च //
text_mt:
In the case of an unnatural birth, a fire oblation, recitation, and the worship of brāhmaṇas and others [should be performed].
When unhitched conveyances move, and hitched ones do not carry [their loads],

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśe tūryanādāś ca mahadbhayamupasthitaṃ /
praviśanti yadā grāmamāraṇyā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ //
meaning:
आकाशे तूर्यनादाश् च महद्भयमुपस्थितं /
प्रविशन्ति यदा ग्राममारण्या मृगपक्षिणः //
text_mt:
and the sounds of musical instruments [are heard] in the sky, great danger is imminent.
When wild beasts and birds enter a village,

sanskrit_iast:
araṇyaṃ yānti vā grāmyāḥ jalaṃ yānti sthalodbhavāḥ /
sthalaṃ vā jalajā yānti rājadvārādike śivāḥ //
meaning:
अरण्यं यान्ति वा ग्राम्याः जलं यान्ति स्थलोद्भवाः /
स्थलं वा जलजा यान्ति राजद्वारादिके शिवाः //
text_mt: or domestic animals go into the forest; when land animals enter water, / or aquatic creatures go onto land; or when jackals [cry] at the king's gate and the like;

sanskrit_iast:
pradoṣe kukkuṭo vāse śivā cārkodaye bhavet /
gṛhaṅkapotaḥ praviśet kravyāhā mūrdhni līyate //
meaning:
प्रदोषे कुक्कुटो वासे शिवा चार्कोदये भवेत् /
गृहङ्कपोतः प्रविशेत् क्रव्याहा मूर्ध्नि लीयते //
text_mt:
or a rooster cries at dusk, or a jackal [howls] at sunrise;
or a pigeon enters a house, or a flesh-eating bird perches on a person's head;

sanskrit_iast:
madhurāṃ makṣikāṃ kuryāt kāko maithunago dṛśi /
prāsādatoraṇodyānadvāraprākāraveśmanāṃ //
meaning:
मधुरां मक्षिकां कुर्यात् काको मैथुनगो दृशि /
प्रासादतोरणोद्यानद्वारप्राकारवेश्मनां //
text_mt:
or a fly produces honey, or a crow is seen mating;
or the motiveless collapse of temples, archways, gardens,

sanskrit_iast:
animittantu patanaṃ dṛḍhānāṃ rājamṛtyave /
rajasā vātha dhūmena diśo yatra samākulāḥ //
:p 463
meaning:
अनिमित्तन्तु पतनं दृढानां राजमृत्यवे /
रजसा वाथ धूमेन दिशो यत्र समाकुलाः //
:प् 463

sanskrit_iast:
ketūdayoparāgau ca chidratā śaśisūryayoḥ /
graharkṣavikṛtiryatra tatrāpi bhayamādiśet //
meaning:
केतूदयोपरागौ च छिद्रता शशिसूर्ययोः /
ग्रहर्क्षविकृतिर्यत्र तत्रापि भयमादिशेत् //
text_mt: The appearance of comets, eclipses, and blemishes on the moon and sun, / and where there is abnormality among the planets and asterisms: there too one should predict danger.

sanskrit_iast:
agniryatra ma dīpyeta sravante codakambhakāḥ /
mṛtirbhayaṃ śūnyatādirutpātānāṃ phalambhavet //
meaning:
अग्निर्यत्र म दीप्येत स्रवन्ते चोदकम्भकाः /
मृतिर्भयं शून्यतादिरुत्पातानां फलम्भवेत् //
text_mt: Where fire does not burn, and water-jars leak, / death, danger, desolation, and the like will be the fruit of portents.

sanskrit_iast:
dvijadevādipūjābhyaḥ śāntirjapyaistu homataḥ //33//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe utpātaśāntirnāma
dviṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
devapūjāvaiśvadevabaliḥ
meaning:
द्विजदेवादिपूजाभ्यः शान्तिर्जप्यैस्तु होमतः //33//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे उत्पातशान्तिर्नाम
द्विषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
देवपूजावैश्वदेवबलिः
text_mt:
Pacification comes from worship of twice-born and deities, and through recitation [of mantras] and fire oblation. // 33
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-second chapter in the great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'Pacification of Portents.'
Now begins the two hundred and sixty-third chapter:
Worship of the deities and the Vaiśvadeva offering.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
devapūjādikaṃ karma vakṣye cotpātamardanam /
āpohiṣṭeti tisṛbhiḥ snāto 'rghyaṃ vioṣṇaverpayet //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
देवपूजादिकं कर्म वक्ष्ये चोत्पातमर्दनम् /
आपोहिष्टेति तिसृभिः स्नातो ऽर्घ्यं विओष्णवेर्पयेत् //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / I will speak of the rite consisting of worship of the gods and the like, which crushes portents. / Having bathed, one should offer water offering to Viṣṇu with the three verses beginning with 'āpo hi ṣṭhā'.

sanskrit_iast:
hiraṇyavarṇā iti ca pādyañca tisṛbhirdvija /
śanna āpo hy ācamanamidamāpo 'bhiṣecanaṃ //
meaning:
हिरण्यवर्णा इति च पाद्यञ्च तिसृभिर्द्विज /
शन्न आपो ह्य् आचमनमिदमापो ऽभिषेचनं //
text_mt: And foot-water with the three verses beginning with 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ', O twice-born, / sipping water with 'śaṃ na āpaḥ', and aspersion with 'idam āpaḥ'.

sanskrit_iast:
rathe akṣe ca tisṛbhirgandhaṃ yuveti(1) vastrakaṃ /
puṣpaṃ puṣpavatītyevaṃ dhūpandhūposi cāpyatha //
meaning:
रथे अक्षे च तिसृभिर्गन्धं युवेति(1) वस्त्रकं /
पुष्पं पुष्पवतीत्येवं धूपन्धूपोसि चाप्यथ //
text_mt: Perfume with the three verses 'rathe akṣe', garment with 'yuvā', / flower with 'puṣpavatī', and incense with 'dhūpo 'si'.

sanskrit_iast:
tejosi śukraṃ dīpaṃ syānmadhuparkaṃ dadhīti ca /
hiraṇyagarbha ity aṣṭāvṛcaḥ proktā nivedane //
meaning:
तेजोसि शुक्रं दीपं स्यान्मधुपर्कं दधीति च /
हिरण्यगर्भ इत्य् अष्टावृचः प्रोक्ता निवेदने //
text_mt: Lamp should be offered with 'tejo 'si śukram', and madhuparka with 'dadhikrāvṇaḥ'. / Eight verses beginning with 'hiraṇyagarbhaḥ' are prescribed for offering

sanskrit_iast:
annasya manujaśreṣṭha pānasya ca sugandhinaḥ /
cāmaravyajanopānacchatraṃ yānāsane tathā //
:n
1 gandhaṃ svadheti ka.. , ga.. ,gha.. , ja.. ca
:p 464
meaning:
अन्नस्य मनुजश्रेष्ठ पानस्य च सुगन्धिनः /
चामरव्यजनोपानच्छत्रं यानासने तथा //
:न्
1 गन्धं स्वधेति क.. , ग.. ,घ.. , ज.. च
:प् 464
text_mt:
food, O best of men, and fragrant drink; / likewise a flywhisk, fan, shoes, parasol, vehicle, and seat.
[Footnote]
1. "gandhaṃ svadhā" thus in manuscripts ka, ga, gha, and ja. / [Page 464]

sanskrit_iast:
yat kiñcidevamādi syātsāvitreṇa nivedayet /
pauruṣantu japet sūktaṃ tadeva juhuyāttathā //
meaning:
यत् किञ्चिदेवमादि स्यात्सावित्रेण निवेदयेत् /
पौरुषन्तु जपेत् सूक्तं तदेव जुहुयात्तथा //
text_mt: Whatever else there may be of this sort, one should offer with the Sāvitrī verse. / One should recite the Puruṣasūkta and also offer fire oblations with it.

sanskrit_iast:
arcābhave tathā vedyāñjale pūrṇaghate tathā /
nadītīre 'tha kamale śāntiḥ syādviṣṇupūjanāt //
meaning:
अर्चाभवे तथा वेद्याञ्जले पूर्णघते तथा /
नदीतीरे ऽथ कमले शान्तिः स्याद्विष्णुपूजनात् //
text_mt: In an image, or on an altar, in water, in a full water-jar, / on a riverbank, or upon a lotus, pacification arises from the worship of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
tato homaḥ prakartavyo dīpyamāne vibhāvasau /
parisammṛjya paryukṣya paristīrya paristaraiḥ //
meaning:
ततो होमः प्रकर्तव्यो दीप्यमाने विभावसौ /
परिसम्मृज्य पर्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य परिस्तरैः //
text_mt: Then fire oblation is to be performed when the fire is blazing, / having swept round, sprinkled round, and strewed [the altar] with strew-grasses.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānnāgraṃ samuddhṛtya juhuyāt prayatastataḥ /
vāsudevāya devāya prabhave cāvyayāya ca //
meaning:
सर्वान्नाग्रं समुद्धृत्य जुहुयात् प्रयतस्ततः /
वासुदेवाय देवाय प्रभवे चाव्ययाय च //
text_mt: Taking a portion of the foremost of all the food, one should then attentively offer fire oblations / to Lord Vāsudeva, the sovereign and imperishable;

sanskrit_iast:
agnaye caiva somāya mitrāya varuṇāya ca /
indrāya ca mahābhāga indrāgnibhyāṃ tathaiva ca //
meaning:
अग्नये चैव सोमाय मित्राय वरुणाय च /
इन्द्राय च महाभाग इन्द्राग्निभ्यां तथैव च //
text_mt: to Agni, to Soma, to Mitra, and to Varuṇa; / to Indra, O noble one, and likewise to Indrāgni;

sanskrit_iast:
viśvebhyaś caiva devebhyaḥ prajānāṃ pataye namaḥ /
anumatyai tathā rāma dhanvantaraya eva ca //
meaning:
विश्वेभ्यश् चैव देवेभ्यः प्रजानां पतये नमः /
अनुमत्यै तथा राम धन्वन्तरय एव च //
text_mt: to the All-Gods, 'Homage to the Lord of Creatures'; / to Anumati, O Rāma, and likewise to Dhanvantari;

sanskrit_iast:
vāstoṣpatyai tato devyai tataḥ sviṣṭikṛte 'gnaye /
sacaturthyantanāmnā(1) tu hutvaitebhyo baliṃ haret //
meaning:
वास्तोष्पत्यै ततो देव्यै ततः स्विष्टिकृते ऽग्नये /
सचतुर्थ्यन्तनाम्ना(1) तु हुत्वैतेभ्यो बलिं हरेत् //
text_mt: then to the goddess presiding over the home, and then to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. / Having offered fire oblations to these with their names ending in the dative case, one should present the food offering.

sanskrit_iast:
takṣopatakṣamabhitaḥ pūrveṇāgnimataḥ param /
aśvānāmapi dharmajña ūrṇānāmāni cāpyatha //
meaning:
तक्षोपतक्षमभितः पूर्वेणाग्निमतः परम् /
अश्वानामपि धर्मज्ञ ऊर्णानामानि चाप्यथ //
text_mt: On either side of Takṣa and Upatakṣa, and beyond that to the east of the fire, / O knower of righteousness, and then the names of the horses and the woolen-clad deities:

sanskrit_iast:
nirundhī dhūmriṇīkā ca asvapantī(2) tathaiva ca /
meghapatnī(3) ca nāmāni sarveṣāmeva bhārgava //
meaning:
निरुन्धी धूम्रिणीका च अस्वपन्ती(2) तथैव च /
मेघपत्नी(3) च नामानि सर्वेषामेव भार्गव //
text_mt: Nirundhī, Dhūmriṇīkā, Asvapantī, / and Meghapatnī—all these names indeed, O Bhārgava,

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyādyāḥ krameṇātha tataḥ śaktiṣu nikṣipet /
nandinyai ca subhāgyai ca sumaṅgalyai ca bhārgava //
:n
1 sa caturthīkanāmneti pāṭhaḥ sādhuḥ
2 aśvaparṇīti ja..
3 meghaparṇīti ja..
:p 465
meaning:
आग्नेयाद्याः क्रमेणाथ ततः शक्तिषु निक्षिपेत् /
नन्दिन्यै च सुभाग्यै च सुमङ्गल्यै च भार्गव //
:न्
1 स चतुर्थीकनाम्नेति पाठः साधुः
2 अश्वपर्णीति ज..
3 मेघपर्णीति ज..
:प् 465
text_mt:
beginning with Agni in order. Then one should cast offerings to the powers: / to Nandinī, to Subhāgyā, and to Sumaṅgalā, O Bhārgava;
[Footnote]
1. The reading "sa caturthīkanāmnā" is correct.
2. "aśvaparṇī" thus in manuscript ja.
3. "meghaparṇī" thus in manuscript ja. / [Page 465]

sanskrit_iast:
bhadrakālyai tato datvā sthūṇāyāñca tathā śriye /
hiraṇyakeśyai ca tathā vanaspataya eva ca //
meaning:
भद्रकाल्यै ततो दत्वा स्थूणायाञ्च तथा श्रिये /
हिरण्यकेश्यै च तथा वनस्पतय एव च //
text_mt: then having given to Bhadrakālī, and likewise at the post to Śrī, / and to Hiraṇyakeśī, and also to Vanaspati;

sanskrit_iast:
dharmādharmamayau dvāre gṛhamadhye dhruvāya ca /
mṛtyave ca vahirdadyādvaruṇāyodakāśaye //
meaning:
धर्माधर्ममयौ द्वारे गृहमध्ये ध्रुवाय च /
मृत्यवे च वहिर्दद्याद्वरुणायोदकाशये //
text_mt: to the two consisting of righteousness and unrighteousness at the door, and in the middle of the house to Dhruva; / one should give outside to Death, and to Varuṇa at a reservoir of water;

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtebhyaś ca bahirdadyāccharaṇe dhanadāya ca /
indrāyendrapuruṣebhyo dadyāt pūrveṇa mānavaḥ //
meaning:
भूतेभ्यश् च बहिर्दद्याच्छरणे धनदाय च /
इन्द्रायेन्द्रपुरुषेभ्यो दद्यात् पूर्वेण मानवः //
text_mt: and outside to the spirits, and in the shelter to the Bestower of Wealth; / a man should give to the east to Indra and Indra's attendants;

sanskrit_iast:
yamāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyāddakṣiṇatas tathā /
varuṇāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyātpaścimatas tathā //
meaning:
यमाय तत्पुरुषेभ्यो दद्याद्दक्षिणतस् तथा /
वरुणाय तत्पुरुषेभ्यो दद्यात्पश्चिमतस् तथा //
text_mt: he should give to the south to Yama and his attendants; / he should give to the west to Varuṇa and his attendants;

sanskrit_iast:
somāya somapuruṣebhya udagdadyādanantaraṃ /
brahmaṇe brahmapuruṣebhyo madhye dadyāttathaiva ca //
meaning:
सोमाय सोमपुरुषेभ्य उदग्दद्यादनन्तरं /
ब्रह्मणे ब्रह्मपुरुषेभ्यो मध्ये दद्यात्तथैव च //
text_mt: thereafter he should give to the north to Soma and Soma's attendants; / and likewise in the center he should give to Brahmā and Brahmā's attendants;

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśe ca tathā cordhve sthaṇḍilāya kṣitau tathā /
divā divācarebhyaś ca rātrau rātricareṣu ca //
meaning:
आकाशे च तथा चोर्ध्वे स्थण्डिलाय क्षितौ तथा /
दिवा दिवाचरेभ्यश् च रात्रौ रात्रिचरेषु च //
text_mt: and likewise above in the sky, and on the ground to the sacrificial ground; / by day to those who roam by day, and at night to those who roam at night.

sanskrit_iast:
baliṃ vahis tathā dadyātsāyaṃ prātastu pratyahaṃ /
piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kuryāt prātaḥ sāyanna kārayet //
meaning:
बलिं वहिस् तथा दद्यात्सायं प्रातस्तु प्रत्यहं /
पिण्डनिर्वपणं कुर्यात् प्रातः सायन्न कारयेत् //
text_mt: He should thus give the food offering outside every day, morning and evening. / He should make the offering of rice-balls in the morning; he should not do it in the evening.

sanskrit_iast:
pitre tu prathamaṃ dadyāttatpitre tadanantaram /
prapitāmahāya tanmātre pitṛmātre tato 'rpayet //
meaning:
पित्रे तु प्रथमं दद्यात्तत्पित्रे तदनन्तरम् /
प्रपितामहाय तन्मात्रे पितृमात्रे ततो ऽर्पयेत् //
text_mt: He should give first to the father, immediately after to his father, / [then] to the paternal great-grandfather, then offer to his mother, [and] to the father's mother;

sanskrit_iast:
tanmātre dakṣiṇāgreṣu kuśeṣvevaṃ yajet pitṝn /
indravāruṇavāyavyā yāmyā vā nairṛtāya ye //
meaning:
तन्मात्रे दक्षिणाग्रेषु कुशेष्वेवं यजेत् पितॄन् /
इन्द्रवारुणवायव्या याम्या वा नैरृताय ये //
text_mt: [and] to her mother; thus he should worship the ancestors on kuśa grass pointing south. / 'Those crows belonging to Indra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Yama, or Nirṛti—

sanskrit_iast:
te kākāḥ pitṛgṛhantu imaṃ piṇḍaṃ mayodvṛtam /
kākapiṇḍantu mantreṇa śunaḥ piṇḍaṃ pradāpayet //
meaning:
ते काकाः पितृगृहन्तु इमं पिण्डं मयोद्वृतम् /
काकपिण्डन्तु मन्त्रेण शुनः पिण्डं प्रदापयेत् //
text_mt: let them take this ball of food raised by me for the ancestors.' / With this mantra for the crow's ball of food, he should also cause a ball of food to be given to the dog:

sanskrit_iast:
vivasvataḥ kule jātau dvau śyāvaśabalau(1) śunau /
teṣāṃ piṇḍaṃ pradāsyāmi pathi rakṣantu me sadā //
:n
1 śyāmaśabalāviti ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 466
meaning:
विवस्वतः कुले जातौ द्वौ श्यावशबलौ(1) शुनौ /
तेषां पिण्डं प्रदास्यामि पथि रक्षन्तु मे सदा //
:न्
1 श्यामशबलाविति ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 466
text_mt:
'The two dark and brindled dogs born in the lineage of Vivasvat: / to them I shall give a ball of food; let them protect me always on the road.'
[Footnote]
1. "śyāmaśabalau" thus in manuscripts ja, ña, and ṭa. / [Page 466]

sanskrit_iast:
saurabheyyaḥ(1) sarvahitāḥ pavitrāḥ pāpanāśanāḥ(2) /
pratigṛhṇantu me grāsaṃ gāvastrailokyamātaraḥ //
meaning:
सौरभेय्यः(1) सर्वहिताः पवित्राः पापनाशनाः(2) /
प्रतिगृह्णन्तु मे ग्रासं गावस्त्रैलोक्यमातरः //
text_mt: 'May the daughters of Surabhi, beneficent to all, pure, destroyers of sin, / mothers of the three worlds, the cows, receive my morsel.'

sanskrit_iast:
grogrāsañca svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣāṃ pradāpayet /
atithīndīnān pūjayitvā gṛhī bhuñjīta ca svayaṃ //
oṃ bhūḥ svāhā oṃ bhūvaḥ svāhā oṃ svaḥ svāhā oṃ
bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā
oṃ devakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ pitṛkṛtasyainaso
'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ ātmakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ
manuṣyakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ enasa enaso 'vayajanamasi
svāhā / yaccāhameno vidvāṃś cakāra yaccavidvāṃstasya sarvasyainaso
'vayajanamasi svāhā agnaye sviṣṭikṛte svāhā oṃ prajāpataye svāhā
||
meaning:
ग्रोग्रासञ्च स्वस्त्ययनं कृत्वा भिक्षां प्रदापयेत् /
अतिथीन्दीनान् पूजयित्वा गृही भुञ्जीत च स्वयं //
ओं भूः स्वाहा ओं भूवः स्वाहा ओं स्वः स्वाहा ओं
भूर्भुवः स्वः स्वाहा
ओं देवकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं पितृकृतस्यैनसो
ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं आत्मकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं
मनुष्यकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं एनस एनसो ऽवयजनमसि
स्वाहा / यच्चाहमेनो विद्वांश् चकार यच्चविद्वांस्तस्य सर्वस्यैनसो
ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा अग्नये स्विष्टिकृते स्वाहा ओं प्रजापतये स्वाहा
||
text_mt:
Having offered the cow's morsel and recited an auspicious blessing, he should bestow alms. / Having honored guests and the afflicted, the householder may eat himself:
'Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā! Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā! Oṃ svaḥ svāhā! Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! / Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against the gods, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against the ancestors, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against oneself, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against humans, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin upon sin, svāhā! And whatever sin I have committed knowingly, and whatever unknowingly, of all that sin you are the expiation, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā! Oṃ, to Prajāpati, svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast:
viṣṇupūjāvaiśvadevabaliste kīrtito mayā //29//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe devapūjāvaiśvadevabalirnāma
triṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catuḥṣaṣṭhyadhiakadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dikpālādisnānaṃ
meaning:
विष्णुपूजावैश्वदेवबलिस्ते कीर्तितो मया //29//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे देवपूजावैश्वदेवबलिर्नाम
त्रिषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुःषष्ठ्यधिअकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दिक्पालादिस्नानं
text_mt:
The worship of Viṣṇu and the Vaiśvadeva food offering have thus been declared to you by me. // 29
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-third chapter in the great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'Worship of Deities and the Vaiśvadeva Offering.'
Now begins the two hundred and sixty-fourth chapter:
Bathing [with mantras] of the guardians of the directions and others.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
sarvārthasādhanaṃ snānaṃ vakṣye śāntikaraṃ śṛṇu /
snāpayecca sarittīre grahān viṣṇuṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ //
:n
1 saurabheyā iti ka.. , gha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
2 puṣparāśaya iti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 467
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
सर्वार्थसाधनं स्नानं वक्ष्ये शान्तिकरं शृणु /
स्नापयेच्च सरित्तीरे ग्रहान् विष्णुं विचक्षणः //
:न्
1 सौरभेया इति क.. , घ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
2 पुष्पराशय इति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 467
text_mt:
Agni said: / Listen to the pacifying bath that accomplishes all aims, which I shall explain. / A wise person should bathe Viṣṇu and the planets on a riverbank;
[Footnote]
1. "saurabheyāḥ" thus in manuscripts ka, gha, cha, and ña.
2. "puṣparāśayaḥ" thus in manuscripts ja and ṭa. / [Page 467]

sanskrit_iast:
devālaye jvarārtyādau vināyakagrahārdite /
vidyārthino hrade gehe jayakāmasya tīrthake //
meaning:
देवालये ज्वरार्त्यादौ विनायकग्रहार्दिते /
विद्यार्थिनो ह्रदे गेहे जयकामस्य तीर्थके //
text_mt: in a temple when suffering from fever and the like, or afflicted by Vināyaka and seizing spirits; / in a pool for one desiring knowledge; in the home or at a sacred ford for one desiring victory.

sanskrit_iast:
padminyāṃ snāpayennārīṃ garbho yasyāḥ sravettathā /
aśokasannidhau snāyājjāto yasyā vinaśyati //
meaning:
पद्मिन्यां स्नापयेन्नारीं गर्भो यस्याः स्रवेत्तथा /
अशोकसन्निधौ स्नायाज्जातो यस्या विनश्यति //
text_mt: One should bathe a woman whose fetus miscarries in a lotus pond; / she whose child perishes upon birth should bathe in the vicinity of an aśoka tree.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpārthināñca puṣpāḍhye putrārthināñca sāgare /
gṛhasaubhāgyakāmānāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣṇusannidhau //
meaning:
पुष्पार्थिनाञ्च पुष्पाढ्ये पुत्रार्थिनाञ्च सागरे /
गृहसौभाग्यकामानां सर्वेषां विष्णुसन्निधौ //
text_mt: For those desiring flowers, [the bath should be] in a place rich in flowers, and in the ocean for those desiring a son; / for all who desire household good fortune, it should be in the presence of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiṣṇave revatīpuṣye sarveṣāṃ snānamuttamaṃ /
snānakāmasya saptāhampūrvamutsādanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
meaning:
वैष्णवे रेवतीपुष्ये सर्वेषां स्नानमुत्तमं /
स्नानकामस्य सप्ताहम्पूर्वमुत्सादनं स्मृतं //
text_mt: Under the asterism of Viṣṇu [Śravaṇā], or Revatī and Puṣya, a bath is supreme for all. / For one desiring a bath, anointing [the body] seven days prior is prescribed.

sanskrit_iast:
punar navāṃ rocanāñca śatāṅgaṃ guruṇī tvacaṃ /
madhūkaṃ rajanī dve ca tagarannāgakeśaram //
meaning:
पुनर् नवां रोचनाञ्च शताङ्गं गुरुणी त्वचं /
मधूकं रजनी द्वे च तगरन्नागकेशरम् //
text_mt: Punar-navā, rocanā, śatāṅga, heavy bark, / madhūka, the two kinds of turmeric, tagara, nāgakeśara,

sanskrit_iast:
ambarīñcaiva mañjiṣṭhāṃ māṃsīyāsakamardanaiḥ /
priyaṅgusarṣapaṃ kuṣṭhambalāmbrāhmīñca kuṅkumaṃ //
meaning:
अम्बरीञ्चैव मञ्जिष्ठां मांसीयासकमर्दनैः /
प्रियङ्गुसर्षपं कुष्ठम्बलाम्ब्राह्मीञ्च कुङ्कुमं //
text_mt: ambarī, mañjiṣṭhā, māṃsī, and rubs of yāsaka, / priyaṅgu, mustard, kuṣṭha, balā, brāhmī, saffron,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcagavyaṃ śaktumiśraṃ udvartya snānamācaret /
maṇḍale karṇikāyāñca viṣṇuṃ brāhmaṇamarcayet //
meaning:
पञ्चगव्यं शक्तुमिश्रं उद्वर्त्य स्नानमाचरेत् /
मण्डले कर्णिकायाञ्च विष्णुं ब्राह्मणमर्चयेत् //
text_mt: and the five products of the cow mixed with barley meal: rubbing [with these], one should perform the bath. / In a maṇḍala, in its pericarp, one should worship Viṣṇu and a Brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣe vāme haraṃ pūrvaṃ patre pūrvādike kramāt /
likhedindrādikāndevān sāyudhān sahabāndhavān(1) //
meaning:
दक्षे वामे हरं पूर्वं पत्रे पूर्वादिके क्रमात् /
लिखेदिन्द्रादिकान्देवान् सायुधान् सहबान्धवान्(1) //
text_mt: On the right [and] on the left, first Hara, and on the petal, beginning with the east in succession, / one should draw Indra and the other gods, with their weapons and their retinues.

sanskrit_iast:
snānamaṇḍalakān dikṣu kuryāccaiva vidikṣu ca /
viṣṇubrahmeśaśakrādīṃstadastrāṇyarcya homayet //
meaning:
स्नानमण्डलकान् दिक्षु कुर्याच्चैव विदिक्षु च /
विष्णुब्रह्मेशशक्रादींस्तदस्त्राण्यर्च्य होमयेत् //
text_mt: One should make bath-maṇḍalas in the directions and in the intermediate directions. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Īśa, Śakra, and the others, and their weapons, one should offer fire oblations.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaikasya tvaṣṭaśataṃ samidhastu tilān dhṛtaṃ /
bhadraḥ subhadraḥ siddhārthaḥ kalasāḥ puṣṭivardhanāḥ //
meaning:
एकैकस्य त्वष्टशतं समिधस्तु तिलान् धृतं /
भद्रः सुभद्रः सिद्धार्थः कलसाः पुष्टिवर्धनाः //
text_mt: One hundred and eight firewood sticks, sesamum, and ghee for each one. / The jars that increase prosperity are Bhadra, Subhadra, Siddhārtha,

sanskrit_iast:
amoghaścitrabhānuś ca parjanyo 'tha sudarśanaḥ /
sthāpayettu vaṭānenān sāśvirudramarudgaṇān //
:n
1 sahavāhanāniti gha.. , ja.. ca
:p 468
meaning:
अमोघश्चित्रभानुश् च पर्जन्यो ऽथ सुदर्शनः /
स्थापयेत्तु वटानेनान् साश्विरुद्रमरुद्गणान् //
:न्
1 सहवाहनानिति घ.. , ज.. च
:प् 468
text_mt:
Amogha, Citrabhānu, Parjanya, and Sudarśana. / One should set up these under a banyan tree, along with the two Aśvins, the Rudras, and the host of the Maruts:
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "with their vehicles" in manuscripts gha and ja. Page 468]

sanskrit_iast:
viśve devas tathā daityā vasavo munayas tathā /
āveśayantu suprītās tathānyā api devatāḥ //
meaning:
विश्वे देवस् तथा दैत्या वसवो मुनयस् तथा /
आवेशयन्तु सुप्रीतास् तथान्या अपि देवताः //
text_mt: "May the Viśvedevas, likewise the Daityas, the Vasus, and the sages, / and likewise the other deities, enter [here] well pleased."

sanskrit_iast:
oṣadhīr nikṣipet kumbhe jayantīṃ vijayāṃ jayāṃ /
śatāvarīṃ śatapuṣpāṃ viṣṇukrāntāparājitām //
meaning:
ओषधीर् निक्षिपेत् कुम्भे जयन्तीं विजयां जयां /
शतावरीं शतपुष्पां विष्णुक्रान्तापराजिताम् //
text_mt: One should place medicinal herbs into the jar: jayantī, vijayā, jayā, / śatāvarī, śatapuṣpā, viṣṇukrāntā, aparājitā,

sanskrit_iast:
jyotiṣmatīmatibalāñcandanośīrakeśaraṃ /
kastūrikāñca karpūraṃ bālakaṃ patrakaṃ tvacaṃ //
meaning:
ज्योतिष्मतीमतिबलाञ्चन्दनोशीरकेशरं /
कस्तूरिकाञ्च कर्पूरं बालकं पत्रकं त्वचं //
text_mt: jyotiṣmatī, atibalā, sandalwood, uśīra, kesara, / musk, camphor, bālaka, leaf, bark,

sanskrit_iast:
jātīphalaṃ lavaṅgañca mṛttikāṃ pañcagavyakaṃ /
bhadrapīṭhe sthitaṃ sādhyaṃ snāpayeyurdvijā balāt //
meaning:
जातीफलं लवङ्गञ्च मृत्तिकां पञ्चगव्यकं /
भद्रपीठे स्थितं साध्यं स्नापयेयुर्द्विजा बलात् //
text_mt: nutmeg, clove, earth, and the five products of the cow. / Stationed on an auspicious seat, the subject should be forcibly bathed by the twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
rājābhiṣekamantroktadevānāṃ homakāḥ pṛthak /
pūrṇāhutintato datvā gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadet //
meaning:
राजाभिषेकमन्त्रोक्तदेवानां होमकाः पृथक् /
पूर्णाहुतिन्ततो दत्वा गुरवे दक्षिणां ददेत् //
text_mt: There are separate homa-offerers for the gods stated in the royal consecration mantra. / Then, having offered the full oblation, he should give a sacrificial fee to the guru.

sanskrit_iast:
indro 'bhiṣikto guruṇā purā daityān jaghāna ha /
dikpālasnānaṅkathitaṃ saṃgrāmādau jayādikaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dikpālādisnānaṃ nāma
catuḥṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vināyakasnānaṃ
meaning:
इन्द्रो ऽभिषिक्तो गुरुणा पुरा दैत्यान् जघान ह /
दिक्पालस्नानङ्कथितं संग्रामादौ जयादिकं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दिक्पालादिस्नानं नाम
चतुःषष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
विनायकस्नानं
text_mt:
Indra, consecrated by his guru in ancient times, indeed slew the Daityas. / The bath of the guardians of the directions has been declared, bringing victory and the like in battle and other [ventures].
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Bath of the Guardians of the Directions and Others."
Now, the two hundred and sixty-fifth chapter:
The bath for Vināyaka.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
vināyakopasṛṣṭānāṃ snānaṃ sarvakaraṃ vade /
vināyakaḥ karmavighnasiddhyarthaṃ viniyojitaḥ //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
विनायकोपसृष्टानां स्नानं सर्वकरं वदे /
विनायकः कर्मविघ्नसिद्ध्यर्थं विनियोजितः //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / I shall state the bath that accomplishes everything for those afflicted by Vināyaka. / Vināyaka was appointed for the achievement of obstacles to actions

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇānāmādhipatye ca keśaveśapitāmahaiḥ /
svapnevagāhate 'tyarthaṃ jalaṃ muṇḍāṃś ca paśyati //
:p 469
meaning:
गणानामाधिपत्ये च केशवेशपितामहैः /
स्वप्नेवगाहते ऽत्यर्थं जलं मुण्डांश् च पश्यति //
:प् 469
text_mt:
and to the overlordship of the gaṇas by Keśava, Īśa, and the Grandfather [Brahmā]. / [One so afflicted] plunges exceedingly into water in dreams and sees shaven-headed men;
[Page 469]

sanskrit_iast:
vināyakopasṛṣṭastu kravyādānadhirohati /
vrajamānas tathātmānaṃ manyate 'nugatamparaiḥ //
meaning:
विनायकोपसृष्टस्तु क्रव्यादानधिरोहति /
व्रजमानस् तथात्मानं मन्यते ऽनुगतम्परैः //
text_mt: afflicted by Vināyaka, he mounts carnivorous animals, / and while walking, he imagines himself pursued by others;

sanskrit_iast:
vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdatyanimittataḥ /
kanyā varaṃ na cāpnoti na cāpatyaṃ varāṅganā //
meaning:
विमना विफलारम्भः संसीदत्यनिमित्ततः /
कन्या वरं न चाप्नोति न चापत्यं वराङ्गना //
text_mt: he is dejected, his undertakings are fruitless, and he falters without cause; / an unmarried woman finds no groom, and a noble woman bears no child;

sanskrit_iast:
ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaś ca na śiṣyo 'dhyayanaṃ labhet /
dhanī na lābhamāpnoti na kṛṣiñca kṛṣībalaḥ //
meaning:
आचार्यत्वं श्रोत्रियश् च न शिष्यो ऽध्ययनं लभेत् /
धनी न लाभमाप्नोति न कृषिञ्च कृषीबलः //
text_mt: the learned Brahmin does not attain the rank of teacher, and the pupil does not gain study; / the wealthy man obtains no gain, and the cultivator reaps no harvest;

sanskrit_iast:
rājā rājyaṃ na cāpnoti snapanantasya kārayet /
hastapuṣyāśvayuksaumye vaiṣṇave bhadrapīṭhake(1) //
meaning:
राजा राज्यं न चाप्नोति स्नपनन्तस्य कारयेत् /
हस्तपुष्याश्वयुक्सौम्ये वैष्णवे भद्रपीठके(1) //
text_mt: the king does not attain kingship. One should cause his bath to be performed / under the asterisms Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvayuj, Saumya, or Vaiṣṇava, on an auspicious seat.

sanskrit_iast:
gaurasarṣapakalkena sājyenotsāditasya ca(2) /
sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ praliptaśirasas tathā //
meaning:
गौरसर्षपकल्केन साज्येनोत्सादितस्य च(2) /
सर्वौषधैः सर्वगन्धैः प्रलिप्तशिरसस् तथा //
text_mt: Having rubbed him with a paste of white mustard together with ghee, / and likewise smeared his head with all medicinal herbs and all fragrant substances,

sanskrit_iast:
caturbhiḥ kalasaiḥ snānanteṣu sarvauṣādhau kṣipet /
aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkāt saṅgamāddhradāt //
meaning:
चतुर्भिः कलसैः स्नानन्तेषु सर्वौषाधौ क्षिपेत् /
अश्वस्थानाद्गजस्थानाद्वल्मीकात् सङ्गमाद्ध्रदात् //
text_mt: the bath is performed with four jars; into them he should put all herbs, / and earth from a horse-stable, from an elephant-stable, from an anthill, from a confluence, and from a deep pool.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛttikāṃ rocanāṅgandhaṅguggulunteṣu nikṣipet /
sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ pāvanaṃ kṛtam //
meaning:
मृत्तिकां रोचनाङ्गन्धङ्गुग्गुलुन्तेषु निक्षिपेत् /
सहस्राक्षं शतधारमृषिभिः पावनं कृतम् //
text_mt: He should put earth, rocanā, fragrant perfume, and guggulu into them: / "The thousand-eyed, hundred-streamed [bath], made purifying by the sages:

sanskrit_iast:
tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānyaḥ(3) punantu te /
bhagavante varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo vṛhaspatiḥ //
meaning:
तेन त्वामभिषिञ्चामि पावमान्यः(3) पुनन्तु ते /
भगवन्ते वरुणो राजा भगं सूर्यो वृहस्पतिः //
text_mt: with that I consecrate you; may the purifying verses purify you! / May King Varuṇa give you fortune; may Sūrya and Bṛhaspati give you fortune;

sanskrit_iast:
bhagamindraś ca vāyuś ca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ /
yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani //
meaning:
भगमिन्द्रश् च वायुश् च भगं सप्तर्षयो ददुः /
यत्ते केशेषु दौर्भाग्यं सीमन्ते यच्च मूर्धनि //
text_mt: may Indra and Vāyu give you fortune; may the Seven Sages give you fortune! / Whatever ill-fortune is in your hair, in your parting, and on your head,

sanskrit_iast:
lalāṭe karṇayorakṣṇorāpastadghnantu sarvadā /
darbhapiñjalimādāya vāmahaste tato guruḥ //
:n
1 hastapuṣyāśvayuksaumyavaiṣṇaveṣu śubheṣu ceti gha.. , ña..
ca
2 sājyenāsāditasya ceti ka.. , cha.. ca
3 imā āpa iti cha.. , ña..
:p 470
meaning:
ललाटे कर्णयोरक्ष्णोरापस्तद्घ्नन्तु सर्वदा /
दर्भपिञ्जलिमादाय वामहस्ते ततो गुरुः //
:न्
1 हस्तपुष्याश्वयुक्सौम्यवैष्णवेषु शुभेषु चेति घ.. , ञ..
च
2 साज्येनासादितस्य चेति क.. , छ.. च
3 इमा आप इति छ.. , ञ..
:प् 470
text_mt:
on your forehead, your ears, and your eyes, may the waters always destroy that!" / Then the guru, taking a bunch of darbha grass in his left hand,
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "under Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvayuj, Saumya, and Vaiṣṇava, and on auspicious [occasions]" in manuscripts gha and ña.]
[Footnote 2: "approached with ghee" in manuscripts ka and cha.]
[Footnote 3: "these waters" in manuscripts cha and ña. Page 470]

sanskrit_iast:
snātasya sārṣapantailaṃ śruveṇauḍumbareṇa ca /
juhuyānmūrdhani kuśān savyena parigṛhya ca //
meaning:
स्नातस्य सार्षपन्तैलं श्रुवेणौडुम्बरेण च /
जुहुयान्मूर्धनि कुशान् सव्येन परिगृह्य च //
text_mt: should offer mustard oil upon the head of the bathed person with a ladle of udumbara wood, / holding the kuśa grasses with the right hand, [saying:]

sanskrit_iast:
mitaś ca sammitaś caiva tathā śālakakaṇṭakau /
kuṣmāṇḍo rājaputraś ca etaiḥ svāhāsamanvitaiḥ //
meaning:
मितश् च सम्मितश् चैव तथा शालककण्टकौ /
कुष्माण्डो राजपुत्रश् च एतैः स्वाहासमन्वितैः //
text_mt: "Mita, Sammita, Śālaka, Kaṇṭaka, / Kuṣmāṇḍa, and Rājaputra"—with these [names] accompanied by "svāhā",

sanskrit_iast:
nāmabhirbalimantraiś ca namaskārasamanvitaiḥ(1) /
dadyāccatuṣpathe śūrpe kuśānāstīrya sarvataḥ //
meaning:
नामभिर्बलिमन्त्रैश् च नमस्कारसमन्वितैः(1) /
दद्याच्चतुष्पथे शूर्पे कुशानास्तीर्य सर्वतः //
text_mt: with the names and offering mantras accompanied by obeisance, / having strewn kuśa grass all around in a winnowing basket at a crossroads, he should offer

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtākṛtāṃstaṇḍulāṃś ca palalaudanameva ca /
matsyānpaṅkāṃstathaivāmān puṣpaṃ citraṃ surāṃ tridhā //
meaning:
कृताकृतांस्तण्डुलांश् च पललौदनमेव च /
मत्स्यान्पङ्कांस्तथैवामान् पुष्पं चित्रं सुरां त्रिधा //
text_mt: cooked and uncooked grains of rice, boiled rice with ground sesamum, / fish from mud as well as raw, flowers of variegated colors, liquor of three kinds,

sanskrit_iast:
mūlakaṃ pūrikāṃ pūpāṃstathaivaiṇḍavikāsrajaḥ /
dadhyannaṃ pāyasaṃ piṣṭaṃ modakaṃ guḍamarpayet //
meaning:
मूलकं पूरिकां पूपांस्तथैवैण्डविकास्रजः /
दध्यन्नं पायसं पिष्टं मोदकं गुडमर्पयेत् //
text_mt: radish, fried cakes, sweet breads, garlands of buns, / curd-rice, milk-rice, flour cakes, sweetmeats, and molasses.

sanskrit_iast:
vināyakasya jananīmupatiṣṭhettato 'mbikāṃ /
dūrvāsarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ datvārghyaṃ pūrṇamañjaliṃ //
meaning:
विनायकस्य जननीमुपतिष्ठेत्ततो ऽम्बिकां /
दूर्वासर्षपपुष्पाणां दत्वार्घ्यं पूर्णमञ्जलिं //
text_mt: Then he should approach Ambikā, the mother of Vināyaka, / offering a full handful as water offering with dūrvā grass, mustard, and flowers:

sanskrit_iast:
rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi saubhāgyaṃ subhage mama /
putraṃ dehi dhanaṃ dehi sarvān kāmāṃś ca dehi me //
meaning:
रूपं देहि यशो देहि सौभाग्यं सुभगे मम /
पुत्रं देहि धनं देहि सर्वान् कामांश् च देहि मे //
text_mt: "Grant beauty, grant fame, grant fortune to me, O fortunate goddess! / Grant a son, grant wealth, and grant all desires to me!"

sanskrit_iast:
bhojayedbrāhmaṇāndadyādvastrayugmaṃ gurorapi /
vināyakaṃ grahānprārcya śriyaṃ karmaphalaṃ labhet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vināyakasnānaṃ nāma
pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 vaṣaṭkārasamanvitair iti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 471
:ś atha ṣaṭṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
māheśvarasnānalakṣakoṭihomādayaḥ
meaning:
भोजयेद्ब्राह्मणान्दद्याद्वस्त्रयुग्मं गुरोरपि /
विनायकं ग्रहान्प्रार्च्य श्रियं कर्मफलं लभेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे विनायकस्नानं नाम
पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 वषट्कारसमन्वितैर् इति घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 471
:श् अथ षट्षष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
माहेश्वरस्नानलक्षकोटिहोमादयः
text_mt:
He should feed Brahmins and give a pair of garments also to the guru. / Having thoroughly worshipped Vināyaka and the planets, he obtains prosperity and the fruit of his deeds.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, entitled "The Bath for Vināyaka."
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "accompanied by the exclamation vaṣaṭ" in manuscripts gha, ja, ña, and ṭa. Page 471]
Now, the two hundred and sixty-sixth chapter:
The Bath for Maheśvara, the Hundred-Thousand and Ten-Million Fire Oblations, and Others.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
snānaṃ māheśvaraṃ vakṣye rājāderjayavardhanam /
dānavendrāya balaye yajjagādośanāḥ purā //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
स्नानं माहेश्वरं वक्ष्ये राजादेर्जयवर्धनम् /
दानवेन्द्राय बलये यज्जगादोशनाः पुरा //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the bath for Maheśvara, which increases victory for kings and others, / which Uśanas taught in ancient times to Bali, the king of the Dānavas.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāskare 'nudite pīṭhe prātaḥ saṃsnāpayed ghaṭaiḥ /
oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya ca balāya ca
pāṇḍarocitabhasmānuliptagātrāya / tadyathā jaya jaya sarvān
śatrūnmūkasya kalahavigrahavivādeṣu bhañjaya / oṃ matha matha
sarvapathikānyosau yugāntakāle didhakṣati imāṃ pūjāṃ
raudramūrtiḥ sahasrāṃśuḥ śukraḥ sa te rakṣatu jīvitaṃ /
sambartakāgnitulyaś ca tripurāntakaraḥ śivaḥ / sarvadevamayaḥ sopi
tava rakṣatu jīvitaṃ likhi likhi khili svāhā ||
evaṃ snatastu mantreṇa juhuyāttilataṇḍulam //
meaning:
भास्करे ऽनुदिते पीठे प्रातः संस्नापयेद् घटैः /
ओं नमो भगवते रुद्राय च बलाय च
पाण्डरोचितभस्मानुलिप्तगात्राय / तद्यथा जय जय सर्वान्
शत्रून्मूकस्य कलहविग्रहविवादेषु भञ्जय / ओं मथ मथ
सर्वपथिकान्योसौ युगान्तकाले दिधक्षति इमां पूजां
रौद्रमूर्तिः सहस्रांशुः शुक्रः स ते रक्षतु जीवितं /
सम्बर्तकाग्नितुल्यश् च त्रिपुरान्तकरः शिवः / सर्वदेवमयः सोपि
तव रक्षतु जीवितं लिखि लिखि खिलि स्वाहा ||
एवं स्नतस्तु मन्त्रेण जुहुयात्तिलतण्डुलम् //
text_mt:
Before the sun has risen, in the morning, one should bathe [him] on the seat with jars:
"Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Rudra and to Bala, whose body is smeared with white, fitting ashes! Thus: conquer, conquer all enemies of so-and-so; smash [them] in quarrels, conflicts, and disputes! Oṃ, crush, crush all travelers! He who at the time of the end of the aeon desires to burn, of terrible form, thousand-rayed, the bright one: may he protect your life! And Śiva, equal to the fire of universal destruction, the destroyer of Tripura, consisting of all gods: may he also protect your life! Likhi likhi khili svāhā!"
Thus bathed with the mantra, he should offer sesamum and unbroken rice into the fire.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcāmṛtaistu saṃsnāpya pūjayecchūlapāṇinaṃ /
snānānyanyāni vakṣyāmi sarvadā vijayāya te //
meaning:
पञ्चामृतैस्तु संस्नाप्य पूजयेच्छूलपाणिनं /
स्नानान्यन्यानि वक्ष्यामि सर्वदा विजयाय ते //
text_mt: Having bathed [him] with the five nectars, one should worship the Trident-Holder. / I shall state other baths for your constant victory.

sanskrit_iast:
snānaṃ ghṛtena kathitamāyuṣyavardhanaṃ param /
gomayena ca lakṣmīḥ syādgomūtreṇāghamardanam //
meaning:
स्नानं घृतेन कथितमायुष्यवर्धनं परम् /
गोमयेन च लक्ष्मीः स्याद्गोमूत्रेणाघमर्दनम् //
text_mt: Bathing with ghee is declared to be the best increaser of longevity. / By cow dung fortune is obtained, and by cow urine the destruction of sins.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīreṇa balabuddhiḥ syāddadhnā lakṣmīvivardhanaṃ /
kuśodakena pāpāntaḥ pañcagavyena sarvabhāk //
meaning:
क्षीरेण बलबुद्धिः स्याद्दध्ना लक्ष्मीविवर्धनं /
कुशोदकेन पापान्तः पञ्चगव्येन सर्वभाक् //
text_mt: By milk there is strength and intellect; by curds, the increase of fortune. / By water with kuśa grass there is an end to sin; by the five products of the cow one possesses all.

sanskrit_iast:
śatamūlena sarvāptirgośṛṅgodakato 'ghajit /
:p 472
palāśabilvakamalakuśasnānantu sarvadaṃ //
meaning:
शतमूलेन सर्वाप्तिर्गोशृङ्गोदकतो ऽघजित् /
:प् 472
पलाशबिल्वकमलकुशस्नानन्तु सर्वदं //
text_mt:
By śatamūlā all is attained; through water [poured over] a cow's horn sins are conquered.
[Page 472]
A bath with palāśa, bilva, lotus, and kuśa bestows everything.

sanskrit_iast:
vacā haridre dve mustaṃ snānaṃ rakṣohaṇaṃ paraṃ /
āyuṣyañca yaśasyañca dharmamedhāvivardhanam //
meaning:
वचा हरिद्रे द्वे मुस्तं स्नानं रक्षोहणं परं /
आयुष्यञ्च यशस्यञ्च धर्ममेधाविवर्धनम् //
text_mt: Vacā, the two turmerics, and mustā make the best bath that slays demons, / increasing longevity, renown, righteousness, and intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
haimādbhiś caiva māṅgalyaṃ rūpyatāmrodakais tathā /
ratnodakaistu vijayaḥ saubhāgyaṃ sarvagandhakaiḥ //
meaning:
हैमाद्भिश् चैव माङ्गल्यं रूप्यताम्रोदकैस् तथा /
रत्नोदकैस्तु विजयः सौभाग्यं सर्वगन्धकैः //
text_mt: Auspiciousness comes from water [infused with] gold, and likewise with silver- and copper-water; / victory comes through gem-infused water, and good fortune through all fragrant substances.

sanskrit_iast:
phalādbhiś ca tathārogyaṃ dhātryadbhiḥ paramāṃ śriyam /
tilasiddhārthakair lakṣmīḥ saubhāgyañca priyaṅguṇā //
meaning:
फलाद्भिश् च तथारोग्यं धात्र्यद्भिः परमां श्रियम् /
तिलसिद्धार्थकैर् लक्ष्मीः सौभाग्यञ्च प्रियङ्गुणा //
text_mt: Likewise, freedom from disease comes from water [steeped with] fruits, and supreme fortune from emblic myrobalan water; / prosperity comes through sesamum and white mustard seeds, and good fortune through priyaṅgu.

sanskrit_iast:
padmotpalakadambaiś ca śrīrbalaṃ balādrumodakaiḥ /
viṣṇupādodakasnānaṃ sarvasnānebhya uttamam //
meaning:
पद्मोत्पलकदम्बैश् च श्रीर्बलं बलाद्रुमोदकैः /
विष्णुपादोदकस्नानं सर्वस्नानेभ्य उत्तमम् //
text_mt: Through lotus, water lily, and kadamba comes prosperity; strength comes from waters [infused with] the balādruma tree. / A bath with water [that has washed] Viṣṇu's feet is the best of all baths.

sanskrit_iast:
ekākī ekakāmāyetyekorkaṃ(1) vidhivaccaret /
akrandayatisūktena prabadhnīyānmaṇiṃ kare //
meaning:
एकाकी एककामायेत्येकोर्कं(1) विधिवच्चरेत् /
अक्रन्दयतिसूक्तेन प्रबध्नीयान्मणिं करे //
text_mt: Alone, for a single desire, one should offer an arka plant according to rule; / with the Akrandayati hymn one should bind an amulet on the hand.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṣṭhapāṭhā vācā śuṇṭhī śaṅkhalohādiko maṇiḥ /
sarveṣāmevakāmānāmīśvaro bhagavān hariḥ //
meaning:
कुष्ठपाठा वाचा शुण्ठी शङ्खलोहादिको मणिः /
सर्वेषामेवकामानामीश्वरो भगवान् हरिः //
text_mt: Kuṣṭha, pāṭhā, vacā, dry ginger, an amulet of conch, iron, and the like [are used]. / The Blessed Lord Hari is indeed the lord of all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya saṃpūjanādeva sarvānkāmānsamaśnute /
snāpayitvā ghṛtakṣīraiḥ pūjayitvā ca pittahā //
meaning:
तस्य संपूजनादेव सर्वान्कामान्समश्नुते /
स्नापयित्वा घृतक्षीरैः पूजयित्वा च पित्तहा //
text_mt: From his worship alone one attains all desires. / Having bathed [him] with ghee and milk and worshipped him, one destroys bile disorders.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamudgabalindatvā atisārāt pramucyate /
pañcagavyena saṃsnāpya vātavyādhiṃ vināśayet //
meaning:
पञ्चमुद्गबलिन्दत्वा अतिसारात् प्रमुच्यते /
पञ्चगव्येन संस्नाप्य वातव्याधिं विनाशयेत् //
text_mt: Having offered the oblation of five varieties of kidney beans, one is freed from diarrhea; / having bathed him with the five products of the cow, one destroys disorders of wind.

sanskrit_iast:
dvisnehasnapanāt śleṣmarogahā cātipūjayā /
ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ snānantu trirasaṃ paraṃ //
meaning:
द्विस्नेहस्नपनात् श्लेष्मरोगहा चातिपूजया /
घृतं तैलं तथा क्षौद्रं स्नानन्तु त्रिरसं परं //
text_mt: From bathing [him] with two unctuous substances and through intense worship, one destroys phlegm disorders. / Ghee, oil, and honey—this bath of three fluids is supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
snānaṃ ghṛtāmbu dvisnehaṃ samalaṃ ghṛtatailakam /
kṣaudramikṣurasaṃ kṣīraṃ snānaṃ trimadhuraṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
स्नानं घृताम्बु द्विस्नेहं समलं घृततैलकम् /
क्षौद्रमिक्षुरसं क्षीरं स्नानं त्रिमधुरं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: A bath of ghee and water is the two unctuous substances; ghee and oil mixed is [another] two unctuous substances. / Honey, sugarcane juice, and milk—this bath is known as the three sweets.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtamiśurasaṃ tailaṃ kṣaudrañca trirasaṃ śriye /
:n
1 yavakāmāyetyekorkamiti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 473
anulepastriśukrastu karpūrośīracandanaiḥ //
meaning:
घृतमिशुरसं तैलं क्षौद्रञ्च त्रिरसं श्रिये /
:न्
1 यवकामायेत्येकोर्कमिति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 473
अनुलेपस्त्रिशुक्रस्तु कर्पूरोशीरचन्दनैः //
text_mt:
Ghee, sugarcane juice, oil, and honey—the bath of three fluids is for prosperity.
[Footnote 1: 'yavakāmāyetyekorkam' in manuscripts ka and cha] / [Page 473]
The three-white unguent consists of camphor, uśīra, and sandalwood.

sanskrit_iast:
candanāgurukarpūramṛgadarpaiḥ sakuṅkumaiḥ /
pañcānulepanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaṃ //
meaning:
चन्दनागुरुकर्पूरमृगदर्पैः सकुङ्कुमैः /
पञ्चानुलेपनं विष्णोः सर्वकामफलप्रदं //
text_mt: With sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, musk, and saffron, / the fivefold unguent of Viṣṇu bestows the fruit of all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
trisugandhañca karpūraṃ tathā candanakuṅkumaiḥ /
mṛgadarpaṃ sakarpūraṃ malayaṃ sarvakāmadam //
meaning:
त्रिसुगन्धञ्च कर्पूरं तथा चन्दनकुङ्कुमैः /
मृगदर्पं सकर्पूरं मलयं सर्वकामदम् //
text_mt: The triple-fragrant one is camphor with sandalwood and saffron; / musk along with camphor and sandalwood grants all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
jātīphalaṃ sakarpūraṃ candanañca triśītakam /
pītāni śuklavarṇāni tathā śuklāni bhārgava //
meaning:
जातीफलं सकर्पूरं चन्दनञ्च त्रिशीतकम् /
पीतानि शुक्लवर्णानि तथा शुक्लानि भार्गव //
text_mt: Nutmeg with camphor and sandalwood is the triple-cooling one. / Yellow and white colors, and likewise white ones, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇāni caiva raktāni pañcavarṇāni nirdiśet /
utpalaṃ padmajātī ca triśītaṃ haripūjane //
meaning:
कृष्णानि चैव रक्तानि पञ्चवर्णानि निर्दिशेत् /
उत्पलं पद्मजाती च त्रिशीतं हरिपूजने //
text_mt: and black and red—one should designate these five colors. / The blue water lily, the lotus, and jasmine are the three cool flowers in the worship of Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
kuṅkumaṃ raktapadmāni triraktamutpalaṃ /
dhūpadīpādibhiḥ prārcya viṣṇuṃ śāntirbhavennṛṇāṃ //
meaning:
कुङ्कुमं रक्तपद्मानि त्रिरक्तमुत्पलं /
धूपदीपादिभिः प्रार्च्य विष्णुं शान्तिर्भवेन्नृणां //
text_mt: Saffron, red lotuses, and red water lilies are the triple-red offering. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu with incense, lamps, and so forth, peace comes to men.

sanskrit_iast:
caturasrakare kuṇḍe brāhmaṇāścāṣṭa śoḍaśa /
lakṣahomaṅkoṭihomantilājyayavadhānyakaiḥ //
meaning:
चतुरस्रकरे कुण्डे ब्राह्मणाश्चाष्ट शोडश /
लक्षहोमङ्कोटिहोमन्तिलाज्ययवधान्यकैः //
text_mt: In a square cubit-sized fire-pit, eight or sixteen brāhmaṇas [perform] / the fire oblation of one hundred thousand or ten million [offerings] with sesamum, clarified butter, barley, and grains.

sanskrit_iast:
grahānabhyarcya gāyatryā sarvaśāntiḥ kramādbhavet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe maheśvarasnānalakṣakoṭihomādayo nāma
ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nīrājanavidhiḥ
meaning:
ग्रहानभ्यर्च्य गायत्र्या सर्वशान्तिः क्रमाद्भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे महेश्वरस्नानलक्षकोटिहोमादयो नाम
षट्षष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नीराजनविधिः
text_mt:
Having worshipped the planets with the Gāyatrī, all pacification shall occur in order.
Thus ends the two hundred sixty-sixth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'The Bath of the Great Lord, the Fire Oblations of One Hundred Thousand and Ten Million Offerings, and Others.'
Now, the two hundred sixty-seventh chapter:
The Rite of Lustration.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
karma sāṃvatsaraṃ rājñāṃ janmarkṣe pūjayecca taṃ /
māsi māsi ca saṃkrāntau sūryasomādidevatāḥ //
:p 474
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
कर्म सांवत्सरं राज्ञां जन्मर्क्षे पूजयेच्च तं /
मासि मासि च संक्रान्तौ सूर्यसोमादिदेवताः //
:प् 474
text_mt:
Puṣkara said: / [Regarding] the annual ritual of kings, one should worship on their natal asterism, / and month by month at the planetary transit, one should worship the deities beginning with the sun and the moon.
[Page 474]

sanskrit_iast:
agastyasyodaye 'gastyañcāturmāsyaṃ hariṃ yajet /
śayanotthāpane pañcadinaṃ kuryātsamutsavam //
meaning:
अगस्त्यस्योदये ऽगस्त्यञ्चातुर्मास्यं हरिं यजेत् /
शयनोत्थापने पञ्चदिनं कुर्यात्समुत्सवम् //
text_mt: At the rising of Agastya one should worship Agastya; during the four-month period of rain one should worship Hari. / At [his] lying down and rising up, one should celebrate a great festival for five days.

sanskrit_iast:
proṣṭhapāde site pakṣe pratipatprabhṛtikramāt /
śivirāt pūrvadigbhāge śakrārthaṃ bhavanañcaret //
meaning:
प्रोष्ठपादे सिते पक्षे प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिक्रमात् /
शिविरात् पूर्वदिग्भागे शक्रार्थं भवनञ्चरेत् //
text_mt: In the month of Bhādrapada, in the bright fortnight, beginning in order from the first lunar day, / one should construct a pavilion in the eastern direction from the camp for Śakra.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra śakradhvajaṃ sthāpya śacī śakrañca pūjayet /
aṣṭamyāṃ vādyaghoṣeṇa tāntu yaṣṭiṃ praveśayet //
meaning:
तत्र शक्रध्वजं स्थाप्य शची शक्रञ्च पूजयेत् /
अष्टम्यां वाद्यघोषेण तान्तु यष्टिं प्रवेशयेत् //
text_mt: Having raised the banner of Śakra there, one should worship Śacī and Śakra; / on the eighth lunar day, one should bring that staff inside to the sound of musical instruments.

sanskrit_iast:
ekādaśyāṃ sopavāso dvādaśyāṃ ketumutthitam /
yajedvastrādisaṃvītaṃ ghaṭasthaṃ(1) surapaṃ śacīṃ //
meaning:
एकादश्यां सोपवासो द्वादश्यां केतुमुत्थितम् /
यजेद्वस्त्रादिसंवीतं घटस्थं(1) सुरपं शचीं //
text_mt: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day, on the twelfth lunar day one should worship / the lord of the gods [placed] in a jar [or on a cloth] and covered with garments and the like, and Śacī, beside the raised banner:

sanskrit_iast:
vardhasvendra jitāmitra vṛtrahan pākaśāsana /
deva deva mahābhāga tvaṃ hi bhūmiṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ //
meaning:
वर्धस्वेन्द्र जितामित्र वृत्रहन् पाकशासन /
देव देव महाभाग त्वं हि भूमिष्ठतां गतः //
text_mt: 'Grow, O Indra, conqueror of enemies, slayer of Vṛtra, subduer of Pāka! / O god of gods, O highly fortunate one, you have indeed come to reside on earth!

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ prabhuḥ śāśvataś caiva sarvabhūtahite rataḥ /
anantatejā vai rājo yaśojayavivardhanaḥ //
meaning:
त्वं प्रभुः शाश्वतश् चैव सर्वभूतहिते रतः /
अनन्ततेजा वै राजो यशोजयविवर्धनः //
text_mt: You are the sovereign lord, eternal and devoted to the welfare of all beings, / of boundless splendor, a king who increases fame and victory!

sanskrit_iast:
tejaste vardhayantvete devāḥ śakraḥ suvṛṣṭikṛt /
brahmaviṣṇumaheśāś ca kārttikeyo vināyakaḥ //
meaning:
तेजस्ते वर्धयन्त्वेते देवाः शक्रः सुवृष्टिकृत् /
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाश् च कार्त्तिकेयो विनायकः //
text_mt: May these gods increase your splendor, O Śakra, maker of good rain! / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, Kārttikeya, Vināyaka,

sanskrit_iast:
ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyāś ca bhṛgavo diśaḥ /
marudguṇā lokapālā grahā yakṣādrinimnagāḥ //
meaning:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्याश् च भृगवो दिशः /
मरुद्गुणा लोकपाला ग्रहा यक्षाद्रिनिम्नगाः //
text_mt: the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Bhṛgus, the directions, / the hosts of Maruts, the world guardians, planets, yakṣas, mountains, and rivers,

sanskrit_iast:
samudrā śrīrmahī gaurī caṇḍikā ca sarasvatī /
pravartayantu te tejo jaya śakra śacīpate //
meaning:
समुद्रा श्रीर्मही गौरी चण्डिका च सरस्वती /
प्रवर्तयन्तु ते तेजो जय शक्र शचीपते //
text_mt: the oceans, Śrī, the Earth, Gaurī, Caṇḍikā, and Sarasvatī! / May they arouse your splendor! Be victorious, O Śakra, consort of Śacī!

sanskrit_iast:
tava cāpi jayānnityaṃ mama sampaṭhyatāṃ śubhaṃ /
prasīda rājñāṃ viprāṇāṃ prajānāmapi sarvaśaḥ //
meaning:
तव चापि जयान्नित्यं मम सम्पठ्यतां शुभं /
प्रसीद राज्ञां विप्राणां प्रजानामपि सर्वशः //
text_mt: And through your constant victory, let auspiciousness be proclaimed for me! / Be gracious to kings, brāhmaṇas, and to the subjects everywhere!

sanskrit_iast:
bhavatprasādāt pṛthivī nityaṃ śasyavatī bhavet /
śivaṃ bhavatu nirvighnaṃ śāmyantāmītayo bhṛśaṃ //
:n
1 paṭasthamiti ka.. , ga.. , cha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 475
meaning:
भवत्प्रसादात् पृथिवी नित्यं शस्यवती भवेत् /
शिवं भवतु निर्विघ्नं शाम्यन्तामीतयो भृशं //
:न्
1 पटस्थमिति क.. , ग.. , छ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 475
text_mt:
By your grace, may the earth ever abound with crops! / May there be auspiciousness without obstacles! May calamities be entirely pacified!'
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: 'paṭastham' in manuscripts ka, ga, cha, ja, and ṭa] / [Page 475]

sanskrit_iast:
mantreṇendraṃ samabhyarcya jitabhūḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
bhadrakālīṃ paṭe likhya pūjayedāśvine jaye //
meaning:
मन्त्रेणेन्द्रं समभ्यर्च्य जितभूः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् /
भद्रकालीं पटे लिख्य पूजयेदाश्विने जये //
text_mt: Having worshipped Indra with the mantra, having conquered the earth, one attains heaven. / Having drawn Bhadrakālī on a cloth, one should worship her in the month of Āśvina for victory,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklapakṣe tathāṣṭamyāmāyudhaṃ kārmukaṃ dhvajam /
chatrañca rājaliṅgāni śastrādyaṃ kusumādibhiḥ //
meaning:
शुक्लपक्षे तथाष्टम्यामायुधं कार्मुकं ध्वजम् /
छत्रञ्च राजलिङ्गानि शस्त्राद्यं कुसुमादिभिः //
text_mt: in the bright fortnight, likewise on the eighth lunar day, [worshipping] the weapon, bow, banner, / umbrella, and royal insignia, weapons and the like, with flowers and other offerings.

sanskrit_iast:
jāgranniśi balindadyāddvitīye 'hni punaryajet /
bhadrakāli mahākāli durge durgārtihāriṇi //
meaning:
जाग्रन्निशि बलिन्दद्याद्द्वितीये ऽह्नि पुनर्यजेत् /
भद्रकालि महाकालि दुर्गे दुर्गार्तिहारिणि //
text_mt: Remaining awake at night, one should offer oblation; on the second day one should worship again: / 'O Bhadrakālī, Mahākālī, Durgā, remover of distress at fortress gates,

sanskrit_iast:
trailokyavijaye caṇḍi mama śāntau jaye bhava /
nīrājanavidhiṃ vakṣye aiśānyānmandiraṃ caret //
meaning:
त्रैलोक्यविजये चण्डि मम शान्तौ जये भव /
नीराजनविधिं वक्ष्ये ऐशान्यान्मन्दिरं चरेत् //
text_mt: victor in the three worlds, O Caṇḍī, be present for my peace and victory!' / I shall declare the rite of lustration: one should build a pavilion in the north-east.

sanskrit_iast:
toraṇatritayaṃ tatra gṛhe devānyajet sadā /
citrāntyaktvā yadā svātiṃ savitā pratipadyate //
meaning:
तोरणत्रितयं तत्र गृहे देवान्यजेत् सदा /
चित्रान्त्यक्त्वा यदा स्वातिं सविता प्रतिपद्यते //
text_mt: There are three arched gateways there; in that house one should constantly worship the gods. / When the sun, leaving Citrā, enters Svātī,

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabhṛti kartavyaṃ yāvat svātau raviḥ sthitaḥ /
brahmā viṣṇuś ca śambhuś ca śakraś caivānalānilau //
meaning:
ततः प्रभृति कर्तव्यं यावत् स्वातौ रविः स्थितः /
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश् च शम्भुश् च शक्रश् चैवानलानिलौ //
text_mt: from that time forth [the rite] is to be performed as long as the sun remains in Svātī. / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Śakra, Fire and Wind,

sanskrit_iast:
vināyakaḥ kumāraś ca varuṇo dhanado yamaḥ /
viśvedevā vaiśravaso gajāścāṣṭau ca tānyajet //
meaning:
विनायकः कुमारश् च वरुणो धनदो यमः /
विश्वेदेवा वैश्रवसो गजाश्चाष्टौ च तान्यजेत् //
text_mt: Vināyaka, Kumāra, Varuṇa, Kubera, Yama, / the Viśvedevas, Kubera, and the eight elephants—one should worship them:

sanskrit_iast:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadantaś ca vāmanaḥ /
supratīko 'ñjano nīlaḥ pūjā kāryā gṛhādike //
meaning:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदन्तश् च वामनः /
सुप्रतीको ऽञ्जनो नीलः पूजा कार्या गृहादिके //
text_mt: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla; the worship is to be performed in the pavilion and other places.

sanskrit_iast:
purodhā juhuyādājyaṃ samitsiddhārthakaṃ tilāḥ /
kumbhā aṣṭau pūjitāś ca taiḥ snāpyāśvagajottamāḥ //
meaning:
पुरोधा जुहुयादाज्यं समित्सिद्धार्थकं तिलाः /
कुम्भा अष्टौ पूजिताश् च तैः स्नाप्याश्वगजोत्तमाः //
text_mt: The royal chaplain should offer ghee, fuel sticks, white mustard, and sesamum seeds into the fire. / Eight jars are worshipped, and with them the excellent horses and elephants should be bathed.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvāḥ snāpyā dadet piṇḍān tato hi prathamaṃ gajān /
niṣkrāmayettoraṇaistu gopurādi(1) na laṅghayet //
meaning:
अश्वाः स्नाप्या ददेत् पिण्डान् ततो हि प्रथमं गजान् /
निष्क्रामयेत्तोरणैस्तु गोपुरादि(1) न लङ्घयेत् //
text_mt: Having bathed the horses, he should offer food balls, and then first of all [the horses and] elephants / he should lead out through the arches; he should not step over the town gate and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
vikrameyustataḥ sarve rājaliṅgaṃ gṛhe yajet /
:n
1 śekharādīti ka..
:p 476
vāruṇe varuṇaṃ prārcya rātrau bhūtabaliṃ dadet //
meaning:
विक्रमेयुस्ततः सर्वे राजलिङ्गं गृहे यजेत् /
:न्
1 शेखरादीति क..
:प् 476
वारुणे वरुणं प्रार्च्य रात्रौ भूतबलिं ददेत् //
text_mt:
Then they all should march out; in the house, one should worship the royal insignia.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: 'śekharādī' in manuscript ka] / [Page 476]
Having worshipped Varuṇa in the west, one should offer an oblation to the spirits at night.

sanskrit_iast:
viśākhāyāṃ(1) gate sūrye āśrame nivasennṛpaḥ /
alaṅkuryāddine tasmin vāhanantu viśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
विशाखायां(1) गते सूर्ये आश्रमे निवसेन्नृपः /
अलङ्कुर्याद्दिने तस्मिन् वाहनन्तु विशेषतः //
text_mt: When the sun has entered the asterism Viśākhā, the king should reside in the hermitage; / and on that day he should especially adorn the mounts.

sanskrit_iast:
pūjitā rājaliṅgāś ca kartavyā narahastagāḥ /
hastinanturagaṃ chatraṃ khaḍgaṃ cāpañca dundubhim //
meaning:
पूजिता राजलिङ्गाश् च कर्तव्या नरहस्तगाः /
हस्तिनन्तुरगं छत्रं खड्गं चापञ्च दुन्दुभिम् //
text_mt: The royal insignia, having been worshipped, should be placed in the hands of men: / the elephant, horse, parasol, sword, bow, drum,

sanskrit_iast:
dhvajaṃ patākāṃ dharmajña kālajñastvabhimantrayet /
abhimantrya tataḥ sarvān kuryāt kuñjaradhūrgatān //
meaning:
ध्वजं पताकां धर्मज्ञ कालज्ञस्त्वभिमन्त्रयेत् /
अभिमन्त्र्य ततः सर्वान् कुर्यात् कुञ्जरधूर्गतान् //
text_mt: standard, and banner, O knower of duty; the knower of time should consecrate them with mantras. / Having consecrated all of them, he should place them before the elephant.

sanskrit_iast:
kuñjaroparigau syātāṃ sāṃvatsarapurohitau /
mantritāṃś ca samāruhya toraṇena vinirgamet //
meaning:
कुञ्जरोपरिगौ स्यातां सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ /
मन्त्रितांश् च समारुह्य तोरणेन विनिर्गमेत् //
text_mt: The astrologer and the family priest should mount upon the elephant. / Having mounted the consecrated ones, he should depart through the ceremonial archway.

sanskrit_iast:
niṣkramya nāgamāruhya toraṇenātha nirgamet /
baliṃ vibhajya vidhivadrājā kuñjaradhūrgataḥ //
meaning:
निष्क्रम्य नागमारुह्य तोरणेनाथ निर्गमेत् /
बलिं विभज्य विधिवद्राजा कुञ्जरधूर्गतः //
text_mt: Having come out and mounted the elephant, he should then depart through the ceremonial archway. / Having distributed the bali according to rule, the king, stationed at the forefront of the elephant,

sanskrit_iast:
unmūkānāntu nicayamādīpitadigantaraṃ /
rājā pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāttrīn vārān susamāhitaḥ //
meaning:
उन्मूकानान्तु निचयमादीपितदिगन्तरं /
राजा प्रदक्षिणं कुर्यात्त्रीन् वारान् सुसमाहितः //
text_mt: should attentively perform circumambulation three times / around a heap of burning brands that illuminates the quarters.

sanskrit_iast:
caturaṅgabalopetaḥ sarvasainyena nādayan /
evaṃ kṛtvā gṛhaṃ gacchedvisarjitajalāñjaliḥ //
meaning:
चतुरङ्गबलोपेतः सर्वसैन्येन नादयन् /
एवं कृत्वा गृहं गच्छेद्विसर्जितजलाञ्जलिः //
text_mt: Accompanied by the fourfold army, making sound with the entire host, / having done so and having poured out a handful of water, he should return to his palace.

sanskrit_iast:
śāntir nīrājanākhyeyaṃ vṛddhaye ripumardanī //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nīrājanāvidhirnāma
saptaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 viśākhāntviti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 477
:ś athāṣṭaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
chatrādimantrādayaḥ
meaning:
शान्तिर् नीराजनाख्येयं वृद्धये रिपुमर्दनी //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नीराजनाविधिर्नाम
सप्तषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 विशाखान्त्विति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 477
:श् अथाष्टषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
छत्रादिमन्त्रादयः
text_mt:
This pacification rite called Nīrājanā is for prosperity and crushes enemies.
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Rule of Nīrājanā,” in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1. "viśākhāṃ tu" thus in manuscripts ka and cha. / [Page 477]
Now, the two hundred and sixty-eighth chapter:
Mantras for the Parasol and Other Items.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
chatrādimantrānvakṣyāmi yaistat pūjya jayādikam /
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
छत्रादिमन्त्रान्वक्ष्यामि यैस्तत् पूज्य जयादिकम् /
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / I will proclaim the mantras for the parasol and other items, by which, when worshipped, victory and other blessings [are attained]. / By the true word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
sūryasya ca prabhāvena vardhasva tvaṃ mahāmate /
pāṇḍarābhapratīkāśa himakundendusuprabha //
meaning:
सूर्यस्य च प्रभावेन वर्धस्व त्वं महामते /
पाण्डराभप्रतीकाश हिमकुन्देन्दुसुप्रभ //
text_mt: and by the splendor of the Sun, prosper, O intelligent one, / O you who resemble white radiance, brilliant like snow, the kunda flower, and the moon!

sanskrit_iast:
yathāmbudaśchādayate śivāyaināṃ vasundharāṃ /
tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye //
meaning:
यथाम्बुदश्छादयते शिवायैनां वसुन्धरां /
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये //
text_mt: Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare, / so cover the king for victory, health, and prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
gandharvakulajātastvaṃ mābhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ /
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca //
meaning:
गन्धर्वकुलजातस्त्वं माभूयाः कुलदूषकः /
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च //
text_mt: You are born of the Gandharva lineage; do not bring disgrace to your lineage! / By the true word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
prabhāvācca hutāśasya vardhasva tvaṃ turaṅgama /
tejasā caiva sūryasya munīnāṃ tapasā tathā //
meaning:
प्रभावाच्च हुताशस्य वर्धस्व त्वं तुरङ्गम /
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा तथा //
text_mt: and by the power of the consumer of oblations, grow strong, O horse! / And by the brilliance of the Sun, and by the ascetic austerity of the sages,

sanskrit_iast:
rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya balena ca /
smara tvaṃ rājaputro 'si kaustubhantu maṇiṃ smara //
meaning:
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य बलेन च /
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रो ऽसि कौस्तुभन्तु मणिं स्मर //
text_mt: by the celibacy of Rudra, and by the strength of the Wind, / remember that you are a prince! Remember the Kaustubha gem!

sanskrit_iast:
yāṃ gatiṃ brahmahā gacchet pitṛhā mātṛhā tathā /
bhūmyarthe 'nṛtavādī ca kṣatriyaś ca parāṅmukhaḥ //
meaning:
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत् पितृहा मातृहा तथा /
भूम्यर्थे ऽनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश् च पराङ्मुखः //
text_mt: The destination to which a killer of a brāhmaṇa, a father, or a mother goes, / or a speaker of falsehood for the sake of land, or a warrior who turns his back on battle—

sanskrit_iast:
vrajestvantāṃ gatiṃ kṣipraṃ mā tat pāpaṃ bhavettava /
vikṛtiṃ māpagacchestvaṃ yuddhe 'dhvani turaṅgama //
meaning:
व्रजेस्त्वन्तां गतिं क्षिप्रं मा तत् पापं भवेत्तव /
विकृतिं मापगच्छेस्त्वं युद्धे ऽध्वनि तुरङ्गम //
text_mt: may you swiftly go to that destination! May that sin not be yours! / May you not become disfigured in battle or on the road, O horse!

sanskrit_iast:
ripūn vinighnansamare saha bhartrā sukhī bhava /
śakraketo mahāvīryaḥ suvarṇastvāmupāśritaḥ //
meaning:
रिपून् विनिघ्नन्समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव /
शक्रकेतो महावीर्यः सुवर्णस्त्वामुपाश्रितः //
text_mt: Slaying enemies in battle, be happy along with your master! / O banner of Indra, the mighty, golden-winged one has resorted to you,

sanskrit_iast:
patatrirāḍvainateyas tathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ /
:p 478
kāśyapeyo 'mṛtāhartā nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ //
meaning:
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस् तथा नारायणध्वजः /
:प् 478
काश्यपेयो ऽमृताहर्ता नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः //
text_mt:
the king of birds, the son of Vinatā, and the emblem of Nārāyaṇa,
[Page 478]
the son of Kaśyapa, the bringer of nectar, the enemy of serpents, the vehicle of Viṣṇu,

sanskrit_iast:
aprameyo durādharṣo raṇe devārisūdanaḥ /
mahābalo māvego mahākāyo 'mṛtāśanaḥ //
meaning:
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो रणे देवारिसूदनः /
महाबलो मावेगो महाकायो ऽमृताशनः //
text_mt: immeasurable, invincible, the slayer of the foes of the gods in battle, / of great strength, great speed, huge body, the consumer of nectar,

sanskrit_iast:
garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ /
viṣṇunā devadevena śakrārthaṃ sthāpito hy asi //
meaning:
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः /
विष्णुना देवदेवेन शक्रार्थं स्थापितो ह्य् असि //
text_mt: Garutmān, who moves like the wind, is stationed present within you. / For you were established by Viṣṇu, the god of gods, for Indra's sake.

sanskrit_iast:
jayāya bhava me nityaṃ vṛddhaye 'tha balasya ca /
sāśvavarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣāsmākaṃ ripūndaha //
meaning:
जयाय भव मे नित्यं वृद्धये ऽथ बलस्य च /
साश्ववर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्माकं रिपून्दह //
text_mt: Be ever for my victory, and for the increase of my army! / Protect our warriors with their horses, armor, and weapons, and burn up the enemies!

sanskrit_iast:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadanto 'tha vāmanaḥ /
supratīko 'ñjano nīla ete 'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ //
meaning:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदन्तो ऽथ वामनः /
सुप्रतीको ऽञ्जनो नील एते ऽष्टौ देवयोनयः //
text_mt: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are born of divine origin.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ /
bhadro mando mṛgaś caiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca //
meaning:
तेषां पुत्राश् च पौत्राश् च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः /
भद्रो मन्दो मृगश् चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च //
text_mt: Their sons and grandsons resort to the eight forces; / [the classes of elephants are:] bhadra, manda, mṛga, and saṃkīrṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
vane vane prasūtāste smarayoniṃ mahāgajāḥ /
pāntu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ //
meaning:
वने वने प्रसूतास्ते स्मरयोनिं महागजाः /
पान्तु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः //
text_mt: Born in forest after forest, remember your origin, O great elephants! / May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, along with the hosts of Maruts, protect you.

sanskrit_iast:
bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaḥ paripālyatāṃ /
airāvatādhirūḍhastu vajrahastaḥ śatakratuḥ //
meaning:
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयः परिपाल्यतां /
ऐरावताधिरूढस्तु वज्रहस्तः शतक्रतुः //
text_mt: Protect your master, O lord of elephants; let your duty be preserved! / Mounted on Airāvata, holding the thunderbolt, Śatakratu,

sanskrit_iast:
pṛṣṭhato 'nugatastveṣa rakṣatu tvāṃ sa devarāṭ /
avāpnuhi jayaṃ yuddhe susthaś caiva sadā vraja //
meaning:
पृष्ठतो ऽनुगतस्त्वेष रक्षतु त्वां स देवराट् /
अवाप्नुहि जयं युद्धे सुस्थश् चैव सदा व्रज //
text_mt: following behind you—may that king of the gods protect you! / Attain victory in battle, and always march in sound condition!

sanskrit_iast:
avāpnuhi balañcaiva airāvatasamaṃ yudhi /
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavo 'nilāt //
meaning:
अवाप्नुहि बलञ्चैव ऐरावतसमं युधि /
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवो ऽनिलात् //
text_mt: Attain strength in battle equal to Airāvata! / May your fortune come from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, brilliance from the Sun, speed from the Wind,

sanskrit_iast:
sthairyaṃ girerjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devāt purandarāt /
yuddhe rakṣantu nāgāstvāṃ diśaś ca saha daivataiḥ //
meaning:
स्थैर्यं गिरेर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात् पुरन्दरात् /
युद्धे रक्षन्तु नागास्त्वां दिशश् च सह दैवतैः //
text_mt: steadfastness from the mountain, victory from Rudra, and renown from the divine Purandara! / May the elephants protect you in battle, and the directions along with their deities!

sanskrit_iast:
aśvinau saha gandharvaiḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvato diśaḥ /
manvo vasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ //
:p 479
meaning:
अश्विनौ सह गन्धर्वैः पान्तु त्वां सर्वतो दिशः /
मन्वो वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः //
:प् 479
text_mt:
May the Aśvins together with the Gandharvas protect you from all quarters! / The Manus, Vasus, Rudras, Vāyu, Soma, the great sages,
[Page 479]

sanskrit_iast:
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣabhūtagaṇā grahāḥ /
pramathāstu sahādityair bhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha //
meaning:
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्षभूतगणा ग्रहाः /
प्रमथास्तु सहादित्यैर् भूतेशो मातृभिः सह //
text_mt: the hosts of nāgas, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, and bhūtas, the planets, / the Pramathas along with the Ādityas, the Lord of spirits with the Mothers,

sanskrit_iast:
śakraḥ senāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritastvayi /
pradahantu ripūn sarvān rājā vijayamṛcchatu //
meaning:
शक्रः सेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितस्त्वयि /
प्रदहन्तु रिपून् सर्वान् राजा विजयमृच्छतु //
text_mt: Indra, Skanda the general of the army, and Varuṇa have resorted to you. / Let them burn all enemies, and let the king attain victory!

sanskrit_iast:
yāni prayuktānyaribhirbhūṣaṇāni samantataḥ /
patantu tava śatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā //
meaning:
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्भूषणानि समन्ततः /
पतन्तु तव शत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा //
text_mt: Whatever ornaments are employed all around by enemies, / may they fall, destroyed by your brilliance, upon your enemies!

sanskrit_iast:
kālanemibadhe yadvat yuddhe tripuraghātane /
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe badhe sarvāsureṣu ca //
meaning:
कालनेमिबधे यद्वत् युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने /
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे बधे सर्वासुरेषु च //
text_mt: Just as in the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle of the destruction of Tripura, / in the battle of Hiraṇyakaśipu, and in the slaughter of all the asuras,

sanskrit_iast:
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhasva samayaṃ smara /
nīlasvetāmimāndṛṣṭvā naśyantvāśu nṛpārayaḥ //
meaning:
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभस्व समयं स्मर /
नीलस्वेतामिमान्दृष्ट्वा नश्यन्त्वाशु नृपारयः //
text_mt: you shone, just so shine today! Remember your duty! / Seeing this black and white [banner], may the king's enemies quickly perish,

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhibhirvividhair ghoraiḥ śastraiś ca yudhi nirjitāḥ /
pūtanā revatī lekhā kālarātrīti paṭhyate //
meaning:
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर् घोरैः शस्त्रैश् च युधि निर्जिताः /
पूतना रेवती लेखा कालरात्रीति पठ्यते //
text_mt: overcome in battle by diverse, terrible diseases and by weapons! / Pūtanā, Revatī, Lekhā, and the one called Kālarātrī—

sanskrit_iast:
dahantvāśu ripūn sarvānpatāke tvāmupāśritāḥ /
sarvamedhe mahāyajñe devadevena śūlinā //
meaning:
दहन्त्वाशु रिपून् सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपाश्रिताः /
सर्वमेधे महायज्ञे देवदेवेन शूलिना //
text_mt: having resorted to you, O banner, let them quickly consume all foes! / In the Sarvamedha great sacrifice, by the god of gods who holds the trident,

sanskrit_iast:
śarveṇa jagataś caiva sāreṇa tvaṃ vinirmitaḥ /
nandakasyāparāṃ mūrtiṃ smara śatrunivarhaṇa //
meaning:
शर्वेण जगतश् चैव सारेण त्वं विनिर्मितः /
नन्दकस्यापरां मूर्तिं स्मर शत्रुनिवर्हण //
text_mt: by Śarva, you were created out of the essence of the entire universe. / Remember the other form of Nandaka, O destroyer of foes!

sanskrit_iast:
nīlotpaladalaśyāma kṛṣṇa duḥsvapnanāśana /
asirviśasanaḥ khaḍgastīkṣṇadhāro durāsadaḥ //
meaning:
नीलोत्पलदलश्याम कृष्ण दुःस्वप्ननाशन /
असिर्विशसनः खड्गस्तीक्ष्णधारो दुरासदः //
text_mt: Dark as a blue lotus petal, black, destroyer of bad dreams! / Asi, Viśasana, Khaḍga, Tīkṣṇadhāra, Durāsada,

sanskrit_iast:
augarbho vijayaś caiva dharmapālastathaiva ca /
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni puroktāni svayambhuvā //
meaning:
औगर्भो विजयश् चैव धर्मपालस्तथैव च /
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि पुरोक्तानि स्वयम्भुवा //
text_mt: Āugarbha, Vijaya, and Dharmapāla— / these are your eight names spoken formerly by the Self-born One.

sanskrit_iast:
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ /
hiraṇyañca śarīrante daivatante janārdanaḥ //
meaning:
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः /
हिरण्यञ्च शरीरन्ते दैवतन्ते जनार्दनः //
text_mt: Your asterism is Kṛttikā, your guru is the god Maheśvara, / your body is gold, and your deity is Janārdana.

sanskrit_iast:
rājānaṃ rakṣa nistriṃśa sabalaṃ sapurantathā /
:p 480
pitā pitāmaho devaḥ sa tvaṃ pālaya sarvadā //
meaning:
राजानं रक्ष निस्त्रिंश सबलं सपुरन्तथा /
:प् 480
पिता पितामहो देवः स त्वं पालय सर्वदा //
text_mt:
Protect the king, O pitiless sword, along with his army and his city!
[Page 480]
The god is your father and grandfather; as such, protect him always!

sanskrit_iast:
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varman sainye yaśo 'dya me /
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo 'hantavānagha namo 'stu te //
meaning:
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्मन् सैन्ये यशो ऽद्य मे /
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयो ऽहन्तवानघ नमो ऽस्तु ते //
text_mt: You bestow comfort in battle, O armor, and renown today in my army. / Protect me, for I am to be protected by you, O sinless one! Homage be to you!

sanskrit_iast:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ ghoṣāddhṛdayakampanaḥ /
bhava bhūmisainyānāṃ yathā vijayavardhanaḥ //
meaning:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां घोषाद्धृदयकम्पनः /
भव भूमिसैन्यानां यथा विजयवर्धनः //
text_mt: O drum, you cause the hearts of adversaries to tremble by your sound; / become the increaser of victory for the armies on earth!

sanskrit_iast:
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyanti varavāraṇāḥ /
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo 'smākaṃ mudāvaha //
meaning:
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यन्ति वरवारणाः /
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षो ऽस्माकं मुदावह //
text_mt: Just as excellent elephants rejoice at the sound of a cloud, / so by your sound let there be joy bringing gladness unto us!

sanskrit_iast:
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso 'bhijāyate /
tathā tu tava śabdena trasyantvasmaddviṣo raṇe //
meaning:
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासो ऽभिजायते /
तथा तु तव शब्देन त्रस्यन्त्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे //
text_mt: Just as terror arises in women by the sound of a thundercloud, / even so by your sound let our enemies tremble in battle!

sanskrit_iast:
mantraiḥ sadārcanīyāste yojanīyā jayādiṣu /
ghṛtakambalaviṣṇādestvabhiṣekañca vatsare //
meaning:
मन्त्रैः सदार्चनीयास्ते योजनीया जयादिषु /
घृतकम्बलविष्णादेस्त्वभिषेकञ्च वत्सरे //
text_mt: These should always be worshipped with mantras and employed for victory and the like. / And consecration by aspersion with a blanket of clarified butter, Viṣṇu, and the rest [should be performed] each year.

sanskrit_iast:
rājño 'bhiṣekaḥ kartavyo daivajñena purodhasā //39//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe chatrādimantrādayaḥ
nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 481
agnipurāṇam
maharṣiśrīmadvedavyāsena praṇītam
śrīlaśrī vaṅgadeśīyāsiyātik-samājānujñayā
śrīrājendralālamitreṇa pariśodhitam
kalikātārājadhānyāṃ gaṇeśayantre mudritañca
saṃvat 1933
agnipurāṇam
:ś athonasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
viṣṇupañjaraṃ
puṣkara uvaca
meaning:
राज्ञो ऽभिषेकः कर्तव्यो दैवज्ञेन पुरोधसा //39//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे छत्रादिमन्त्रादयः
नामाष्टषष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 481

कलिकाताराजधान्यां गणेशयन्त्रे मुद्रितञ्च

text_mt:
The consecration by aspersion of the king should be performed by the astrologer and the family priest. //39
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-eighth chapter, entitled "The Mantras for the Royal Umbrella and Other Regalia", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
