Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and sixty-ninth chapter:
The Viṣṇu-Armour.
Puṣkara said:

sanskrit_iast:
tripurañjaghnuṣaḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā viṣṇupañjaraṃ /
śaṅkarasya dvijaśreṣtha rakṣaṇāya nirūpitaṃ //
meaning:
त्रिपुरञ्जघ्नुषः पूर्वं ब्रह्मणा विष्णुपञ्जरं /
शङ्करस्य द्विजश्रेष्थ रक्षणाय निरूपितं //
text_mt: Anciently, when Śaṅkara set out to slay Tripura, the Viṣṇu-armour was prescribed / by Brahmā, O best of the twice-born, for his protection;

sanskrit_iast:
vāgīśena ca śakrasya balaṃ hantuṃ prayāsyataḥ /
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi tattvaṃ śṛṇu jayādimat //
meaning:
वागीशेन च शक्रस्य बलं हन्तुं प्रयास्यतः /
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वं शृणु जयादिमत् //
text_mt: and by the Lord of Speech [Bṛhaspati] for Indra when he set out to slay Bala. / I shall explain its nature; hear its reality, which bestows victory and other blessings.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣṇuḥ prācyāṃ sthitaś cakrī harirdakṣinaṇato gadī /
pratīcyāṃ śārṅgadhṛgviṣṇurjiṣṇuḥ khaḍgī mamottare //
meaning:
विष्णुः प्राच्यां स्थितश् चक्री हरिर्दक्षिनणतो गदी /
प्रतीच्यां शार्ङ्गधृग्विष्णुर्जिष्णुः खड्गी ममोत्तरे //
text_mt: May Viṣṇu, bearing the discus, stand in the east; Hari, bearing the mace, on the south; / may Viṣṇu, bearing the Śārṅga bow, stand in the west; and the victorious [Lord], bearing the sword, on my north.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛṣīkeśo vikoṇeṣu tacchidreṣu janārdanaḥ /
kroḍarūpī harirbhūmau narasiṃho 'mbare mama //
meaning:
हृषीकेशो विकोणेषु तच्छिद्रेषु जनार्दनः /
क्रोडरूपी हरिर्भूमौ नरसिंहो ऽम्बरे मम //
text_mt: May Hṛṣīkeśa be in the intermediate directions, and Janārdana in the intervals between them; / may Hari in the form of a boar protect me on earth, and Narasiṃha in the sky.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣurāntamamalañcakraṃ bhramatyetat sudarśanaṃ /
asyāṃśumālā duṣprekṣyā hantuṃ pretaniśācarān //
meaning:
क्षुरान्तममलञ्चक्रं भ्रमत्येतत् सुदर्शनं /
अस्यांशुमाला दुष्प्रेक्ष्या हन्तुं प्रेतनिशाचरान् //
text_mt: This spotless Sudarśana discus revolves with razor-sharp edges; / the garland of its rays is dazzling to behold, [set] to slay ghosts and night-wandering demons.

sanskrit_iast:
gadā ceyaṃ sahasrārciḥpradīptapāvakojjvalā /
rakṣobhūtapiśācānāṃ ḍākinīnāñca nāśanī //
meaning:
गदा चेयं सहस्रार्चिःप्रदीप्तपावकोज्ज्वला /
रक्षोभूतपिशाचानां डाकिनीनाञ्च नाशनी //
text_mt: And this mace, blazing with fire ignited by a thousand flames, / destroys Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, and Ḍākinīs.

sanskrit_iast:
śārṅgavisphūrjitañcaiva vāsudevasya madripūn /
tiryaṅmanuṣyakuṣmāṇḍapretādīn hantvaśeṣataḥ //
:p 1
meaning:
शार्ङ्गविस्फूर्जितञ्चैव वासुदेवस्य मद्रिपून् /
तिर्यङ्मनुष्यकुष्माण्डप्रेतादीन् हन्त्वशेषतः //
:प् 1
text_mt:
And may the twang of Vāsudeva's Śārṅga bow utterly destroy my enemies: / animals, humans, kūṣmāṇḍa demons, ghosts, and the rest.
[Page 1]

sanskrit_iast:
khaḍgadhārojjvalajjo 'tsnānirdhūtā ye samāhitāḥ /
te yāntu śāmyatāṃ sadyo garuḍeneva pannagāḥ //
meaning:
खड्गधारोज्ज्वलज्जो ऽत्स्नानिर्धूता ये समाहिताः /
ते यान्तु शाम्यतां सद्यो गरुडेनेव पन्नगाः //
text_mt: Those assembled who are scattered by the bright moonlight of the sword's blade— / may they instantly be pacified, just as serpents [are subdued] by Garuḍa.

sanskrit_iast:
ye kuṣmāṇḍāsthā yakṣā ye daityā ye niśācarāḥ /
pretā vināyakāḥ krūrā manuṣyā jambhagāḥ khagāḥ //
meaning:
ये कुष्माण्डास्था यक्षा ये दैत्या ये निशाचराः /
प्रेता विनायकाः क्रूरा मनुष्या जम्भगाः खगाः //
text_mt: Whatever kūṣmāṇḍas, yakṣas, daityas, and night-wandering demons there are, / ghosts, cruel vināyakas, humans, jambhagas, and birds,

sanskrit_iast:
siṃhādayaś ca paśavo dandaśūkāś ca pannagāḥ /
sarve bhavantu te saumyāḥ kṛṣṇaśaṅkharavāhatāḥ //
meaning:
सिंहादयश् च पशवो दन्दशूकाश् च पन्नगाः /
सर्वे भवन्तु ते सौम्याः कृष्णशङ्खरवाहताः //
text_mt: beasts such as lions, biting vermin, and serpents— / struck by the sound of Kṛṣṇa's conch, may they all become gentle.

sanskrit_iast:
cittavṛttiharā ye me ye janāḥ smṛtihārakāḥ /
balaujasañca hartāraśchāyāvibhraṃśakāś ca ye //
meaning:
चित्तवृत्तिहरा ये मे ये जनाः स्मृतिहारकाः /
बलौजसञ्च हर्तारश्छायाविभ्रंशकाश् च ये //
text_mt: Those entities that rob my mental faculties, that steal memory, / that steal strength and vitality, and that destroy my aura,

sanskrit_iast:
ye copabhogahartāro ye ca lakṣaṇanāśakāḥ /
kuṣmāṇḍāste praṇaśyantu viṣṇucakraravāhatāḥ //
meaning:
ये चोपभोगहर्तारो ये च लक्षणनाशकाः /
कुष्माण्डास्ते प्रणश्यन्तु विष्णुचक्ररवाहताः //
text_mt: and those that rob enjoyments and destroy auspicious marks— / struck by the sound of Viṣṇu's discus, may those kūṣmāṇḍas perish.

sanskrit_iast:
buddhisvāsthyaṃ manaḥsvāsthyaṃ svāsthyamaindriyakaṃ tathā /
mamāstu devadevasya vāsudevasya kīrtanāt //
meaning:
बुद्धिस्वास्थ्यं मनःस्वास्थ्यं स्वास्थ्यमैन्द्रियकं तथा /
ममास्तु देवदेवस्य वासुदेवस्य कीर्तनात् //
text_mt: May I have health of intellect, health of mind, and likewise health of the senses, / through celebrating the God of gods, Vāsudeva.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛṣṭhe purastānmama dakṣiṇottare vikoṇataścāstu janārdanohariḥ /
tamīḍyamīśānamanantamacyutaṃ janārdanaṃ praṇipatito na sīdati //
meaning:
पृष्ठे पुरस्तान्मम दक्षिणोत्तरे विकोणतश्चास्तु जनार्दनोहरिः /
तमीड्यमीशानमनन्तमच्युतं जनार्दनं प्रणिपतितो न सीदति //
text_mt: May Janārdana Hari be behind me, before me, to my right and left, and in the intermediate directions; / having bowed down to that praiseworthy Lord, the endless, unchanging Janārdana, one does not perish.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā paraṃ brahma haris tathā paraḥ jagatsvarūpaś ca sa eva keśavaḥ /
satyena tenācyutanāmakīrtanāt praṇāśayettu trividhaṃmamāśubhaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe viṣṇupañjaraṃ
nāmonasapratyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 2
:ś atha saptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vedaśākhadikīrtanaṃ
meaning:
यथा परं ब्रह्म हरिस् तथा परः जगत्स्वरूपश् च स एव केशवः /
सत्येन तेनाच्युतनामकीर्तनात् प्रणाशयेत्तु त्रिविधंममाशुभं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे विष्णुपञ्जरं
नामोनसप्रत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 2
:श् अथ सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
वेदशाखदिकीर्तनं
text_mt:
Just as Hari is the supreme Brahman, supreme, and Keśava himself embodies the universe, / by that truth, may he destroy my threefold misfortune through the recitation of Acyuta's name.
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Viṣṇu-Armour", in the great Agni Purāṇa. / [Page 2]
Now, the two hundred and seventieth chapter:
Proclamation of the Branches of the Veda and Other Subjects.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
sarvānugrāhakā mantrāś caturvargaprasādhakāḥ /
ṛgatharva tathā sāma yajuḥ saṃkhyā tu lakṣakaṃ //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
सर्वानुग्राहका मन्त्राश् चतुर्वर्गप्रसाधकाः /
ऋगथर्व तथा साम यजुः संख्या तु लक्षकं //
text_mt: Puṣkara said: / The mantras confer grace on all and accomplish the four goals of life; / the Ṛg, Atharvan, Sāman, and Yajus total one hundred thousand [verses].

sanskrit_iast:
bhedaḥ sāṅkhyāyanaś caika āśvalāyano dvitīyakaḥ /
śatāni daśa mantrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇā dvisahasrakaṃ //
meaning:
भेदः साङ्ख्यायनश् चैक आश्वलायनो द्वितीयकः /
शतानि दश मन्त्राणां ब्राह्मणा द्विसहस्रकं //
text_mt: One division is the Sāṅkhyāyana, and the second is the Āśvalāyana; / there are ten hundred mantras, and the Brāhmaṇa [portion] contains two thousand.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgvedo hi pramāṇena smṛto dvaipāyanādibhiḥ /
ekonidvisahasrantu mantrāṇāṃ yajuṣas tathā //
meaning:
ऋग्वेदो हि प्रमाणेन स्मृतो द्वैपायनादिभिः /
एकोनिद्विसहस्रन्तु मन्त्राणां यजुषस् तथा //
text_mt: The Ṛgveda is recorded according to standard measure by Dvaipāyana and others; / and nineteen hundred are the mantras of the Yajus.

sanskrit_iast:
śatāni daśa viprāṇāṃ ṣaḍaśītiś ca śākhikāḥ /
kāṇvamādhyandinī saṃjñā kaṭhī mādhyakaṭhī tathā //
meaning:
शतानि दश विप्राणां षडशीतिश् च शाखिकाः /
काण्वमाध्यन्दिनी संज्ञा कठी माध्यकठी तथा //
text_mt: There are ten hundred for the brāhmaṇas and eighty-six branches: / the one called Kāṇva, the Mādhyandina, the Kaṭha, and likewise the Mādhyakaṭha,

sanskrit_iast:
maitrāyaṇī ca saṃjñā ca taittirīyābhidhānikā /
vaiśampāyaniketyādyāḥ śākhā yajuṣi saṃsthitāḥ //
meaning:
मैत्रायणी च संज्ञा च तैत्तिरीयाभिधानिका /
वैशम्पायनिकेत्याद्याः शाखा यजुषि संस्थिताः //
text_mt: and the one named Maitrāyaṇī, the branch called Taittirīya, / the Vaiśampāyanikā, and others established in the Yajurveda.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmnaḥ kauthumasaṃjñaikā dvitīyātharvaṇāyanī /
gānānyapi ca catvāri veda āraṇyakantathā //
meaning:
साम्नः कौथुमसंज्ञैका द्वितीयाथर्वणायनी /
गानान्यपि च चत्वारि वेद आरण्यकन्तथा //
text_mt: Of the Sāmaveda, one is called Kauthuma, and the second is the Ātharvaṇāyani; / there are also four song collections, the Veda, and the Āraṇyaka,

sanskrit_iast:
ukthā ūhacaturthañca mantrā navasahasrakāḥ /
sacatuḥśatakāś caiva brahmasaṅghaṭakāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
उक्था ऊहचतुर्थञ्च मन्त्रा नवसहस्रकाः /
सचतुःशतकाश् चैव ब्रह्मसङ्घटकाः स्मृताः //
text_mt: the ukthas, and the ūha as the fourth; nine thousand / four hundred mantras are recorded as constituting Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcaviṃśatirevātra sāmamānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
sumanturjājaliś caiva ślokāyaniratharvake //
meaning:
पञ्चविंशतिरेवात्र साममानं प्रकीर्तितं /
सुमन्तुर्जाजलिश् चैव श्लोकायनिरथर्वके //
text_mt: Twenty-five [thousand] is declared here to be the measure of the Sāmaveda. / Sumantu, Jājali, and Ślokāyani belong to the Atharvaveda,

sanskrit_iast:
śaunakaḥ pippalādaś ca muñjakeśādayo 'pare /
mantrāṇāmayutaṃ ṣaṣṭiśatañcopaniṣacchataṃ //
meaning:
शौनकः पिप्पलादश् च मुञ्जकेशादयो ऽपरे /
मन्त्राणामयुतं षष्टिशतञ्चोपनिषच्छतं //
text_mt: as well as Śaunaka, Pippalāda, Muñjakeśa, and others; / it contains ten thousand mantras, one hundred and sixty [hymns], and one hundred Upaniṣads.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāsarūpī sa bhagavān śākhābhedadyakārayat /
:p 3
śākhābhedādayo viṣṇuritihāsaḥ purāṇakaṃ //
meaning:
व्यासरूपी स भगवान् शाखाभेदद्यकारयत् /
:प् 3
शाखाभेदादयो विष्णुरितिहासः पुराणकं //
text_mt:
The Blessed One in the form of Vyāsa effected the division of the branches.
[Page 3]
Viṣṇu is the division into branches and the rest; he is the epic and the Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
prāpya vyāsāt purāṇādi sūto vai lomaharṣaṇaḥ /
sumatiścāgnivarcāś ca mitrayuḥśiṃśapāyanaḥ //
meaning:
प्राप्य व्यासात् पुराणादि सूतो वै लोमहर्षणः /
सुमतिश्चाग्निवर्चाश् च मित्रयुःशिंशपायनः //
text_mt: Having received the Purāṇas and other works from Vyāsa, the Sūta Lomaharṣaṇa, / Sumati, Agnivarcas, Mitrayu, Śiṃśapāyana,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtavratotha sāvarṇiḥ ṣaṭśiṣyāstasya cābhavan /
śāṃśapāyanādayaś cakruḥ(1) purāṇānāntu saṃhitāḥ //
meaning:
कृतव्रतोथ सावर्णिः षट्शिष्यास्तस्य चाभवन् /
शांशपायनादयश् चक्रुः(1) पुराणानान्तु संहिताः //
text_mt: Kṛtavrata, and Sāvarṇi—these six became his disciples. / Śāṃśapāyana and the others composed the collections of the Purāṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmādīni purāṇāni harividyā daśāṣṭa ca /
mahāpurāṇe hy āgneye vidyārūpo hariḥ sthitaḥ //
meaning:
ब्राह्मादीनि पुराणानि हरिविद्या दशाष्ट च /
महापुराणे ह्य् आग्नेये विद्यारूपो हरिः स्थितः //
text_mt: The eighteen Purāṇas, beginning with the Brāhma, are the wisdom of Hari; / and in this great Agni Purāṇa, Hari resides in the form of sacred wisdom.

sanskrit_iast:
saprapañco niṣprapañco mūrtāmūrtasvarūpadhṛk /
taṃ jñātvābhyarcya saṃstūya bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt //
meaning:
सप्रपञ्चो निष्प्रपञ्चो मूर्तामूर्तस्वरूपधृक् /
तं ज्ञात्वाभ्यर्च्य संस्तूय भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: Possessing both cosmic differentiation and transcendence, assuming manifest and unmanifest forms, / by knowing him, worshipping him, and praising him, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣṇurjiṣṇurbhaviṣṇuś ca agnisūryādirūpavān /
agnirūpeṇa devādermukhaṃ viṣṇuḥ parā gatiḥ //
meaning:
विष्णुर्जिष्णुर्भविष्णुश् च अग्निसूर्यादिरूपवान् /
अग्निरूपेण देवादेर्मुखं विष्णुः परा गतिः //
text_mt: Viṣṇu is victorious, continually becoming, having the form of Agni, the Sun, and others; / in the form of Agni, Viṣṇu is the mouth of the gods and the supreme goal.

sanskrit_iast:
vedeṣu sapurāṇeṣu yajñamūrtiś ca gīyate /
āgneyākhyaṃ purāṇantu rūpaṃ viṣṇormahattaraṃ //
meaning:
वेदेषु सपुराणेषु यज्ञमूर्तिश् च गीयते /
आग्नेयाख्यं पुराणन्तु रूपं विष्णोर्महत्तरं //
text_mt: In the Vedas and Purāṇas he is sung as the embodiment of sacrifice; / and the Purāṇa named after Agni is the superior form of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyākhyapurāṇasya kartā śrotā janārdanaḥ /
tasmātpurāṇamāgneyaṃ sarvavedamayaṃ mahat //
meaning:
आग्नेयाख्यपुराणस्य कर्ता श्रोता जनार्दनः /
तस्मात्पुराणमाग्नेयं सर्ववेदमयं महत् //
text_mt: Janārdana is both the author and the listener of the Agni Purāṇa; / therefore, the great Agni Purāṇa is composed of all the Vedas.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvavidyāmayaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvajñānamayaṃ varam(2) /
sarvātma harirūpaṃ hi paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ nṛṇāṃ //
meaning:
सर्वविद्यामयं पुण्यं सर्वज्ञानमयं वरम्(2) /
सर्वात्म हरिरूपं हि पठतां शृण्वतां नृणां //
text_mt: It is full of all lore, meritorious, full of all knowledge, and supreme; / for it is the very form of Hari, the Self of all, to human beings who read and listen to it.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyārthināñca vidyādamarthināṃ śrīdhanapradam(3) /
rājyārthināṃ rājyadañca dharmadaṃ dharmakāminām //
meaning:
विद्यार्थिनाञ्च विद्यादमर्थिनां श्रीधनप्रदम्(3) /
राज्यार्थिनां राज्यदञ्च धर्मदं धर्मकामिनाम् //
text_mt: To those who desire knowledge it gives knowledge; to seekers of wealth it grants prosperity and riches; / to those who desire kingship it gives a kingdom; and it bestows righteousness upon those who desire righteousness.

sanskrit_iast:
svargārthināṃ svargadañca putradaṃ putrakāmināṃ /
gavādikāmināṅgodaṃ grāmadaṃ grāmakāmināṃ //
:n
1 śiṃśapāyanādayaś cakruriti kha ..
2 paramiti ña ..
3 śrībalapradamiti ña ..
:p 4
meaning:
स्वर्गार्थिनां स्वर्गदञ्च पुत्रदं पुत्रकामिनां /
गवादिकामिनाङ्गोदं ग्रामदं ग्रामकामिनां //
:न्
1 शिंशपायनादयश् चक्रुरिति ख ..
2 परमिति ञ ..
3 श्रीबलप्रदमिति ञ ..
:प् 4
text_mt:
To those desiring heaven it gives heaven; it grants a son to those desiring a son; / to those desiring cattle and the like it grants cows; it grants a village to those desiring a village.
[Footnote]
1 Manuscript kha reads: "śiṃśapāyanādayaś cakruḥ".
2 Manuscript ña reads: "param".
3 Manuscript ña reads: "śrībalapradam". / [Page 4]

sanskrit_iast:
kāmārthināṃ kāmadañca sarvasaubhāgyasampradam /
guṇakīrtipradannṝṇāṃ jayadañjayakāminām //
meaning:
कामार्थिनां कामदञ्च सर्वसौभाग्यसम्प्रदम् /
गुणकीर्तिप्रदन्नॄणां जयदञ्जयकामिनाम् //
text_mt: It grants desires to those seeking their fulfillment, and bestows all good fortune; / it grants virtue and fame to men, and gives victory to those desiring victory.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvepsūnāṃ sarvadantu muktidaṃ muktikāmināṃ /
pāpaghnaṃ pāpakartṝṇāmāgneyaṃ hi purāṇakam //
ityāgneye mahāpurāṇe vedaśākhādikīrtinaṃ nāma
saptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athaikasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dānādimāhatmyaṃ
meaning:
सर्वेप्सूनां सर्वदन्तु मुक्तिदं मुक्तिकामिनां /
पापघ्नं पापकर्तॄणामाग्नेयं हि पुराणकम् //
इत्याग्नेये महापुराणे वेदशाखादिकीर्तिनं नाम
सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दानादिमाहत्म्यं
text_mt:
It grants everything to those desiring all things; it gives liberation to those desiring liberation; / the Agni Purāṇa indeed destroys the sin of those who commit sin.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventieth chapter in the Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'The Glorification of the Branches of the Veda and Related Topics'.
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-first chapter.
The Greatness of the Gift [of the Purāṇas] and Related Matters

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkara uvāca
brahmaṇābhihitaṃ pūrvaṃ yāvanmātraṃ marīcaye /
lakṣārdhāddhantu tadbrāhmaṃ likhitvā sampradāpayet //
meaning:
पुष्कर उवाच
ब्रह्मणाभिहितं पूर्वं यावन्मात्रं मरीचये /
लक्षार्धाद्धन्तु तद्ब्राह्मं लिखित्वा सम्प्रदापयेत् //
text_mt:
Puṣkara said:
Whatever was previously spoken by Brahmā to Marīci, / having written down that Brāhma [Purāṇa] of fifty thousand [verses], one should give it away [in gift].

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśākhyāmpaurṇamāsyāñca svargārthī jaladhenumat /
pādmaṃ dvādaśasāhasraṃ dyaiṣṭhe dadyācca dhenumat //
meaning:
वैशाख्याम्पौर्णमास्याञ्च स्वर्गार्थी जलधेनुमत् /
पाद्मं द्वादशसाहस्रं द्यैष्ठे दद्याच्च धेनुमत् //
text_mt: One desirous of heaven [should give it] on the full moon day of Vaiśākha along with a water-cow. / One should give the Pādma [Purāṇa] of twelve thousand [verses] in the month of Jyaiṣṭha along with a cow.

sanskrit_iast:
varāhakalpavṛttāntamadhikṛtya parāśaraḥ /
trayoviṃśatisāhasraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ prāha cārpayet //
meaning:
वराहकल्पवृत्तान्तमधिकृत्य पराशरः /
त्रयोविंशतिसाहस्रं वैष्णवं प्राह चार्पयेत् //
text_mt: Setting forth the events of the Varāha Kalpa, Parāśara / declared the Vaiṣṇava [Purāṇa] of twenty-three thousand [verses]; and one should present it.

sanskrit_iast:
jaladhenumadāṣāḍhyāṃ viṣṇoḥ padamavāpnuyāt /
caturdaśasahasrāṇi vāyavīyaṃ haripriyaṃ //
meaning:
जलधेनुमदाषाढ्यां विष्णोः पदमवाप्नुयात् /
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि वायवीयं हरिप्रियं //
text_mt: [Giving it] with a water-cow on the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, one attains Viṣṇu's realm. / The Vāyavīya [Purāṇa], dear to Hari, consists of fourteen thousand [verses].

sanskrit_iast:
śvetakalpaprasaṅgena dharmān vāyurihābravīt /
dadyāllikhitvā tadvipre śrāvaṇyāṃ guḍadhenumat //
meaning:
श्वेतकल्पप्रसङ्गेन धर्मान् वायुरिहाब्रवीत् /
दद्याल्लिखित्वा तद्विप्रे श्रावण्यां गुडधेनुमत् //
text_mt: In connection with the Śveta Kalpa, Vāyu proclaimed dharmas here. / Having written it down, one should give it to a Brahmin on the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa along with a jaggery-cow.

sanskrit_iast:
yatrādhikṛtya gāyatrīṃ kīrtyate dharmavistaraḥ /
:p 5
vṛtrāsurabadhopetaṃ tadbhāgavatamucyate //
meaning:
यत्राधिकृत्य गायत्रीं कीर्त्यते धर्मविस्तरः /
:प् 5
वृत्रासुरबधोपेतं तद्भागवतमुच्यते //

sanskrit_iast:
sārasvatasta kalpasya proṣṭhapadyāntu taddadet /
aṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi hemasiṃhasamanvitaṃ //
meaning:
सारस्वतस्त कल्पस्य प्रोष्ठपद्यान्तु तद्ददेत् /
अष्टादशसहस्राणि हेमसिंहसमन्वितं //
text_mt: Relating to the Sārasvata Kalpa, one should give it on the full moon day of Proṣṭhapadā; / it contains eighteen thousand [verses], accompanied by a golden lion.

sanskrit_iast:
yatrāha nārado dharmān vṛhatkalpāśritānihaṃ /
pañcaviṃśasahasrāṇi nāradīyaṃ taducyate //
meaning:
यत्राह नारदो धर्मान् वृहत्कल्पाश्रितानिहं /
पञ्चविंशसहस्राणि नारदीयं तदुच्यते //
text_mt: Wherein Nārada proclaimed dharmas based upon the Bṛhat Kalpa, / containing twenty-five thousand [verses], that is called the Nāradīya [Purāṇa].

sanskrit_iast:
sadhenuñcāśvine dadyātsiddhimātyantikīṃ labhet /
yatrādhikṛtya śatrūnāndharmādharmavicāraṇā //
meaning:
सधेनुञ्चाश्विने दद्यात्सिद्धिमात्यन्तिकीं लभेत् /
यत्राधिकृत्य शत्रूनान्धर्माधर्मविचारणा //
text_mt: One should give it in the month of Āśvina with a cow; one obtains ultimate perfection. / Wherein, based on enemies, the deliberation on virtue and vice is held,

sanskrit_iast:
kārttikyāṃ navasāhasraṃ mārkaṇḍeyamathārpayet /
agninā yadvaśiṣṭhāya proktañcāgneyameva tat //
meaning:
कार्त्तिक्यां नवसाहस्रं मार्कण्डेयमथार्पयेत् /
अग्निना यद्वशिष्ठाय प्रोक्तञ्चाग्नेयमेव तत् //
text_mt: One should then present the Mārkaṇḍeya [Purāṇa] of nine thousand [verses] on the full moon day of Kārttika. / And that which was spoken by Agni to Vasiṣṭha is the Āgneya [Purāṇa].

sanskrit_iast:
likhitvā pustakaṃ dadyānmārgaśīrṣyāṃ sa sarvadaḥ /
dvādaśaiva sahasrāṇi sarvavidyāvabodhanaṃ(1) //
meaning:
लिखित्वा पुस्तकं दद्यान्मार्गशीर्ष्यां स सर्वदः /
द्वादशैव सहस्राणि सर्वविद्यावबोधनं(1) //
text_mt: Having written the book, he who gives it on the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa grants everything; / it consists of twelve thousand [verses], imparting all knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśasahasrāṇi bhaviṣyaṃ sūryasambhavaṃ /
bhavastu manave prāha dadyāt pauṣyāṃ guḍādimat //
meaning:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि भविष्यं सूर्यसम्भवं /
भवस्तु मनवे प्राह दद्यात् पौष्यां गुडादिमत् //
text_mt: The Bhaviṣya [Purāṇa], of fourteen thousand [verses], originated from Sūrya, / which Bhava proclaimed to Manu; one should give it on the full moon day of Pauṣa along with jaggery and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
sāvarṇinā nāradāya brahmavaivartamīritaṃ /
rathāntarasya vṛttāntamaṣṭādaśasahasrakaṃ //
meaning:
सावर्णिना नारदाय ब्रह्मवैवर्तमीरितं /
रथान्तरस्य वृत्तान्तमष्टादशसहस्रकं //
text_mt: The Brahmavaivarta [Purāṇa] was declared by Sāvarṇi to Nārada; / it contains the account of the Rathantara [Kalpa] and consists of eighteen thousand [verses].

sanskrit_iast:
māghyāndadyādvarāhasya caritaṃ brahmalokabhāk /
yatragniliṅgamadhyastho dharmānprāha maheśvaraḥ //
meaning:
माघ्यान्दद्याद्वराहस्य चरितं ब्रह्मलोकभाक् /
यत्रग्निलिङ्गमध्यस्थो धर्मान्प्राह महेश्वरः //
text_mt: One should give it on the full moon day of Māgha, [together with] the deeds of Varāha, and one partakes in the world of Brahmā. / Wherein Maheśvara, situated within the fire-liṅga, proclaimed dharmas,

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyakalpe talliṅgamekādaśasahasrakam /
taddatvā śivamāpnoti phālgunyāṃ tiladhenumat //
meaning:
आग्नेयकल्पे तल्लिङ्गमेकादशसहस्रकम् /
तद्दत्वा शिवमाप्नोति फाल्गुन्यां तिलधेनुमत् //
text_mt: In the Āgneya Kalpa, that is the Liṅga [Purāṇa] of eleven thousand [verses]. / Giving that along with a sesame-cow on the full moon day of Phālguna, one attains Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśasahasrāṇi vārāhaṃ viṣṇuṇeritam /
bhūmau varāhacaritaṃ mānavasya pravṛttitaḥ //
meaning:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि वाराहं विष्णुणेरितम् /
भूमौ वराहचरितं मानवस्य प्रवृत्तितः //
text_mt: The Vārāha [Purāṇa] of fourteen thousand [verses] was spoken by Viṣṇu, / [describing] the deeds of the Boar on the earth, arising from Manu.

sanskrit_iast:
sahemagaruḍañcaitryāṃ padamāpnoti vaiṣṇavam /
:n
1 sarvavidyāvadhāraṇamiti ña ..
:p 6
caturaśītisāhasraṃ skāndaṃ skanderitaṃ mahat //
meaning:
सहेमगरुडञ्चैत्र्यां पदमाप्नोति वैष्णवम् /
:न्
1 सर्वविद्यावधारणमिति ञ ..
:प् 6
चतुरशीतिसाहस्रं स्कान्दं स्कन्देरितं महत् //
text_mt:
[Given] on the full moon day of Caitra along with a golden Garuḍa, one attains Viṣṇu's realm.
:n
1. 'sarvavidyāvadhāraṇam' according to manuscript ña..
:p 6
The great Skānda [Purāṇa] declared by Skanda has eighty-four thousand [verses].

sanskrit_iast:
adhikṛtya sadharmāṃś ca kalpe tatpuruṣe 'rpayet /
vāmanaṃ daśasāhasraṃ dhaumakalpe hareḥ kathāṃ //
meaning:
अधिकृत्य सधर्मांश् च कल्पे तत्पुरुषे ऽर्पयेत् /
वामनं दशसाहस्रं धौमकल्पे हरेः कथां //
text_mt: Dealing with righteous duties, in the Tatpuruṣa Kalpa, one should present it. / The Vāmana [Purāṇa] of ten thousand [verses], the story of Hari in the Dhauma Kalpa,

sanskrit_iast:
dadyāt śaradi viṣuve dharmārthādinibodhanam /
kūrmañcāṣṭasahasrañca kūrmoktañca rasātale //
meaning:
दद्यात् शरदि विषुवे धर्मार्थादिनिबोधनम् /
कूर्मञ्चाष्टसहस्रञ्च कूर्मोक्तञ्च रसातले //
text_mt: One should give at the autumn equinox, imparting understanding of dharma, artha, and the rest. / And the Kūrma [Purāṇa] of eight thousand [verses], spoken by the Tortoise in Rasātala

sanskrit_iast:
indradyumnaprasaṅgena dadyāttaddhemakūrmavat /
trayodaśasahasrāṇi mātsyaṃ kalpādito 'bravīt //
meaning:
इन्द्रद्युम्नप्रसङ्गेन दद्यात्तद्धेमकूर्मवत् /
त्रयोदशसहस्राणि मात्स्यं कल्पादितो ऽब्रवीत् //
text_mt: In connection with Indradyumna, one should give with a golden tortoise. / The Mātsya [Purāṇa] contains thirteen thousand [verses], spoken from the beginning of the kalpa.

sanskrit_iast:
matsyo hi manave dadyādviṣuve hemamatsyavat /
gāruḍañcāṣṭasāhasraṃ viṣṇūktantārkṣakalpake //
meaning:
मत्स्यो हि मनवे दद्याद्विषुवे हेममत्स्यवत् /
गारुडञ्चाष्टसाहस्रं विष्णूक्तन्तार्क्षकल्पके //
text_mt: The Fish indeed [spoke it] to Manu; one should give it at the equinox with a golden fish. / The Gāruḍa [Purāṇa] has eight thousand [verses], spoken by Viṣṇu in the Tārkṣya Kalpa,

sanskrit_iast:
viśvāṇḍādgaruḍotpattiṃ taddadyāddhemahaṃsavat /
brahmā brahmāṇḍamāhātmyamadhikṛtyābrabīttu yat //
meaning:
विश्वाण्डाद्गरुडोत्पत्तिं तद्दद्याद्धेमहंसवत् /
ब्रह्मा ब्रह्माण्डमाहात्म्यमधिकृत्याब्रबीत्तु यत् //
text_mt: Treating the origin of Garuḍa from the universal egg; one should give that with a golden swan. / What Brahmā declared taking as its subject the greatness of the Brahmāṇḍa,

sanskrit_iast:
tacca dvādaśasāhasraṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ taddvije 'rpayet /
bhārate parvasamāptau vastragandhasragādibhiḥ //
meaning:
तच्च द्वादशसाहस्रं ब्रह्माण्डं तद्द्विजे ऽर्पयेत् /
भारते पर्वसमाप्तौ वस्त्रगन्धस्रगादिभिः //
text_mt: That is the Brahmāṇḍa [Purāṇa] of twelve thousand [verses]; that one should present to a Brahmin. / At the conclusion of a section of the Mahābhārata, with garments, incense, garlands, and other things,

sanskrit_iast:
vācakaṃ pūjayedādau bhojayet pāyasair dvijān /
gobhūgrāmasuvarṇādi dadyātparvaṇi parvaṇi //
meaning:
वाचकं पूजयेदादौ भोजयेत् पायसैर् द्विजान् /
गोभूग्रामसुवर्णादि दद्यात्पर्वणि पर्वणि //
text_mt: One should first honor the reciter and feed the Brahmins with milk-rice; / one should give cattle, land, villages, gold, and other gifts at each festival section.

sanskrit_iast:
samāpte bhārate vipraṃ saṃhitāpustakānyajet /
śubhe deśe niveśyātha kṣaumavastrādināvṛtān //
meaning:
समाप्ते भारते विप्रं संहितापुस्तकान्यजेत् /
शुभे देशे निवेश्याथ क्षौमवस्त्रादिनावृतान् //
text_mt: When the Bhārata is concluded, one should worship the Brahmin and the manuscript of the Saṃhitā, / having placed them in an auspicious place and covered them with linen cloth and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
naranārayaṇau pūjyau pustakāḥ kusumādibhiḥ /
go 'nnabhūhema dadvātha bhojayitvā kṣamāpayet //
meaning:
नरनारयणौ पूज्यौ पुस्तकाः कुसुमादिभिः /
गो ऽन्नभूहेम दद्वाथ भोजयित्वा क्षमापयेत् //
text_mt: Nara and Nārāyaṇa are to be worshipped, and the manuscripts with flowers and the like. / Having given cattle, food, land, and gold, and having fed him, one should ask his forgiveness.

sanskrit_iast:
mahādānāni deyāni ratnāni vividhāni ca /
māsakau dvau trayaś caiva māse māse pradāpayet //
meaning:
महादानानि देयानि रत्नानि विविधानि च /
मासकौ द्वौ त्रयश् चैव मासे मासे प्रदापयेत् //
text_mt: Great gifts are to be given, as well as various kinds of jewels. / One should have [them] given month after month, for two or three months.

sanskrit_iast:
ayanādau śrābakasya dānamādau vidhīyate /
śrotṛbhiḥ sakalaiḥ kāryaṃ śrāvake pūjanaṃ dvija //
:p 7
meaning:
अयनादौ श्राबकस्य दानमादौ विधीयते /
श्रोतृभिः सकलैः कार्यं श्रावके पूजनं द्विज //
:प् 7
text_mt:
At the solstice and the like, a gift is first ordained for the reciter; / all the listeners must perform the worship of the reciter, O twice-born one.
[Page 7]

sanskrit_iast:
itihāsapurāṇānāṃ pustakāni prayacchati /
pūjayitvāyurārogyaṃ svargamokṣamavāpnuyāt //
ityagneye mahapuraṇe dānādimāhatmyaṃ nāmaika
saptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dvisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sūryavaṃśakīrtanaṃ
meaning:
इतिहासपुराणानां पुस्तकानि प्रयच्छति /
पूजयित्वायुरारोग्यं स्वर्गमोक्षमवाप्नुयात् //
इत्यग्नेये महपुरणे दानादिमाहत्म्यं नामैक
सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्विसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सूर्यवंशकीर्तनं
text_mt:
Whoever presents manuscripts of the histories and the Purāṇas, / having worshipped [them], obtains long life, health, heaven, and liberation.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-first chapter, entitled 'The Glorification of Gifts and the Like,' in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now follows the two hundred and seventy-second chapter.
The Recitation of the Solar Dynasty.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
sūryavaṃśaṃ somavaṃśaṃ rajñāṃ vaṃśaṃ vadami te /
harerbrahmā padmago 'bhūnmarīcirbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
सूर्यवंशं सोमवंशं रज्ञां वंशं वदमि ते /
हरेर्ब्रह्मा पद्मगो ऽभून्मरीचिर्ब्रह्मणः सुतः //
text_mt: Agni said: / I shall tell you of the Solar Dynasty, the Lunar Dynasty, and the dynasty of kings. / From Hari, Brahmā arose seated on a lotus; Marīci was the son of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
marīceḥ kaśyapastasmādvivasvāṃstasya patnyapi /
saṃjñā rājñī(1) prabhā tisro rājñī raivataputrikā //
meaning:
मरीचेः कश्यपस्तस्माद्विवस्वांस्तस्य पत्न्यपि /
संज्ञा राज्ञी(1) प्रभा तिस्रो राज्ञी रैवतपुत्रिका //
text_mt: From Marīci came Kaśyapa; from him Vivasvat. His wives also were / Saṃjñā, Rājñī, and Prabhā—the three; Rājñī was the daughter of Raivata.

sanskrit_iast:
revantaṃ suṣuve putraṃ prabhātañca prabhā raveḥ /
tvāṣṭrī saṃjñā manuṃ putraṃ yamalau yamunāṃ yamam //
meaning:
रेवन्तं सुषुवे पुत्रं प्रभातञ्च प्रभा रवेः /
त्वाष्ट्री संज्ञा मनुं पुत्रं यमलौ यमुनां यमम् //
text_mt: Prabhā bore to the Sun a son Revanta, and Prabhāta; / Saṃjñā, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, bore the son Manu, and the twins Yamunā and Yama.

sanskrit_iast:
chāyā saṃjñā ca sāvarṇiṃ manuṃ vaivasvataṃ sutam /
śaniñca tapatīṃ viṣṭiṃ saṃjñāyāñcāśvinau punaḥ //
meaning:
छाया संज्ञा च सावर्णिं मनुं वैवस्वतं सुतम् /
शनिञ्च तपतीं विष्टिं संज्ञायाञ्चाश्विनौ पुनः //
text_mt: Chāyā-Saṃjñā bore the son Sāvarṇi Manu, [and] Vaivasvata, / and Śani, Tapatī, and Viṣṭi; and on Saṃjñā [he begot] the two Aśvins again.

sanskrit_iast:
manorvaivasvatasyāsan putrā vai na ca tatsamāḥ /
ikṣvākuś caiva nābhāgo dhṛṣṭaḥśaryātireva ca //
meaning:
मनोर्वैवस्वतस्यासन् पुत्रा वै न च तत्समाः /
इक्ष्वाकुश् चैव नाभागो धृष्टःशर्यातिरेव च //
text_mt: The sons of Vaivasvata Manu were indeed peerless: / Ikṣvāku, Nābhāga, Dhṛṣṭa, and Śaryāti,

sanskrit_iast:
nariṣyantas tathā prāṃśurnābhāgādiṣṭasattamāḥ /
karuṣaś ca pṛṣadhraś ca ayodhyāyāṃ mahābalāḥ //
meaning:
नरिष्यन्तस् तथा प्रांशुर्नाभागादिष्टसत्तमाः /
करुषश् च पृषध्रश् च अयोध्यायां महाबलाः //
text_mt: Nariṣyanta, Prāṃśu, the best of men Nābhāgādiṣṭa, / Karuṣa, and Pṛṣadhra, mighty in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit_iast:
kanyelā ca manorāsīdbudhāttasyāṃ purūravāḥ /
purūravasamucpādya selā sudyumnatāṅgatā //
:n
1 atra chāyetipāṭho yuktaḥ
:p 8
meaning:
कन्येला च मनोरासीद्बुधात्तस्यां पुरूरवाः /
पुरूरवसमुच्पाद्य सेला सुद्युम्नताङ्गता //
:न्
1 अत्र छायेतिपाठो युक्तः
:प् 8
text_mt:
And Manu had a daughter, Ilā; from Budha, Purūravas was born of her. / Having produced Purūravas, that Ilā became Sudyumna.
[Note]
1 Here the reading 'Chāyā' is appropriate. / [Page 8]

sanskrit_iast:
sudyumnādutkalagayau vinatāśvastrayo nṛpāḥ /
utkalasyotkalaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vinatāśvasya paścimā //
meaning:
सुद्युम्नादुत्कलगयौ विनताश्वस्त्रयो नृपाः /
उत्कलस्योत्कलं राष्ट्रं विनताश्वस्य पश्चिमा //
text_mt: From Sudyumna came the three kings Utkala, Gaya, and Vinatāśva. / Utkala's kingdom was Utkala; the western region belonged to Vinatāśva,

sanskrit_iast:
dik sarvā rājavaryasya gayasya tu gayāpurī /
vaśiṣṭhavākyāt sudyumnaḥ pratiṣṭhānamavāpa ha //
meaning:
दिक् सर्वा राजवर्यस्य गयस्य तु गयापुरी /
वशिष्ठवाक्यात् सुद्युम्नः प्रतिष्ठानमवाप ह //
text_mt: the entire [direction] to that best of kings, and Gaya's was Gayāpurī. / By the word of Vasiṣṭha, Sudyumna obtained Pratiṣṭhāna.

sanskrit_iast:
tat purūravase prādātsudyumno rājyamāpya tu /
nariṣyataḥ śakāḥ putrā nābhāgasya ca vaiṣṇavaḥ //
meaning:
तत् पुरूरवसे प्रादात्सुद्युम्नो राज्यमाप्य तु /
नरिष्यतः शकाः पुत्रा नाभागस्य च वैष्णवः //
text_mt: Having obtained that kingdom, Sudyumna gave it to Purūravas. / The Śakas were the sons of Nariṣyanta; and of Nābhāga, the Vaiṣṇava

sanskrit_iast:
ambarīṣaḥ prajāpālo dhārṣṭakaṃ dhṛṣṭataḥ kulam /
sukalpānartau śaryārtervairohyānartato nṛpaḥ //
meaning:
अम्बरीषः प्रजापालो धार्ष्टकं धृष्टतः कुलम् /
सुकल्पानर्तौ शर्यार्तेर्वैरोह्यानर्ततो नृपः //
text_mt: Ambarīṣa, the protector of subjects; the Dhārṣṭaka family descended from Dhṛṣṭa. / Sukalpa and Ānarta were [the sons] of Śaryāti; from Vairohya-Ānarta, the king,

sanskrit_iast:
ānartaviṣayaścāsīt purī cāsīt kuśasthalī /
revasya raivataḥ putraḥ kakudmī nāma dhārmikaḥ //
meaning:
आनर्तविषयश्चासीत् पुरी चासीत् कुशस्थली /
रेवस्य रैवतः पुत्रः ककुद्मी नाम धार्मिकः //
text_mt: there was the region of Ānarta, and the city was Kuśasthalī. / The righteous son of Reva was Raivata, named Kakudmin.

sanskrit_iast:
jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasyāsīdrājyaṃ prāpya kuśasthalīm /
sa kanyāsahitaḥ śrutvā gāndharvaṃ brahmaṇo 'ntike //
meaning:
ज्येष्ठः पुत्रशतस्यासीद्राज्यं प्राप्य कुशस्थलीम् /
स कन्यासहितः श्रुत्वा गान्धर्वं ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तिके //
text_mt: He was the eldest of a hundred sons, having obtained the kingdom Kuśasthalī. / Having listened, together with his daughter, to celestial music in the presence of Brahmā,

sanskrit_iast:
muhūrtabhūtaṃ devasya martye bahuyugaṃ gatam /
ājagāma javenātha svāṃ purīṃ yādavair vṛtām //
meaning:
मुहूर्तभूतं देवस्य मर्त्ये बहुयुगं गतम् /
आजगाम जवेनाथ स्वां पुरीं यादवैर् वृताम् //
text_mt: for what seemed a moment of the god, many ages passed in the mortal realm. / Then he quickly came to his city, which was surrounded by the Yādavas,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtāṃ dvāravatīṃ nāma bahudvārāṃ manoramām /
bhojavṛṣṇyandhakair guptāṃ(?) vāsudevapurogamaiḥ //
meaning:
कृतां द्वारवतीं नाम बहुद्वारां मनोरमाम् /
भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकैर् गुप्तां(?) वासुदेवपुरोगमैः //
text_mt: made charming with many gates and named Dvāravatī, / protected by the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, led by Vāsudeva.

sanskrit_iast:
revatīṃ baladevāya dadau jñātvā hy aninditām /
tapaḥ sumeruśikhare taptvā viṣṇvālayaṃ gataḥ //
meaning:
रेवतीं बलदेवाय ददौ ज्ञात्वा ह्य् अनिन्दिताम् /
तपः सुमेरुशिखरे तप्त्वा विष्ण्वालयं गतः //
text_mt: Knowing [this], he gave the faultless Revatī to Baladeva. / Having performed ascetic austerity on the summit of Mount Sumeru, he went to the abode of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
nābhāgasya ca putrau dvau vaiśyau brāhmaṇatāṃ gatau /
karūṣasya tu kārūṣāḥ kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ //
meaning:
नाभागस्य च पुत्रौ द्वौ वैश्यौ ब्राह्मणतां गतौ /
करूषस्य तु कारूषाः क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः //
text_mt: And the two sons of Nābhāga, [though born] Vaiśyas, attained the status of Brahmins. / But the descendants of Karūṣa were the Kārūṣas, Kṣatriyas intoxicatingly fierce in battle.

sanskrit_iast:
śūdratvañca pṛṣadhro 'gāddhiṃsayitvā guroś ca gām /
manuputrādathekṣākorvikukṣirdevarāḍabhūt //
meaning:
शूद्रत्वञ्च पृषध्रो ऽगाद्धिंसयित्वा गुरोश् च गाम् /
मनुपुत्रादथेक्षाकोर्विकुक्षिर्देवराडभूत् //
text_mt: Pṛṣadhra fell to the status of a Śūdra by slaying his guru's cow. / Then from Manu's son Ikṣvāku was born Vikukṣi, king among men.

sanskrit_iast:
vikukṣestu kakutstho 'bhūttasya putraḥ suyodhanaḥ /
:p 9
tasya putraḥ pṛthur nāma viśvagaśvaḥ pṛthoḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
विकुक्षेस्तु ककुत्स्थो ऽभूत्तस्य पुत्रः सुयोधनः /
:प् 9
तस्य पुत्रः पृथुर् नाम विश्वगश्वः पृथोः सुतः //
text_mt:
From Vikukṣi was Kakutstha; his son was Suyodhana.
[Page 9]
His son was named Pṛthu; Viśvagaśva was the son of Pṛthu.

sanskrit_iast:
āyustasya ca putro 'bhūdyuvanāśvas tathā sutaḥ /
yuvanāśvācca śrāvantaḥ pūrve śrāvantikā purī //
meaning:
आयुस्तस्य च पुत्रो ऽभूद्युवनाश्वस् तथा सुतः /
युवनाश्वाच्च श्रावन्तः पूर्वे श्रावन्तिका पुरी //
text_mt: His son was Āyus, and Yuvanāśva was his son; / and from Yuvanāśva came Śrāvanta; formerly, [his city] was the city Śrāvantikā.

sanskrit_iast:
śrāvantād vṛhadaśvo 'bhūt kubalāśvastato nṛpaḥ /
dhundhumāratvamagamaddhundhor nāmnā ca vai purā //
meaning:
श्रावन्ताद् वृहदश्वो ऽभूत् कुबलाश्वस्ततो नृपः /
धुन्धुमारत्वमगमद्धुन्धोर् नाम्ना च वै पुरा //
text_mt: From Śrāvanta was Bṛhadaśva; from him the king was Kuvalāśva. / He attained the title 'Dhundhumāra' ('slayer of Dhundhu') of old on account of Dhundhu.

sanskrit_iast:
dhundhumārāstrayo bhūpā dṛḍhāśvo daṇḍa eva ca /
kapilo 'tha dṛḍhāśvāttu haryaśvaś ca pramodakaḥ //
meaning:
धुन्धुमारास्त्रयो भूपा दृढाश्वो दण्ड एव च /
कपिलो ऽथ दृढाश्वात्तु हर्यश्वश् च प्रमोदकः //
text_mt: The three kings [descended] from Dhundhumāra were Dṛḍhāśva, Daṇḍa, / and Kapila; from Dṛḍhāśva came Haryaśva and Pramodaka.

sanskrit_iast:
haryaśvācca nikumbho 'bhūt saṃhatāśvo nikumbhataḥ /
akṛśāśvo raṇāśvaś ca saṃhatāśvasutāvubhau //
meaning:
हर्यश्वाच्च निकुम्भो ऽभूत् संहताश्वो निकुम्भतः /
अकृशाश्वो रणाश्वश् च संहताश्वसुतावुभौ //
text_mt: From Haryaśva came Nikumbha; from Nikumbha, Saṃhatāśva. / Akṛśāśva and Raṇāśva were both sons of Saṃhatāśva.

sanskrit_iast:
yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya māndhātā yuvanāśvataḥ /
māndhātuḥ purukutso 'bhūnmucukundo dvitīyakaḥ //
meaning:
युवनाश्वो रणाश्वस्य मान्धाता युवनाश्वतः /
मान्धातुः पुरुकुत्सो ऽभून्मुचुकुन्दो द्वितीयकः //
text_mt: Yuvanāśva was [the son] of Raṇāśva; from Yuvanāśva came Māndhātṛ. / From Māndhātṛ came Purukutsa, and Mucukunda was the second.

sanskrit_iast:
purukutsādasasyuś ca sambhūto narmadābhavaḥ /
sambhūtasya sudhanvābhūttridhanvātha sudhanvanaḥ //
meaning:
पुरुकुत्सादसस्युश् च सम्भूतो नर्मदाभवः /
सम्भूतस्य सुधन्वाभूत्त्रिधन्वाथ सुधन्वनः //
text_mt: From Purukutsa, Asasyu was born of Narmadā; / of Sambhūta was Sudhanvan; then Tridhanvan was from Sudhanvan.

sanskrit_iast:
tridhanvanastu taruṇastasya satyavrataḥ sutaḥ /
satyavratātsatyaratho hariś candraś ca tatsutaḥ //
meaning:
त्रिधन्वनस्तु तरुणस्तस्य सत्यव्रतः सुतः /
सत्यव्रतात्सत्यरथो हरिश् चन्द्रश् च तत्सुतः //
text_mt: From Tridhanvan was Taruṇa; his son was Satyavrata. / From Satyavrata was Satyaratha, and Hariścandra was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
hariś candrādrohitāśvo rohitāśvādvṛko 'bhavat /
vṛkādvāhuś ca vāhoś ca sagarastasya ca priyā //
meaning:
हरिश् चन्द्राद्रोहिताश्वो रोहिताश्वाद्वृको ऽभवत् /
वृकाद्वाहुश् च वाहोश् च सगरस्तस्य च प्रिया //
text_mt: From Hariścandra came Rohitāśva; from Rohitāśva was Vṛka. / From Vṛka came Bāhu; and from Bāhu, Sagara. And his beloved wife,

sanskrit_iast:
prabhā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇāṃ sutānāṃ jananī hy abhūt /
tuṣṭādaurvānnṛpādekaṃ bhānumatyasamañjasam //
meaning:
प्रभा षष्टिसहस्राणां सुतानां जननी ह्य् अभूत् /
तुष्टादौर्वान्नृपादेकं भानुमत्यसमञ्जसम् //
text_mt: Prabhā, was the mother of sixty thousand sons. / Through the grace of Aurva, Bhānumatī bore to the king one [son], Asamañjas.

sanskrit_iast:
khanantaḥ pṛthivīṃ dagdhā viṣṇunā(1) bahusāgarāḥ /
asamañjaso 'ṃśrumāṃś ca dilīpo 'ṃśumato 'bhavat //
meaning:
खनन्तः पृथिवीं दग्धा विष्णुना(1) बहुसागराः /
असमञ्जसो ऽंश्रुमांश् च दिलीपो ऽंशुमतो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Digging the earth, the many sons of Sagara were burned by Viṣṇu. / Asamañjas's [son] was Aṃśumat, and Dilīpa was born from Aṃśumat.

sanskrit_iast:
bhagīratho dilīpāttu yena gaṅgāvatāritā /
:n
1 munineti ja..
:p 10
bhagīrathāttu nābhāgo nābhāgādambarīṣakaḥ //
meaning:
भगीरथो दिलीपात्तु येन गङ्गावतारिता /
:न्
1 मुनिनेति ज..
:प् 10
भगीरथात्तु नाभागो नाभागादम्बरीषकः //
text_mt:
From Dilīpa was Bhagīratha, by whom the Gaṅgā was brought down.
[Note]
1 Ja reads 'muninā' ('by the sage'). / [Page 10]
From Bhagīratha came Nābhāga; from Nābhāga, Ambarīṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
sindhudvīpo 'mbarīṣāttu śrutāyustatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śrutāyorṛtaparṇo 'bhūttasya kalmāṣapādakaḥ //
meaning:
सिन्धुद्वीपो ऽम्बरीषात्तु श्रुतायुस्तत्सुतः स्मृतः /
श्रुतायोरृतपर्णो ऽभूत्तस्य कल्माषपादकः //
text_mt: From Ambarīṣa came Sindhudvīpa; Śrutāyus is remembered as his son. / From Śrutāyus came Ṛtuparṇa; his [son] was Kalmāṣapāda.

sanskrit_iast:
kalmāṣāṅghreḥ sarvakarmā(1) hy anaraṇyastato 'bhavat /
anaraṇyāttu nighno 'tha anamitrastato raghuḥ //
meaning:
कल्माषाङ्घ्रेः सर्वकर्मा(1) ह्य् अनरण्यस्ततो ऽभवत् /
अनरण्यात्तु निघ्नो ऽथ अनमित्रस्ततो रघुः //
text_mt: From Kalmāṣāṅghri came Sarvakarman, and from him was Anaraṇya. / From Anaraṇya came Nighna, then Anamitra, and from him Raghu.

sanskrit_iast:
raghorabhuddilīpastu dilīpāccāpyajo nṛpaḥ /
dīrghavāhurajāt kālastvajāpālastato 'bhavat //
meaning:
रघोरभुद्दिलीपस्तु दिलीपाच्चाप्यजो नृपः /
दीर्घवाहुरजात् कालस्त्वजापालस्ततो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: From Raghu was Dilīpa; and from Dilīpa was King Aja. / From Aja came Dīrghabāhu, and from Ajapāla came Kāla.

sanskrit_iast:
tatha daśaratho jātastasya putracatuṣṭayam /
nārāyaṇātmakāḥ sarve rāmastasyāgrajo 'bhavat //
meaning:
तथ दशरथो जातस्तस्य पुत्रचतुष्टयम् /
नारायणात्मकाः सर्वे रामस्तस्याग्रजो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Then Daśaratha was born; his sons were four, / all having the nature of Nārāyaṇa; Rāma was his eldest son,

sanskrit_iast:
rāvaṇāntakaro rājā hy ayodhyāyāṃ raghūttamaḥ /
vālmīkiryasya caritaṃ cakre tannāradaśravāt //
meaning:
रावणान्तकरो राजा ह्य् अयोध्यायां रघूत्तमः /
वाल्मीकिर्यस्य चरितं चक्रे तन्नारदश्रवात् //
text_mt: the king who destroyed Rāvaṇa, the best of the Raghus in Ayodhyā, / whose deeds Vālmīki composed upon hearing [them] from Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
rāmaputrau kuśalavau sītāyāṃ kulavardhanau /
atithiś ca kuśājjajñe niṣadhastasya cātmajaḥ //
meaning:
रामपुत्रौ कुशलवौ सीतायां कुलवर्धनौ /
अतिथिश् च कुशाज्जज्ञे निषधस्तस्य चात्मजः //
text_mt: Rāma's sons on Sītā were Kuśa and Lava, who made their lineage prosper. / Atithi was born from Kuśa, and Niṣadha was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
niṣadhāttu nalo jajñe nabho 'jāyata vai nalāt /
nabhasaḥ puṇḍarīko 'bhūt sudhanvā ca tato 'bhavat //
meaning:
निषधात्तु नलो जज्ञे नभो ऽजायत वै नलात् /
नभसः पुण्डरीको ऽभूत् सुधन्वा च ततो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: From Niṣadha was born Nala; Nabhas was indeed born from Nala. / From Nabhas came Puṇḍarīka, and from him was Sudhanvan.

sanskrit_iast:
sudhanvano devānīko hy ahīnāśvaś ca tatsutaḥ /
ahīnāśvāt sahasrāśvaś candrālokastato 'bhavat //
meaning:
सुधन्वनो देवानीको ह्य् अहीनाश्वश् च तत्सुतः /
अहीनाश्वात् सहस्राश्वश् चन्द्रालोकस्ततो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: From Sudhanvan came Devānīka, and Ahīnāśva was his son. / From Ahīnāśva came Sahasrharśva, and Candrāvaloka was from him.

sanskrit_iast:
candrāvalokatastārāpīḍo 'smāccandraparvataḥ /
candragirerbhānurathaḥ śrutāyustasya cātmajaḥ /
ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavāḥ sūryavaṃśadharāḥ smṛtāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe suryavaṃśakīrtanaṃ nāma
dvisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n

:ś atha trisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
somavaṃśavarṇanaṃ
meaning:
चन्द्रावलोकतस्तारापीडो ऽस्माच्चन्द्रपर्वतः /
चन्द्रगिरेर्भानुरथः श्रुतायुस्तस्य चात्मजः /
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवाः सूर्यवंशधराः स्मृताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सुर्यवंशकीर्तनं नाम
द्विसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः

सोमवंशवर्णनं
text_mt:
From Candrāvaloka came Tārāpīḍa; from him Candraparvata; / from Candragiri was Bhānuratha, and Śrutāyus was his son. / Those born in the lineage of Ikṣvāku are remembered as upholder of the Solar Dynasty.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-second chapter in the Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'The Glorification of the Solar Dynasty'.

Now begins the two hundred and seventy-third chapter.
Description of the Lunar Dynasty

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
somavaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi paṭhitaṃ pāpanāśanam /
viṣṇunābhyabjajo brahmā brahmaputro 'triratritaḥ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
सोमवंशं प्रवक्ष्यामि पठितं पापनाशनम् /
विष्णुनाभ्यब्जजो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मपुत्रो ऽत्रिरत्रितः //
text_mt:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the Lunar Dynasty, which destroys sins when recited: / Brahmā was born from Viṣṇu's navel-lotus; Brahmā's son was Atri; from Atri [arose] Soma.

sanskrit_iast:
somaś cakre rājasūyaṃ trailokyaṃ dakṣiṇāndadau /
samāpte 'vabhṛthe somaṃ tadrūpālokanecchavaḥ //
meaning:
सोमश् चक्रे राजसूयं त्रैलोक्यं दक्षिणान्ददौ /
समाप्ते ऽवभृथे सोमं तद्रूपालोकनेच्छवः //
text_mt: Soma performed the rājasūya sacrifice and gave the three worlds as the sacrificial fee. / When the concluding ablution was completed, desirous of beholding his form,

sanskrit_iast:
kāmavāṇābhitaptāṅgyo naradevyaḥ siṣevire /
lakṣmīr narāyaṇaṃ tyaktvā sinīvālī ca kardamama //
meaning:
कामवाणाभितप्ताङ्ग्यो नरदेव्यः सिषेविरे /
लक्ष्मीर् नरायणं त्यक्त्वा सिनीवाली च कर्दमम //
text_mt: Their limbs tormented by the arrows of love, divine wives attended upon Soma: / Lakṣmī abandoning Nārāyaṇa, and Sinīvālī [abandoning] Kardama,

sanskrit_iast:
dyutiṃ vibhāvasuntyaktvā puṣṭirdhātāramavyayam /
prabhā prabhākarantyaktvā haviṣmantaṃ kuhūḥ svayam //
meaning:
द्युतिं विभावसुन्त्यक्त्वा पुष्टिर्धातारमव्ययम् /
प्रभा प्रभाकरन्त्यक्त्वा हविष्मन्तं कुहूः स्वयम् //
text_mt: Dyuti abandoning Vibhāvasu, Puṣṭi [abandoning] the imperishable Dhātṛ, / Prabhā abandoning Prabhākara, Kuhū herself [abandoning] Haviṣmat,

sanskrit_iast:
kīrtirjayantambhartāraṃ vasurmārīcakaśyayam /
dhṛtistyaktvā patiṃ nandīṃ somamevābhajattadā //
meaning:
कीर्तिर्जयन्तम्भर्तारं वसुर्मारीचकश्ययम् /
धृतिस्त्यक्त्वा पतिं नन्दीं सोममेवाभजत्तदा //
text_mt: Kīrti [abandoning] her husband Jayanta, Vasu [abandoning] Kaśyapa son of Marīci, / Dhṛti abandoning her husband Nandī—they all resorted to Soma at that time.

sanskrit_iast:
svakīyā iva somo 'pi kāmayāmāsa tāstadā /
evaṃ kṛtāpacārasya tāsāṃ bhartṛgaṇastadā //
meaning:
स्वकीया इव सोमो ऽपि कामयामास तास्तदा /
एवं कृतापचारस्य तासां भर्तृगणस्तदा //
text_mt: Soma too desired them then, as though they were his own wives. / Though he had thus committed transgression, the assembly of their husbands then

sanskrit_iast:
na śaśākāpacārāya(1) śāpaiḥ śastrādibhiḥ punaḥ /
saptalokaikanāthatvamavāptastapasā hy uta //
meaning:
न शशाकापचाराय(1) शापैः शस्त्रादिभिः पुनः /
सप्तलोकैकनाथत्वमवाप्तस्तपसा ह्य् उत //
text_mt: Were unable to harm him by curses, weapons, or other means, / for he had attained singular lordship over the seven worlds by his ascetic austerity.

sanskrit_iast:
vivabhrāma matistasya vinayādanayā hatā /
vṛhaspateḥ sa vai bhāryāṃ tārāṃ nāma yaśasvinīm //
meaning:
विवभ्राम मतिस्तस्य विनयादनया हता /
वृहस्पतेः स वै भार्यां तारां नाम यशस्विनीम् //
text_mt: His intellect wandered astray, ruined by misconduct away from propriety. / The illustrious wife of Bṛhaspati, named Tārā,

sanskrit_iast:
jahāra tarasā somo hy avamanyāṅgiraḥsutam /
tatastadyuddhamabhavat prakhyātaṃ tārakāmayam //
:n
1 na śaśākāpakārāyeti ña..
:p 12
meaning:
जहार तरसा सोमो ह्य् अवमन्याङ्गिरःसुतम् /
ततस्तद्युद्धमभवत् प्रख्यातं तारकामयम् //
:न्
1 न शशाकापकारायेति ञ..
:प् 12
text_mt:
Soma forcibly abducted, slighting the son of Aṅgiras. / Then there arose that great war, renowned as Tārakāmaya,
:n
1. 'na śaśākāpakārāya' according to manuscript ña..
:p 12

sanskrit_iast:
devānāṃ dānavānāñca lokakṣayakaraṃ mahat /
brahmā nivāryośanasantārāmaṅgirase dadau //
meaning:
देवानां दानवानाञ्च लोकक्षयकरं महत् /
ब्रह्मा निवार्योशनसन्तारामङ्गिरसे ददौ //
text_mt: Between the gods and demons, causing the great destruction of worlds. / Brahmā, having restrained Uśanas, gave Tārā back to the son of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit_iast:
tāmantaḥprasavāṃ dṛṣṭvā garbhaṃ tyajābravīdguruḥ /
garbhastyaktaḥ pradīpto 'tha prāhāhaṃ somasanbhavaḥ //
meaning:
तामन्तःप्रसवां दृष्ट्वा गर्भं त्यजाब्रवीद्गुरुः /
गर्भस्त्यक्तः प्रदीप्तो ऽथ प्राहाहं सोमसन्भवः //
text_mt: Seeing her pregnant, Guru said: 'Cast out the child!' / Cast out, the radiant fetus then said: 'I am Soma's son.'

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ somādbudhaḥ puttraḥ puttrastasya purūravāḥ /
svargantyaktvorvaśī sā taṃ varayāmāsa cāpsarāḥ //
meaning:
एवं सोमाद्बुधः पुत्त्रः पुत्त्रस्तस्य पुरूरवाः /
स्वर्गन्त्यक्त्वोर्वशी सा तं वरयामास चाप्सराः //
text_mt: Thus Budha was born as a son to Soma; his son was Purūravas. / Abandoning heaven, that apsaras Urvaśī chose him [as husband].

sanskrit_iast:
tayā sahācaradrājā daśavarṣāṇi pañca ca /
pañca ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau ca daśa cāṣṭau mahāmune //
meaning:
तया सहाचरद्राजा दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च /
पञ्च षट् सप्त चाष्टौ च दश चाष्टौ महामुने //
text_mt: With her the king lived for ten years and five, / and five, six, seven, and eight, and ten and eight, O great sage.

sanskrit_iast:
eko 'gnirabhavat pūrvaṃ tena tretā pravartitā /
purūravā yogaśīlo gāndharvalokamīyivān //
meaning:
एको ऽग्निरभवत् पूर्वं तेन त्रेता प्रवर्तिता /
पुरूरवा योगशीलो गान्धर्वलोकमीयिवान् //
text_mt: Formerly there was one fire; by him the threefold sacrificial fire was instituted. / Devoted to yoga, Purūravas went to the world of the Gandharvas.

sanskrit_iast:
āyurdṛ.ḍhāyuraśvāyurdhanāyurdhṛtimān vasuḥ /
divijātaḥ śatāyuś ca suṣuve corvaśī nṛpān //
meaning:
आयुर्दृ.ढायुरश्वायुर्धनायुर्धृतिमान् वसुः /
दिविजातः शतायुश् च सुषुवे चोर्वशी नृपान् //
text_mt: Āyus, Dṛḍhāyus, Aśvāyus, Dhanāyus, Dhṛtimat, Vasu, / Divijāta, and Śatāyus—Urvaśī gave birth to these kings.

sanskrit_iast:
āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ putro vṛddhaśarmā rajis tathā /
darbho vipāpmā pañcāgnyaṃ(1) rajeḥ putraśataṃ hy abhūt //
meaning:
आयुषो नहुषः पुत्रो वृद्धशर्मा रजिस् तथा /
दर्भो विपाप्मा पञ्चाग्न्यं(1) रजेः पुत्रशतं ह्य् अभूत् //
text_mt: The sons of Āyus were Nahuṣa, Vṛddhaśarman, as well as Raji, / Darbha, and Vipāpman—five like the sacred fires. Raji indeed had a hundred sons,

sanskrit_iast:
rājeyā iti vikhyātā viṣṇudattavaro rajiḥ /
devāsure raṇe daityānabadhītsurayācitaḥ //
meaning:
राजेया इति विख्याता विष्णुदत्तवरो रजिः /
देवासुरे रणे दैत्यानबधीत्सुरयाचितः //
text_mt: Known as the Rājeyas. Raji received a boon from Viṣṇu; / solicited by the gods, he slew the Daityas in the war between gods and demons.

sanskrit_iast:
gatāyendrāya putratvaṃ datvā rājyaṃ divaṅgataḥ /
rajeḥ putrair hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śakrasyātha sudurmanāḥ //
meaning:
गतायेन्द्राय पुत्रत्वं दत्वा राज्यं दिवङ्गतः /
रजेः पुत्रैर् हृतं राज्यं शक्रस्याथ सुदुर्मनाः //
text_mt: Having granted sonship to Indra when his life was spent, he went to heaven. / Then Indra's kingdom was seized by the sons of Raji, and Śakra was deeply dejected.

sanskrit_iast:
grahaśāntyādividhinā gururindrāya taddadau /
mohayitvā rajisutānāsaṃste nijadharmagāḥ //
meaning:
ग्रहशान्त्यादिविधिना गुरुरिन्द्राय तद्ददौ /
मोहयित्वा रजिसुतानासंस्ते निजधर्मगाः //
text_mt: Guru restored it to Indra through rites such as the pacification of planets; / having deluded the sons of Raji, they fell away from their own proper duty.

sanskrit_iast:
nahuṣasya sutāḥ sapta yatiryayātiruttamaḥ /
udbhavaḥ pañcakaś caiva śaryātimeghapālakau //
:n
1 pañcāgnyā iti ja.. / pañcāgnyamiti ña..
:p 13
meaning:
नहुषस्य सुताः सप्त यतिर्ययातिरुत्तमः /
उद्भवः पञ्चकश् चैव शर्यातिमेघपालकौ //
:न्
1 पञ्चाग्न्या इति ज.. / पञ्चाग्न्यमिति ञ..
:प् 13
text_mt:
Nahuṣa had seven sons: Yati, the excellent Yayāti, / Udbhava, Pañcaka, and Śaryāti and Meghapālaka.
[Footnote]
1 'pañcāgnyaḥ' in ja.. / 'pañcāgnyam' in ña..
[Page 13]

sanskrit_iast:
yatiḥ kumārabhāve 'pi viṣṇuṃ dhyātvā hariṃ gataḥ /
devayānī śakrakanyā yayāteḥ patny abhūt tadā //
meaning:
यतिः कुमारभावे ऽपि विष्णुं ध्यात्वा हरिं गतः /
देवयानी शक्रकन्या ययातेः पत्न्य् अभूत् तदा //
text_mt: Yati, even in boyhood, meditating on Viṣṇu, attained Hari. / Devayānī, daughter of Śakra, then became the wife of Yayāti.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣaparvajā śarmiṣṭhā yayāteḥ pañca tatsutāḥ /
yaduñca turvasuñcaiva devayānī vyajāyata //
meaning:
वृषपर्वजा शर्मिष्ठा ययातेः पञ्च तत्सुताः /
यदुञ्च तुर्वसुञ्चैव देवयानी व्यजायत //
text_mt: Śarmiṣṭhā was the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan. Yayāti had five sons from them: / Devayānī gave birth to Yadu and Turvasu,

sanskrit_iast:
druhyañcānūñca pūruñca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī /
yaduḥ pūruścābhavatānteṣāṃ vaṃśavivardhanau //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe somavaṃśavarṇanaṃ nama
trisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
atha catuḥsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yaduvaṃśavarṇanaṃ
meaning:
द्रुह्यञ्चानूञ्च पूरुञ्च शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी /
यदुः पूरुश्चाभवतान्तेषां वंशविवर्धनौ //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सोमवंशवर्णनं नम
त्रिसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अथ चतुःसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
यदुवंशवर्णनं
text_mt:
And Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, [gave birth to] Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru. / Yadu and Pūru became the increasers of their lineages.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Lunar Dynasty', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-fourth chapter:
Description of the Yadu Dynasty

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
yadorāsanpañca putrā jyeṣṭhasteṣu sahasrajit /
nīlāñjako radhuḥ kroṣṭuḥ śatajicca sahasrajit //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
यदोरासन्पञ्च पुत्रा ज्येष्ठस्तेषु सहस्रजित् /
नीलाञ्जको रधुः क्रोष्टुः शतजिच्च सहस्रजित् //
text_mt: Agni said: / Yadu had five sons, the eldest among them was Sahasrajit: / Nīlāñjaka, Raghu, Kroṣṭu, Śatajit, and Sahasrajit.

sanskrit_iast:
śatajiddhaihayo reṇuhayo haya iti trayaḥ /
dharmanetro haihayasya dharmanetrasya saṃhanaḥ //
meaning:
शतजिद्धैहयो रेणुहयो हय इति त्रयः /
धर्मनेत्रो हैहयस्य धर्मनेत्रस्य संहनः //
text_mt: [From] Śatajit [were born] three: Haihaya, Reṇuhaya, and Haya. / Haihaya's [son was] Dharmanetra; Dharmanetra's [son was] Saṃhana.

sanskrit_iast:
mahimā saṃhanasyāsīnmahimnao bhadrasenakaḥ /
bhadrasenād durgamo 'bhūddurgamātkanako 'bhavat //
meaning:
महिमा संहनस्यासीन्महिम्नओ भद्रसेनकः /
भद्रसेनाद् दुर्गमो ऽभूद्दुर्गमात्कनको ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Mahiman was [the son] of Saṃhana; from Mahiman came Bhadrasenaka; / from Bhadrasena came Durgama; from Durgama was Kanaka.

sanskrit_iast:
kanakāt kṛtavīryastu kṛtāgniḥ karavīrakaḥ /
kṛtaujāś ca caturtho 'bhūt kṛtavīryāttu so 'rjunaḥ //
meaning:
कनकात् कृतवीर्यस्तु कृताग्निः करवीरकः /
कृतौजाश् च चतुर्थो ऽभूत् कृतवीर्यात्तु सो ऽर्जुनः //
text_mt: From Kanaka came Kṛtavīrya, Kṛtāgni, Karavīraka, / and Kṛtaujas was the fourth; and from Kṛtavīrya came that Arjuna.

sanskrit_iast:
datto 'rjunāya tapate saptadvīpamahīśatām /
dadau bāhusahasrañca ajeyatvaṃ raṇe 'riṇā //
:p 14
meaning:
दत्तो ऽर्जुनाय तपते सप्तद्वीपमहीशताम् /
ददौ बाहुसहस्रञ्च अजेयत्वं रणे ऽरिणा //
:प् 14
text_mt:
Datta gave to Arjuna, as he practiced ascetic austerity, lordship over the earth of seven continents, / and gave him a thousand arms and unconquerability in battle by foes,
[Page 14]

sanskrit_iast:
adharme vartamānasya viṣṇuhastānmṛtirdhruvā /
daśa yajñasahasrāṇi so 'rjunaḥ kṛtavānnṛpāḥ //
meaning:
अधर्मे वर्तमानस्य विष्णुहस्तान्मृतिर्ध्रुवा /
दश यज्ञसहस्राणि सो ऽर्जुनः कृतवान्नृपाः //
text_mt: And certain death from the hand of Viṣṇu should he turn to unrighteousness. / That Arjuna performed ten thousand sacrifices, O kings.

sanskrit_iast:
anaṣṭadravyatā rāṣṭre tasya saṃsmaraṇādabhūt /
na nūnaṃ kārttavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti vai nṛpaḥ //
meaning:
अनष्टद्रव्यता राष्ट्रे तस्य संस्मरणादभूत् /
न नूनं कार्त्तवीर्यस्य गतिं यास्यन्ति वै नृपः //
text_mt: By mere remembrance of him, no property was lost in his realm. / Truly, no kings will attain the rank of Kārttavīrya,

sanskrit_iast:
yajñair dānaistapobhiś ca vikrameṇa śrutena ca /
kartavīryasya ca śataṃ putrāṇāṃ pañca vai parāḥ //
meaning:
यज्ञैर् दानैस्तपोभिश् च विक्रमेण श्रुतेन च /
कर्तवीर्यस्य च शतं पुत्राणां पञ्च वै पराः //
text_mt: In sacrifices, gifts, ascetic austerities, valor, and sacred learning. / Kārtavīrya had a hundred sons, among whom five were pre-eminent:

sanskrit_iast:
sūrasenaś ca sūraś ca dhṛṣṭoktaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca /
jayadhvajaś ca nāmāsīdāvantyo nṛpatirmahān //
meaning:
सूरसेनश् च सूरश् च धृष्टोक्तः कृष्ण एव च /
जयध्वजश् च नामासीदावन्त्यो नृपतिर्महान् //
text_mt: Śūrasena, Śūra, the one called Dhṛṣṭa, and Kṛṣṇa, / and Jayadhvaja by name, who was the great king of Avanti.

sanskrit_iast:
jayadhvajāttālajaṅghastālajaṅghāttataḥ sutāḥ /
haihayānāṃ kulāḥ pañca bhojāścāvantayas tathā //
meaning:
जयध्वजात्तालजङ्घस्तालजङ्घात्ततः सुताः /
हैहयानां कुलाः पञ्च भोजाश्चावन्तयस् तथा //
text_mt: From Jayadhvaja came Tālajaṅgha; from Tālajaṅgha were born sons: / the five clans of the Haihayas, the Bhojas, and likewise the Āvantyas,

sanskrit_iast:
vītihotrāḥ svayaṃ jātāḥ śauṇḍikeyāstathaiva ca /
vītihotrādananto 'bhudanantāddurjayo nṛpaḥ //
meaning:
वीतिहोत्राः स्वयं जाताः शौण्डिकेयास्तथैव च /
वीतिहोत्रादनन्तो ऽभुदनन्ताद्दुर्जयो नृपः //
text_mt: The Vītihotras born of himself, and likewise the Śauṇḍikeyas. / From Vītihotra came Ananta; from Ananta came King Durjaya.

sanskrit_iast:
kroṣṭorvaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi yatra jāto hariḥ svayam /
kroṣṭostu vṛjinīvāṃś ca svāhābhūdvṛjinīvataḥ //
meaning:
क्रोष्टोर्वंशं प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्र जातो हरिः स्वयम् /
क्रोष्टोस्तु वृजिनीवांश् च स्वाहाभूद्वृजिनीवतः //
text_mt: I shall declare the lineage of Kroṣṭu, in which Hari himself was born: / From Kroṣṭu came Vṛjinīvat; Svāhā was born from Vṛjinīvat.

sanskrit_iast:
svāhāputrao ruṣadguś ca(1) tasya citrarathaḥ sutaḥ /
śaśavinduścitrarathāccakravartī harau rataḥ //
meaning:
स्वाहापुत्रओ रुषद्गुश् च(1) तस्य चित्ररथः सुतः /
शशविन्दुश्चित्ररथाच्चक्रवर्ती हरौ रतः //
text_mt: Svāhā's son was Ruṣadgu; his son was Citraratha. / From Citraratha came Śaśabindu, a universal emperor devoted to Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
śaśavindoś ca puttrāṇāṃ śatānāmabhavacchatam /
dhīmatāṃ cārurūpāṇāṃ bhūridraviṇatejasām //
meaning:
शशविन्दोश् च पुत्त्राणां शतानामभवच्छतम् /
धीमतां चारुरूपाणां भूरिद्रविणतेजसाम् //
text_mt: Śaśabindu had a hundred hundred sons, / wise, of handsome form, possessing abundant wealth and splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthuśravāḥ pradhāno 'bhūttasya putraḥ suyajñakaḥ /
suyajñasyośanāḥ putrastitikṣuruśanaḥsutaḥ //
meaning:
पृथुश्रवाः प्रधानो ऽभूत्तस्य पुत्रः सुयज्ञकः /
सुयज्ञस्योशनाः पुत्रस्तितिक्षुरुशनःसुतः //
text_mt: Pṛthuśravas was foremost among them; his son was Suyajñaka. / Suyajña's son was Uśanas; Titikṣu was the son of Uśanas.

sanskrit_iast:
titikṣostu marutto 'bhūttasmātkambalavarhiṣaḥ /
pañcāśadrukmakavacādrukmeṣuḥ pṛthurukmakaḥ //
:n
1 viṣāṃśuśceti ja..
:p 15
meaning:
तितिक्षोस्तु मरुत्तो ऽभूत्तस्मात्कम्बलवर्हिषः /
पञ्चाशद्रुक्मकवचाद्रुक्मेषुः पृथुरुक्मकः //
:न्
1 विषांशुश्चेति ज..
:प् 15
text_mt:
From Titikṣu came Marutta; from him Kambalabarhis. / From Rukmakavaca came fifty [sons, including] Rukmeṣu and Pṛthurukmaka,
[Footnote]
1 'viṣāṃśuś ca' in ja..
[Page 15]

sanskrit_iast:
havirjyāmaghaḥ pāpaghno jyāmaghaḥ strījito 'bhavat /
sevyāyāṃ jyāmaghādāsīdvidarbhastasya kauśikaḥ //
meaning:
हविर्ज्यामघः पापघ्नो ज्यामघः स्त्रीजितो ऽभवत् /
सेव्यायां ज्यामघादासीद्विदर्भस्तस्य कौशिकः //
text_mt: Havis, and the destroyer of sins Jyāmagha; Jyāmagha was subjugated by his wife. / From Jyāmagha on Sevyā was Vidarbha; his [son was] Kauśika.

sanskrit_iast:
lomapādaḥ krathaḥ śreṣṭhāt kṛtiḥ(1) syāllomapadataḥ /
kauśikasya cidiḥ putrastasmāccaidyā nṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
लोमपादः क्रथः श्रेष्ठात् कृतिः(1) स्याल्लोमपदतः /
कौशिकस्य चिदिः पुत्रस्तस्माच्चैद्या नृपाः स्मृताः //
text_mt: From the best Lomapāda came Kratha; Kṛti came from Lomapāda. / Kauśika's son was Cidi; from him the Caidya kings are remembered.

sanskrit_iast:
krathādvidarbhaputrāś ca kuntiḥ kuntestu dhṛṣṭakaḥ /
dhṛṣṭasya nidhṛtistasya udarkākhyo vidūrathaḥ //
meaning:
क्रथाद्विदर्भपुत्राश् च कुन्तिः कुन्तेस्तु धृष्टकः /
धृष्टस्य निधृतिस्तस्य उदर्काख्यो विदूरथः //
text_mt: From Kratha, son of Vidarbha, came sons: Kunti; from Kunti came Dhṛṣṭaka; / from Dhṛṣṭa came Nidhṛti; his son was Vidūratha, known as Udarka.

sanskrit_iast:
daśārhaputro vyomastu vyomājjīmūta ucyate /
jīmūtaputro vikalastasya bhīmarathaḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
दशार्हपुत्रो व्योमस्तु व्योमाज्जीमूत उच्यते /
जीमूतपुत्रो विकलस्तस्य भीमरथः सुतः //
text_mt: The son of Daśārha was Vyoman; from Vyoman, Jīmūta is spoken of. / Jīmūta's son was Vikala; his son was Bhīmaratha.

sanskrit_iast:
bhīmarathānnavarathastato dṛḍharatho 'bhavat /
śakuntiś ca dṛḍharathāt śakunteś ca karambhakaḥ //
meaning:
भीमरथान्नवरथस्ततो दृढरथो ऽभवत् /
शकुन्तिश् च दृढरथात् शकुन्तेश् च करम्भकः //
text_mt: From Bhīmaratha came Navaratha; from him came Dṛḍharatha. / Śakunti was from Dṛḍharatha, and Karambhaka was from Śakunti.

sanskrit_iast:
karambhāddevalāto 'bhūt(2) devakṣetraś ca tatsutaḥ /
devakṣetrānmadhurnāma madhordravaraso 'bhavat //
meaning:
करम्भाद्देवलातो ऽभूत्(2) देवक्षेत्रश् च तत्सुतः /
देवक्षेत्रान्मधुर्नाम मधोर्द्रवरसो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: From Karambha came Devalāta, and Devakṣetra was his son. / From Devakṣetra came one named Madhu; from Madhu came Dravarasa.

sanskrit_iast:
dravarasāt puruhūto 'bhūjjanturāsīttu tatsutaḥ /
guṇī tu yādavo rājā jantuputrastu sāttvataḥ //
meaning:
द्रवरसात् पुरुहूतो ऽभूज्जन्तुरासीत्तु तत्सुतः /
गुणी तु यादवो राजा जन्तुपुत्रस्तु सात्त्वतः //
text_mt: From Dravarasa came Puruhūta; his son was Jantu. / The virtuous Yādava king, the son of Jantu, was Sāttvata.

sanskrit_iast:
sāttvatādbhajamānastu vṛṣṇirandhaka eva ca /
devāvṛdhaś ca catvārasteṣāṃ vaṃśāstu viśrutāḥ(3) //
meaning:
सात्त्वताद्भजमानस्तु वृष्णिरन्धक एव च /
देवावृधश् च चत्वारस्तेषां वंशास्तु विश्रुताः(3) //
text_mt: From Sāttvata came Bhajamāna, Vṛṣṇi, Andhaka, / and Devāvṛdha—four whose lineages are renowned.

sanskrit_iast:
bhajamānasya vāhyo 'bhūdvṛṣṭiḥ kṛmirnimis tathā /
devāvṛdhādvabhrurāsīttasya śloko 'tra gīyate //
meaning:
भजमानस्य वाह्यो ऽभूद्वृष्टिः कृमिर्निमिस् तथा /
देवावृधाद्वभ्रुरासीत्तस्य श्लोको ऽत्र गीयते //
text_mt: Of Bhajamāna were Bāhya, Vṛṣṭi, Kṛmi, and Nimi. / From Devāvṛdha came Babhru; about him this verse is sung:

sanskrit_iast:
yathaiva śṛṇumo dūrāt guṇāṃstadvatsamantikāt /
vabhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṃ devair devāvṛdhaḥsamaḥ //
meaning:
यथैव शृणुमो दूरात् गुणांस्तद्वत्समन्तिकात् /
वभ्रुः श्रेष्ठो मनुष्याणां देवैर् देवावृधःसमः //
text_mt: 'Just as we hear of his virtues from afar, so are they found close at hand: / Babhru is foremost among men; Devāvṛdha is equal to the gods.'

sanskrit_iast:
catvāraś ca sutā vabhrorvāsudevaparā nṛpāḥ /
:n
1 dhṛtiriti ña..
2 devarāto 'bhuditi kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. , ca
3 vistṛtā iti ka.. , cha.. , ca
:p 16
kuhuro bhajamānastu(1) śiniḥ kambalavarhiṣaḥ //
meaning:
चत्वारश् च सुता वभ्रोर्वासुदेवपरा नृपाः /
:न्
1 धृतिरिति ञ..
2 देवरातो ऽभुदिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. , च
3 विस्तृता इति क.. , छ.. , च
:प् 16
कुहुरो भजमानस्तु(1) शिनिः कम्बलवर्हिषः //
text_mt:
And the four sons of Babhru were kings devoted to Vāsudeva.
[Footnote]
1 'dhṛtiḥ' in ña..
2 'devarāto 'bhūt' in kha.., ga.., gha.., ja.., ña.., ṭa.., and
3 'vistṛtāḥ' in ka.., cha.., and
[Page 16]
Kuhura, Bhajamāna, Śini, and Kambalabarhis.

sanskrit_iast:
kuhurasya(2) suto dhṛṣṇudhṛṣṇostu tanayo dhṛtiḥ /
dhṛteḥ kapotaromābhūttasya putrastu tittiriḥ //
meaning:
कुहुरस्य(2) सुतो धृष्णुधृष्णोस्तु तनयो धृतिः /
धृतेः कपोतरोमाभूत्तस्य पुत्रस्तु तित्तिरिः //
text_mt: The son of Kuhura was Dhṛṣṇu; Dhṛṣṇu's son was Dhṛti. / From Dhṛti came Kapotaroman; his son was Tittiri.

sanskrit_iast:
tittirestu naraḥ putrastasya candanadundubhiḥ /
punarvasustasya putra āhukaścāhukīsutaḥ //
meaning:
तित्तिरेस्तु नरः पुत्रस्तस्य चन्दनदुन्दुभिः /
पुनर्वसुस्तस्य पुत्र आहुकश्चाहुकीसुतः //
text_mt: The son of Tittiri was Nara; his [son was] Candanadundubhi. / His son was Punarvasu; Āhuka and the daughter Āhukī [were his children].

sanskrit_iast:
āhukāddevako jajñe ugrasenastato 'bhavat /
devavānupadevaś ca devakasya sutāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
आहुकाद्देवको जज्ञे उग्रसेनस्ततो ऽभवत् /
देववानुपदेवश् च देवकस्य सुताः स्मृताः //
text_mt: From Āhuka was born Devaka; then Ugrasena came into being. / Devavat and Upadeva are known as the sons of Devaka.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptāsan vasudevāya tā dadau /
devakī śrutadevī ca mitradevī yathodharā //
meaning:
तेषां स्वसारः सप्तासन् वसुदेवाय ता ददौ /
देवकी श्रुतदेवी च मित्रदेवी यथोधरा //
text_mt: They had seven sisters; he gave them to Vasudeva: / Devakī, Śrutadevī, Mitradevī, Yathodharā,

sanskrit_iast:
śrīdevī satyadevī ca surāpī ceti saptamī /
navograsenasya sutāḥ kaṃsasteṣāñca pūrvajaḥ //
meaning:
श्रीदेवी सत्यदेवी च सुरापी चेति सप्तमी /
नवोग्रसेनस्य सुताः कंसस्तेषाञ्च पूर्वजः //
text_mt: Śrīdevī, Satyadevī, and Surāpī as the seventh. / Ugrasena had nine sons, Kaṃsa being the eldest among them,

sanskrit_iast:
nyagrodhaś ca sunāmā ca kaṅkaḥ śaṅkuś ca bhūmipaḥ /
sutanūrāṣṭrapālaś ca yuddhamuṣṭiḥ sumuṣṭikaḥ //
meaning:
न्यग्रोधश् च सुनामा च कङ्कः शङ्कुश् च भूमिपः /
सुतनूराष्ट्रपालश् च युद्धमुष्टिः सुमुष्टिकः //
text_mt: As well as Nyagrodha, Sunāman, Kaṅka, and King Śaṅku, / Sutanu, Rāṣṭrapāla, Yuddhamuṣṭi, and Sumuṣṭika.

sanskrit_iast:
bhajamānasya putro 'tha rathamukhyo vidūrathaḥ /
rājādhidevaḥ śūraś ca vidūrathasuto 'bhavat //
meaning:
भजमानस्य पुत्रो ऽथ रथमुख्यो विदूरथः /
राजाधिदेवः शूरश् च विदूरथसुतो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Then the son of Bhajamāna was Vidūratha, foremost of charioteers. / Rājādhideva and Śūra were the sons of Vidūratha.

sanskrit_iast:
rājādhidevaputrau dvau śoṇāś caḥ śvetavāhanaḥ /
śoṇāśvasya sutāḥ pañca śamī śatrujidādayaḥ(3) //
meaning:
राजाधिदेवपुत्रौ द्वौ शोणाश् चः श्वेतवाहनः /
शोणाश्वस्य सुताः पञ्च शमी शत्रुजिदादयः(3) //
text_mt: The two sons of Rājādhideva were Śoṇāśva and Śvetavāhana. / Śoṇāśva had five sons: Śamī, Śatrujit, and the rest.

sanskrit_iast:
śamīputraḥ pratikṣetraḥ pratikṣetrasya bhojakaḥ /
bhojasya hṛdikaḥ putro hy adikasya daśātmajāḥ //
meaning:
शमीपुत्रः प्रतिक्षेत्रः प्रतिक्षेत्रस्य भोजकः /
भोजस्य हृदिकः पुत्रो ह्य् अदिकस्य दशात्मजाः //
text_mt: Śamī's son was Pratikṣetra; of Pratikṣetra, Bhojaka. / The son of Bhoja was Hṛdika; and Hṛdika had ten sons:

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtavarmā śatadhanvā devārho bhīṣaṇādayaḥ /
:n
1 kukuro bhajamānastviti ka.. / sundaro bhajamānastviti ja..
2 kukurasyeti ka..
3 śakrajidādaya iti kha..
:p 17
devārhāt kambalavarhirasamaujāstato 'bhavat //
meaning:
कृतवर्मा शतधन्वा देवार्हो भीषणादयः /
:न्
1 कुकुरो भजमानस्त्विति क.. / सुन्दरो भजमानस्त्विति ज..
2 कुकुरस्येति क..
3 शक्रजिदादय इति ख..
:प् 17
देवार्हात् कम्बलवर्हिरसमौजास्ततो ऽभवत् //
text_mt:
Kṛtavarman, Śatadhanvan, Devārha, Bhīṣaṇa, and the rest.
[Footnote]
1 'kukuro bhajamānastu' in ka.. / 'sundaro bhajamānastu' in ja..
2 'kukurasya' in ka..
3 'Śakrajit and others' in manuscript kha.
From Devārha came Kambalabarhis; from him was Asamaujas.

sanskrit_iast:
sudaṃṣṭraś ca suvāsaś ca dhṛṣṭo 'bhūdasamaujasaḥ /
gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca dhṛṣṭabhārye babhūvatuḥ //
meaning:
सुदंष्ट्रश् च सुवासश् च धृष्टो ऽभूदसमौजसः /
गान्धारी चैव माद्री च धृष्टभार्ये बभूवतुः //
text_mt: Sudaṃṣṭra, Suvāsa, and Dhṛṣṭa were sons of Asamaujas. / Gāndhārī and Mādrī became the two wives of Dhṛṣṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
sumitro 'bhūcca gāndhāryāṃ mādrī jajñe yudhājitam(1) /
anamitraḥ śinirdhṛṣṭāttato vai devamīḍhuṣaḥ //
meaning:
सुमित्रो ऽभूच्च गान्धार्यां माद्री जज्ञे युधाजितम्(1) /
अनमित्रः शिनिर्धृष्टात्ततो वै देवमीढुषः //
text_mt: Sumitra was born of Gāndhārī, and Mādrī gave birth to Yudhājit. / Anamitra and Śini were born from Dhṛṣṭa, and from him indeed came Devamīḍhuṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
anamitrasuto nighno nighnasyāpi prasenakaḥ /
satrājitaḥ praseno 'tha maṇiṃ sūryātsyamantakam //
meaning:
अनमित्रसुतो निघ्नो निघ्नस्यापि प्रसेनकः /
सत्राजितः प्रसेनो ऽथ मणिं सूर्यात्स्यमन्तकम् //
text_mt: Anamitra's son was Nighna, and Nighna's son was Prasena. / Prasena and Satrājit [were his sons]. Then, [having obtained] the Syamantaka jewel from Sūrya,

sanskrit_iast:
prāpyāraṇye carantantu siṃho hatvāgrahīnmaṇiṃ /
hato jāmbavatā siṃho jāmbavān hariṇā jitaḥ //
meaning:
प्राप्यारण्ये चरन्तन्तु सिंहो हत्वाग्रहीन्मणिं /
हतो जाम्बवता सिंहो जाम्बवान् हरिणा जितः //
text_mt: a lion killed [Prasena] wandering in the forest and took the jewel. / The lion was slain by Jāmbavat, and Jāmbavat was conquered by Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmānmaṇiṃ jāmbavatīṃ prāpyāgāddārakāṃ purīm /
satrājitāya pradadau śatadhanvā jaghāna tam //
meaning:
तस्मान्मणिं जाम्बवतीं प्राप्यागाद्दारकां पुरीम् /
सत्राजिताय प्रददौ शतधन्वा जघान तम् //
text_mt: Having obtained the jewel and Jāmbavatī from him, [Hari] went to the city of Dvārakā. / He gave it to Satrājit; [then] Śatadhanvan killed him.

sanskrit_iast:
hatvā śatadhanuṃ kṛṣṇo maṇimādāya kīrtibhāk /
balayādavamukhyāgre akrūrānmaṇimarpayet //
meaning:
हत्वा शतधनुं कृष्णो मणिमादाय कीर्तिभाक् /
बलयादवमुख्याग्रे अक्रूरान्मणिमर्पयेत् //
text_mt: Having slain Śatadhanu and taken the jewel, renowned Kṛṣṇa / presented the jewel, [recovered] from Akrūra, before Bala and the foremost Yādavas.

sanskrit_iast:
mithyābhiśastiṃ kṛṣṇasya tyaktvā svargī ca sampaṭhan /
satrājito bhaṅgakāraḥ satyabhāmā hareḥ priyā //
meaning:
मिथ्याभिशस्तिं कृष्णस्य त्यक्त्वा स्वर्गी च सम्पठन् /
सत्राजितो भङ्गकारः सत्यभामा हरेः प्रिया //
text_mt: Having recited [this], one is freed from false accusations concerning Kṛṣṇa and attains heaven. / Satrājit was the causer of discord; Satyabhāmā was the beloved of Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
anamitrācchinirjajñe satyakastu śineḥ sutaḥ /
satyakātsātyakirjajñe yuyudhānāddhunirhyabhūt //
meaning:
अनमित्राच्छिनिर्जज्ञे सत्यकस्तु शिनेः सुतः /
सत्यकात्सात्यकिर्जज्ञे युयुधानाद्धुनिर्ह्यभूत् //
text_mt: From Anamitra was born Śini, and Satyaka was the son of Śini. / From Satyaka, Sātyaki was born; from Yuyudhāna came Dhuni.

sanskrit_iast:
dhuneryugandharaḥ putraḥ svāhyo 'bhut(2) sa yudhājitaḥ /
ṛṣabhakṣetrakau tasya hy ṛṣabhācca svaphalkakaḥ //
meaning:
धुनेर्युगन्धरः पुत्रः स्वाह्यो ऽभुत्(2) स युधाजितः /
ऋषभक्षेत्रकौ तस्य ह्य् ऋषभाच्च स्वफल्ककः //
text_mt: Dhuni's son was Yugandhara; Svāhya was born from Yudhājit. / Ṛṣabha and Kṣetraka were his sons; and from Ṛṣabha came Svaphalka.

sanskrit_iast:
svaphalkaputro hy akrūro akūrācca sudhanvakaḥ /
śūrāttu vasudevādyāḥ pṛthā pāṇḍoḥ priyābhavat //
:n
1 sudhājitamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 svāndhobhūditi kha.. , cha.. ca / sākṣo 'bhūditi ja..
:p 18
meaning:
स्वफल्कपुत्रो ह्य् अक्रूरो अकूराच्च सुधन्वकः /
शूरात्तु वसुदेवाद्याः पृथा पाण्डोः प्रियाभवत् //
:न्
1 सुधाजितमिति ख.. , छ.. च
2 स्वान्धोभूदिति ख.. , छ.. च / साक्षो ऽभूदिति ज..
:प् 18
text_mt:
Svaphalka's son was Akrūra, and from Akrūra came Sudhanvan. / From Śūra came Vasudeva and the others; Pṛthā became the beloved [wife] of Pāṇḍu.
[Footnote]
1 'Sudhājitam' in manuscripts kha and cha.
2 'Svāndho 'bhūt' in manuscripts kha and cha; 'sākṣo 'bhūt' in manuscript ja.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmādyudhiṣṭhiraḥ pāṇḍorvāyoḥ kuntyāṃ vṛkodaraḥ /
indrāddhanañjayo mādryāṃ nakulaḥ sahadevakaḥ //
meaning:
धर्माद्युधिष्ठिरः पाण्डोर्वायोः कुन्त्यां वृकोदरः /
इन्द्राद्धनञ्जयो माद्र्यां नकुलः सहदेवकः //
text_mt: From Dharma [was born] Yudhiṣṭhira to Pāṇḍu; from Vāyu, Vṛkodara in Kuntī; / from Indra, Dhanañjaya; [and] in Mādrī, Nakula and Sahadeva.

sanskrit_iast:
vasudevācca rohiṇyāṃ rāmaḥ sāraṇadurgamau /
vasudevācca devakyāmādau jātaḥ susenakaḥ //
meaning:
वसुदेवाच्च रोहिण्यां रामः सारणदुर्गमौ /
वसुदेवाच्च देवक्यामादौ जातः सुसेनकः //
text_mt: From Vasudeva in Rohiṇī were born Rāma, Sāraṇa, and Durgama. / And from Vasudeva in Devakī was first born Susena,

sanskrit_iast:
kīrtimān bhadrasenaś ca jārukhyo viṣṇudāsakaḥ /
bhadradehaḥ kaṃśa etān ṣaḍgarbhānnijaghāna ha //
meaning:
कीर्तिमान् भद्रसेनश् च जारुख्यो विष्णुदासकः /
भद्रदेहः कंश एतान् षड्गर्भान्निजघान ह //
text_mt: Kīrtimat, Bhadrasena, the one named Jāru, Viṣṇudāsa, / [and] Bhadradeha. Kaṃsa indeed killed these six embryos.

sanskrit_iast:
tato balastataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ subhadrā bhadrabhāṣiṇī /
cārudeṣṇaś ca śāmbādyāḥ kṛṣṇājjāmbavatīsutāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yaduvaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma
catuḥsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dvādaśasaṅgrāmāḥ
meaning:
ततो बलस्ततः कृष्णः सुभद्रा भद्रभाषिणी /
चारुदेष्णश् च शाम्बाद्याः कृष्णाज्जाम्बवतीसुताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यदुवंशवर्णनं नाम
चतुःसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
द्वादशसङ्ग्रामाः
text_mt:
Then [was born] Bala; then Kṛṣṇa; [and] Subhadrā of auspicious speech. / Cārudeṣṇa, Śāmba, and others were the sons of Kṛṣṇa from Jāmbavatī.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Lineage of Yadu', in the Mahāpurāṇa called Āgneya.
Now, the two hundred and seventy-fifth chapter.
The Twelve Battles

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
kaśyapo vasudevo 'bhūddevakī cāditirvarā /
devakyāṃ vasudevāttu kṛṣṇo 'bhūttapasānvitaḥ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
कश्यपो वसुदेवो ऽभूद्देवकी चादितिर्वरा /
देवक्यां वसुदेवात्तु कृष्णो ऽभूत्तपसान्वितः //
text_mt: Agni said: / Kaśyapa became Vasudeva, and Devakī was the excellent Aditi. / From Vasudeva in Devakī was born Kṛṣṇa, endowed with ascetic austerity,

sanskrit_iast:
dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārthāya hy adharmaharaṇāya ca /
surādeḥ pālanārthañca daityādermathanāya ca //
meaning:
धर्मसंरक्षणार्थाय ह्य् अधर्महरणाय च /
सुरादेः पालनार्थञ्च दैत्यादेर्मथनाय च //
text_mt: for the protection of righteousness and the removal of unrighteousness, / for the guarding of the gods and others, and for the destruction of the Daityas and others.

sanskrit_iast:
rukmaṇī satyabhāmā ca satyā nagnajitī priyā /
satyabhāmā hareḥ sevyā gāndhārī lakṣmaṇā tathā //
meaning:
रुक्मणी सत्यभामा च सत्या नग्नजिती प्रिया /
सत्यभामा हरेः सेव्या गान्धारी लक्ष्मणा तथा //
text_mt: Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Satyā the daughter of Nagnajit, his beloved, / Satyabhāmā who was worthy of Hari's service, Gāndhārī, and Lakṣmaṇā,

sanskrit_iast:
mitravindā(1) ca kālindī devī jāmbavatī tathā /
suśīlā ca tathā mādrī kauśalyā vijayā jayā //
:n
1 citravindeti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 19
meaning:
मित्रविन्दा(1) च कालिन्दी देवी जाम्बवती तथा /
सुशीला च तथा माद्री कौशल्या विजया जया //
:न्
1 चित्रविन्देति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 19
text_mt:
Mitravindā, Kālindī, Queen Jāmbavatī, / Suśīlā, Mādrī, Kauśalyā, Vijayā, and Jayā—
[Footnote]
1 'Citravindā' in manuscripts kha and cha.

sanskrit_iast:
evamādīni devīnāṃ sahasrāṇi tu ṣoḍaśa /
pradyumnādyāś ca rukmiṇyāṃ bhīmādyāḥ satyabhāmayā //
meaning:
एवमादीनि देवीनां सहस्राणि तु षोडश /
प्रद्युम्नाद्याश् च रुक्मिण्यां भीमाद्याः सत्यभामया //
text_mt: these and others were the sixteen thousand queens. / Pradyumna and others were born of Rukmiṇī; Bhīma and others of Satyabhāmā;

sanskrit_iast:
jāmbavatyāñca śāmbādyāḥ kṛṣṇasyāsaṃs tathāpare /
śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ tasya dhīmataḥ //
meaning:
जाम्बवत्याञ्च शाम्बाद्याः कृष्णस्यासंस् तथापरे /
शतं शतसहस्राणां पुत्राणां तस्य धीमतः //
text_mt: and Śāmba and others of Jāmbavatī. Such were the sons of Kṛṣṇa and others. / One hundred times one hundred thousand were the sons of that wise one,

sanskrit_iast:
aśītiś ca sahasrāṇi yādavāḥ kṛṣṇarakṣitāḥ /
pradyumnasya tu vaidarbhyāmaniruddho raṇapriyaḥ //
meaning:
अशीतिश् च सहस्राणि यादवाः कृष्णरक्षिताः /
प्रद्युम्नस्य तु वैदर्भ्यामनिरुद्धो रणप्रियः //
text_mt: and eighty thousand Yādavas were protected by Kṛṣṇa. / To Pradyumna from the Vaidarbha princess was born Aniruddha, who loved battle.

sanskrit_iast:
aniruddhasya vajrādyā yādavāḥ sumahābalāḥ /
tisraḥ koṭyo yādavānāṃ ṣaṣṭirlakṣāṇi dānavāḥ //
meaning:
अनिरुद्धस्य वज्राद्या यादवाः सुमहाबलाः /
तिस्रः कोट्यो यादवानां षष्टिर्लक्षाणि दानवाः //
text_mt: Of Aniruddha were born Vajra and other exceedingly mighty Yādavas. / Thirty million were the Yādavas, and sixty hundred thousand were the Dānavas.

sanskrit_iast:
manuṣye bādhakā ye tu tannāśāya babhūva saḥ /
kartuṃ karmavyavasthānaṃ manuṣyo jāyate hariḥ //
meaning:
मनुष्ये बाधका ये तु तन्नाशाय बभूव सः /
कर्तुं कर्मव्यवस्थानं मनुष्यो जायते हरिः //
text_mt: For the destruction of those who caused harm to mankind, he came to be. / In order to establish the order of karma, Hari is born as a man.

sanskrit_iast:
devāsurāṇāṃ saṅgrāmā dāyārthaṃ dvādaśābhavan /
prathamo nārasiṃhastu dvitīyo vāmano raṇaḥ //
meaning:
देवासुराणां सङ्ग्रामा दायार्थं द्वादशाभवन् /
प्रथमो नारसिंहस्तु द्वितीयो वामनो रणः //
text_mt: Twelve were the battles between the gods and asuras over their heritage: / the first was the Nārasiṃha [battle], and the second was the Vāmana conflict;

sanskrit_iast:
saṅgrāmastvatha vārāhaś caturtho 'mṛtamanthanaḥ /
tārakāmayasaṅgrāmaḥ ṣaṣṭho hy ājīvako raṇaḥ //
meaning:
सङ्ग्रामस्त्वथ वाराहश् चतुर्थो ऽमृतमन्थनः /
तारकामयसङ्ग्रामः षष्ठो ह्य् आजीवको रणः //
text_mt: the [third] battle was the Vārāha, the fourth was the Churning for Nectar, / the [fifth] was the Tārakāmaya battle, and the sixth was the conflict named Ājīvaka;

sanskrit_iast:
traipuraścāndhakabadho navamo vṛtraghātakaḥ /
jito hālāhalaścātha ghoraḥ kolāhalo raṇaḥ //
meaning:
त्रैपुरश्चान्धकबधो नवमो वृत्रघातकः /
जितो हालाहलश्चाथ घोरः कोलाहलो रणः //
text_mt: the Traipura, the Slaying of Andhaka, the ninth was the Slaying of Vṛtra, / then Hālāhala was conquered, and the dreadful battle called Kolāhala.

sanskrit_iast:
hiraṇyakaśipoścoro vidārya ca nakhaiḥ purā /
nārasiṃho devapālaḥ prahnādaṃ kṛtavān nṛpam //
meaning:
हिरण्यकशिपोश्चोरो विदार्य च नखैः पुरा /
नारसिंहो देवपालः प्रह्नादं कृतवान् नृपम् //
text_mt: Formerly, having torn open the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu with his claws, / Nārasiṃha, the protector of the gods, made Prahlāda king.

sanskrit_iast:
devāsure vāmanaś ca chalitvā balimūrjitam /
mahendrāya dadau rājyaṃ kāśyapo 'ditisambhavaḥ //
meaning:
देवासुरे वामनश् च छलित्वा बलिमूर्जितम् /
महेन्द्राय ददौ राज्यं काश्यपो ऽदितिसम्भवः //
text_mt: In the battle of the gods and asuras, Vāmana, having deceived the mighty Bali, / gave sovereignty to Mahendra, being Kaśyapa's son born of Aditi.

sanskrit_iast:
varāhastu hiraṇyākṣaṃ hatvā devānapālayat /
ujjahāra bhuvaṃ devadevair abhiṣṭutaḥ //
meaning:
वराहस्तु हिरण्याक्षं हत्वा देवानपालयत् /
उज्जहार भुवं देवदेवैर् अभिष्टुतः //
text_mt: Varāha, having slain Hiraṇyākṣa, protected the gods; / praised by the foremost of the gods, he lifted up the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā netraṃ kṛtvā tu vāsukim /
:p 20
surāsuraiś ca mathitaṃ(1) devebhyaścāmṛtaṃ dadau //
meaning:
मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा नेत्रं कृत्वा तु वासुकिम् /
:प् 20
सुरासुरैश् च मथितं(1) देवेभ्यश्चामृतं ददौ //
text_mt:
Having made Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the churning rope,
[Page 20]
it was churned by the gods and asuras, and he gave the nectar to the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
tārakāmayasaṅgrāme tadā devāś ca pālitāḥ /
nivāryendraṃ gurūn devān dānavānsomavaṃśakṛtam //
meaning:
तारकामयसङ्ग्रामे तदा देवाश् च पालिताः /
निवार्येन्द्रं गुरून् देवान् दानवान्सोमवंशकृतम् //
text_mt: In the Tārakāmaya battle, the gods were then protected; / having held back Indra, the preceptors, the gods, and the Dānavas, [he established] the progenitor of the Lunar Dynasty.

sanskrit_iast:
viśvāmitravaśiṣṭhātrikavayaś ca raṇe surān /
apālayante nirvārya rāgadveṣādidānavān //
meaning:
विश्वामित्रवशिष्ठात्रिकवयश् च रणे सुरान् /
अपालयन्ते निर्वार्य रागद्वेषादिदानवान् //
text_mt: Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha, Atri, and Kavya in battle / protected the gods, warding off the Dānavas such as passion and hatred.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthvīrathe brahmayanturīśasya śaraṇo hariḥ /
dadāha tripuraṃ devapālako daityamardanaḥ //
meaning:
पृथ्वीरथे ब्रह्मयन्तुरीशस्य शरणो हरिः /
ददाह त्रिपुरं देवपालको दैत्यमर्दनः //
text_mt: With the earth as the chariot and Brahmā as the charioteer, Hari became the arrow of the Lord / and burned Tripura, [as] the protector of the gods and crusher of the Daityas.

sanskrit_iast:
gaurīṃ jihīrṣuṇā rudramandhakenārditaṃ hariḥ /
anuraktaś ca revatyāṃ cakrecāndhāsurārdanam //
meaning:
गौरीं जिहीर्षुणा रुद्रमन्धकेनार्दितं हरिः /
अनुरक्तश् च रेवत्यां चक्रेचान्धासुरार्दनम् //
text_mt: When Rudra was troubled by Andhaka who sought to abduct Gaurī, Hari, / attached to Revatī, brought about the destruction of the asura Andhaka.

sanskrit_iast:
apāṃ phenamayo bhūtvā devāsuraraṇe haran(2) /
vṛtraṃ devaharaṃ viṣṇurdevadharmānapālayat //
meaning:
अपां फेनमयो भूत्वा देवासुररणे हरन्(2) /
वृत्रं देवहरं विष्णुर्देवधर्मानपालयत् //
text_mt: Becoming the foam of the waters in the battle between the gods and asuras, / destroying Vṛtra, the destroyer of the gods, Viṣṇu preserved the religious duties of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
śālvādīn dānavān jitvā hariḥ paraśurāmakaḥ /
apālayat surādīṃś ca duṣṭakṣatraṃ nihatya ca //
meaning:
शाल्वादीन् दानवान् जित्वा हरिः परशुरामकः /
अपालयत् सुरादींश् च दुष्टक्षत्रं निहत्य च //
text_mt: Having conquered Śālva and other Dānavas, Hari as Paraśurāma / protected the gods and others, having slain the wicked Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit_iast:
hālāhalaṃ viṣaṃ daityaṃ nirākṛtya maheśvarāt /
bhayaṃ nirṇāśayāmāsa devānāṃ madhusūdanaḥ //
meaning:
हालाहलं विषं दैत्यं निराकृत्य महेश्वरात् /
भयं निर्णाशयामास देवानां मधुसूदनः //
text_mt: Having dispelled the Daitya Hālāhala, the poison, Madhusūdana / destroyed the fear of the gods from the great lord [Śiva].

sanskrit_iast:
devāsure raṇe yaś ca daityaḥ kolāhalo jitaḥ /
pālitāś ca surāḥ sarve viṣṇunā dharmapālanāt //
meaning:
देवासुरे रणे यश् च दैत्यः कोलाहलो जितः /
पालिताश् च सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना धर्मपालनात् //
text_mt: And in the battle of the gods and asuras, the Daitya Kolāhala was conquered; / and all the gods were protected by Viṣṇu through the preservation of righteousness.

sanskrit_iast:
rājāno rājaputrāś ca munayo devatā hariḥ /
yaduktaṃ yacca naivoktamavatārā harerime //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dvādaśasaṅgrāmā nāma
pañcasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 surāsurair amanthābdhimiti ka.. , cha.. ca..
2 devāsuraharo 'bhavaditi ka.. , gha.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca..
:p 21
:ś atha ṣaṭsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājavaṃśavarṇanaṃ
meaning:
राजानो राजपुत्राश् च मुनयो देवता हरिः /
यदुक्तं यच्च नैवोक्तमवतारा हरेरिमे //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे द्वादशसङ्ग्रामा नाम
पञ्चसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 सुरासुरैर् अमन्थाब्धिमिति क.. , छ.. च..
2 देवासुरहरो ऽभवदिति क.. , घ.. , ञ.. , ट.. च..
:प् 21
:श् अथ षट्सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजवंशवर्णनं
text_mt:
Kings, princes, sages, and deities are Hari; / whatever has been spoken of and whatever has not been spoken of—these are the incarnations of Hari.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Twelve Battles', in the Mahāpurāṇa called Āgneya.
[Footnote]
1 'Surāsurair amanthābdhim' in manuscripts ka and cha.
2 'Devāsuraharo 'bhavat' in manuscripts ka, gha, ña, and ṭa.
Now, the two hundred and seventy-sixth chapter.
The Description of the Royal Dynasties

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
turvasoś ca suto vargo gobhānustasya cātmajaḥ(1) /
gobhānorāsīt(2) traiśānistraiśānestu karandhamaḥ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
तुर्वसोश् च सुतो वर्गो गोभानुस्तस्य चात्मजः(1) /
गोभानोरासीत्(2) त्रैशानिस्त्रैशानेस्तु करन्धमः //
