text_mt: Agni said: / Turvasu's son was Varga, and Gobhānu was his son. / From Gobhānu came Traiśāni, and from Traiśāni came Karandhama.

sanskrit_iast:
karandhamānmaruttobhūd duṣmantastasya cātmajaḥ /
duṣmantasya varūtho 'bhūdgāṇḍīrastu varūthataḥ //
meaning:
करन्धमान्मरुत्तोभूद् दुष्मन्तस्तस्य चात्मजः /
दुष्मन्तस्य वरूथो ऽभूद्गाण्डीरस्तु वरूथतः //
text_mt: From Karandhama arose Marutta, and Duṣmanta was his son. / From Duṣmanta arose Varūtha, and Gāṇḍīra from Varūtha.

sanskrit_iast:
gāṇḍīrāccaiva gāndhāraḥ pañca jānapadāstataḥ /
gāndhārāḥ keralāścolāḥ pāṇḍyāḥ kolā(3) mahābalāḥ //
meaning:
गाण्डीराच्चैव गान्धारः पञ्च जानपदास्ततः /
गान्धाराः केरलाश्चोलाः पाण्ड्याः कोला(3) महाबलाः //
text_mt: And from Gāṇḍīra came Gāndhāra; from him arose five peoples: / the Gāndhāras, Keralas, Colas, Pāṇḍyas, and the mighty Kolas.

sanskrit_iast:
druhyastu vabhrusetuś ca babhrusetoḥ purovasuḥ /
tato gāndhārā gāndhārair dharmo dharmād ghṛto 'bhavat //
meaning:
द्रुह्यस्तु वभ्रुसेतुश् च बभ्रुसेतोः पुरोवसुः /
ततो गान्धारा गान्धारैर् धर्मो धर्माद् घृतो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Druhyu's [son] was Babhrusetu, and from Babhrusetu came Purovasu; / from him came the Gāndhāras. From Gāndhāra came Dharma, and from Dharma, Ghṛta.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtāttu viduṣastasmāt pracetāstasya vai śatam /
ānadraś ca sabhānaraścākṣuṣaḥ parameṣukaḥ //
meaning:
घृतात्तु विदुषस्तस्मात् प्रचेतास्तस्य वै शतम् /
आनद्रश् च सभानरश्चाक्षुषः परमेषुकः //
text_mt: From Ghṛta came Viduṣ; from him Pracetas, who indeed had a hundred [sons]: / Ānadrā, Sabhānara, Cākṣuṣa, and Parameṣuka.

sanskrit_iast:
sabhānarāt kālānalaḥ kālānalajasrṛñjayaḥ /
purañjayaḥ sṛñjayasya tatputro janamejayaḥ //
meaning:
सभानरात् कालानलः कालानलजस्रृञ्जयः /
पुरञ्जयः सृञ्जयस्य तत्पुत्रो जनमेजयः //
text_mt: From Sabhānara came Kālānala; Sṛñjaya was born of Kālānala. / Purañjaya was the son of Sṛñjaya, and his son was Janamejaya.

sanskrit_iast:
tatputrastu mahāśālastatputro 'bhunmahāmanāḥ /
tasmāduśīnaro brahmannṛgāyāntu nṛgastataḥ //
meaning:
तत्पुत्रस्तु महाशालस्तत्पुत्रो ऽभुन्महामनाः /
तस्मादुशीनरो ब्रह्मन्नृगायान्तु नृगस्ततः //
text_mt: His son was Mahāśāla; his son was Mahāmanas. / From him came Uśīnara, O Brahmin; and then Nṛga upon Nṛgā.

sanskrit_iast:
narāyāntu naraścāsīt kṛmistu kṛmitaḥ sutaḥ /
:n
1 śobhānustasya cātmaja iti kha ..
2 śobhānorāsīditi kha ..
3 karṇā iti ja.. , ṭa.. ca ..
:p 22
daśāyāṃ subrato jajñe dṛśadvatyāṃ śivis tathā //
meaning:
नरायान्तु नरश्चासीत् कृमिस्तु कृमितः सुतः /
:न्
1 शोभानुस्तस्य चात्मज इति ख ..
2 शोभानोरासीदिति ख ..
3 कर्णा इति ज.. , ट.. च ..
:प् 22
दशायां सुब्रतो जज्ञे दृशद्वत्यां शिविस् तथा //
text_mt:
Upon Narā was Nara, and Kṛmi was the son born of Kṛmī.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "Śobhānu was his son" in manuscript kha.
[Variant reading:] "From Śobhānu arose" in manuscript kha.
[Variant reading:] "Karṇas" in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
Subrata was born upon Daśā, and likewise Śivi upon Dṛṣadvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
śive putrāstu catvāraḥ pṛthudarbhaś ca vīrakaḥ /
kaikeyo bhadrakasteṣāṃ nāmrā janapadāḥ śubhāḥ //
meaning:
शिवे पुत्रास्तु चत्वारः पृथुदर्भश् च वीरकः /
कैकेयो भद्रकस्तेषां नाम्रा जनपदाः शुभाः //
text_mt: Śivi had four sons: Pṛthudarbha, Vīraka, / Kaikeya, and Bhadraka; auspicious realms bear their names.

sanskrit_iast:
titikṣuruśīnarajastitikṣoś ca ruṣadrathaḥ /
ruṣadrathādabhūtpailaḥ pailācca sutapāḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
तितिक्षुरुशीनरजस्तितिक्षोश् च रुषद्रथः /
रुषद्रथादभूत्पैलः पैलाच्च सुतपाः सुतः //
text_mt: Titikṣu was born of Uśīnara, and from Titikṣu came Ruṣadratha. / From Ruṣadratha arose Paila, and from Paila his son Sutapas.

sanskrit_iast:
mahāyogi balistasmādaṅgo vaṅgaś ca mukhyakaḥ /
puṇḍraḥ kaliṅgo bāleyo baliryogī balānvitaḥ //
meaning:
महायोगि बलिस्तस्मादङ्गो वङ्गश् च मुख्यकः /
पुण्ड्रः कलिङ्गो बालेयो बलिर्योगी बलान्वितः //
text_mt: From him came the great yogi Bali. The chief [sons] were Aṅga and Vaṅga, / Puṇḍra, Kaliṅga, and Bāleya; Bali was a yogi endowed with might.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgāddadhivāhano 'bhūt(1) tasmāddiviratho nṛpaḥ /
divirathāddharmarathastasya citrarathaḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
अङ्गाद्दधिवाहनो ऽभूत्(1) तस्माद्दिविरथो नृपः /
दिविरथाद्धर्मरथस्तस्य चित्ररथः सुतः //
text_mt: From Aṅga arose Dadhivāhana; from him King Diviratha. / From Diviratha came Dharmaratha; his son was Citraratha.

sanskrit_iast:
citrarathātsatyaratho lomapadaś ca tatsutaḥ /
lomapādāccaturaṅgaḥ pṛthulākṣaś ca tatsutaḥ //
meaning:
चित्ररथात्सत्यरथो लोमपदश् च तत्सुतः /
लोमपादाच्चतुरङ्गः पृथुलाक्षश् च तत्सुतः //
text_mt: From Citraratha came Satyaratha, and Lomapāda was his son. / From Lomapāda came Caturaṅga, and Pṛthulākṣa was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthulākṣācca campo 'bhūccampāddharyaṅgako 'bhavat /
haryaṅgācca bhadraratho bṛhatkarmā ca tatsutaḥ //
meaning:
पृथुलाक्षाच्च चम्पो ऽभूच्चम्पाद्धर्यङ्गको ऽभवत् /
हर्यङ्गाच्च भद्ररथो बृहत्कर्मा च तत्सुतः //
text_mt: From Pṛthulākṣa arose Campa; from Campa arose Haryaṅgaka. / From Haryaṅga came Bhadraratha, and his son was Bṛhatkarman.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādabhūdvṝhadbhānurvṛhadbhānorbṛhātmavān /
tasmājjayadratho hy āsījjayadrathādvṛhadrathaḥ //
meaning:
तस्मादभूद्वॄहद्भानुर्वृहद्भानोर्बृहात्मवान् /
तस्माज्जयद्रथो ह्य् आसीज्जयद्रथाद्वृहद्रथः //
text_mt: From him arose Bṛhadbhānu; from Bṛhadbhānu, Bṛhātmavat. / From him indeed was Jayadratha; from Jayadratha, Bṛhadratha.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛhadrathādviśvajicca karṇo viśvajito 'bhavat /
karṇasya vṛṣasenastu pṛthusenastadātmajaḥ /
eto 'ṅgavaṃśajā bhūpāḥ pūrorvaṃśaṃ vibodha me //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājavaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma
ṣaṭsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 dadhivāmanobhūditi kha.. , cha.. , ña.. , ca..
:p 23
:ś atha saptasapratyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
puruvaṃśavarṇanaṃ
meaning:
वृहद्रथाद्विश्वजिच्च कर्णो विश्वजितो ऽभवत् /
कर्णस्य वृषसेनस्तु पृथुसेनस्तदात्मजः /
एतो ऽङ्गवंशजा भूपाः पूरोर्वंशं विबोध मे //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजवंशवर्णनं नाम
षट्सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 दधिवामनोभूदिति ख.. , छ.. , ञ.. , च..
:प् 23
:श् अथ सप्तसप्रत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पुरुवंशवर्णनं
text_mt:
From Bṛhadratha came Viśvajit, and Karṇa was born of Viśvajit. / Karṇa's [son] was Vṛṣasena, and Pṛthusena was his son. / These kings were born in the lineage of Aṅga; learn now from me the lineage of Pūru.
Thus ends the two hundred seventy-sixth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Description of the Royal Dynasties.'
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "Dadhivāmana arose" in manuscripts kha, cha, ña, and ca.
Now, the two hundred seventy-seventh chapter.
Description of the Lineage of Pūru

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
purorjanamejayo 'bhūtprācīnnantastu tatsutaḥ /
prācīnnantānmanastyustu tasmādvītamayo nṛpaḥ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
पुरोर्जनमेजयो ऽभूत्प्राचीन्नन्तस्तु तत्सुतः /
प्राचीन्नन्तान्मनस्त्युस्तु तस्माद्वीतमयो नृपः //
text_mt: Agni said: / From Pūru arose Janamejaya, and Prācīnvat was his son. / From Prācīnvat came Manasyu; from him King Vītamaya.

sanskrit_iast:
śundhurvītamayāccābhūcchundhorbahuvidhaḥ(1) sutaḥ /
bahuvidhācca saṃyātirahovādī ca tatsutaḥ //
meaning:
शुन्धुर्वीतमयाच्चाभूच्छुन्धोर्बहुविधः(1) सुतः /
बहुविधाच्च संयातिरहोवादी च तत्सुतः //
text_mt: Śundhu arose from Vītamaya; Bahuvidha was the son of Śundhu. / From Bahuvidha came Saṃyāti, and Rahovādin was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya putro 'tha bhadrāśoa bhadrāśvasya daśātmajāḥ /
ṛceyuś ca kṛṣeyuś ca sannateyus tathātmajaḥ //
meaning:
तस्य पुत्रो ऽथ भद्राशोअ भद्राश्वस्य दशात्मजाः /
ऋचेयुश् च कृषेयुश् च सन्नतेयुस् तथात्मजः //
text_mt: His son then was Bhadrāśva; Bhadrāśva had ten sons: / Ṛceyu, Kṛṣeyu, and likewise his son Sannateyu,

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛteyuś ca citeyuś ca sthaṇḍileyuś ca sattamaḥ /
dharmeyuḥ sannateyuś ca kṛceyurmatinārakaḥ //
meaning:
घृतेयुश् च चितेयुश् च स्थण्डिलेयुश् च सत्तमः /
धर्मेयुः सन्नतेयुश् च कृचेयुर्मतिनारकः //
text_mt: Ghṛteyu, Citeyu, and Sthaṇḍileyu the most excellent, / Dharmeyu, Sannateyu, Kṛceyu, and Matināra.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃsuroghaḥ pratirathaḥ purasto matinārajāḥ /
āsītpatirathātkaṇvaḥ kaṇvānmedhātithistvabhūt //
meaning:
तंसुरोघः प्रतिरथः पुरस्तो मतिनारजाः /
आसीत्पतिरथात्कण्वः कण्वान्मेधातिथिस्त्वभूत् //
text_mt: Taṃsurogha, Pratiratha, and Purasta were born of Matināra. / From Pratiratha was Kaṇva, and from Kaṇva arose Medhātithi.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃsuroghācca catvāro duṣmanto 'tha pravīrakaḥ /
sumantaścānayo vīro duṣmantādbharato 'bhavat //
meaning:
तंसुरोघाच्च चत्वारो दुष्मन्तो ऽथ प्रवीरकः /
सुमन्तश्चानयो वीरो दुष्मन्ताद्भरतो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: From Taṃsurogha came four: Duṣmanta, then Pravīraka, / Sumanta, and Anaya the hero. From Duṣmanta arose Bharata

sanskrit_iast:
śakuntalāyāntu balī yasya nāmnā tu bhāratāḥ /
suteṣu mātṛkopena naṣṭeṣu bharatasya ca //
meaning:
शकुन्तलायान्तु बली यस्य नाम्ना तु भारताः /
सुतेषु मातृकोपेन नष्टेषु भरतस्य च //
text_mt: upon Śakuntalā, mighty, after whose name the Bhāratas are called. / And when the sons of Bharata were lost through their mother's wrath,

sanskrit_iast:
tato marudbhirānīya putraḥ sa tu vṛhaspateḥ /
saṃkrāmito bharadvājaḥ kratubhirvitatho 'bhavat //
meaning:
ततो मरुद्भिरानीय पुत्रः स तु वृहस्पतेः /
संक्रामितो भरद्वाजः क्रतुभिर्वितथो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: then that son of Bṛhaspati, Bharadvāja, having been brought by the Maruts / and transferred [to him], became Vitatha through sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast:
sa cāpi vitathaḥ putrān janayāmāsa pañca vai /
:n
1 śagbhurvītamayāścābhūcchambhorbahuvidha iti kha.. , ja.. , ca..
:p 24
suhotrañca suhotāraṅgayaṅgarbhantathaiva ca //
meaning:
स चापि वितथः पुत्रान् जनयामास पञ्च वै /
:न्
1 शग्भुर्वीतमयाश्चाभूच्छम्भोर्बहुविध इति ख.. , ज.. , च..
:प् 24
सुहोत्रञ्च सुहोतारङ्गयङ्गर्भन्तथैव च //
text_mt:
And he, Vitatha, fathered five sons indeed:
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "Śaṅbhu arose from Vītamaya; Bahuvidha was Śambhu's [son]" in manuscripts kha, ja, and ca.
Suhotra, Suhotṛ, Gaya, and likewise Garbha,

sanskrit_iast:
kapilaś ca mahātmānaṃ suketuñca sutadvayam /
kauśikañca gṛtsapatiṃ tathā gṛtsapateḥ sutāḥ //
meaning:
कपिलश् च महात्मानं सुकेतुञ्च सुतद्वयम् /
कौशिकञ्च गृत्सपतिं तथा गृत्सपतेः सुताः //
text_mt: Kapila, and the two sons the noble [one] and Suketu, / and Kauśika, and Gṛtsapati; and the sons of Gṛtsapati

sanskrit_iast:
brahmāṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ kāśe dīrghatamāḥ(1)sutāḥ /
tato dhanvantariścāsīttatsuto 'bhūcca ketumān //
meaning:
ब्रह्माणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः काशे दीर्घतमाः(1)सुताः /
ततो धन्वन्तरिश्चासीत्तत्सुतो ऽभूच्च केतुमान् //
text_mt: were Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas. In Kāśi were the sons of Dīrghatamas; / then arose Dhanvantari, and Ketumat was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
ketumato hemaratho divodāsa itiśrutaḥ /
pratardano divodāsādbhargavatsau pratardanāt //
meaning:
केतुमतो हेमरथो दिवोदास इतिश्रुतः /
प्रतर्दनो दिवोदासाद्भर्गवत्सौ प्रतर्दनात् //
text_mt: Hemaratha was the son of Ketumat; he is famed as Divodāsa. / From Divodāsa came Pratardana; Bharga and Vatsa were from Pratardana.

sanskrit_iast:
vatsādanarka āsīcca anarkāt kṣemako 'bhavat /
kṣemakadvarṣaketuś ca varṣaketorvibhuḥ smṛtaḥ(2) //
meaning:
वत्सादनर्क आसीच्च अनर्कात् क्षेमको ऽभवत् /
क्षेमकद्वर्षकेतुश् च वर्षकेतोर्विभुः स्मृतः(2) //
text_mt: From Vatsa was Anarka, and from Anarka arose Kṣemaka. / From Kṣemaka came Varṣaketu, and from Varṣaketu, Vibhu is remembered.

sanskrit_iast:
vibhorānartaḥ putro 'bhūdvibhoś ca sukumārakaḥ /
sukumārātsatyaketurvatsabhūmistu vatsakāt //
meaning:
विभोरानर्तः पुत्रो ऽभूद्विभोश् च सुकुमारकः /
सुकुमारात्सत्यकेतुर्वत्सभूमिस्तु वत्सकात् //
text_mt: Anarta was the son of Vibhu, and also Sukumāraka from Vibhu. / From Sukumāra came Satyaketu, and Vatsabhūmi from Vatsaka.

sanskrit_iast:
suhotrasya vṛhatputro vṛhatastanayāstrayaḥ /
ajamīḍho dvimīḍhaś ca purumīḍhaś ca vīryavān //
meaning:
सुहोत्रस्य वृहत्पुत्रो वृहतस्तनयास्त्रयः /
अजमीढो द्विमीढश् च पुरुमीढश् च वीर्यवान् //
text_mt: Suhotra's son was Bṛhat; Bṛhat had three sons: / Ajamīḍha, Dvimīḍha, and Purumīḍha endowed with valor.

sanskrit_iast:
ajamīḍhasya keśinyāṃ jajñe jahnuḥ pratāpavān(3) /
jahnorabhūdajakāśvo balākāśvastadātmajaḥ //
meaning:
अजमीढस्य केशिन्यां जज्ञे जह्नुः प्रतापवान्(3) /
जह्नोरभूदजकाश्वो बलाकाश्वस्तदात्मजः //
text_mt: To Ajamīḍha upon Keśinī was born the radiant Jahnu. / From Jahnu arose Ajakāśva; Balākāśva was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
valākāśvasya kuśikaḥ kuśikāt gādhirindrakaḥ /
gādheḥ satyavatī kanyā viśvāmitraḥ sūtottamaḥ //
meaning:
वलाकाश्वस्य कुशिकः कुशिकात् गाधिरिन्द्रकः /
गाधेः सत्यवती कन्या विश्वामित्रः सूतोत्तमः //
text_mt: Kuśika was the son of Valākāśva; from Kuśika came Gādhi, an Indra [among men]. / Gādhi's daughter was Satyavatī, and Viśvāmitra was his excellent son.

sanskrit_iast:
devarātaḥ katimukhā viśvāmitrasya te sutāḥ /
śunaḥśepho 'ṣṭakaścānyo hy ajamīḍhāt suto 'bhavat //
meaning:
देवरातः कतिमुखा विश्वामित्रस्य ते सुताः /
शुनःशेफो ऽष्टकश्चान्यो ह्य् अजमीढात् सुतो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Devarāta, those headed by Kati, Śunaḥśepha, / and another, Aṣṭaka, were the sons of Viśvāmitra. From Ajamīḍha another son arose

sanskrit_iast:
nīlinyāṃ śāntiraparaḥ purujātiḥ suśāntitaḥ /
:n
1 kāśadīrghatamā iti ja..
2 suta iti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ca
3 prabhāvavāniti kha..
:p 25
purujātestu vāhyāśvo vāhyāścvāt pañca pārthivāḥ //
meaning:
नीलिन्यां शान्तिरपरः पुरुजातिः सुशान्तितः /
:न्
1 काशदीर्घतमा इति ज..
2 सुत इति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. , च
3 प्रभाववानिति ख..
:प् 25
पुरुजातेस्तु वाह्याश्वो वाह्याश्च्वात् पञ्च पार्थिवाः //
text_mt:
upon Nīlinī, Śānti; Purujāti came from Suśānti.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "kāśadīrghatamāḥ" in manuscript ja.
[Variant reading:] "son" in manuscripts kha, cha, ja, and ca.
[Variant reading:] "endowed with power" in manuscript kha.
From Purujāti came Vāhyāśva; from Vāhyāśva came five rulers:

sanskrit_iast:
mukulaḥ sṛñjayaś caiva rājā vṛhadiṣus tathā /
yavīnaraś ca(1) kṛmilaḥ pāñcālā iti viśrutāḥ //
meaning:
मुकुलः सृञ्जयश् चैव राजा वृहदिषुस् तथा /
यवीनरश् च(1) कृमिलः पाञ्चाला इति विश्रुताः //
text_mt: Mukula, Sṛñjaya, King Bṛhadiṣu, / Yavīnara, and Kṛmila; they are renowned as the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit_iast:
mukulasya tu maukulyāḥ kṣetropetā dvijātayaḥ /
cañcāśvo mukulājjajñe cañcāśvānmithunaṃ hy abhut //
meaning:
मुकुलस्य तु मौकुल्याः क्षेत्रोपेता द्विजातयः /
चञ्चाश्वो मुकुलाज्जज्ञे चञ्चाश्वान्मिथुनं ह्य् अभुत् //
text_mt: The descendants of Mukula were the Maukulyas, twice-born endowed with fields. / Cañcāśva was born of Mukula; from Cañcāśva a twin pair arose:

sanskrit_iast:
divodāso hy ahalyā ca ahalyāyāṃ śaradvatāt /
śatānandaḥ śatānandāt satyadhṛnmithunantataḥ //
meaning:
दिवोदासो ह्य् अहल्या च अहल्यायां शरद्वतात् /
शतानन्दः शतानन्दात् सत्यधृन्मिथुनन्ततः //
text_mt: Divodāsa and Ahalyā. Upon Ahalyā from Śaradvat / was born Śatānanda; from Śatānanda, Satyadhṛti; then a twin pair:

sanskrit_iast:
kṛpaḥ kṛpī kivodāsānmaitreyaḥ somapastataḥ /
sṛñjayāt pañcadhanuṣaḥ somadattaś ca tatsutaḥ //
meaning:
कृपः कृपी किवोदासान्मैत्रेयः सोमपस्ततः /
सृञ्जयात् पञ्चधनुषः सोमदत्तश् च तत्सुतः //
text_mt: Kṛpa and Kṛpī. From Divodāsa came Maitreya; then Somapa. / From Sṛñjaya came Pañcadhanuṣ, and Somadatta was his son.

sanskrit_iast:
sahadevaḥ somadattāt sahadevāttu somakaḥ /
āsīcca somakājjanturjantoś ca pṛṣataḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
सहदेवः सोमदत्तात् सहदेवात्तु सोमकः /
आसीच्च सोमकाज्जन्तुर्जन्तोश् च पृषतः सुतः //
text_mt: Sahadeva came from Somadatta; from Sahadeva came Somaka. / From Somaka was Jantu, and Pṛṣata was Jantu's son.

sanskrit_iast:
pṛṣatāddrupadastasmāddhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha tatsutaḥ /
dhṛṣṭhaketuś ca dhūminyāmṛkṣo 'bhūdajamīḍhataḥ //
meaning:
पृषताद्द्रुपदस्तस्माद्धृष्टद्युम्नो ऽथ तत्सुतः /
धृष्ठकेतुश् च धूमिन्यामृक्षो ऽभूदजमीढतः //
text_mt: From Pṛṣata came Drupada; from him Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and then his son / Dhṛṣṭaketu. Upon Dhūminī arose Ṛkṣa from Ajamīḍha.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛkṣātsamvaraṇo jajñe kuruḥ samvaraṇāttataḥ /
yaḥ prayāgādapākramya kurukṣetrañcakāra ha //
meaning:
ऋक्षात्सम्वरणो जज्ञे कुरुः सम्वरणात्ततः /
यः प्रयागादपाक्रम्य कुरुक्षेत्रञ्चकार ह //
text_mt: From Ṛkṣa was born Saṃvaraṇa, and Kuru then from Saṃvaraṇa, / who, setting out from Prayāga, established Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit_iast:
kuroḥ sudhanvā sudhanuḥ parikṣiccārimejayaḥ /
sudhanvanaḥ suhotro 'bhūt suhotrāccyavano hy abhūt //
meaning:
कुरोः सुधन्वा सुधनुः परिक्षिच्चारिमेजयः /
सुधन्वनः सुहोत्रो ऽभूत् सुहोत्राच्च्यवनो ह्य् अभूत् //
text_mt:
From Kuru sprang Sudhanvan, Sudhanus, Parikṣit, and Arimejaya.
From Sudhanvan was Suhotra, and from Suhotra sprang Cyavana.

sanskrit_iast:
vaśiṣṭhaparicārābhyāṃ saptāsan girikāsutāḥ /
vṛhadrathaḥ kuśo vīro yaduḥ pratyagraho balaḥ //
meaning:
वशिष्ठपरिचाराभ्यां सप्तासन् गिरिकासुताः /
वृहद्रथः कुशो वीरो यदुः प्रत्यग्रहो बलः //
text_mt:
By Vaśiṣṭha and Paricāra, Girikā had seven sons:
Bṛhadratha, Kuśa, the hero Yadu, Pratyagraha, and Bala,

sanskrit_iast:
matsyakālī kuśāgro 'to hy āsīdrājño vṛhadrathāt /
kuśāgrādvṛṣabho jajñe tasya satyahitaḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
मत्स्यकाली कुशाग्रो ऽतो ह्य् आसीद्राज्ञो वृहद्रथात् /
कुशाग्राद्वृषभो जज्ञे तस्य सत्यहितः सुतः //
text_mt:
Matsyakālī, and Kuśāgra; these came from King Bṛhadratha.
From Kuśāgra was born Vṛṣabha; his son was Satyahita.

sanskrit_iast:
sudhanvā tatsutaścorja ūrjādāsīcca sambhavaḥ /
:n
1 yavīnacaśceti kha.., cha.. , ña.. , ca
:p 26
sambhavācca jarāsandhaḥ sahadevaś ca tatsutaḥ //
meaning:
सुधन्वा तत्सुतश्चोर्ज ऊर्जादासीच्च सम्भवः /
:न्
1 यवीनचश्चेति ख.., छ.. , ञ.. , च
:प् 26
सम्भवाच्च जरासन्धः सहदेवश् च तत्सुतः //
text_mt:
His son was Sudhanvan; then Ūrja; and from Ūrja came Sambhava.
[Note]
1. 'yavīnacaś ca' in manuscripts kha, cha, ña, and ca. / [Page 26]
And from Sambhava came Jarāsandha, and his son was Sahadeva.

sanskrit_iast:
sahadevādudāpiś ca udāpeḥ śrutakarmakaḥ /
parikṣitasya dāyādo dhārmiko janamejayaḥ //
meaning:
सहदेवादुदापिश् च उदापेः श्रुतकर्मकः /
परिक्षितस्य दायादो धार्मिको जनमेजयः //
text_mt:
From Sahadeva was Udāpi, and from Udāpi was Śrutakarmaka.
The righteous Janamejaya was the heir of Parikṣit.

sanskrit_iast:
janamejayāttrasadasyurjahnostu surathaḥ sutaḥ /
śrutasenograsenau ca bhīmasenaś ca nāmataḥ //
meaning:
जनमेजयात्त्रसदस्युर्जह्नोस्तु सुरथः सुतः /
श्रुतसेनोग्रसेनौ च भीमसेनश् च नामतः //
text_mt:
From Janamejaya came Trasadasyu; but of Jahnu, the son was Suratha;
and by name Śrutasena, Ugrasena, and Bhīmasena.

sanskrit_iast:
janamejayasya putrau tu suratho mahimāṃs tathā /
surathādvidūratho 'bhūdṛkṣa āsīdvidūrathāt //
meaning:
जनमेजयस्य पुत्रौ तु सुरथो महिमांस् तथा /
सुरथाद्विदूरथो ऽभूदृक्ष आसीद्विदूरथात् //
text_mt:
The sons of Janamejaya were Suratha and Mahīmant.
From Suratha came Vidūratha; from Vidūratha came Ṛkṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛkṣasya tu dvitīyasya bhīmaseno 'bhavatsutaḥ /
pratīpo bhīmasenāttu pratīpasya tu śāntanuḥ //
meaning:
ऋक्षस्य तु द्वितीयस्य भीमसेनो ऽभवत्सुतः /
प्रतीपो भीमसेनात्तु प्रतीपस्य तु शान्तनुः //
text_mt:
The son of the second Ṛkṣa was Bhīmasena.
From Bhīmasena came Pratīpa; and of Pratīpa was Śāntanu.

sanskrit_iast:
devāpirvāhlikaś caiva somadattastu śāntanoḥ /
vāhlikātsomadatto 'bhudbhūrirbhūrisravāḥ śalaḥ //
meaning:
देवापिर्वाह्लिकश् चैव सोमदत्तस्तु शान्तनोः /
वाह्लिकात्सोमदत्तो ऽभुद्भूरिर्भूरिस्रवाः शलः //
text_mt:
Śāntanu's [brothers] were Devāpi and Bāhlika, and Somadatta [was Bāhlika's son].
From Bāhlika was Somadatta, and [from him] Bhūri, Bhūriśravas, and Śala.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṅgāyāṃ śāntanorbhīṣmaḥ kālyāyāṃ vicitravīryakaḥ /
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaś caiva kṣetre vaicitravīryake //
meaning:
गङ्गायां शान्तनोर्भीष्मः काल्यायां विचित्रवीर्यकः /
कृष्णद्वैपायनश् चैव क्षेत्रे वैचित्रवीर्यके //
text_mt:
From Śāntanu by Gaṅgā was Bhīṣma; by Kālī was Vicitravīrya;
and Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, in the wife of Vicitravīrya,

sanskrit_iast:
dhṛtaraṣṭrañca pāṇḍuñca vidurañcāpyajījanat /
pāṇḍoryudhiṣṭhiraḥ kuntyāṃ bhīmaś caivārjunastrayaḥ //
meaning:
धृतरष्ट्रञ्च पाण्डुञ्च विदुरञ्चाप्यजीजनत् /
पाण्डोर्युधिष्ठिरः कुन्त्यां भीमश् चैवार्जुनस्त्रयः //
text_mt:
begot Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and also Vidura.
To Pāṇḍu by Kuntī were three: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, and Arjuna.

sanskrit_iast:
nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca pāṇḍormādyrāñca daivataḥ /
arjunasya ca saubhadraḥ parikṣidabhimanyutaḥ //
meaning:
नकुलः सहदेवश् च पाण्डोर्माद्य्राञ्च दैवतः /
अर्जुनस्य च सौभद्रः परिक्षिदभिमन्युतः //
text_mt:
Nakula and Sahadeva were Pāṇḍu's by Mādrī through the deities.
Arjuna's son was the son of Subhadrā [Abhimanyu], and Parikṣit was from Abhimanyu.

sanskrit_iast:
draupadī pāṇḍavānāñca priyā tasyāṃ yudhiṣṭhirāt /
prativindhyo bhīmasenācchrutakīrtirdhanañjayāt(1) //
meaning:
द्रौपदी पाण्डवानाञ्च प्रिया तस्यां युधिष्ठिरात् /
प्रतिविन्ध्यो भीमसेनाच्छ्रुतकीर्तिर्धनञ्जयात्(1) //
text_mt:
And Draupadī was the beloved of the Pāṇḍavas; on her, from Yudhiṣṭhira,
was Prativindhya; from Bhīmasena [was Sutasoma]; from Dhanañjaya was Śrutakīrti;

sanskrit_iast:
sahadevācchrutakarmā śatānīkastu nākuliḥ /
bhīmasenāddhiḍimbāyāmanya āsīd ghaṭītkacaḥ //
meaning:
सहदेवाच्छ्रुतकर्मा शतानीकस्तु नाकुलिः /
भीमसेनाद्धिडिम्बायामन्य आसीद् घटीत्कचः //
text_mt:
from Sahadeva was Śrutakarman; and Śatānīka was the son of Nakula.
From Bhīmasena by Hiḍimbā another son was Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit_iast:
ete bhūtā bhaviṣyāś ca nṛpāḥ saṃkhyā na vidyate /
:n
1 atra pāṭhaḥ patitaḥ dhanañjayāt ka utpanna iti
viśeṣāprāpteḥ
:p 27
gatāḥ kālena kālo hi haristaṃ pūjayeddvija //
homamagnausamuddiśya kuru sarvapradaṃ yataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe puruvaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma
saptasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
siddhauṣadhāni
meaning:
एते भूता भविष्याश् च नृपाः संख्या न विद्यते /
:न्
1 अत्र पाठः पतितः धनञ्जयात् क उत्पन्न इति
विशेषाप्राप्तेः
:प् 27
गताः कालेन कालो हि हरिस्तं पूजयेद्द्विज //
होममग्नौसमुद्दिश्य कुरु सर्वप्रदं यतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पुरुवंशवर्णनं नाम
सप्तसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सिद्धौषधानि
text_mt:
These kings, past and future, are beyond reckoning.
[Note]
1. Here the text is deficient, as it does not clearly specify who was born from Dhanañjaya. / [Page 27]
They have passed away in time; for Time is Hari. A twice-born should worship him.
Perform a fire oblation aimed into the fire, since it bestows all things.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Puru Lineage', in the great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-eighth chapter:
Proven Remedies.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
āyurvedaṃ pravakṣyāmi suśrutāya yamabravīt /
devo dhanvantariḥ sāraṃ mṛtasañjīvanīkaraṃ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
आयुर्वेदं प्रवक्ष्यामि सुश्रुताय यमब्रवीत् /
देवो धन्वन्तरिः सारं मृतसञ्जीवनीकरं //
text_mt:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the Āyurveda which the divine Dhanvantari
spoke to Suśruta—the essence that revives the dead.

sanskrit_iast:
suśruta uvāca
āyurvedaṃ mama brūhi narāśvebharugardanam /
siddhayogānsiddhamantrānmṛtasañjīvanīkarān //
meaning:
सुश्रुत उवाच
आयुर्वेदं मम ब्रूहि नराश्वेभरुगर्दनम् /
सिद्धयोगान्सिद्धमन्त्रान्मृतसञ्जीवनीकरान् //
text_mt:
Suśruta said:
Tell me the Āyurveda that removes the diseases of men, horses, and elephants,
proven formulations, proven mantras that revive the dead.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
rakṣan balaṃ hi jvaritaṃ laṅghitaṃ bhojayedbhiṣak /
saviśvaṃ lājamaṇḍantu tṛḍjvarāntaṃ śṛtaṃ jalam //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
रक्षन् बलं हि ज्वरितं लङ्घितं भोजयेद्भिषक् /
सविश्वं लाजमण्डन्तु तृड्ज्वरान्तं शृतं जलम् //
text_mt:
Dhanvantari said:
Preserving strength, the physician should feed one who has fasted in fever
scum of parched paddy with ginger, and boiled water that ends thirst and fever.

sanskrit_iast:
mustaparpaṭakośīracandanodīcyanāgaraiḥ /
ṣaḍahe ca vyatikrānte tittakaṃ pāyayeddhruvaṃ //
meaning:
मुस्तपर्पटकोशीरचन्दनोदीच्यनागरैः /
षडहे च व्यतिक्रान्ते तित्तकं पाययेद्ध्रुवं //
text_mt:
With nut-grass, parpaṭaka, vetiver, sandalwood, bālā, and dry ginger;
and when six days have passed, he should unfailingly make him drink a bitter [decoction].

sanskrit_iast:
snehayettaktadoṣantu(1) tatastañca virecayet /
jīrṇāḥ ṣaṣṭikanīvāraraktaśālipramodakāḥ //
meaning:
स्नेहयेत्तक्तदोषन्तु(1) ततस्तञ्च विरेचयेत् /
जीर्णाः षष्टिकनीवाररक्तशालिप्रमोदकाः //
text_mt:
He should lubricate one whose humours are mature, and then purge him.
Old ṣaṣṭika, wild rice, red rice, pramodaka,

sanskrit_iast:
tadvidhāste jvareṣviṣṭā yavānāṃ vikṛtis tathā /
mudgā masūrāś ca ṇakāḥ kulatthāś ca sakuṣṭhakāḥ //
:n
1 pakvadoṣantviti ña..
:p 28
meaning:
तद्विधास्ते ज्वरेष्विष्टा यवानां विकृतिस् तथा /
मुद्गा मसूराश् च णकाः कुलत्थाश् च सकुष्ठकाः //
:न्
1 पक्वदोषन्त्विति ञ..
:प् 28
text_mt:
and similar grains are recommended in fevers, as well as barley preparations,
mudga, lentils, chickpeas, and horse gram along with kuṣṭha,
[Note]
1. 'pakvadoṣantv' in manuscript ña. / [Page 28]

sanskrit_iast:
āṭakyo nārakādyāś ca karkoṭakakatolvakam /
paṭolaṃ saphalaṃ nimbaṃ parpaṭaṃ dāḍimaṃ jvare //
meaning:
आटक्यो नारकाद्याश् च कर्कोटककतोल्वकम् /
पटोलं सफलं निम्बं पर्पटं दाडिमं ज्वरे //
text_mt:
pigeon peas, oranges and the like, spine gourd, katphala,
pointed gourd with fruit, neem, parpaṭa, and pomegranate in fever.

sanskrit_iast:
adhoge vamanaṃ śastamūrdhvage ca virecanam /
raktapitte tathā pānaṃ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ śuṇṭhivarjitam //
meaning:
अधोगे वमनं शस्तमूर्ध्वगे च विरेचनम् /
रक्तपित्ते तथा पानं षडङ्गं शुण्ठिवर्जितम् //
text_mt:
In downward hemorrhage, emesis is commended; in upward, purgation;
in internal hemorrhage, the six-fold drink without dry ginger [is commended].

sanskrit_iast:
śaktugodhūmalājāś ca yavaśālimasūrakāḥ /
sakuṣṭhacaṇakā mudgā bhakṣyā godhūmakā hitāḥ //
meaning:
शक्तुगोधूमलाजाश् च यवशालिमसूरकाः /
सकुष्ठचणका मुद्गा भक्ष्या गोधूमका हिताः //
text_mt:
Barley meal, wheat, parched grain, barley, rice, and lentils,
chickpeas with kuṣṭha, mudga, and cooked wheat preparations are wholesome.

sanskrit_iast:
sādhitā ghṛtadugdhābhyāṃ kṣaudraṃ vṛṣaraso madhu /
atīsāre purāṇānāṃ śālīnāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ hitaṃ //
meaning:
साधिता घृतदुग्धाभ्यां क्षौद्रं वृषरसो मधु /
अतीसारे पुराणानां शालीनां भक्षणं हितं //
text_mt:
Prepared with ghee and milk, small honey, juice of vāsā, and honey.
In diarrhea, the eating of aged rice is wholesome,

sanskrit_iast:
anabhiṣyandi yaccānnaṃ lodhravalkalasaṃyutam /
mārutaṃ varjayed yatnaḥ kāryo gulmeṣu sarvathā //
meaning:
अनभिष्यन्दि यच्चान्नं लोध्रवल्कलसंयुतम् /
मारुतं वर्जयेद् यत्नः कार्यो गुल्मेषु सर्वथा //
text_mt:
and food that does not cause obstruction of channels, combined with lodhra bark.
In phantom tumours, one must avoid wind-generating foods; every effort should be made [to that end].

sanskrit_iast:
vāṭyaṃ kṣīreṇa cāśnīyādvāstūkaṃ ghṛtasādhitaṃ /
godhūmaśālayastiktā hitā jaṭhariṇāmatha //
meaning:
वाट्यं क्षीरेण चाश्नीयाद्वास्तूकं घृतसाधितं /
गोधूमशालयस्तिक्ता हिता जठरिणामथ //
text_mt:
One should eat barley gruel with milk, and goosefoot cooked with ghee.
Wheat and rice dishes, and bitters, are beneficial for patients with abdominal disease.

sanskrit_iast:
godhūmaśālayo mudgā brahmarkṣakhadiro 'bhayā /
pañcakolañjāṅgalāś ca nimbadhātryaḥ paṭolakāḥ //
meaning:
गोधूमशालयो मुद्गा ब्रह्मर्क्षखदिरो ऽभया /
पञ्चकोलञ्जाङ्गलाश् च निम्बधात्र्यः पटोलकाः //
text_mt:
Wheat, rice, mudga, brahmadāru, khadira, chebulic myrobalan,
the five spices, dry-land game meat, neem, āmalakī, pointed gourd,

sanskrit_iast:
mātulaṅgarasājātiśuṣkamūlakasaindhavāḥ /
kuṣṭhināñca tathā śastaṃ pānārthe khadirodakaṃ //
meaning:
मातुलङ्गरसाजातिशुष्कमूलकसैन्धवाः /
कुष्ठिनाञ्च तथा शस्तं पानार्थे खदिरोदकं //
text_mt:
citron juice, jasmine, dried radish, and rock salt;
and for leprosy patients, khadira-infused water is commended for drinking.

sanskrit_iast:
masūrasudgau peyārthe bhojyā jirṇāś ca śālayaḥ /
nimbaparpaṭakaiḥ śākair jāṅgalānāṃ tathā rasaḥ //
meaning:
मसूरसुद्गौ पेयार्थे भोज्या जिर्णाश् च शालयः /
निम्बपर्पटकैः शाकैर् जाङ्गलानां तथा रसः //
text_mt:
Lentils and mudga are for drinks, and aged rice for meals,
with neem and parpaṭaka greens, and meat broth of dry-land animals.

sanskrit_iast:
viḍaṅgaṃ maricaṃ mustaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ lodhraṃ suvarcikā /
manaḥśilā ca vāleyaḥ kuṣṭhahā mūtrapeṣitaḥ //
meaning:
विडङ्गं मरिचं मुस्तं कुष्ठं लोध्रं सुवर्चिका /
मनःशिला च वालेयः कुष्ठहा मूत्रपेषितः //
text_mt:
Viḍaṅga, black pepper, nut-grass, kuṣṭha, lodhra, natron,
realgar, and [donkey] dung, ground with [cow] urine, destroy leprosy.

sanskrit_iast:
apūpakuṣṭhakulmāṣayavādyā mehināṃ hitāḥ /
yavānnavikṛtirmudgā kulatthā jīrṇaśālayaḥ //
meaning:
अपूपकुष्ठकुल्माषयवाद्या मेहिनां हिताः /
यवान्नविकृतिर्मुद्गा कुलत्था जीर्णशालयः //
text_mt:
Cakes, kuṣṭha, steamed barley grains, and the like are beneficial for patients with urinary disorders;
preparations of barley food, mudga, horse gram, and aged rice;

sanskrit_iast:
tiktarukṣāṇi śākāni tiktāni haritāni ca /
:p 29
tailāni tilaśigrukavibhītakeṅgudāni ca //
meaning:
तिक्तरुक्षाणि शाकानि तिक्तानि हरितानि च /
:प् 29
तैलानि तिलशिग्रुकविभीतकेङ्गुदानि च //

sanskrit_iast:
mudgāḥ sayavagodhūmā dhānyaṃ varṣasthatañca yat /
jāṅgalasya rasaḥ śasto bhojane rājayakṣmiṇāṃ //
meaning:
मुद्गाः सयवगोधूमा धान्यं वर्षस्थतञ्च यत् /
जाङ्गलस्य रसः शस्तो भोजने राजयक्ष्मिणां //
text_mt:
Mudga with barley and wheat, grain that has aged for a year,
and broth of dry-land animals is commended as food for those suffering from consumption.

sanskrit_iast:
kaulatthamaudgako rāsnāśuṣkamūlakajāṅgalaiḥ /
pūpair vā viskaraiḥ siddhair dadhidāḍimasādhitaiḥ //
meaning:
कौलत्थमौद्गको रास्नाशुष्कमूलकजाङ्गलैः /
पूपैर् वा विस्करैः सिद्धैर् दधिदाडिमसाधितैः //
text_mt:
With horse-gram, mudga, rāsnā, dried radish, and dry-land game,
or cakes, or birds that scatter food, prepared with curd and pomegranate,

sanskrit_iast:
mātulaṅgarasakṣaudradrākṣāvyoṣādisaṃskṛtaiḥ /
yavagodhūmaśālyannair bhojayecchvāsakāsinaṃ //
meaning:
मातुलङ्गरसक्षौद्रद्राक्षाव्योषादिसंस्कृतैः /
यवगोधूमशाल्यन्नैर् भोजयेच्छ्वासकासिनं //
text_mt:
seasoned with citron juice, small honey, grapes, the three pungents, and so on,
with food of barley, wheat, and rice, one should feed one who suffers from asthma and cough.

sanskrit_iast:
daṣamūlavalārāsnākulatthair upasādhitāḥ /
peyāḥ pūparasāḥ kvāthāḥ śvāsahikkānivāraṇāḥ //
meaning:
दषमूलवलारास्नाकुलत्थैर् उपसाधिताः /
पेयाः पूपरसाः क्वाथाः श्वासहिक्कानिवारणाः //
text_mt:
Prepared with the ten roots, balā, rāsnā, and horse gram,
drinks, pastry soups, and decoctions dispel asthma and hiccups.

sanskrit_iast:
śuṣkamūlakakaulatthamūlajāṅgalajairasaiḥ(?) /
yavagodhūmaśālyannaṃ jīrṇam sośīramācaret //
meaning:
शुष्कमूलककौलत्थमूलजाङ्गलजैरसैः(?) /
यवगोधूमशाल्यन्नं जीर्णम् सोशीरमाचरेत् //
text_mt:
With broths made from dried radish, horse gram, roots, and dry-land game,
one should consume aged barley, wheat, and rice food, along with vetiver.

sanskrit_iast:
sothavān saguḍāṃ pathyāṃ khādedvā guḍanāgaram /
takrañca citrakañcobhau grahaṇīroganāśanau //
meaning:
सोथवान् सगुडां पथ्यां खादेद्वा गुडनागरम् /
तक्रञ्च चित्रकञ्चोभौ ग्रहणीरोगनाशनौ //
text_mt:
One with edema should eat chebulic myrobalan with molasses, or molasses with dry ginger.
Both buttermilk and plumbago destroy diseases of the duodenum.

sanskrit_iast:
purāṇayavagodhūmaśālayo jaṅgalo rasaḥ /
mudgāmalakakharjūramṛdvīkāvadarāṇi ca //
meaning:
पुराणयवगोधूमशालयो जङ्गलो रसः /
मुद्गामलकखर्जूरमृद्वीकावदराणि च //
text_mt:
Aged barley, wheat, and rice; meat broth of dry-land animals;
mudga, āmalakī, dates, grapes, and jujube fruits;

sanskrit_iast:
madhu sarpiḥ payaḥ śakraṃ nimbaparpaṭakau vṛṣam /
takrāriṣṭāś ca(1) śasyante satataṃ vātarogiṇām //
meaning:
मधु सर्पिः पयः शक्रं निम्बपर्पटकौ वृषम् /
तक्रारिष्टाश् च(1) शस्यन्ते सततं वातरोगिणाम् //
text_mt:
honey, ghee, milk, curd, neem, parpaṭaka, and vāsā,
and fermented buttermilk preparations are constantly commended for patients of wind disorders.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdrogiṇo virecyāstu pippalyo hikkināṃ hitāḥ /
takrāvalālasindhūni muktāni śiśirāmbhasā //
meaning:
हृद्रोगिणो विरेच्यास्तु पिप्पल्यो हिक्किनां हिताः /
तक्रावलालसिन्धूनि मुक्तानि शिशिराम्भसा //
text_mt:
Those with heart disease must be purged; long pepper is beneficial for those with hiccups;
churned curd with black salt, mixed with cold water,

sanskrit_iast:
muktāḥ sauvarcalājādi madyaṃ śastaṃ madātyaye(2) /
sakṣaudrapayasā lākṣāṃ pivecca kṣatavānnaraḥ //
:n
1 bhadrāviṣṭāśceti kha..
2 sadāmaye iti ña.. / damātyaye iti ṭa..
:p 30
meaning:
मुक्ताः सौवर्चलाजादि मद्यं शस्तं मदात्यये(2) /
सक्षौद्रपयसा लाक्षां पिवेच्च क्षतवान्नरः //
:न्
1 भद्राविष्टाश्चेति ख..
2 सदामये इति ञ.. / दमात्यये इति ट..
:प् 30
text_mt:
pearls, black salt, and roasted grain; wine is commended in alcohol intoxication;
and an injured person should drink lac resin with milk and small honey.
[Note]
1. 'bhadrāviṣṭāś ca' in manuscript kha.
2. In manuscript ña, “sadāmaye”; in manuscript ṭa, “damātyaye”.
[Section] 30

sanskrit_iast:
kṣayaṃ māṃsarasāhāro vahnisaṃrakṣaṇājjayet /
śālayo bhojane raktā nīvārakalamādayaḥ //
meaning:
क्षयं मांसरसाहारो वह्निसंरक्षणाज्जयेत् /
शालयो भोजने रक्ता नीवारकलमादयः //
text_mt:
One should conquer consumption through a diet of meat broth by preserving the digestive fire.
Red rice, wild rice, kalamā rice, and the like are recommended for food;

sanskrit_iast:
yavānnavikṛtirmāsaṃ śākaṃ sauvarcalaṃ śaṭī /
pathyā tathaivārśasāṃ yanmaṇḍaṃ takrañca vāriṇā(1) //
meaning:
यवान्नविकृतिर्मासं शाकं सौवर्चलं शटी /
पथ्या तथैवार्शसां यन्मण्डं तक्रञ्च वारिणा(1) //
text_mt:
preparations of barley, meat, suvarcala greens, and śaṭī,
and likewise for piles, yellow myrobalan, rice scum, and buttermilk with water.

sanskrit_iast:
mustābhyāsas tathā lepaścitrakeṇa haridrayā /
yavānnavikṛtiḥ śālirvāstūkaṃ sasuvarcalam //
meaning:
मुस्ताभ्यासस् तथा लेपश्चित्रकेण हरिद्रया /
यवान्नविकृतिः शालिर्वास्तूकं ससुवर्चलम् //
text_mt:
Constant use of mustā, an ointment with leadwort and turmeric,
preparations of barley, winter rice, and goosefoot with suvarcala [are beneficial].

sanskrit_iast:
trapuṣarvārugodhūmāḥ kṣīrekṣughṛtasaṃyutāḥ /
mūtrakṛcchre ca śastāḥ syuḥ pāne maṇḍasurādayaḥ //
meaning:
त्रपुषर्वारुगोधूमाः क्षीरेक्षुघृतसंयुताः /
मूत्रकृच्छ्रे च शस्ताः स्युः पाने मण्डसुरादयः //
text_mt:
Cucumbers, snake melons, and wheat combined with milk, sugarcane juice, and ghee,
and for dysuria, rice scum, wine, and the like are recommended for drink.

sanskrit_iast:
lājāḥ śaktus tathā kṣaudraṃ śūnyaṃ māṃsaṃ parūṣakam /
vārtākulāvaśikhinaśchardighnāḥ pānakāni ca //
meaning:
लाजाः शक्तुस् तथा क्षौद्रं शून्यं मांसं परूषकम् /
वार्ताकुलावशिखिनश्छर्दिघ्नाः पानकानि च //
text_mt:
Parched grain, barley flour, honey, dried meat, parūṣaka fruit,
eggplants, kulmāṣa grains, quail, partridge, and syrups cure vomiting.

sanskrit_iast:
śālyannantoyapayasī kevaloṣṇe śṛte 'pi vā /
tṛṣṇāghne mustaguḍayorguṭikā vā mukhe dhṛtā //
meaning:
शाल्यन्नन्तोयपयसी केवलोष्णे शृते ऽपि वा /
तृष्णाघ्ने मुस्तगुडयोर्गुटिका वा मुखे धृता //
text_mt:
Boiled winter rice, water and milk drunk hot or boiled,
or a pill of mustā and jaggery held in the mouth, removes thirst.

sanskrit_iast:
yavānnavikṛtiḥ pūpaṃ(2) śuṣkamūlakajantathā /
śākaṃ paṭolavetrāgramurustambhavināśanam //
meaning:
यवान्नविकृतिः पूपं(2) शुष्कमूलकजन्तथा /
शाकं पटोलवेत्राग्रमुरुस्तम्भविनाशनम् //
text_mt:
A preparation of barley, cake, and dried radishes,
and greens of trichosanthes and cane-tips destroy stiffness of the thighs.

sanskrit_iast:
mudgāḍhakamasūrāṇāṃ satilair jāṅgalairasaiḥ(?) /
sasaindhavaghṛtadrākṣāśuṇṭhyāmalakakolajaiḥ //
meaning:
मुद्गाढकमसूराणां सतिलैर् जाङ्गलैरसैः(?) /
ससैन्धवघृतद्राक्षाशुण्ठ्यामलककोलजैः //
text_mt:
With juices of mung bean, pigeon pea, and lentil, together with sesame and broth of wild animals,
prepared with rock salt, ghee, raisins, dried ginger, emblic myrobalan, and jujube,

sanskrit_iast:
yūṣaiḥ purāṇagodhūmayavaśālyannamabhyaset /
visarpī sasitākṣaudramṛdvīkādāḍimodakam //
meaning:
यूषैः पुराणगोधूमयवशाल्यन्नमभ्यसेत् /
विसर्पी ससिताक्षौद्रमृद्वीकादाडिमोदकम् //
text_mt:
with these soups one should eat old wheat, barley, and winter rice.
For erysipelas: sugar, honey, raisins, and pomegranate water;

sanskrit_iast:
raktayaṣṭikagodhūmayavamudgādikaṃ laghu /
kākamārī ca vetrāgraṃ vāstukañca suvarcalā //
meaning:
रक्तयष्टिकगोधूमयवमुद्गादिकं लघु /
काकमारी च वेत्राग्रं वास्तुकञ्च सुवर्चला //
text_mt:
red yaṣṭika rice, wheat, barley, mung beans, and the like, which are light,
black nightshade, cane-tips, goosefoot, and suvarcala greens;

sanskrit_iast:
vātaśoṇitanāśāya toyaṃ śastaṃ sitaṃ madhu /
:n
1 pathyā tathaiva kāśasya maṇḍaṃ takrañca vāruṇamiti kha.. , ña.. ,
ca
2 yūṣamiti kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 31
nāśārogeśu ca hitaṃ ghṛtaṃ durvāprasādhitam //
meaning:
वातशोणितनाशाय तोयं शस्तं सितं मधु /
:न्
1 पथ्या तथैव काशस्य मण्डं तक्रञ्च वारुणमिति ख.. , ञ.. ,
च
2 यूषमिति ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 31
नाशारोगेशु च हितं घृतं दुर्वाप्रसाधितम् //
text_mt:
for destroying gout, water, sugar, and honey are praised.
[Footnote]
1. In manuscripts kha, ña, and ca: “pathyā tathaiva kāśasya maṇḍaṃ takrañca vāruṇam”.
2. In manuscripts kha and ja: “yūṣam”.
[Section] 31
And in diseases of the nose, ghee prepared with dūrvā grass is beneficial.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛṅgarājarase siddhaṃ tailaṃ dhātrīrase 'pi vā /
naśyaṃ sarvāmayeṣviṣṭaṃ mūrdhajantūdbhaveṣu ca //
meaning:
भृङ्गराजरसे सिद्धं तैलं धात्रीरसे ऽपि वा /
नश्यं सर्वामयेष्विष्टं मूर्धजन्तूद्भवेषु च //
text_mt:
Oil prepared in the juice of bhṛṅgarāja or in the juice of emblic myrobalan
is recommended as nasal drops in all diseases and when worms arise in the head.

sanskrit_iast:
śītatoyānnapānañca tilānāṃ vipra bhakṣaṇam /
dvijadārḍhyakaraṃ proktaṃ tathā tuṣṭikaramparam //
meaning:
शीततोयान्नपानञ्च तिलानां विप्र भक्षणम् /
द्विजदार्ढ्यकरं प्रोक्तं तथा तुष्टिकरम्परम् //
text_mt:
Food and drink with cold water, and eating sesame seeds, O brāhmaṇa,
is declared to produce firmness of the teeth and to give supreme satisfaction.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇḍūṣaṃ tilatailena dvijadārḍhyakaraṃ paraṃ /
viḍaṅgacūrṇaṃ gomūtraṃ sarvatra kṛmināśane //
meaning:
गण्डूषं तिलतैलेन द्विजदार्ढ्यकरं परं /
विडङ्गचूर्णं गोमूत्रं सर्वत्र कृमिनाशने //
text_mt:
Gargling with sesame oil produces supreme firmness of the teeth.
Powder of viḍaṅga with cow's urine destroys worms in every circumstance.

sanskrit_iast:
dhātrīphalānyathājyañca śirolepanamuttamam /
śirorogavināśāya snigdhamuṣṇañca bhojanam //
meaning:
धात्रीफलान्यथाज्यञ्च शिरोलेपनमुत्तमम् /
शिरोरोगविनाशाय स्निग्धमुष्णञ्च भोजनम् //
text_mt:
Fruits of emblic myrobalan with ghee are an excellent plaster for the head.
For curing head diseases, warm and unctuous food [is prescribed].

sanskrit_iast:
tailaṃ vā vastamūtrañca karṇapūraṇamuttamam /
karṇaśūlavināśāya sarvaśuktāni(1) vā dvija //
meaning:
तैलं वा वस्तमूत्रञ्च कर्णपूरणमुत्तमम् /
कर्णशूलविनाशाय सर्वशुक्तानि(1) वा द्विज //
text_mt:
Oil or goat's urine is an excellent ear-drop;
or all vinegars, O twice-born, destroy earache.

sanskrit_iast:
girimṛccandanaṃ lākṣā mālatī kalikā tathā /
saṃyojyā yā kṛtā vartiḥ kṣataśukraharī tu sā //
meaning:
गिरिमृच्चन्दनं लाक्षा मालती कलिका तथा /
संयोज्या या कृता वर्तिः क्षतशुक्रहरी तु सा //
text_mt:
Red chalk, sandalwood, lac, and jasmine bud
combined into a wick destroy corneal ulcer.

sanskrit_iast:
vyoṣaṃ triphalayā yuktaṃ tucchakañca tathā jalam /
sarvākṣirogaśamanaṃ tathā caiva rasāñjanaṃ //
meaning:
व्योषं त्रिफलया युक्तं तुच्छकञ्च तथा जलम् /
सर्वाक्षिरोगशमनं तथा चैव रसाञ्जनं //
text_mt:
The three pungents joined with the three fruits, and empty water,
and rasāñjana soothe all eye diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
ājyabhṛṣṭaṃ śilāpiṣṭaṃ lodhrakāñjikasaindhavaiḥ /
āścyotanāvināśāya sarvanetrāmaye hitam //
meaning:
आज्यभृष्टं शिलापिष्टं लोध्रकाञ्जिकसैन्धवैः /
आश्च्योतनाविनाशाय सर्वनेत्रामये हितम् //
text_mt:
Lodhra fried in ghee, ground on a stone with sour gruel and rock salt,
is beneficial in eye-drops for curing all afflictions of the eye.

sanskrit_iast:
girimṛccandanair lepo vahirnetrasya śasyate /
netrāmayavighātārthaṃ triphalāṃ śīlayet sadā //
meaning:
गिरिमृच्चन्दनैर् लेपो वहिर्नेत्रस्य शस्यते /
नेत्रामयविघातार्थं त्रिफलां शीलयेत् सदा //
text_mt:
A plaster of red chalk and sandalwood is recommended outside the eye.
To counteract eye diseases, one should continually use the three fruits.

sanskrit_iast:
rātrau tu madhusarpirbhyāṃ dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ /
śatāvarīrase siddhau vṛṣyau kṣīraghṛtau smṛtau //
meaning:
रात्रौ तु मधुसर्पिर्भ्यां दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः /
शतावरीरसे सिद्धौ वृष्यौ क्षीरघृतौ स्मृतौ //
text_mt:
At night, one desiring a long life [takes them] with honey and ghee.
Milk and ghee prepared in the juice of asparagus are regarded as aphrodisiacs.

sanskrit_iast:
kalambikāni māṣāś ca vṛṣyau kṣīraghṛtau tathā /
:n
1 sarvaśuklānnīti kha..
:p 32
āyuṣyā triphalā jñeyā pūrvavanmadhukānvitā //
meaning:
कलम्बिकानि माषाश् च वृष्यौ क्षीरघृतौ तथा /
:न्
1 सर्वशुक्लान्नीति ख..
:प् 32
आयुष्या त्रिफला ज्ञेया पूर्ववन्मधुकान्विता //
text_mt:
Kalambīka and black gram, as well as milk and ghee, are aphrodisiacs;
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha: “sarvaśuklānni”.
[Section] 32
the three fruits combined with licorice as before are to be known as promoting longevity.

sanskrit_iast:
madhukādirasopetā balīpalitanāśinī /
vacāsiddhaghṛtaṃ vipra bhūtadoṣavināśanam //
meaning:
मधुकादिरसोपेता बलीपलितनाशिनी /
वचासिद्धघृतं विप्र भूतदोषविनाशनम् //
text_mt:
Endowed with the juice of licorice and other [drugs], they destroy wrinkles and grey hair.
Ghee prepared with sweet flag, O brāhmaṇa, destroys spirit afflictions;

sanskrit_iast:
kavyaṃ buddhipradañcaiva(1) tathā sarvārthasādhanam /
valākalkakaṣāyeṇa siddhamabhyañjane hitam //
meaning:
कव्यं बुद्धिप्रदञ्चैव(1) तथा सर्वार्थसाधनम् /
वलाकल्ककषायेण सिद्धमभ्यञ्जने हितम् //
text_mt:
it confers poetic wisdom and accomplishes all aims.
[Ghee] prepared with the paste and decoction of balā is beneficial for massage,

sanskrit_iast:
rāsnāsahacarair vāpi tailaṃ vātavikāriṇām /
anabhiṣyandi yaccānnaṃ tadbraṇeṣu praśasyate //
meaning:
रास्नासहचरैर् वापि तैलं वातविकारिणाम् /
अनभिष्यन्दि यच्चान्नं तद्ब्रणेषु प्रशस्यते //
text_mt:
or oil [prepared] with rāsnā and sahacara for those suffering from wind disorders.
And whatever food is non-catarrhal is recommended for wounds.

sanskrit_iast:
śaktupiṇḍī tathaivāmlā pācanāya praśasyate /
pakvasya ca tathā bhede nimbacūrṇañca ropaṇe //
meaning:
शक्तुपिण्डी तथैवाम्ला पाचनाय प्रशस्यते /
पक्वस्य च तथा भेदे निम्बचूर्णञ्च रोपणे //
text_mt:
A sour ball of barley flour is recommended for suppurating;
and for the bursting of a ripe [abscess], nimba powder [is praised] for healing.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā śūcyupacāraś ca(2) balikarma viśeṣataḥ /
sūtikā ca tathā rakṣā prāṇināntu sadā hitā //
meaning:
तथा शूच्युपचारश् च(2) बलिकर्म विशेषतः /
सूतिका च तथा रक्षा प्राणिनान्तु सदा हिता //
text_mt:
So too, pure practice, and especially sacrificial offerings,
and protection in the lying-in room are always beneficial to living beings.

sanskrit_iast:
bhakṣaṇaṃ nimbapatrāṇāṃ sarpadaṣṭasya bheṣajam /
tālanimbadalaṅkeśyaṃ jīrṇantailaṃ yavāghṛtam //
meaning:
भक्षणं निम्बपत्राणां सर्पदष्टस्य भेषजम् /
तालनिम्बदलङ्केश्यं जीर्णन्तैलं यवाघृतम् //
text_mt:
Eating nimba leaves is a remedy for one bitten by a snake.
Palm-fruit and nimba leaves are good for hair; aged oil and barley ghee [are effective].

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpo vṛścikadaṣṭasya śikhipatraghṛtena vā /
arkakṣīreṇa saṃpiṣṭaṃ lopā vījaṃ palāśajaṃ //
meaning:
धूपो वृश्चिकदष्टस्य शिखिपत्रघृतेन वा /
अर्कक्षीरेण संपिष्टं लोपा वीजं पलाशजं //
text_mt:
Incense [is prescribed] for one bitten by a scorpion, or with peacock feathers and ghee;
or seeds of palāśa ground with the milk of calotropis [made into] a plaster.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛścikārtasya kṛṣṇā vā śivā ca phalasaṃyutā(3) /
arkakṣīraṃ tilaṃ tailaṃ palalañca guḍaṃ samam //
meaning:
वृश्चिकार्तस्य कृष्णा वा शिवा च फलसंयुता(3) /
अर्कक्षीरं तिलं तैलं पललञ्च गुडं समम् //
text_mt:
For one afflicted by a scorpion, black pepper or yellow myrobalan with fruits [may be used].
Calotropis milk, sesame, oil, meat, and jaggery in equal parts,

sanskrit_iast:
pānājjayati durvāraṃ śvaviṣaṃ śīghrameva tu /
pītvā mūlaṃ trivṛttulyaṃ taṇḍulīyasya sarpiṣā //
meaning:
पानाज्जयति दुर्वारं श्वविषं शीघ्रमेव तु /
पीत्वा मूलं त्रिवृत्तुल्यं तण्डुलीयस्य सर्पिषा //
text_mt:
by drinking, swiftly overcomes the irresistible poison of a dog.
Having drunk the root of taṇḍulīya equal to trivṛt along with ghee,

sanskrit_iast:
sarpakīṭaviṣāṇyāśu jayatyatibalānyapi /
candanaṃ padmakaṅkuṣṭhaṃ latāmbūśīrapāṭalāḥ //
:n
1 kanṭhyaṃ vṛddhipradañcaiveti kha..
2 pratyupacāraiśceti kha..
3 kalasaṃyuteti ka..
:p 33
meaning:
सर्पकीटविषाण्याशु जयत्यतिबलान्यपि /
चन्दनं पद्मकङ्कुष्ठं लताम्बूशीरपाटलाः //
:न्
1 कन्ठ्यं वृद्धिप्रदञ्चैवेति ख..
2 प्रत्युपचारैश्चेति ख..
3 कलसंयुतेति क..
:प् 33
text_mt:
one swiftly conquers the poison of snakes and insects, even when extremely strong.
Sandalwood, padmaka, costus, latā, vetiver, and pāṭalā,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha: “kaṇṭhyaṃ vṛddhipradañcaiva”.
2. In manuscript kha: “pratyupacāraiśceti”.
3. In manuscript ka: “kalasaṃyuteti”.
[Section] 33

sanskrit_iast:
nirguṇḍī śārivā selurlūtāviṣaharo gadaḥ /
śirovirecanaṃ śastaṃ guḍanāgarakaṃ dvija //
meaning:
निर्गुण्डी शारिवा सेलुर्लूताविषहरो गदः /
शिरोविरेचनं शस्तं गुडनागरकं द्विज //
text_mt:
nirguṇḍī, Indian sarsaparilla, and selu form an ailment-curing remedy against spider poison.
For head evacuation, jaggery and ginger are commended, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
snehapāne tathā vastau tailaṃ dhṛtamanuttamam /
svedanīyaḥ paro vahniḥ śītāmbhaḥstambhanaṃ param //
meaning:
स्नेहपाने तथा वस्तौ तैलं धृतमनुत्तमम् /
स्वेदनीयः परो वह्निः शीताम्भःस्तम्भनं परम् //
text_mt:
In the drinking of unctuous substances and in enemas, oil and ghee are unsurpassed.
Fire is the supreme sweating agent, and cold water is the supreme astringent.

sanskrit_iast:
trivṛddhi recane śreṣṭhā vamane madanaṃ tathā /
vastirvireko vamanaṃ tailaṃ sarpis tathā madhu /
vātapittabalāśānāṃ krameṇa paramauṣadhaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe siddhauṣadhāni
nāmāṣṭsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athaikonāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sarvarogaharāṇyauṣadhāni
meaning:
त्रिवृद्धि रेचने श्रेष्ठा वमने मदनं तथा /
वस्तिर्विरेको वमनं तैलं सर्पिस् तथा मधु /
वातपित्तबलाशानां क्रमेण परमौषधं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सिद्धौषधानि
नामाष्ट्सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकोनाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सर्वरोगहराण्यौषधानि
text_mt:
Trivṛt is best for purging, and madana fruit for vomiting;
enema, purging, and vomiting, as well as oil, ghee, and honey,
are the supreme remedies respectively for wind, bile, and phlegm.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-eighth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named “Proven Remedies”.
Now the two hundred and seventy-ninth chapter:
Remedies Destroying All Diseases

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
śārīramānamāgantusahajā vyādhayo matāḥ /
śārīrā jvarakuṣṭhādyā krodhādyā mānasā matāḥ //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
शारीरमानमागन्तुसहजा व्याधयो मताः /
शारीरा ज्वरकुष्ठाद्या क्रोधाद्या मानसा मताः //

sanskrit_iast:
āgantavo vighātotthā sahajāḥ kṣujjarādayaḥ /
śārīrāgantunāśāya sūryavāre ghṛtaṃ guḍam //
meaning:
आगन्तवो विघातोत्था सहजाः क्षुज्जरादयः /
शारीरागन्तुनाशाय सूर्यवारे घृतं गुडम् //
text_mt:
exogenous [diseases] arise from trauma; innate [diseases] are hunger, old age, and so on.
For the destruction of bodily and exogenous [diseases], on a Sunday one should offer

sanskrit_iast:
lavaṇaṃ sahiraṇyañca viprāyāpūpamarpayet /
candre cābhyaṅgado vipre sarvarogaiḥ pramucyate //
meaning:
लवणं सहिरण्यञ्च विप्रायापूपमर्पयेत् /
चन्द्रे चाभ्यङ्गदो विप्रे सर्वरोगैः प्रमुच्यते //
text_mt:
ghee, jaggery, salt, and sweet cakes along with gold to a brāhmaṇa;
and giving an unction on a Monday to a brāhmaṇa, one is freed from all diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
tailaṃ śanaiś care dadyādāśvine gorasānnadaḥ /
ghṛtena payasā liṅgaṃ saṃsnāpya syādrugujjhitaḥ //
:p 34
meaning:
तैलं शनैश् चरे दद्यादाश्विने गोरसान्नदः /
घृतेन पयसा लिङ्गं संस्नाप्य स्याद्रुगुज्झितः //
:प् 34
text_mt:
One should give oil on a Saturday; in the month of Āśvina, giving dairy products and food,
and bathing the liṅga with ghee and milk, one becomes free from disease.
[Section] 34

sanskrit_iast:
gāyatryā hāvayedvahnau dūrvāntrimadhurāplutām /
yasmin bhe vyādhimāpnoti tasmin snānaṃ baliḥ śubhe //
meaning:
गायत्र्या हावयेद्वह्नौ दूर्वान्त्रिमधुराप्लुताम् /
यस्मिन् भे व्याधिमाप्नोति तस्मिन् स्नानं बलिः शुभे //
text_mt:
One should sacrifice into the fire with the Gāyatrī dūrvā grass smeared with the three sweets.
Under whichever asterism one contracts a disease, under that auspicious one bath and offering [are prescribed].

sanskrit_iast:
mānasānāṃ rujādīnāṃ viṣṇoḥ stotraṃ haraṃ bhavet /
vātapittakaphā doṣā dhātavaś ca tathā śṛṇu //
meaning:
मानसानां रुजादीनां विष्णोः स्तोत्रं हरं भवेत् /
वातपित्तकफा दोषा धातवश् च तथा शृणु //
text_mt:
For mental afflictions and the like, a hymn of praise to Viṣṇu will be the remover.
Wind, bile, and phlegm are the humours, and also the bodily tissues; hear about them:

sanskrit_iast:
bhuktaṃ pakvāśayādannaṃ dvidhā yāti ca suśruta /
aṃśenaikena kiṭṭadvaṃ rasatāñcāpareṇa ca //
meaning:
भुक्तं पक्वाशयादन्नं द्विधा याति च सुश्रुत /
अंशेनैकेन किट्टद्वं रसताञ्चापरेण च //
text_mt:
O Suśruta, the food eaten from the digestive tract goes two ways:
by one portion into waste, and into the state of nutrient fluid by the other.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṭṭabhāgo malastatra vinmūtrasvedadūṣikāḥ /
nāsāmalaṅkarṇamalaṃ tathā dehamalañca yat //
meaning:
किट्टभागो मलस्तत्र विन्मूत्रस्वेददूषिकाः /
नासामलङ्कर्णमलं तथा देहमलञ्च यत् //
text_mt:
There the waste portion is excretion: feces, urine, sweat, rheum of the eyes,
nasal mucus, earwax, and whatever is bodily excrement.

sanskrit_iast:
rasabhāgādrasastatra samācchoṇitatāṃ vrajet /
māṃsaṃ raktattito medo medaso 'sthnaś ca sambhavaḥ //
meaning:
रसभागाद्रसस्तत्र समाच्छोणिततां व्रजेत् /
मांसं रक्तत्तितो मेदो मेदसो ऽस्थ्नश् च सम्भवः //
text_mt: From the nutrient part, the chyle there duly turns into blood; / from blood, flesh; from that, fat; and from fat occurs the production of bone.

sanskrit_iast:
asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukādrāgastathaujasaḥ /
deśamārtiṃ balaṃ śaktiṃ kālaṃ prakṛtimeva ca //
meaning:
अस्थ्नो मज्जा ततः शुक्रं शुकाद्रागस्तथौजसः /
देशमार्तिं बलं शक्तिं कालं प्रकृतिमेव च //
text_mt: From bone comes marrow; from that, semen; from semen comes lustrous vigor, and similarly vitality. / Having considered the place, the disease, the bodily strength, digestive power, season, and constitution,

sanskrit_iast:
jñātvā cikitsataṃ kuryādbheṣajasya tathā balam /
tithiṃ riktāntyajed bhaumaṃ mandabhandāruṇograkam //
meaning:
ज्ञात्वा चिकित्सतं कुर्याद्भेषजस्य तथा बलम् /
तिथिं रिक्तान्त्यजेद् भौमं मन्दभन्दारुणोग्रकम् //
text_mt: as well as the strength of the medicine, one should administer treatment. / One should avoid an empty lunar day, Tuesday, Saturday, and a fierce, unfavorable [day].

sanskrit_iast:
harigodvijacandrārkasurādīn pratipūjya ca /
śṛṇu mantramimaṃ vidvan bheṣajārambhamācaret //
meaning:
हरिगोद्विजचन्द्रार्कसुरादीन् प्रतिपूज्य च /
शृणु मन्त्रमिमं विद्वन् भेषजारम्भमाचरेत् //
text_mt: Having worshipped Hari, the cow, the twice-born, the moon, the sun, the gods, and others, / listen to this mantra, O wise one, and begin [administering] the medicine:

sanskrit_iast:
brahmadakṣāśvirudrendrabhūcandrārkānilānalāḥ /
ṛṣayaś cauṣadhigrāmā bhūtasaṅghāś ca pāntu te //
meaning:
ब्रह्मदक्षाश्विरुद्रेन्द्रभूचन्द्रार्कानिलानलाः /
ऋषयश् चौषधिग्रामा भूतसङ्घाश् च पान्तु ते //
text_mt: "May Brahmā, Dakṣa, the Aśvins, Rudra, Indra, Earth, the Moon, the Sun, Wind, and Fire, / the sages, the multitude of medicinal herbs, and the hosts of beings protect you!

sanskrit_iast:
rasāyanamivarṣīṇāṃ devānāmamṛtaṃ yathā /
sudhevottamanāgānāṃ bhaiṣajyamidamastu te //
meaning:
रसायनमिवर्षीणां देवानाममृतं यथा /
सुधेवोत्तमनागानां भैषज्यमिदमस्तु ते //
text_mt: Just as the elixir of life is to the sages, just as nectar is to the gods, / just as heavenly ambrosia is to the foremost serpents, so may this medicine be to you!"

sanskrit_iast:
vātaśleṣmātako deśo bahuvṛkṣo bahūdakaḥ /
anūpaḍtibikhyāto jāṅgalastadvivarjitaḥ //
meaning:
वातश्लेष्मातको देशो बहुवृक्षो बहूदकः /
अनूपड्तिबिख्यातो जाङ्गलस्तद्विवर्जितः //
text_mt: A region that aggravates wind and phlegm, having many trees and much water, / is known as marshy; the arid [region] is devoid of these.

sanskrit_iast:
kiñcidvṛkṣodako deśas tathā sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
:p 35
jāṅgalaḥ pittabahulo madhyaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
किञ्चिद्वृक्षोदको देशस् तथा साधारणः स्मृतः /
:प् 35
जाङ्गलः पित्तबहुलो मध्यः साधारणः स्मृतः //
text_mt:
A region with some trees and water is regarded as moderate.
[Page 35]
The arid [region] has an excess of bile; the intermediate is regarded as moderate.

sanskrit_iast:
rūkṣmaḥ śītaś calo vāyuḥ pittamuṣṇaṃ kaṭutrayam /
sthirāmlasnigdhamadhuraṃ balāśañca pracakṣate //
meaning:
रूक्ष्मः शीतश् चलो वायुः पित्तमुष्णं कटुत्रयम् /
स्थिराम्लस्निग्धमधुरं बलाशञ्च प्रचक्षते //
text_mt: Wind is dry, cold, and mobile; bile is hot, pungent, and sharp; / phlegm is declared to be stable, sour, unctuous, and sweet.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛddhiḥ samānair eteṣāṃ viparītair viparyayaḥ /
rasāḥ svādvamlalavaṇāḥ śleṣmalā vāyunāśanāḥ //
meaning:
वृद्धिः समानैर् एतेषां विपरीतैर् विपर्ययः /
रसाः स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः श्लेष्मला वायुनाशनाः //
text_mt: Their increase is caused by similar [qualities], their decrease by opposite ones. / Tastes that are sweet, sour, and salty increase phlegm and destroy wind.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭutiktakaṣāyāś ca vātalāḥ śleṣmanāśanāḥ /
kaṭvamlalavaṇā jñeyās tathā pittavivardhanāḥ //
meaning:
कटुतिक्तकषायाश् च वातलाः श्लेष्मनाशनाः /
कट्वम्ललवणा ज्ञेयास् तथा पित्तविवर्धनाः //
text_mt: Pungent, bitter, and astringent [tastes] increase wind and destroy phlegm. / Pungent, sour, and salty [tastes] are to be known as increasing bile.

sanskrit_iast:
tiktasvādukaṣāyāś ca tathā pittavināśanāḥ /
rasasyaitadguṇaṃ nāsti vipākasyaitadiṣyate //
meaning:
तिक्तस्वादुकषायाश् च तथा पित्तविनाशनाः /
रसस्यैतद्गुणं नास्ति विपाकस्यैतदिष्यते //
text_mt: Bitter, sweet, and astringent [tastes] destroy bile. / This is not a quality of the taste [alone]; it is held to belong to the post-digestive effect.

sanskrit_iast:
vīryoṣṇāḥ kaphavātaghnāḥ śītāḥ pittavināśanāḥ /
prabhāvatas tathā karma te kurvanti ca suśruta //
meaning:
वीर्योष्णाः कफवातघ्नाः शीताः पित्तविनाशनाः /
प्रभावतस् तथा कर्म ते कुर्वन्ति च सुश्रुत //
text_mt: Substances hot in potency destroy phlegm and wind; cold ones destroy bile; / and they also act by their specific potency, O Suśruta.

sanskrit_iast:
śiśire ca vasante ca nidāghe ca tathā kramāt /
cayaprakopapraśamāḥ kaphasya tu prakīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
शिशिरे च वसन्ते च निदाघे च तथा क्रमात् /
चयप्रकोपप्रशमाः कफस्य तु प्रकीर्तिताः //
text_mt: In the cold season, spring, and summer, respectively, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of phlegm are proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
nidāghavarṣārātrau ca tathā śaradi suśruta /
cayaprakopapraśamāḥ pavanasya prakīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
निदाघवर्षारात्रौ च तथा शरदि सुश्रुत /
चयप्रकोपप्रशमाः पवनस्य प्रकीर्तिताः //
text_mt: In summer, the rainy season, and autumn, O Suśruta, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of wind are proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
meghakāle ca śaradi hemante ca yathākramāt /
cayaprakopapraśamās tathā pittasya kīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
मेघकाले च शरदि हेमन्ते च यथाक्रमात् /
चयप्रकोपप्रशमास् तथा पित्तस्य कीर्तिताः //
text_mt: In the rainy season, autumn, and early winter, respectively, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of bile are declared.

sanskrit_iast:
varṣādyo visargastu hemantādyās tathā trayaḥ /
śiśirādyās tathādānaṃ grīṣmāntā ṛtavastrayaḥ //
meaning:
वर्षाद्यो विसर्गस्तु हेमन्ताद्यास् तथा त्रयः /
शिशिराद्यास् तथादानं ग्रीष्मान्ता ऋतवस्त्रयः //
text_mt: The release [period] begins with the rainy season, consisting of the three starting with early winter; / the period of absorption begins with the cold season, consisting of the three seasons ending with summer.

sanskrit_iast:
saumyo visargastvādānamāgneyaṃ parikīrtitam /
varṣādīṃstrīnṛtūn somaś caran paryāyaśo rasān //
meaning:
सौम्यो विसर्गस्त्वादानमाग्नेयं परिकीर्तितम् /
वर्षादींस्त्रीनृतून् सोमश् चरन् पर्यायशो रसान् //
text_mt: The release [period] is lunar, while the period of absorption is proclaimed to be solar. / The moon, traversing the three seasons beginning with the rainy season, in turn,

sanskrit_iast:
janayatyamlalavaṇamadhurāṃstrīn yathākramam /
śiśirādīnṛtūnarkaś caran paryayaśo rasān //
:p 36
meaning:
जनयत्यम्ललवणमधुरांस्त्रीन् यथाक्रमम् /
शिशिरादीनृतूनर्कश् चरन् पर्ययशो रसान् //
:प् 36
text_mt:
produces the three tastes: sour, salty, and sweet, respectively. / The sun, traversing the seasons beginning with the cold season, in turn,
[Page 36]

sanskrit_iast:
vivardhayettathā tiktakaṣāyakaṭukān kramāt /
yathā rajanyo vardhante valamekaṃ hi vardhate //
meaning:
विवर्धयेत्तथा तिक्तकषायकटुकान् क्रमात् /
यथा रजन्यो वर्धन्ते वलमेकं हि वर्धते //
text_mt: increases bitter, astringent, and pungent [tastes] in succession. / As the nights lengthen, strength alone increases;

sanskrit_iast:
kramaśo 'tha manuṣyāṇāṃ hīyamānāsu hīyate /
rātribhuktadinānāñca vayasaś ca tathaiva ca //
meaning:
क्रमशो ऽथ मनुष्याणां हीयमानासु हीयते /
रात्रिभुक्तदिनानाञ्च वयसश् च तथैव च //
text_mt: and gradually, as they diminish, it diminishes in human beings. / In the beginning, middle, and end of the night, of digestion, of the day,

sanskrit_iast:
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu kaphapittasamīraṇāḥ /
prakopaṃ yānti kopādau kāle teṣāñcayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
आदिमध्यावसानेषु कफपित्तसमीरणाः /
प्रकोपं यान्ति कोपादौ काले तेषाञ्चयः स्मृतः //
text_mt: and likewise of life, phlegm, bile, and wind / undergo aggravation. Their accumulation is remembered at the time prior to aggravation;

sanskrit_iast:
prakopottarake kāle śamasteṣāṃ prakīrtitaḥ /
adibhojanato vipra tathā cābhojanena ca //
meaning:
प्रकोपोत्तरके काले शमस्तेषां प्रकीर्तितः /
अदिभोजनतो विप्र तथा चाभोजनेन च //
text_mt: their pacification is proclaimed at the time following aggravation. / From overeating, O twice-born one, and likewise from fasting,

sanskrit_iast:
rogā hi sarve jāyante vegodīraṇadhāraṇaiḥ /
annena kukṣerdvāvaṃśāvekaṃ pānena pūrayet //
meaning:
रोगा हि सर्वे जायन्ते वेगोदीरणधारणैः /
अन्नेन कुक्षेर्द्वावंशावेकं पानेन पूरयेत् //
text_mt: indeed all diseases arise, [and also] by exciting or suppressing natural urges. / One should fill two parts of the stomach with food, and one with drink;

sanskrit_iast:
āśrayaṃ pavanādīnāṃ tathaikamavaśeṣayet /
vyādher nidānasya tathā viparītamathauṣadham //
meaning:
आश्रयं पवनादीनां तथैकमवशेषयेत् /
व्याधेर् निदानस्य तथा विपरीतमथौषधम् //
text_mt: and one should leave one part empty for the movement of wind and the others. / Medicine should be administered that is contrary to the disease and its cause;

sanskrit_iast:
kartavyametadevātra mayā sāraṃ prakīrtitam /
nābherūrdhvamadhaś caiva gudaśroṇyostathaiva ca //
meaning:
कर्तव्यमेतदेवात्र मया सारं प्रकीर्तितम् /
नाभेरूर्ध्वमधश् चैव गुदश्रोण्योस्तथैव च //
text_mt: this alone should be done; I have stated the essence here. / Above the navel, below it, and likewise in the anus and pelvis,

sanskrit_iast:
balāśapittavātānāṃ dehe sthānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
tathāpi sarvagāś caite dehe vāyurviśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
बलाशपित्तवातानां देहे स्थानं प्रकीर्तितं /
तथापि सर्वगाश् चैते देहे वायुर्विशेषतः //
text_mt: the locations of phlegm, bile, and wind in the body are declared; / nevertheless, these move throughout the whole body, especially wind.

sanskrit_iast:
dehasya madhye hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ tanmanasaḥ smṛtam /
kṛśo 'lpakeśaś capalo bahuvāgviṣamānalaḥ //
meaning:
देहस्य मध्ये हृदयं स्थानं तन्मनसः स्मृतम् /
कृशो ऽल्पकेशश् चपलो बहुवाग्विषमानलः //
text_mt: The heart in the center of the body is remembered as the seat of the mind. / A person who is emaciated, has little hair, is fickle, talkative, has irregular digestive fire,

sanskrit_iast:
vyomagaś ca tathā svapne vātaprakṛtirucyate /
akālapalitaḥ krodhī prasvedī madhurapriyaḥ //
meaning:
व्योमगश् च तथा स्वप्ने वातप्रकृतिरुच्यते /
अकालपलितः क्रोधी प्रस्वेदी मधुरप्रियः //
text_mt: and moves through the sky in dreams, is said to have a wind constitution. / One whose hair greys prematurely, who is wrathful, sweats profusely, is fond of sweets,

sanskrit_iast:
svapne ca dīptimatprekṣī pittaprakṛtirucyate /
dṛḍhāṅgaḥ sthiracittaś ca suprabhaḥ snigdhasūrdhajaḥ //
meaning:
स्वप्ने च दीप्तिमत्प्रेक्षी पित्तप्रकृतिरुच्यते /
दृढाङ्गः स्थिरचित्तश् च सुप्रभः स्निग्धसूर्धजः //
text_mt: and sees bright lights in dreams, is said to have a bile constitution. / One whose limbs are firm, whose mind is steady, who has good luster, glossy hair,

sanskrit_iast:
śuddhāmbudarśī svapne ca kaphaprakṛtiko naraḥ /
:p 37
tāmasā rājasāś caiva sātvikāś ca tathā smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
शुद्धाम्बुदर्शी स्वप्ने च कफप्रकृतिको नरः /
:प् 37
तामसा राजसाश् चैव सात्विकाश् च तथा स्मृताः //
text_mt:
and sees clear water in dreams, is a person of phlegm constitution.
[Page 37]
They are also regarded as tamasic, rajasic, and sattvic, respectively,

sanskrit_iast:
manuṣyā munirśādūla vātapittakaphātmakāḥ /
raktapittaṃ vyavāyācca gurukarmapravartanaiḥ //
meaning:
मनुष्या मुनिर्शादूल वातपित्तकफात्मकाः /
रक्तपित्तं व्यवायाच्च गुरुकर्मप्रवर्तनैः //
text_mt: O tiger among sages—men characterized by wind, bile, and phlegm. / From sexual intercourse, undertaking heavy labor,

sanskrit_iast:
kadannabhojanādvāyurdehe śokācca kupyati /
vidāhināṃ tatholkānāmuṣṇānnādhvanisevināṃ(1) //
meaning:
कदन्नभोजनाद्वायुर्देहे शोकाच्च कुप्यति /
विदाहिनां तथोल्कानामुष्णान्नाध्वनिसेविनां(1) //
text_mt: eating bad food, and from grief, wind is aggravated in the body. / In those who consume burning substances, firebrands, hot food, and engage in travel,

sanskrit_iast:
pittaṃ prakopamāyāti bhayena ca tathā dvija /
atyambupānagurvannabhojināṃ bhuktaśāyinām //
meaning:
पित्तं प्रकोपमायाति भयेन च तथा द्विज /
अत्यम्बुपानगुर्वन्नभोजिनां भुक्तशायिनाम् //
text_mt: bile becomes aggravated, and likewise from fear, O twice-born one. / In those who drink too much water, eat heavy food, sleep after meals,

sanskrit_iast:
ślekeṣmāprakopamāyāti tathā ye cālasā janāḥ /
vātādyutthāni rogāṇi jñātvā śāmyāni lakṣaṇaiḥ //
meaning:
श्लेकेष्माप्रकोपमायाति तथा ये चालसा जनाः /
वाताद्युत्थानि रोगाणि ज्ञात्वा शाम्यानि लक्षणैः //
text_mt: and people who are indolent, phlegm becomes aggravated. / Having identified diseases arising from wind and the others, which are pacified through their symptoms:

sanskrit_iast:
asthibhaṅgaḥ kaṣāyatvamāsye śuṣkāsyatā tathā /
jṛmbhaṇaṃ lomaharṣaś ca vātikavyādhilakṣaṇam //
meaning:
अस्थिभङ्गः कषायत्वमास्ये शुष्कास्यता तथा /
जृम्भणं लोमहर्षश् च वातिकव्याधिलक्षणम् //
text_mt: bone fracture, astringency in the mouth, dryness of the mouth, / yawning, and horripilation are the signs of a wind-born disease.

sanskrit_iast:
nakhanetraśirāṇāntu pītatvaṃ kaṭutā mukhe /
tṛṣṇā dāhoṣṇatā caiva pittavyādhinidarśanam //
meaning:
नखनेत्रशिराणान्तु पीतत्वं कटुता मुखे /
तृष्णा दाहोष्णता चैव पित्तव्याधिनिदर्शनम् //
text_mt: Yellowness of the nails, eyes, and veins, bitterness in the mouth, / thirst, a burning sensation, and feverish heat are the indicators of a bile disease.

sanskrit_iast:
ālasyañca prasekaś ca gurutā madhurāsyatā /
uṣṇābhilāṣitā ceti ślaiṣmikavyādhilakṣaṇam //
meaning:
आलस्यञ्च प्रसेकश् च गुरुता मधुरास्यता /
उष्णाभिलाषिता चेति श्लैष्मिकव्याधिलक्षणम् //
text_mt: Lethargy, excessive salivation, heaviness, sweetness in the mouth, / and a craving for warmth are the signs of a phlegm disease.

sanskrit_iast:
snigdhoṣṇamannamabhyaṅgastailapānādi vātanut /
ājyaṃ kṣīraṃ sitādyañca candraraśmyādi pittanut //
meaning:
स्निग्धोष्णमन्नमभ्यङ्गस्तैलपानादि वातनुत् /
आज्यं क्षीरं सिताद्यञ्च चन्द्ररश्म्यादि पित्तनुत् //
text_mt: Unctuous, hot food, massage, drinking medicated oils, and the like dispel wind. / Ghee, milk, sugar, and moonbeams dispel bile.

sanskrit_iast:
sakṣaudraṃ triphalātailaṃ vyāyāmādi kaphāpaham /
sarvarogapraśāntyai syadviṣṇordhyānañca pūjanam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sarvarogaharāṇyauṣadhāni
nāmonāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
tatholkānāmuṣmaṇāmadhvasevināmiti kha..
:p 38
:ś athāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
rasādilakṣaṇaṃ
meaning:
सक्षौद्रं त्रिफलातैलं व्यायामादि कफापहम् /
सर्वरोगप्रशान्त्यै स्यद्विष्णोर्ध्यानञ्च पूजनम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सर्वरोगहराण्यौषधानि
नामोनाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
तथोल्कानामुष्मणामध्वसेविनामिति ख..
:प् 38
:श् अथाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
रसादिलक्षणं
text_mt:
Triphalā oil with honey, exercise, and the like remove phlegm. / Meditation upon and worship of Viṣṇu will effect the pacification of all diseases.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and seventy-ninth chapter, entitled "Medicines That Dispel All Diseases."
[Note]
"tatholkānāmuṣmaṇāmadhvasevinām" in manuscript Kha. / [Page 38]
Now, the two hundred and eightieth chapter.
Characteristics of Tastes and Other Properties.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
rasādilakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye bheṣajānāṃ guṇaṃ śṛṇu /
rasavīryavipākajño nṛpādīnrakṣayennaraḥ //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
रसादिलक्षणं वक्ष्ये भेषजानां गुणं शृणु /
रसवीर्यविपाकज्ञो नृपादीन्रक्षयेन्नरः //
text_mt: Dhanvantari said: / I shall state the characteristics of tastes and so forth; listen to the qualities of medicines. / A person who understands taste, potency, and post-digestive effect can protect kings and others.

sanskrit_iast:
rasāḥ svādvamlalavaṇāḥ somajāḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
kaṭutiktakaṣāyāni tathāgneyā mahābhuja //
meaning:
रसाः स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः सोमजाः परिकीर्तिताः /
कटुतिक्तकषायानि तथाग्नेया महाभुज //
text_mt: Sweet, sour, and salty tastes are declared to be born of Soma; / pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes are fiery, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit_iast:
tridhā vipāko dravyasya kaṭvamlalavaṇātmakaḥ /
dvidhā vīyya samuddiṣṭamuṣṇaṃ śītaṃ tathaiva ca //
meaning:
त्रिधा विपाको द्रव्यस्य कट्वम्ललवणात्मकः /
द्विधा वीय्य समुद्दिष्टमुष्णं शीतं तथैव च //
text_mt: The post-digestive effect of a substance is threefold, consisting of pungent, sour, and sweet. / Potency is declared to be twofold: hot and cold.

sanskrit_iast:
anirdeśyaprabhāvaś ca oṣadhīnāṃ dvijottama /
madhuraś ca kaṣāyaś ca tiktaś caiva tathā rasaḥ //
meaning:
अनिर्देश्यप्रभावश् च ओषधीनां द्विजोत्तम /
मधुरश् च कषायश् च तिक्तश् चैव तथा रसः //
text_mt: And the specific potency of medicinal plants is inexplicable, O best of the twice-born. / Sweet, astringent, and bitter tastes

sanskrit_iast:
śītavīryāḥ samuddiṣṭāḥ śeṣāstūṣṇāḥprakīrtitāḥ /
guḍucī tatra tiktapi bhavatyuṣṇātivīryataḥ //
meaning:
शीतवीर्याः समुद्दिष्टाः शेषास्तूष्णाःप्रकीर्तिताः /
गुडुची तत्र तिक्तपि भवत्युष्णातिवीर्यतः //
text_mt: are taught to be cold in potency, while the remaining ones are proclaimed to be hot. / Among them, guḍūcī, though bitter, is hot due to its superior potency.

sanskrit_iast:
uṣṇā kaṣāyāpi tathā pathyā bhavati mānada /
madhuropi tathā māṃsa uṣṇa eva prakīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
उष्णा कषायापि तथा पथ्या भवति मानद /
मधुरोपि तथा मांस उष्ण एव प्रकीर्तितः //
text_mt: Likewise pathyā, though astringent, is hot, O giver of honor; / meat also, though sweet, is declared to be hot.

sanskrit_iast:
lavaṇo madhraś caiva vipākamadhurau smṛtau /
amloṣṇaś ca tathā proktaḥ śeṣāḥ kaṭuvipākinaḥ //
meaning:
लवणो मध्रश् चैव विपाकमधुरौ स्मृतौ /
अम्लोष्णश् च तथा प्रोक्तः शेषाः कटुविपाकिनः //
text_mt: Salty and sweet tastes are taught to have sweet post-digestive effects; / sour is hot, and the rest have pungent post-digestive effects.

sanskrit_iast:
vīryapāke viparyaste prabhāvāttatra niś cayaḥ /
madhuro 'pi kaṭuḥ pāke yacca kṣaudraṃ(1) prakīrtitaṃ //
meaning:
वीर्यपाके विपर्यस्ते प्रभावात्तत्र निश् चयः /
मधुरो ऽपि कटुः पाके यच्च क्षौद्रं(1) प्रकीर्तितं //
text_mt: When potency and post-digestive transformation are inverted, the decision is based on specific action (prabhāva); / thus honey, though sweet, is taught to be pungent in post-digestive effect.

sanskrit_iast:
kvāthayet ṣoḍaśaguṇaṃ viveddravyāccaturguṇam /
:n
1 yavakṣaudramiti kha..
:p 39
kalpanaiṣā kaṣāyasya yatra nokto vidhirbhavet //
meaning:
क्वाथयेत् षोडशगुणं विवेद्द्रव्याच्चतुर्गुणम् /
:न्
1 यवक्षौद्रमिति ख..
:प् 39
कल्पनैषा कषायस्य यत्र नोक्तो विधिर्भवेत् //
text_mt:
One should boil sixteen times [as much water], and drink four times [as much as] the substance.
[Footnote]
1. 'Yavakṣaudram' in manuscript kha. / [page 39]
This is the formulation of a decoction where no specific rule has been declared.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṣāyantu bhavettoyaṃ snehapāke caturguṇaṃ(1) /
dravyatulyaṃ samuddhṛtya dravyaṃ snehaṃ kṣipedbudhaḥ //
meaning:
कषायन्तु भवेत्तोयं स्नेहपाके चतुर्गुणं(1) /
द्रव्यतुल्यं समुद्धृत्य द्रव्यं स्नेहं क्षिपेद्बुधः //
text_mt: The decoction water in cooking unctuous substance should be fourfold; / having taken equal substance to substance, the wise one should add the unctuous substance.

sanskrit_iast:
tāvatpramāṇaṃ dravyasya snehapādaṃ tataḥ kṣipet /
toyavarjantu yaddravyaṃ snehadravyaṃ tathā bhavet //
meaning:
तावत्प्रमाणं द्रव्यस्य स्नेहपादं ततः क्षिपेत् /
तोयवर्जन्तु यद्द्रव्यं स्नेहद्रव्यं तथा भवेत् //
text_mt: One should then add a fourth part of the unctuous substance of the substance's measure; / and that which is substance devoid of water becomes the unctuous substance.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvartitauṣadhaḥ pākaḥ snehānāṃ parikīrtitaḥ /
tattulyatā tu lehyasya tathā bhavati suśruta(2) //
meaning:
संवर्तितौषधः पाकः स्नेहानां परिकीर्तितः /
तत्तुल्यता तु लेह्यस्य तथा भवति सुश्रुत(2) //
text_mt: The cooking of unctuous substances is declared to be [done] when the medicinal paste rolls together into a ball; / its equality, O Suśruta, becomes likewise for an electuary.

sanskrit_iast:
svacchamalpauṣadhaṃ kvāthaṃ kaṣāyañcoktavadbhavet /
akṣaṃ cūrṇasya nirdiṣṭaṃ kaṣāyasya catuṣpalaṃ //
meaning:
स्वच्छमल्पौषधं क्वाथं कषायञ्चोक्तवद्भवेत् /
अक्षं चूर्णस्य निर्दिष्टं कषायस्य चतुष्पलं //
text_mt: A clear decoction with little medicine and an astringent drink are as described; / an akṣa is declared for a powder, and four palas for a decoction.

sanskrit_iast:
madhyamaiṣā smṛtā mātrā nāsti mātrāvikalpanā /
vayaḥ kālaṃ balaṃ vahniṃ deśaṃ dravyaṃ rujaṃ tathā //
meaning:
मध्यमैषा स्मृता मात्रा नास्ति मात्राविकल्पना /
वयः कालं बलं वह्निं देशं द्रव्यं रुजं तथा //
text_mt: This is considered the middling dose; there is no fixed determination of dose; / observing age, season, strength, digestive fire, region, substance, and disease,

sanskrit_iast:
samavekṣya mahābhāga mātrāyāḥ kalpanā bhavet /
saumyāstatra rasāḥ prāyo vijñeyā dhātuvardhanāḥ //
meaning:
समवेक्ष्य महाभाग मात्रायाः कल्पना भवेत् /
सौम्यास्तत्र रसाः प्रायो विज्ञेया धातुवर्धनाः //
text_mt: the formulation of the dosage should be made, O fortunate one. / Gentle tastes there are generally to be known as increasing the bodily tissues.

sanskrit_iast:
madhurāstu viśeṣeṇa vijñeyā dhātuvardhanāḥ /
doṣāṇāñcaiva dhātūnāṃ dravyaṃ samaguṇantu yat //
meaning:
मधुरास्तु विशेषेण विज्ञेया धातुवर्धनाः /
दोषाणाञ्चैव धातूनां द्रव्यं समगुणन्तु यत् //
text_mt: Sweet tastes especially are to be known as increasing the bodily tissues. / A substance that possesses qualities equal to the humors and bodily tissues

sanskrit_iast:
tadeva vṛddhaye jñeyaṃ viparītaṃ kṣamāvaham /
upastambhatrayaṃ proktaṃ dehe 'sminmanujottama //
meaning:
तदेव वृद्धये ज्ञेयं विपरीतं क्षमावहम् /
उपस्तम्भत्रयं प्रोक्तं देहे ऽस्मिन्मनुजोत्तम //
text_mt: is to be known as producing their increase, while one of opposite qualities brings about their decrease. / Three supporting pillars are declared in this body, O best of men:

sanskrit_iast:
āhāro maithunaṃ nidrā teṣu yatnaḥ sadā bhavet /
asevanāt sevanācca atyantaṃ nāśamāpnuyāt //
meaning:
आहारो मैथुनं निद्रा तेषु यत्नः सदा भवेत् /
असेवनात् सेवनाच्च अत्यन्तं नाशमाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: food, sexual intercourse, and sleep; one must always take care in these; / through non-practice or excessive practice one would meet total ruin.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣayasya bṛṃhaṇaṃ kāryaṃ sthuladehasya karṣaṇam /
rakṣaṇaṃ madhyakāyasya dehabhedāstrayo matāḥ //
:n
1 snehapāke ca tadguṇamiti kha..
2 tattulyatāpyasya tathā yathā bhavati suśruta iti kha..
:p 40
meaning:
क्षयस्य बृंहणं कार्यं स्थुलदेहस्य कर्षणम् /
रक्षणं मध्यकायस्य देहभेदास्त्रयो मताः //
:न्
1 स्नेहपाके च तद्गुणमिति ख..
2 तत्तुल्यताप्यस्य तथा यथा भवति सुश्रुत इति ख..
:प् 40
text_mt:
Nourishment is to be given to the emaciated; reduction for the obese body; / preservation for the middling body—three divisions of bodies are recognized.
[Footnote]
1. 'And in the cooking of an unctuous substance, that quality' in manuscript kha.
2. 'Its equality also becomes as it is, O Suśruta' in manuscript kha. / [page 40]

sanskrit_iast:
upakramadvayaṃ proktaṃ tarpaṇaṃ vāpyatarpaṇaṃ /
hitāśī ca mitāśī ca jīrṇāśī ca tathā bhavet //
meaning:
उपक्रमद्वयं प्रोक्तं तर्पणं वाप्यतर्पणं /
हिताशी च मिताशी च जीर्णाशी च तथा भवेत् //
text_mt: Two treatments are declared: nourishing or depletive. / One should eat wholesome food, eat measured food, and eat when previous food is digested.

sanskrit_iast:
oṣadhīnāṃ pañcavidhā tathā bhavati kalpanā /
rasaḥ kalkaḥ śṛtaḥ śītaḥ phāṇḍaś ca manujottama //
meaning:
ओषधीनां पञ्चविधा तथा भवति कल्पना /
रसः कल्कः शृतः शीतः फाण्डश् च मनुजोत्तम //
text_mt: The preparation of herbs is fivefold, O best of men: / fresh juice, paste, decoction, cold infusion, and hot infusion.

sanskrit_iast:
rasaś ca pīḍako jñeyaḥ kalka āloḍitād bhavet /
kvathitaś ca śṛto jñeyaḥ śītaḥ paryuṣito niśāṃ //
meaning:
रसश् च पीडको ज्ञेयः कल्क आलोडिताद् भवेत् /
क्वथितश् च शृतो ज्ञेयः शीतः पर्युषितो निशां //
text_mt: Fresh juice should be known as obtained by pressing; paste comes from churning [or grinding]; / decoction is known as boiled; cold infusion is what has stood overnight;

sanskrit_iast:
sadyobhiśṛtapūtaṃ yat tat phāṇṭamabhidhīyate /
karaṇānāṃ śatañcaiva ṣaṣṭiś caivādhikā smṛtā //
meaning:
सद्योभिशृतपूतं यत् तत् फाण्टमभिधीयते /
करणानां शतञ्चैव षष्टिश् चैवाधिका स्मृता //
text_mt: that which is instantly boiled and filtered is called a hot infusion. / The operations are remembered to be one hundred and sixty in addition.

sanskrit_iast:
yo vetti sa hy ajeyaḥ sthātsambandhe vāhuśauṇḍikaḥ /
āhāraśuddhiragnyarthamagnimūlaṃ balaṃ nṛṇāṃ //
meaning:
यो वेत्ति स ह्य् अजेयः स्थात्सम्बन्धे वाहुशौण्डिकः /
आहारशुद्धिरग्न्यर्थमग्निमूलं बलं नृणां //
text_mt: He who knows this would indeed be unconquerable, skilled in bodily wrestling. / Purity of food is for the sake of the digestive fire; the digestive fire is the root of men's strength.

sanskrit_iast:
sasindhutriphalāñcādyātsurājñi abhivarṇadāṃ /
jāṅgalañca rasaṃ sindhuyuktaṃ dadhi payaḥ kaṇāṃ //
meaning:
ससिन्धुत्रिफलाञ्चाद्यात्सुराज्ञि अभिवर्णदां /
जाङ्गलञ्च रसं सिन्धुयुक्तं दधि पयः कणां //
text_mt: One should consume triphalā with rock salt, O good king, as it imparts complexion; / and wild meat broth with rock salt, curd, milk, and pippalī.

sanskrit_iast:
rasādhikaṃ samaṃ kuryānnaro vātādhiko 'pi vā /
nidāghe mardanaṃ proktaṃ śiśire ca samaṃ bahu //
meaning:
रसाधिकं समं कुर्यान्नरो वाताधिको ऽपि वा /
निदाघे मर्दनं प्रोक्तं शिशिरे च समं बहु //
text_mt: A man should make an excess of bodily fluid equal, or if he has an excess of vāta. / Massage is prescribed in the summer, and equally extensive in the dewy season;

sanskrit_iast:
vasante madhyamaṃ jñeyannidāghe mardanolvaṇaṃ /
tvacantu prathamaṃ mardyamaṅgañca tadanantaraṃ //
meaning:
वसन्ते मध्यमं ज्ञेयन्निदाघे मर्दनोल्वणं /
त्वचन्तु प्रथमं मर्द्यमङ्गञ्च तदनन्तरं //
text_mt: it should be known as moderate in spring, and intense massage in summer. / First the skin should be massaged, and immediately after, the limb.

sanskrit_iast:
snāyurudhiradeheṣu asthi bhātīva māṃsalaṃ /
skandhau bāhū tathaiveha tathā jaṅghe sajānunī //
meaning:
स्नायुरुधिरदेहेषु अस्थि भातीव मांसलं /
स्कन्धौ बाहू तथैवेह तथा जङ्घे सजानुनी //
text_mt: In bodies having tendons and blood, the bone appears as if fleshy; / the shoulders, the arms, and likewise here the shanks with the knees,

sanskrit_iast:
arivanmardayet prajño jatru vakṣaś ca pūrvavat /
aṅgasandhiṣu sarveṣu niṣpīḍya bahulaṃ tathā //
meaning:
अरिवन्मर्दयेत् प्रज्ञो जत्रु वक्षश् च पूर्ववत् /
अङ्गसन्धिषु सर्वेषु निष्पीड्य बहुलं तथा //
text_mt: the wise one should massage like an enemy, and the collarbones and chest as before; / and pressing firmly upon all the joints of the limbs,

sanskrit_iast:
prasārayedaṅgasandhīnna ca kṣepeṇa cākramāt /
nījīrṇe tu śramaṃ kuryānna bhuktvā pītavānnaraḥ //
meaning:
प्रसारयेदङ्गसन्धीन्न च क्षेपेण चाक्रमात् /
नीजीर्णे तु श्रमं कुर्यान्न भुक्त्वा पीतवान्नरः //
text_mt: he should extend the joints of the limbs, but not with sudden jerk or out of order. / A man should not exert himself when food is undigested, nor after eating or drinking.

sanskrit_iast:
dinasya tu caturbhāga ūrdhvantu praharārdhake /
:p 41
vyāyāmaṃ naiva kartavyaṃ snāyācchītāmbunā sakṛt //
meaning:
दिनस्य तु चतुर्भाग ऊर्ध्वन्तु प्रहरार्धके /
:प् 41
व्यायामं नैव कर्तव्यं स्नायाच्छीताम्बुना सकृत् //
text_mt:
At the fourth part of the day, but after half a prahara,
[page 41]
exercise should not be done; one should bathe once with cold water.

sanskrit_iast:
vāryuṣṇañca śramaṃ jahyāddhṛdā śvāsanna dhārayet /
vyāyāmaś ca kaphaṃ hanyādvātaṃ hanyācca mardanaṃ //
meaning:
वार्युष्णञ्च श्रमं जह्याद्धृदा श्वासन्न धारयेत् /
व्यायामश् च कफं हन्याद्वातं हन्याच्च मर्दनं //
text_mt: Warm water dispels exhaustion; one should not hold the breath with the chest. / Exercise destroys kapha, and massage destroys vāta;

sanskrit_iast:
snānaṃ pittādhikaṃ hanyāttasyānte cātapāḥ priyāḥ /
ātapakleśakarmādau kṣemavyāyāmino narāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rasādilakṣaṇaṃ
nāmāśītyadhikadvisatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vṛkṣāyurvedaḥ
meaning:
स्नानं पित्ताधिकं हन्यात्तस्यान्ते चातपाः प्रियाः /
आतपक्लेशकर्मादौ क्षेमव्यायामिनो नराः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे रसादिलक्षणं
नामाशीत्यधिकद्विसततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
वृक्षायुर्वेदः
text_mt:
bathing destroys excess pitta, and at the end of it sunshine is pleasant. / In heat, toil, exertion and the like, people are secure exercises.
Thus ends the two hundred and eightieth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named 'Characteristics of Tastes and the Rest'.
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-first chapter.
Arbori-horticulture (Vṛkṣāyurveda).

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
vṛkṣāyurvedamākhyāsye plakṣaścottarataḥ śubhaḥ /
prāgvaṭo yāmyatastvāmra āpye 'śvatthaḥ karmeṇa tu //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
वृक्षायुर्वेदमाख्यास्ये प्लक्षश्चोत्तरतः शुभः /
प्राग्वटो याम्यतस्त्वाम्र आप्ये ऽश्वत्थः कर्मेण तु //
text_mt: Dhanvantari said: / I shall declare arbori-horticulture. The plakṣa is auspicious to the north; / the banyan to the east, the mango to the south, and the aśvattha in order to the west.

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇāṃ diśamutpannāḥ samīpe kaṇṭakadrumāḥ /
udyānaṃ gṛhavāse(1) syāt tilān vāpyatha puṣpitān //
meaning:
दक्षिणां दिशमुत्पन्नाः समीपे कण्टकद्रुमाः /
उद्यानं गृहवासे(1) स्यात् तिलान् वाप्यथ पुष्पितान् //
text_mt: Thorny trees growing in the southern direction near [the dwelling] / should be in the garden of the dwelling, or [one should sow] flowering sesamum seeds.

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhṇīyādropayedvṛkṣān dvijañcandraṃ prapūjya ca /
dhruvāṇi pañca vāyavyaṃ hastaṃ prājeśavaiṣṇavaṃ //
meaning:
गृह्णीयाद्रोपयेद्वृक्षान् द्विजञ्चन्द्रं प्रपूज्य च /
ध्रुवाणि पञ्च वायव्यं हस्तं प्राजेशवैष्णवं //
text_mt: Having worshipped a brāhmaṇa and the moon, one should take and plant the trees / during the five fixed nakṣatras, the windy nakṣatra (Svāti), Hasta, Prajāpati's (Rohiṇī), and Viṣṇu's (Śravaṇa).

sanskrit_iast:
nakṣatrāṇi tathā mūlaṃ śasyante drumaropaṇe /
praveśayennadīvāhān puṣkariṇyāntu(2) kārayet //
:n
1 gṛhavāme iti ña..
2 puṣkariṇyāntviti pāṭho na samyak pratibhāti
:p 42
meaning:
नक्षत्राणि तथा मूलं शस्यन्ते द्रुमरोपणे /
प्रवेशयेन्नदीवाहान् पुष्करिण्यान्तु(2) कारयेत् //
:न्
1 गृहवामे इति ञ..
2 पुष्करिण्यान्त्विति पाठो न सम्यक् प्रतिभाति
:प् 42
text_mt:
These lunar asterisms and Mūla are praised for planting trees. / One should cause river currents to enter and make lotus ponds.
[Footnote]
1. 'To the left of the house' in manuscript ña.
2. 'In a lotus pond' does not seem a proper reading. / [page 42]

sanskrit_iast:
hastā maghā tathā maitramādyaṃ puṣyaṃ savāsavaṃ /
jalāśayasamārambhe vāruṇañcottarātrayam //
meaning:
हस्ता मघा तथा मैत्रमाद्यं पुष्यं सवासवं /
जलाशयसमारम्भे वारुणञ्चोत्तरात्रयम् //
text_mt: Hasta, Maghā, Maitra (Anurādhā), Ādya (Aśvinī), Puṣya, Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā), / Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), and the three Uttarās (Uttaraphālgunī, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Uttarabhādrapadā) [are auspicious] when undertaking a reservoir of water.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃpūjya varuṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ parjanyaṃ tat samācaret /
ariṣṭāśokapunnāgaśirīṣāḥ sapriyaṅgavaḥ //
meaning:
संपूज्य वरुणं विष्णुं पर्जन्यं तत् समाचरेत् /
अरिष्टाशोकपुन्नागशिरीषाः सप्रियङ्गवः //
