text_mt: Having worshipped Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, and Parjanya, one should undertake it: / soapberry, aśoka, punnāga, śirīṣa, together with priyaṅgu,

sanskrit_iast:
aśokaḥ kadalī jambus tathā vakuladāḍimāḥ /
sāyaṃ prātastu gharmartau śītakāle dināntare //
meaning:
अशोकः कदली जम्बुस् तथा वकुलदाडिमाः /
सायं प्रातस्तु घर्मर्तौ शीतकाले दिनान्तरे //
text_mt: aśoka, plantain, rose apple, as well as bakula and pomegranate. / In the hot season, [they should be watered] evening and morning; in the cold season, every other day;

sanskrit_iast:
varṣāratrau bhuvaḥ śoṣe sektavyā ropitā drumāḥ /
uttamaṃ viṃśatirhastā madhyamaṃ ṣoḍaśāntaram //
meaning:
वर्षारत्रौ भुवः शोषे सेक्तव्या रोपिता द्रुमाः /
उत्तमं विंशतिर्हस्ता मध्यमं षोडशान्तरम् //
text_mt: in the rainy season, when the earth is dry, the planted trees must be watered. / An interval of twenty cubits is best, sixteen is middling,

sanskrit_iast:
sthānāt sthānāntaraṃ kāryaṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ dvādaśāvaraṃ /
viphalāḥ syurghanā vṛkṣāḥ śastreṇādau hi śodhanam //
meaning:
स्थानात् स्थानान्तरं कार्यं वृक्षाणां द्वादशावरं /
विफलाः स्युर्घना वृक्षाः शस्त्रेणादौ हि शोधनम् //
text_mt: and twelve from place to place is the least for trees. / Densely planted trees become fruitless; first, indeed, cleansing with a weapon [is done].

sanskrit_iast:
viḍaṅgaghṛtapaṅkāktān secayecchītavāriṇā /
phalanāśe kulathaiś ca māsair mudgair yavaistilaiḥ //
meaning:
विडङ्गघृतपङ्काक्तान् सेचयेच्छीतवारिणा /
फलनाशे कुलथैश् च मासैर् मुद्गैर् यवैस्तिलैः //
text_mt: One should sprinkle with cold water those smeared with viḍaṅga, ghee, and mud. / When fruit is lost, [watering] with horse-gram, black gram, mung bean, barley, and sesamum,

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtaśītapayaḥsekaḥ phalapuṣpāya sarvadā /
āvikājaśakṛccūrṇam yavacūrṇaṃ tilāni ca //
meaning:
घृतशीतपयःसेकः फलपुष्पाय सर्वदा /
आविकाजशकृच्चूर्णम् यवचूर्णं तिलानि च //
text_mt: and sprinkling with ghee and cold milk always brings about fruit and flowers. / Powdered sheep and goat dung, barley powder, and sesamum seeds,

sanskrit_iast:
gomāṃsamudakañcaiva saptarātraṃ nidhāpayet /
utsekaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ phalapuṣpādivṛddhidaḥ //
meaning:
गोमांसमुदकञ्चैव सप्तरात्रं निधापयेत् /
उत्सेकः सर्ववृक्षाणां फलपुष्पादिवृद्धिदः //
text_mt: beef, and water should be kept set aside for seven nights; / this effusion causes an increase of fruits, flowers, and the like in all trees.

sanskrit_iast:
matsyāmbhasā tu sekena vṛddhirbhavati śākhinaḥ /
viḍaṅgataṇḍulopetaṃ matsyaṃ māṃsaṃ hi dohadaṃ /
sarveṣāmaviśeṣeṇa vṛkṣāṇāṃ rogamardanam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vṛkṣāyurvedo
nāmaikāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 43
:ś atha dvyaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānārogaharāṇyauṣadhāni
meaning:
मत्स्याम्भसा तु सेकेन वृद्धिर्भवति शाखिनः /
विडङ्गतण्डुलोपेतं मत्स्यं मांसं हि दोहदं /
सर्वेषामविशेषेण वृक्षाणां रोगमर्दनम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वृक्षायुर्वेदो
नामैकाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 43
:श् अथ द्व्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानारोगहराण्यौषधानि
text_mt:
By sprinkling with fish-water, growth of the tree occurs. / Fish and meat mixed with viḍaṅga and rice grains are a fertilizer (dohada) / that removes disease from all trees without exception.
Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-first chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named 'Arbori-horticulture'.
[page 43]
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-second chapter.
Medicines that cure various diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
siṃhī śaṭī(1) niśāyugmaṃ vatsakaṃ kvāthasevanaṃ /
śiśoḥ sarvātisāreṣu stanyadoṣeṣu śasyate //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
सिंही शटी(1) निशायुग्मं वत्सकं क्वाथसेवनं /
शिशोः सर्वातिसारेषु स्तन्यदोषेषु शस्यते //
text_mt:
Dhanvantari said:
Bṛhatī, śaṭī, the two kinds of turmeric, and kutaja—drinking a decoction of these / is commended for all kinds of diarrhea in a child, and for disorders caused by [vitiated] mother's milk.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgīṃ sakṛṣṇātiviṣāṃ cūrṇitāṃ madhunā lihet /
ekā cātiviśā kāśacchardijvaraharī śiśoḥ //
meaning:
शृङ्गीं सकृष्णातिविषां चूर्णितां मधुना लिहेत् /
एका चातिविशा काशच्छर्दिज्वरहरी शिशोः //
text_mt: One should lick karkaṭaśṛṅgī combined with pippalī and ativiṣā, pulverized and mixed with honey; / and ativiṣā alone cures cough, vomiting, and fever in a child.

sanskrit_iast:
bālaiḥ sevyā vacā sājyā sadugdhā vātha tailayuk /
yaṣṭikāṃ śaṅkhapuṣpīṃ vā bālaḥ kṣīrānvitāṃ pivet //
meaning:
बालैः सेव्या वचा साज्या सदुग्धा वाथ तैलयुक् /
यष्टिकां शङ्खपुष्पीं वा बालः क्षीरान्वितां पिवेत् //
text_mt: Vacā mixed with ghee, or with milk, or accompanied by oil, should be taken by children. / Or a child should drink yaṣṭīmadhu or śaṅkhapuṣpī combined with milk.

sanskrit_iast:
vāgrūpasampadyuktāyurmedhāśrīrvardhate śiśoḥ /
vacāhyagniśikhāvāsāśuṇṭhīkṛṣṇāniśāgadaṃ //
meaning:
वाग्रूपसम्पद्युक्तायुर्मेधाश्रीर्वर्धते शिशोः /
वचाह्यग्निशिखावासाशुण्ठीकृष्णानिशागदं //
text_mt: The child's longevity, intellect, prosperity, and wealth of eloquence and beauty will increase. / Vacā, agniśikhā, vāsā, ginger, pippalī, turmeric, and kuṣṭha,

sanskrit_iast:
sayaṣṭisaindhavaṃ bālaḥ prātarmedhākaraṃ pivet /
devadārumahāśigruphalatrayapayomucāṃ //
meaning:
सयष्टिसैन्धवं बालः प्रातर्मेधाकरं पिवेत् /
देवदारुमहाशिग्रुफलत्रयपयोमुचां //
text_mt: along with yaṣṭīmadhu and rock salt, a child should drink in the morning to produce intellect. / A decoction of devadāru, mahāśigru, the three fruits (triphalā), and mustā,

sanskrit_iast:
kvāthaḥ sakṛṣṇā mṛdvīkā kalkaḥ sarvān kṛmīnharet /
triphalābhṛṅgaviśvānāṃ raseṣu madhusarpiṣoḥ //
meaning:
क्वाथः सकृष्णा मृद्वीका कल्कः सर्वान् कृमीन्हरेत् /
त्रिफलाभृङ्गविश्वानां रसेषु मधुसर्पिषोः //
text_mt: [or] a paste of them with pippalī and raisins, removes all worms. / [A preparation] processed in the juices of triphalā, bhṛṅgarāja, and ginger, along with honey and ghee,

sanskrit_iast:
meṣīkṣīre ca gomūtre siktaṃ roge hitaṃ śiśoḥ /
nāsāraktaharo nasyāddurvārasa ihottamaḥ //
meaning:
मेषीक्षीरे च गोमूत्रे सिक्तं रोगे हितं शिशोः /
नासारक्तहरो नस्याद्दुर्वारस इहोत्तमः //
text_mt: and mixed with ewe's milk and cow's urine, is beneficial in childhood diseases. / Juice of dūrvā grass administered as an errhine is the best here for stopping nasal hemorrhage.

sanskrit_iast:
laśunārdrakaśigrūṇāṃ rasaḥ karṇasya pūraṇam /
tailamārdrakajātyaṃ vā śūlahā(2) cauṣṭharoganut(3) //
:n
1 siṃhī ṣaṣṭīti kha..
2 śūlahā ity atra puṃstvanirdeśa ārṣaḥ
3 mūtrahā śoṣaroganuditi ña..
:p 44
meaning:
लशुनार्द्रकशिग्रूणां रसः कर्णस्य पूरणम् /
तैलमार्द्रकजात्यं वा शूलहा(2) चौष्ठरोगनुत्(3) //
:न्
1 सिंही षष्टीति ख..
2 शूलहा इत्य् अत्र पुंस्त्वनिर्देश आर्षः
3 मूत्रहा शोषरोगनुदिति ञ..
:प् 44
text_mt:
The juice of garlic, ginger, and śigru is used for filling the ear; / or an oil prepared with fresh ginger relieves earache and removes diseases of the lips.
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha, "siṃhī ṣaṣṭī".
2. Here, the masculine inflection in 'śūlahā' is an archaic (ārṣa) usage.
3. In manuscript ña, "mūtrahā śoṣaroganud". / [Page 44]

sanskrit_iast:
jātīpatraṃ phalaṃ vyoṣaṃ kavalaṃ mūtrakaṃ niśā /
dugdhakvāthe 'bhayākalke siddhaṃ tailaṃ dvijārtinut //
meaning:
जातीपत्रं फलं व्योषं कवलं मूत्रकं निशा /
दुग्धक्वाथे ऽभयाकल्के सिद्धं तैलं द्विजार्तिनुत् //
text_mt: Jasmine leaf, nut-meg, the three pungents, [used as] a mouth rinse with cow's urine and turmeric; / oil processed in a decoction of milk with a paste of harītakī removes toothache.

sanskrit_iast:
dhānyāmbu nārikelaṃ gomūtraṃ kramūkaviśvayuk /
kvāthitaṃ kabalaṃ kāryamadhijihvādhiśāntaye //
meaning:
धान्याम्बु नारिकेलं गोमूत्रं क्रमूकविश्वयुक् /
क्वाथितं कबलं कार्यमधिजिह्वाधिशान्तये //
text_mt: Coriander water, coconut water, and cow's urine with betel nut and dry ginger, / boiled and used as a gargle, should be applied to pacify ranula (adhijihvikā).

sanskrit_iast:
sādhitaṃ lāṅgalīkalke tailaṃ nirguṇḍikārasaiḥ /
gaṇḍamālāgalagaṇḍau nāśayennasyakarmaṇā //
meaning:
साधितं लाङ्गलीकल्के तैलं निर्गुण्डिकारसैः /
गण्डमालागलगण्डौ नाशयेन्नस्यकर्मणा //
text_mt: Oil prepared with a paste of lāṅgalī in the juice of nirguṇḍī / destroys cervical lymphadenitis and goiter by means of an errhine procedure.

sanskrit_iast:
pallavair arkapūtīkasnuhīrugghātajātikaiḥ /
udvartayet sagomūtraḥ sarvatvagdoṣanāśanaiḥ //
meaning:
पल्लवैर् अर्कपूतीकस्नुहीरुग्घातजातिकैः /
उद्वर्तयेत् सगोमूत्रः सर्वत्वग्दोषनाशनैः //
text_mt: With tender leaves of arka, pūtīka, snuhī, karañja, and jātī / together with cow's urine, one should perform anointment, which cures all skin diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
vākucī satilā bhuktā vatsarāt kuṣṭhanāśanī /
pathyā bhallātakī tailaguḍapiṇḍī tu kuṣṭhajit //
meaning:
वाकुची सतिला भुक्ता वत्सरात् कुष्ठनाशनी /
पथ्या भल्लातकी तैलगुडपिण्डी तु कुष्ठजित् //
text_mt: Bākučī eaten with sesame destroys leprosy after one year. / But a paste-ball of harītakī, bhallātaka, oil, and jaggery conquers leprosy.

sanskrit_iast:
pūtīkavahnirajanī triphalāvyoṣacūrṇayuk /
takraṃ gudāṅkure peyaṃ bhakṣyā vā saguḍābhayā //
meaning:
पूतीकवह्निरजनी त्रिफलाव्योषचूर्णयुक् /
तक्रं गुदाङ्कुरे पेयं भक्ष्या वा सगुडाभया //
text_mt: Buttermilk combined with powder of pūtīka, citraka, turmeric, triphalā, and the three pungents / should be drunk for piles, or harītakī eaten with jaggery.

sanskrit_iast:
phaladārvīviṣāṇāntu kvātho dhātrīraso 'thavā /
pātavyo rajanīkalkaḥ kṣaudrākṣaudrapramehiṇā //
meaning:
फलदार्वीविषाणान्तु क्वाथो धात्रीरसो ऽथवा /
पातव्यो रजनीकल्कः क्षौद्राक्षौद्रप्रमेहिणा //
text_mt: A decoction of the three fruits, dāruharidrā, and ativiṣā, or āmalakī juice, / or a paste of turmeric should be drunk with honey by one suffering from urinary disorder (prameha).

sanskrit_iast:
vāsāgarbho vyādhighātakvātha eraṇḍatailayuk /
vātaśoṇitahṛt pānāt pippalī syāt plīhāharī //
meaning:
वासागर्भो व्याधिघातक्वाथ एरण्डतैलयुक् /
वातशोणितहृत् पानात् पिप्पली स्यात् प्लीहाहरी //
text_mt: A decoction of vyādhighāta (āragvadha) containing a paste of vāsā, mixed with castor oil / and drunk, cures gout (vātarakta); pippalī removes splenic disease.

sanskrit_iast:
sevyā jaṭhariṇā kṛṣṇā snukṣīravahubhāvitā /
payo vā racyadantyāgniviḍaṅgavyoṣakalkayuk //
meaning:
सेव्या जठरिणा कृष्णा स्नुक्षीरवहुभाविता /
पयो वा रच्यदन्त्याग्निविडङ्गव्योषकल्कयुक् //
text_mt: Pippalī soaked many times in the milky latex of snuhī should be taken by one with abdominal enlargement, / or milk combined with the paste of pleasing dantī, citraka, viḍaṅga, and the three pungents.

sanskrit_iast:
granthikogrābhayā kṛṣṇā viḍaṅgāktā ghṛte sthitā /
sāṃsantakraṃ grahaṇyarśaḥpāṇḍugulmakṛmīn haret //
meaning:
ग्रन्थिकोग्राभया कृष्णा विडङ्गाक्ता घृते स्थिता /
सांसन्तक्रं ग्रहण्यर्शःपाण्डुगुल्मकृमीन् हरेत् //
text_mt: Pippalīmūla, vacā, harītakī, and pippalī smeared with viḍaṅga and kept in ghee, / [taken] with meat soup and buttermilk, cures sprue, piles, anemia, abdominal tumors, and worms.

sanskrit_iast:
phalatrayāmṛtā vāsā tiktabhūnimbajas tathā /
kvāthaḥ samākṣiko hanyāt pāṇḍurogaṃ sakāmalaṃ //
meaning:
फलत्रयामृता वासा तिक्तभूनिम्बजस् तथा /
क्वाथः समाक्षिको हन्यात् पाण्डुरोगं सकामलं //
text_mt: A decoction of the three fruits, guḍūcī, vāsā, and kirātatikta / mixed with honey destroys anemia along with jaundice.

sanskrit_iast:
raktapittī pivedvāsāsurasaṃ sasitaṃ madhu /
:p 45
varīdrākṣābalāśuṇṭhīsādhitaṃ vā payaḥ pṛthak //
meaning:
रक्तपित्ती पिवेद्वासासुरसं ससितं मधु /
:प् 45
वरीद्राक्षाबलाशुण्ठीसाधितं वा पयः पृथक् //
text_mt:
One suffering from internal hemorrhage should drink the juice of vāsā with sugar and honey,
[Page 45]
or milk separately prepared with śatāvarī, grapes, balā, and dry ginger.

sanskrit_iast:
varī vidārī pathyā balātrayaṃ savāsakaṃ /
śvadaṃṣṭrāmadhusarpirbhyāmālihet kṣayarogavān //
meaning:
वरी विदारी पथ्या बलात्रयं सवासकं /
श्वदंष्ट्रामधुसर्पिर्भ्यामालिहेत् क्षयरोगवान् //
text_mt: Śatāvarī, vidārī, harītakī, the three kinds of balā along with vāsā, / and gokṣura—one suffering from consumption should lick these with honey and ghee.

sanskrit_iast:
pathyāśigrukarañjārkatvaksāraṃ madhusindhumat /
samūtraṃ vidradhiṃ hanti paripākāya tantrajit //
meaning:
पथ्याशिग्रुकरञ्जार्कत्वक्सारं मधुसिन्धुमत् /
समूत्रं विद्रधिं हन्ति परिपाकाय तन्त्रजित् //
text_mt: The bark-pith of harītakī, śigru, karañja, and arka, with honey and rock salt, / along with cow's urine, cures abscess; expertly applied, it brings about suppuration.

sanskrit_iast:
trivṛtā jīvatī dantī mañjiṣṭhā śarvarīdvayaṃ /
tārkṣajaṃ nimbapatrañca lepaḥ śasto bhagandare //
meaning:
त्रिवृता जीवती दन्ती मञ्जिष्ठा शर्वरीद्वयं /
तार्क्षजं निम्बपत्रञ्च लेपः शस्तो भगन्दरे //
text_mt: Trivṛt, jīvantī, dantī, mañjiṣṭhā, the two kinds of turmeric, / rasāñjana, and neem leaves—a plaster [of these] is commended in fistula-in-ano.

sanskrit_iast:
rugghātajanīlākṣācūrṇājakṣaudrasaṃyutā /
vāsovattirvraṇe yojyā śodhanī gatināśanī //
meaning:
रुग्घातजनीलाक्षाचूर्णाजक्षौद्रसंयुता /
वासोवत्तिर्व्रणे योज्या शोधनी गतिनाशनी //
text_mt: A cloth wick smeared with goat's milk and honey, along with the powder of āragvadha, turmeric, and lac, / should be applied to a wound to purify it and destroy sinus tracts.

sanskrit_iast:
śyāmāyaṣṭiniśālodhrapadmakotpalacandanaiḥ /
samarīcaiḥ śṛtaṃ tailaṃ kṣīre syādbraṇarohaṇaṃ //
meaning:
श्यामायष्टिनिशालोध्रपद्मकोत्पलचन्दनैः /
समरीचैः शृतं तैलं क्षीरे स्याद्ब्रणरोहणं //
text_mt: Oil boiled with milk, along with priyaṅgu, yaṣṭīmadhu, turmeric, lodhra, padmaka, blue lotus, sandalwood, / and black pepper, brings about the healing of wounds.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīkārpāsadalair bhasmaphalopalavaṇā niśā /
tatpiṇḍīsvedanaṃ tāmre satailaṃ syāt kṣatauṣadhaṃ //
meaning:
श्रीकार्पासदलैर् भस्मफलोपलवणा निशा /
तत्पिण्डीस्वेदनं ताम्रे सतैलं स्यात् क्षतौषधं //
text_mt: Ash of sacred cotton leaves, bibhītaka, and rock salt, along with turmeric— / fomentation with that paste-ball in a copper vessel, with oil, is the medicine for cuts.

sanskrit_iast:
kumbhīsāraṃ payoyuktaṃ vahnidagdhaṃ vraṇe lipet /
tadeva nāśayetsekānnārikelarajoghṛtam //
meaning:
कुम्भीसारं पयोयुक्तं वह्निदग्धं व्रणे लिपेत् /
तदेव नाशयेत्सेकान्नारिकेलरजोघृतम् //
text_mt: One should apply to a wound the pith of kumbhī mixed with milk, charred in fire; / [or] coconut powder mixed with ghee destroys the same when applied as an irrigation.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣvājamodasindhūtthaciñcātvagbhiḥ samābhayā /
takreṇoṣṇāmbunā vātha pītātīsāranāśanī //
meaning:
विष्वाजमोदसिन्धूत्थचिञ्चात्वग्भिः समाभया /
तक्रेणोष्णाम्बुना वाथ पीतातीसारनाशनी //
text_mt: Harītakī combined equally with dry ginger, ajamodā, rock salt, and tamarind bark, / drunk with buttermilk or warm water, destroys diarrhea.

sanskrit_iast:
vatsakātiviṣāviśvavillamustaśṛtaṃ jalaṃ /
sāme purāṇe 'tīsāre sāmṛkśūle ca pāyayet //
meaning:
वत्सकातिविषाविश्वविल्लमुस्तशृतं जलं /
सामे पुराणे ऽतीसारे सामृक्शूले च पाययेत् //
text_mt: Water boiled with indrayava, ativiṣā, dry ginger, bael fruit, and mustā, / one should administer in acute or chronic diarrhea, and in colic accompanied by mucous and blood.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgāradagdhaṃ sugataṃ sindhumuṣṇāmbunā pivet /
śūlavānatha vā taddhi sindhuhiṃgukaṇābhayā //
meaning:
अङ्गारदग्धं सुगतं सिन्धुमुष्णाम्बुना पिवेत् /
शूलवानथ वा तद्धि सिन्धुहिंगुकणाभया //
text_mt: Burned on embers and purified, one should drink rock salt with warm water / when suffering from colic; or likewise that rock salt, asafoetida, pippalī, and harītakī.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭurohotkaṇātaṅkalājacūrṇaṃ(1) madhuplutaṃ /
:n
1 kaṭurohotpalātaṅkalājacūrṇamiti ṭa..
:p 46
vastracchidragataṃ vaktre nyastaṃ tṛṣṇāṃ vināśayet //
meaning:
कटुरोहोत्कणातङ्कलाजचूर्णं(1) मधुप्लुतं /
:न्
1 कटुरोहोत्पलातङ्कलाजचूर्णमिति ट..
:प् 46
वस्त्रच्छिद्रगतं वक्त्रे न्यस्तं तृष्णां विनाशयेत् //
text_mt:
Powder of kaṭukā, utpalikā, and puffed paddy steeped in honey,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript ṭa, "kaṭurohotpalātaṅkalājacūrṇam". / [Page 46]
placed inside a cloth pouch and held in the mouth, destroys thirst.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṭhādārvījātidalaṃ drākṣāmūlaphalatrayaiḥ(1) /
sādhitaṃ samadhu kvāthaṃ kavalaṃ mukhapāpahṛt //
meaning:
पाठादार्वीजातिदलं द्राक्षामूलफलत्रयैः(1) /
साधितं समधु क्वाथं कवलं मुखपापहृत् //
text_mt: Pāṭhā, dāruharidrā, jasmine leaf, grapes, root of [eranda?], and the three fruits, / prepared as a decoction and held as a gargle with honey, cures diseases of the mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇātiviṣatiktendradārūpāṭhāpayomucāṃ /
kvātho mūtre śṛtaḥ kṣaudrī sarvakaṇṭhagadāpahaḥ //
meaning:
कृष्णातिविषतिक्तेन्द्रदारूपाठापयोमुचां /
क्वाथो मूत्रे शृतः क्षौद्री सर्वकण्ठगदापहः //
text_mt: A decoction of pippalī, ativiṣā, tikta, indrayava, devadāru, pāṭhā, and mustā, / boiled in cow's urine and mixed with honey, removes all throat disorders.

sanskrit_iast:
pathyāgokṣuradusparśarājavṛkṣaśilābhidāṃ /
kaṣāyaḥ samadhuḥ pīto mūtrakṛcchraṃ vyapohati //
meaning:
पथ्यागोक्षुरदुस्पर्शराजवृक्षशिलाभिदां /
कषायः समधुः पीतो मूत्रकृच्छ्रं व्यपोहति //
text_mt: A decoction of harītakī, gokṣura, yavāsa, āragvadha, and pāsāṇabheda, / drunk with honey, dispels painful micturition.

sanskrit_iast:
vaṃśatvagvaruṇakvāthaḥ śarkarāśmavighātanaḥ /
śākhoṭakvāthasakṣaudrakṣīrāśī ślīpadī bhavet //
meaning:
वंशत्वग्वरुणक्वाथः शर्कराश्मविघातनः /
शाखोटक्वाथसक्षौद्रक्षीराशी श्लीपदी भवेत् //
text_mt: A decoction of bamboo bark and varuṇa destroys gravel and urinary calculi. / One drinking a decoction of śākhoṭaka with honey and living on milk will overcome elephantiasis.

sanskrit_iast:
māsārkatvakpayastailaṃ madhusiktañca saindhavaṃ /
pādarogaṃ haretsarpirjālakukkuṭajaṃ tathā //
meaning:
मासार्कत्वक्पयस्तैलं मधुसिक्तञ्च सैन्धवं /
पादरोगं हरेत्सर्पिर्जालकुक्कुटजं तथा //
text_mt: Milk of arka, black gram, bark, milk, and oil, with beeswax and rock salt, / destroys foot disease; likewise ghee [processed with] jālakukkuṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
śuṇṭhīsīvarcalāhiṅgucūrṇaṃ śūṇṭhīrasair ghṛtam /
rujaṃ haredatha kvātho viddhi baddhāgnisādhane //
meaning:
शुण्ठीसीवर्चलाहिङ्गुचूर्णं शूण्ठीरसैर् घृतम् /
रुजं हरेदथ क्वाथो विद्धि बद्धाग्निसाधने //
text_mt: Powder of dry ginger, sauvarcala salt, and asafoetida, [taken with] ghee and ginger juice, / relieves pain; and know this decoction to be effective for rekindling suppressed digestive fire.

sanskrit_iast:
sauvarcalāgnihiṅgūnāṃ sadīpyānāṃ rasair yutaṃ /
viḍadīpyakayuktaṃ vā takraṃ gulmāturaḥ pivet //
meaning:
सौवर्चलाग्निहिङ्गूनां सदीप्यानां रसैर् युतं /
विडदीप्यकयुक्तं वा तक्रं गुल्मातुरः पिवेत् //
text_mt: A patient suffering from abdominal tumor should drink buttermilk combined with the juices of / sauvarcala salt, citraka, asafoetida, and ajamodā, or mixed with viḍa salt and ajamodā.

sanskrit_iast:
dhātrīpaṭolamudgānāṃ kvāthaḥ sājyo visarpahā /
śuṇṭhīdārunavākṣīrakvātho mūtrānvito 'paraḥ //
meaning:
धात्रीपटोलमुद्गानां क्वाथः साज्यो विसर्पहा /
शुण्ठीदारुनवाक्षीरक्वाथो मूत्रान्वितो ऽपरः //
text_mt: A decoction of āmalakī, paṭola, and mudga beans, with ghee, cures erysipelas. / Another [remedy] is a decoction of ginger, devadāru, and fresh milk, combined with cow's urine.

sanskrit_iast:
savyoṣāyorajaḥkṣāraḥ phalakvāthaś ca śothahṛt /
guḍaśigrutrivṛddhiś ca saindhavānāṃ rajoyutaḥ //
meaning:
सव्योषायोरजःक्षारः फलक्वाथश् च शोथहृत् /
गुडशिग्रुत्रिवृद्धिश् च सैन्धवानां रजोयुतः //
text_mt: A decoction of the three fruits with the three pungents, iron powder, and alkali relieves dropsy; / as does jaggery, śigru, and trivṛt combined with the powder of rock salt.

sanskrit_iast:
trivṛtāphalakakvāthaḥ saguḍaḥ syādvirecanaḥ /
vacāphalakaṣāyotthaṃ payo vamanakṛbhavet //
meaning:
त्रिवृताफलकक्वाथः सगुडः स्याद्विरेचनः /
वचाफलकषायोत्थं पयो वमनकृभवेत् //
text_mt: A decoction of trivṛt and [harītakī] fruit with jaggery serves as a purgative. / Milk prepared from a decoction of vacā and madana fruit causes vomiting.

sanskrit_iast:
triphalāyāḥ palaśataṃ pṛthagbhṛṅgajabhāvitam /
:n
1 drākṣāmṛtaphalatrayair iti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 47
viḍaṅgaṃ lohacūrṇañca daśabhāgasamanvitam //
meaning:
त्रिफलायाः पलशतं पृथग्भृङ्गजभावितम् /
:न्
1 द्राक्षामृतफलत्रयैर् इति ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 47
विडङ्गं लोहचूर्णञ्च दशभागसमन्वितम् //
text_mt:
One hundred palas of triphalā, each separately macerated in bhṛṅgarāja juice,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscripts ña and ṭa, "drākṣāmṛtaphalatrayaiḥ". / [Page 47]
combined with a tenth part of viḍaṅga and iron powder,

sanskrit_iast:
śatāvarīguḍucyagnipalānāṃ śataviṃśatiḥ(1) /
madhvājyatilajair lihyādbalīpalitavarjitaḥ //
meaning:
शतावरीगुडुच्यग्निपलानां शतविंशतिः(1) /
मध्वाज्यतिलजैर् लिह्याद्बलीपलितवर्जितः //
text_mt: [and] one hundred and twenty palas each of śatāvarī, guḍūcī, and citraka, / one should lick with honey, ghee, and sesame oil: he is freed from wrinkles and gray hair,

sanskrit_iast:
śatamabdaṃ hi jīveta sarvarogavivarjitaḥ /
triphalā sarvarogaghnī samadhuḥ śarkvarānvitā //
meaning:
शतमब्दं हि जीवेत सर्वरोगविवर्जितः /
त्रिफला सर्वरोगघ्नी समधुः शर्क्वरान्विता //
text_mt: and lives for a hundred years, completely free from all diseases. / Triphalā cures all diseases when accompanied by honey and sugar.

sanskrit_iast:
sitāmadhughṛtair yuktā sakṛṣṇā triphalā tathā /
pathyācitrakaśuṇṭhāś ca guḍucīmuṣalīrajaḥ //
meaning:
सितामधुघृतैर् युक्ता सकृष्णा त्रिफला तथा /
पथ्याचित्रकशुण्ठाश् च गुडुचीमुषलीरजः //
text_mt: Likewise, triphalā mixed with sugar candy, honey, and ghee, along with pippalī. / Harītakī, citraka, dry ginger, guḍūcī, and powder of muśalī,

sanskrit_iast:
saguḍaṃ bhakṣitaṃ rogaharaṃ triśatavarṣakṛt /
kiñciccūrṇaṃ javāpuṣpaṃ piṇḍitaṃ visṛjejjale //
meaning:
सगुडं भक्षितं रोगहरं त्रिशतवर्षकृत् /
किञ्चिच्चूर्णं जवापुष्पं पिण्डितं विसृजेज्जले //
text_mt: eaten with jaggery, cures diseases and makes one live three hundred years. / A little powder of hibiscus flower made into a ball should be placed in water.

sanskrit_iast:
tailaṃ bhaved ghṛtākāraṃ kiñciccūrṇaṃ jalānvitaṃ /
dhūpārthaṃ dṛśyate citraṃ vṛṣadaṃśajarāyunā //
meaning:
तैलं भवेद् घृताकारं किञ्चिच्चूर्णं जलान्वितं /
धूपार्थं दृश्यते चित्रं वृषदंशजरायुना //
text_mt: The oil becomes like clarified butter; [and] a little powder mixed with water, / for the purpose of incense, appears wonderful together with the placenta of a cat.

sanskrit_iast:
punarmākṣikadhūpena dṛśyate tadyathā purā /
karpūrajalakābhekatailaṃ(2) pāṭalimūlayuk //
meaning:
पुनर्माक्षिकधूपेन दृश्यते तद्यथा पुरा /
कर्पूरजलकाभेकतैलं(2) पाटलिमूलयुक् //
text_mt: Again, with the fumes of honey, it appears as it was before. / Oil of camphor, leech, and frog mixed with the root of pāṭalī,

sanskrit_iast:
piṣṭvā lipya pade dve ca caredaṅgārake naraḥ /
tṛṇautthānādikaṃ vyūhya darśayanvai kutūhalaṃ //
meaning:
पिष्ट्वा लिप्य पदे द्वे च चरेदङ्गारके नरः /
तृणौत्थानादिकं व्यूह्य दर्शयन्वै कुतूहलं //
text_mt: having been ground and smeared on both feet, a man may walk upon burning coals, / tossing about grass, straw, and the like, showing indeed a wonder.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣagraharujadhvaṃsakṣudranarma ca kāmikaṃ /
tatte ṣaṭkarmakaṃ proktaṃ siddhidvayasamāśrayaṃ //
meaning:
विषग्रहरुजध्वंसक्षुद्रनर्म च कामिकं /
तत्ते षट्कर्मकं प्रोक्तं सिद्धिद्वयसमाश्रयं //
text_mt: Destruction of poison, planetary afflictions, and diseases, small entertainments, and rituals performed according to desire: / that is declared to you as the six acts, which rest upon the two kinds of supernatural power.

sanskrit_iast:
mantradhyānauṣadhikathāmudrejyā yatra muṣṭayaḥ /
caturvargaphalaṃ proktaṃ yaḥ paṭhetsa divaṃ vrajet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānārogaharāṇyauṣadhāni nāma
dvyaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 pañcaviśatiriti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 karpūrajahukātailamiti kha.. / karpūrajānukātailamiti ja..
:p 48
:ś atha tryaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mantrarūpauṣadhakathanaṃ
meaning:
मन्त्रध्यानौषधिकथामुद्रेज्या यत्र मुष्टयः /
चतुर्वर्गफलं प्रोक्तं यः पठेत्स दिवं व्रजेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानारोगहराण्यौषधानि नाम
द्व्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 पञ्चविशतिरिति ञ.. , ट.. च
2 कर्पूरजहुकातैलमिति ख.. / कर्पूरजानुकातैलमिति ज..
:प् 48
:श् अथ त्र्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मन्त्ररूपौषधकथनं
text_mt:
Where mantras, meditation, talk of herbs, ritual gestures, worship, and medicinal handfuls [are taught], / the fruit of the four goals of life is declared; whoever recites it goes to heaven.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and eighty-second chapter, called “Remedies That Remove Various Diseases.”
[Notes]
1. "pañcaviśatiḥ" in manuscripts ña and ṭa.
2. "karpūrajahukātailam" in manuscript kha; "karpūrajānukātailam" in manuscript ja. / [Page 48]
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-third chapter.
Account of Remedies in the Form of Mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
āyurārogyakartara oṃkāradyāś ca nākadāḥ /
oṃkāraḥ paramo mantrastaṃ japtvā cāmaro bhavet //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
आयुरारोग्यकर्तर ओंकारद्याश् च नाकदाः /
ओंकारः परमो मन्त्रस्तं जप्त्वा चामरो भवेत् //
text_mt: Dhanvantari said: / The bringers of longevity and health, beginning with Oṃkāra, also grant heaven. / Oṃkāra is the supreme mantra; having recited it, one becomes immortal.

sanskrit_iast:
gāyatrī paramo mantrastaṃ japtvā bhuktimuktibhāk /
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ //
meaning:
गायत्री परमो मन्त्रस्तं जप्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् /
ओं नमो नारायणाय मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः //
text_mt: The Gāyatrī is the supreme mantra; having recited it, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / The mantra "oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya" accomplishes all aims.

sanskrit_iast:
oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya sarvadaḥ /
oṃ hūṃ namo viṣṇave mantroyañcauṣadhaṃ paraṃ //
meaning:
ओं नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय सर्वदः /
ओं हूं नमो विष्णवे मन्त्रोयञ्चौषधं परं //
text_mt: "oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya" bestows everything. / The mantra "oṃ hūṃ namo viṣṇave" is the supreme medicine.

sanskrit_iast:
anena devā hy asurāḥ saśriyo nirujo 'bhavat /
bhūtānāmupakāraś ca tathā dharmo mahauṣadham //
meaning:
अनेन देवा ह्य् असुराः सश्रियो निरुजो ऽभवत् /
भूतानामुपकारश् च तथा धर्मो महौषधम् //
text_mt: By this, the gods and asuras became endowed with prosperity and free from disease; / and helping living beings, as well as righteousness, is the great remedy.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmaḥ saddharmakṛddharmī etair dharmaiś ca nirmalaḥ /
śrīdaḥ śrīṣaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīdharaḥśrīniketanaḥ //
meaning:
धर्मः सद्धर्मकृद्धर्मी एतैर् धर्मैश् च निर्मलः /
श्रीदः श्रीषः श्रीनिवासः श्रीधरःश्रीनिकेतनः //
text_mt: "Dharma," "Saddharmakṛt," "Dharmī": and through these righteous names, one becomes spotless. / "Śrīda," "Śrīśa," "Śrīnivāsa," "Śrīdhara," "Śrīniketana,"

sanskrit_iast:
śriyaḥ patiḥ śrīparama etaiḥ śriyamavāpnuyāt /
kāmī kāmapradaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapālas tathā hariḥ //
meaning:
श्रियः पतिः श्रीपरम एतैः श्रियमवाप्नुयात् /
कामी कामप्रदः कामः कामपालस् तथा हरिः //
text_mt: "Śriyaḥpati," "Śrīparama": through these [names] one attains prosperity. / "Kāmī," "Kāmaprada," "Kāma," "Kāmapāla," as well as "Hari,"

sanskrit_iast:
ānando mādhavaś caiva nāma kāmāya vai hareḥ /
rāmaḥ paraśurāmaś ca nṛsiṃho viṣṇureva ca //
meaning:
आनन्दो माधवश् चैव नाम कामाय वै हरेः /
रामः परशुरामश् च नृसिंहो विष्णुरेव च //
text_mt: "Ānanda," and "Mādhava": these indeed are the names of Hari for desire. / "Rāma," "Paraśurāma," "Nṛsiṃha," and "Viṣṇu,"

sanskrit_iast:
trivikramaś ca nāmāni japtavyāni jigīṣubhiḥ /
vidyāmabhyasyatāṃ nityaṃ japtavyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ //
meaning:
त्रिविक्रमश् च नामानि जप्तव्यानि जिगीषुभिः /
विद्यामभ्यस्यतां नित्यं जप्तव्यः पुरुषोत्तमः //
text_mt: and "Trivikrama": these names should be recited by those wishing for victory. / For those studying learning, "Puruṣottama" should be recited constantly.

sanskrit_iast:
dāmodaro bandhaharaḥ puṣkarākṣo 'kṣiroganut /
hṛṣīkeśo bhayaharo japedauṣadhakarmaṇi //
:p 49
meaning:
दामोदरो बन्धहरः पुष्कराक्षो ऽक्षिरोगनुत् /
हृषीकेशो भयहरो जपेदौषधकर्मणि //
:प् 49
text_mt:
"Dāmodara" removes bondage; "Puṣkarākṣa" removes eye disease; / "Hṛṣīkeśa" removes fear; one should recite [these] in medicinal treatments.
[Page 49]

sanskrit_iast:
acyutañcāmṛtaṃ mantraṃ saṅgrāme cāparājitaḥ /
jalatāre nārasiṃhaṃ pūrvādau kṣemakāmavān //
meaning:
अच्युतञ्चामृतं मन्त्रं सङ्ग्रामे चापराजितः /
जलतारे नारसिंहं पूर्वादौ क्षेमकामवान् //
text_mt: And "Acyuta" is the deathless mantra; and in battle one is undefeated [by reciting it]. / In crossing water, one desiring safety [should recite] "Nārasimha" at the beginning, toward the east, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast:
cakriṇaṅgadinañcaiva śārṅgiṇaṃ khaḍginaṃ smaret /
nārāyaṇaṃ sarvakāle nṛsiṃho 'khilabhītinut //
meaning:
चक्रिणङ्गदिनञ्चैव शार्ङ्गिणं खड्गिनं स्मरेत् /
नारायणं सर्वकाले नृसिंहो ऽखिलभीतिनुत् //
text_mt: One should remember the Holder of the Discus, the Mace-bearer, the Archer, and the Sword-bearer; / Nārāyaṇa at all times; Nṛsiṃha removes all fear.

sanskrit_iast:
garuḍadhvajaś ca viṣahṛt vāsudevaṃ sadājapet /
dhānyādisthāpane svapne anantācyutamīrayet //
meaning:
गरुडध्वजश् च विषहृत् वासुदेवं सदाजपेत् /
धान्यादिस्थापने स्वप्ने अनन्ताच्युतमीरयेत् //
text_mt: And "Garuḍadhvaja" removes poison; one should always recite "Vāsudeva." / When storing grains and the like, or in sleep, one should utter "Ananta" and "Acyuta."

sanskrit_iast:
nārāyaṇañca duḥsvapne dāhādau jalaśāyinaṃ /
hayagrīvañca vidyārthī jagatsūtiṃ sutāptaye /
balabhadraṃ śaurakārye(1) ekaṃ nāmārthasādhakam(2) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mantrarūpauṣadhakathanaṃ nāma
tryaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha caturaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mṛtasañjīvanīkarasiddhayogaḥ
meaning:
नारायणञ्च दुःस्वप्ने दाहादौ जलशायिनं /
हयग्रीवञ्च विद्यार्थी जगत्सूतिं सुताप्तये /
बलभद्रं शौरकार्ये(1) एकं नामार्थसाधकम्(2) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मन्त्ररूपौषधकथनं नाम
त्र्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुरशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मृतसञ्जीवनीकरसिद्धयोगः
text_mt:
And one should remember Nārāyaṇa in a bad dream; the One Who Sleeps on the Waters in burning and the like; / one desiring knowledge, Hayagrīva; the Origin of the World, for obtaining a son; / and Balabhadra in valiant deeds: each single name accomplishes its object.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and eighty-third chapter, called “Account of Remedies in the Form of Mantras.”
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-fourth chapter.
Proven Recipes That Revive the Dead.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
siddhayogān punarvakṣe mṛtasañjīvanīkarān/
ātreyabhāṣitān divyān sarvavyādhivimardanān(3) //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
सिद्धयोगान् पुनर्वक्षे मृतसञ्जीवनीकरान्/
आत्रेयभाषितान् दिव्यान् सर्वव्याधिविमर्दनान्(3) //
text_mt: Dhanvantari said: / I shall further declare proven recipes that revive the dead, / divine remedies spoken by Ātreya that crush all diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
ātreya uvāca
vilvādipañcamūlasya kvāthaḥ syādvātike jvare /
pāvanaṃ pippalīmūlaṃ guḍūcī viṣvajo 'tha vā //
:n
1 vīrakārye iti kha..
2 ekanāmātha sarthakamiti kha.. , ña.. ca
3 sarvavyādhivināśakāniti kha..
:p 50
meaning:
आत्रेय उवाच
विल्वादिपञ्चमूलस्य क्वाथः स्याद्वातिके ज्वरे /
पावनं पिप्पलीमूलं गुडूची विष्वजो ऽथ वा //
:न्
1 वीरकार्ये इति ख..
2 एकनामाथ सर्थकमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
3 सर्वव्याधिविनाशकानिति ख..
:प् 50
text_mt:
Ātreya said: / A decoction of the five roots beginning with bilva is [prescribed] in fever of vāta origin; / or pure long pepper root, guḍūcī, and dried ginger.
[Notes]
1. "vīrakārye" in manuscript kha.
2. "ekanāmātha sarthakam" in manuscripts kha and ña.
3. "sarvavyādhivināśakān" in manuscript kha. / [Page 50]

sanskrit_iast:
āmalakyabhayā kṛṣṇa vahniḥ sarvajvarāntakaḥ /
vilvāgnimanthaśyonākakāśmaryaḥ pārlā sthirā //
meaning:
आमलक्यभया कृष्ण वह्निः सर्वज्वरान्तकः /
विल्वाग्निमन्थश्योनाककाश्मर्यः पार्ला स्थिरा //
text_mt: Emblic myrobalan, chebulic myrobalan, black pepper, and leadwort destroy all fevers. / Bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, kāśmarya, pāṭalā, sthirā,

sanskrit_iast:
trikaṇṭakaṃ pṛśnaparṇī vṛhatī kaṇṭakārikāḥ /
jvarāvipākapārśvārtikāśanut kuśamūlakam //
meaning:
त्रिकण्टकं पृश्नपर्णी वृहती कण्टकारिकाः /
ज्वराविपाकपार्श्वार्तिकाशनुत् कुशमूलकम् //
text_mt: trikaṇṭaka, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, and kaṇṭakārī, / [along with] root of kuśa grass, remove fever, indigestion, flank pain, and cough.

sanskrit_iast:
guḍūcī parpaṭī mustaṃ kirātaṃ viśvabheṣajam /
vātapittajvare deyaṃ pañcabhadramidaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
गुडूची पर्पटी मुस्तं किरातं विश्वभेषजम् /
वातपित्तज्वरे देयं पञ्चभद्रमिदं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Guḍūcī, parpaṭī, mustā, kirātatikta, and ginger: / this is remembered as "the five auspicious remedies," to be given in fever caused by vāta and pitta.

sanskrit_iast:
trivṛdviśālakaṭukātriphalāragbadhaiḥ kṛtaḥ /
sṃskāro bhedanakvāthaḥ peyaḥ sarvajvarāpahaḥ //
meaning:
त्रिवृद्विशालकटुकात्रिफलारग्बधैः कृतः /
स्ंस्कारो भेदनक्वाथः पेयः सर्वज्वरापहः //
text_mt: Prepared with trivṛt, indravāruṇī, kaṭukā, triphalā, and āragvadha, / a purgative decoction should be drunk; it dispels all fevers.

sanskrit_iast:
devadārubalāvāsātriphalāvyopapadmakaiḥ(1) /
saviḍaṅgaiḥ sitātulyaṃ taccurṇaṃ pañcakāśajit //
meaning:
देवदारुबलावासात्रिफलाव्योपपद्मकैः(1) /
सविडङ्गैः सितातुल्यं तच्चुर्णं पञ्चकाशजित् //
text_mt: Devadāru, balā, vāsā, triphalā, the three pungents, and padmaka, / along with viḍaṅga, with sugar equal to the whole: that powder cures the five kinds of cough.

sanskrit_iast:
daśamūlīśaṭīrāsnāpippalībilvapauṣkaraiḥ /
śṛṅgītāmalakībhārgīguḍūcīnāgavallibhiḥ //
meaning:
दशमूलीशटीरास्नापिप्पलीबिल्वपौष्करैः /
शृङ्गीतामलकीभार्गीगुडूचीनागवल्लिभिः //
text_mt: With daśamūla, śaṭī, rāsnā, pippalī, bilva, puṣkaramūla, / śṛṅgī, āmalakī, bhārgī, guḍūcī, and betel leaves,

sanskrit_iast:
yavāgraṃ vidhinā siddhaṃ kaśāyaṃ vā pivennaraḥ /
kāśahṛdgrahaṇīpārśvahikvāśvāsapraśāntaye //
meaning:
यवाग्रं विधिना सिद्धं कशायं वा पिवेन्नरः /
काशहृद्ग्रहणीपार्श्वहिक्वाश्वासप्रशान्तये //
text_mt: or a decoction prepared properly from barley groats, a man should drink / for the relief of cough, heart disease, chronic diarrhoea, flank pain, hiccups, and asthma.

sanskrit_iast:
madhukaṃ madhunā yuktaṃ vippalīṃ śarkarānvitāṃ /
nāgaraṃ guḍasaṃyuktaṃ hikvāghnaṃ lāvaṇatrayam //
meaning:
मधुकं मधुना युक्तं विप्पलीं शर्करान्वितां /
नागरं गुडसंयुक्तं हिक्वाघ्नं लावणत्रयम् //
text_mt: Licorice mixed with honey, long pepper combined with sugar, / ginger combined with jaggery, [or] the three salts: these destroy hiccups.

sanskrit_iast:
kāravyajājīmaricaṃ drākṣā vṛkṣāmladāḍimam /
sauvarcalaṃ guḍaṃ kṣaudraṃ sarvārocananāśanam //
meaning:
कारव्यजाजीमरिचं द्राक्षा वृक्षाम्लदाडिमम् /
सौवर्चलं गुडं क्षौद्रं सर्वारोचननाशनम् //
text_mt: Black cumin, cumin, black pepper, raisins, kokum, pomegranate, / black salt, jaggery, and honey destroy all loss of appetite.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgaverarasañcaiva madhunā saha pāyayet /
aruciśvāsakāśaghnaṃ pratiśyāyakaphāntakam //
meaning:
शृङ्गवेररसञ्चैव मधुना सह पाययेत् /
अरुचिश्वासकाशघ्नं प्रतिश्यायकफान्तकम् //
text_mt: And one should administer fresh ginger juice along with honey; / it cures loss of appetite, asthma, and cough, and ends catarrh and kapha disorders.

sanskrit_iast:
vaṭaṃ śṛṅgī śilālodhradāḍimaṃ madhukaṃ madhu /
pivet taṇḍulatoyena ccharditṛṣṇānivāraṇam //
:n
1 devadārubalārāsnātriphalāvyoṣapadmakair iti kha..
:p 51
meaning:
वटं शृङ्गी शिलालोध्रदाडिमं मधुकं मधु /
पिवेत् तण्डुलतोयेन च्छर्दितृष्णानिवारणम् //
:न्
1 देवदारुबलारास्नात्रिफलाव्योषपद्मकैर् इति ख..
:प् 51
text_mt:
Banyan, śṛṅgī, red ochre, lodhra, pomegranate, licorice, and honey: / one should drink [this] with rice water; it dispels vomiting and thirst.
[Notes]
1. "devadārubalārāsnātriphalāvyoṣapadmakaiḥ" in manuscript kha. / [Page 51]

sanskrit_iast:
guḍucī vāsakaṃ lodhraṃ pippalīkṣaudrasaṃyutam /
kaphānvitañjayedraktaṃ tṛṣṇākāsajvarāpaham //
meaning:
गुडुची वासकं लोध्रं पिप्पलीक्षौद्रसंयुतम् /
कफान्वितञ्जयेद्रक्तं तृष्णाकासज्वरापहम् //
text_mt: Guḍūcī, vāsā, and lodhra, combined with long pepper and honey, / conquer [bleeding] accompanied by kapha and dispel thirst, cough, and fever.

sanskrit_iast:
vāsakasya rasastadvat samadhustāmrajo rasaḥ /
śirīṣapuṣpasurasabhāvitaṃ maricaṃ hitaṃ //
meaning:
वासकस्य रसस्तद्वत् समधुस्ताम्रजो रसः /
शिरीषपुष्पसुरसभावितं मरिचं हितं //
text_mt: Likewise, juice of vāsā, [and] ash of copper with honey; / black pepper macerated in the juice of siris flowers and holy basil is beneficial.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvārtinunmasūro 'tha pittamuk taṇḍlīyakaṃ /
nirguṇḍī śārivā śelu raṅgolaś ca(1) viṣāpahaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वार्तिनुन्मसूरो ऽथ पित्तमुक् तण्ड्लीयकं /
निर्गुण्डी शारिवा शेलु रङ्गोलश् च(1) विषापहः //
text_mt: Lentils remove all pain; and spiny amaranth releases pitta; / nirguṇḍī, śārivā, śelu, and aṅkoṭha remove poison.

sanskrit_iast:
mahauṣadhaṃ mṛtāṃ kṣudrāṃ puṣkaraṃ(2)granthikodbhavaṃ(3) /
pivet kaṇāyutaṃ kvāthaṃ mūrchāyāñca madeṣu ca //
meaning:
महौषधं मृतां क्षुद्रां पुष्करं(2)ग्रन्थिकोद्भवं(3) /
पिवेत् कणायुतं क्वाथं मूर्छायाञ्च मदेषु च //
text_mt: Ginger, guḍūcī, kaṇṭakārī, puṣkaramūla, and pippalīmūla: / one should drink the decoction mixed with pippalī in cases of fainting and intoxications.

sanskrit_iast:
hiṅgusaurcalavyoṣairdviplāṃśairghṛtāḍhakaṃ(?) /
caturguṇe gavāṃ mūtre siddhamunmādanāśanaṃ //
meaning:
हिङ्गुसौर्चलव्योषैर्द्विप्लांशैर्घृताढकं(?) /
चतुर्गुणे गवां मूत्रे सिद्धमुन्मादनाशनं //
text_mt: One āḍhaka of clarified butter with asafoetida, black salt, and the three pungents, two palas of each, / boiled down in four times as much cow's urine, destroys madness.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkhapuṣpīvattākuṣṭhaiḥ siddhaṃ brāhmīrasair yutaṃ /
purāṇaṃ hantyapasmāraṃ sonmādaṃ medhyamuttamaṃ //
meaning:
शङ्खपुष्पीवत्ताकुष्ठैः सिद्धं ब्राह्मीरसैर् युतं /
पुराणं हन्त्यपस्मारं सोन्मादं मेध्यमुत्तमं //
text_mt: [Ghee] prepared with śaṅkhapuṣpī, vacā, and kuṣṭha, combined with juice of brāhmī, / aged, destroys epilepsy along with insanity; it is supreme for intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcagavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tadvat kuṣṭhanuccābhayāyutaṃ /
paṭolatriphalānimbaguḍucīdhāvaṇīvṛṣaiḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चगव्यं घृतं तद्वत् कुष्ठनुच्चाभयायुतं /
पटोलत्रिफलानिम्बगुडुचीधावणीवृषैः //
text_mt: Clarified butter [prepared with] the five products of the cow, likewise, combined with chebulic myrobalan, cures skin diseases. / With paṭola, triphalā, neem, guḍūcī, dhāvanī, and vāsā,

sanskrit_iast:
sakarañjair ghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ kuṣṭhanudvajrakaṃ smṛtaṃ /
nimbaṃ paṭolaṃ vyāghrī ca guḍūcī vāsakaṃ tathā //
meaning:
सकरञ्जैर् घृतं सिद्धं कुष्ठनुद्वज्रकं स्मृतं /
निम्बं पटोलं व्याघ्री च गुडूची वासकं तथा //
text_mt: clarified butter prepared along with karañja is considered the "Vajraka" [ghee], which cures skin diseases. / Neem, paṭola, kaṇṭakārī, guḍūcī, and vāsā:

sanskrit_iast:
kuryāddaśapalān bhāgān ekaikasya sakuṭṭitān /
jaladroṇe vipaktavyaṃ yāvatpādāvaśeṣitaṃ //
meaning:
कुर्याद्दशपलान् भागान् एकैकस्य सकुट्टितान् /
जलद्रोणे विपक्तव्यं यावत्पादावशेषितं //
text_mt: one should make portions of ten palas of each, crushed; / it is to be boiled in a droṇa of water until one quarter remains.

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtaprasthampacettena triphalāgarbhasaṃyutaṃ(4) /
pañcatiktamiti khyātaṃ sarpiḥ kuṣṭhavināśanaṃ //
meaning:
घृतप्रस्थम्पचेत्तेन त्रिफलागर्भसंयुतं(4) /
पञ्चतिक्तमिति ख्यातं सर्पिः कुष्ठविनाशनं //
text_mt: With that, one should cook a prastha of ghee containing a paste of triphalā. / This clarified butter, renowned as pañcatikta, is the destroyer of skin disease (kuṣṭha).

sanskrit_iast:
aśītiṃ vātajānrogān catvāriṃśacca paittikān /
:n
1 vaṅkolaśceti kha.. , ña.. , ca
2 puṣpakamiti ja..
3 granthilodbhavamiti kha..
4 triphalāśarkarāyutamiti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 52
viṃśatiṃ ślaiṣmikān kāsapīnasārśovraṇādikān //
meaning:
अशीतिं वातजान्रोगान् चत्वारिंशच्च पैत्तिकान् /
:न्
1 वङ्कोलश्चेति ख.. , ञ.. , च
2 पुष्पकमिति ज..
3 ग्रन्थिलोद्भवमिति ख..
4 त्रिफलाशर्करायुतमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 52
विंशतिं श्लैष्मिकान् कासपीनसार्शोव्रणादिकान् //
text_mt:
Eighty diseases born of vāta, forty born of pitta,
[Notes]
1. "vaṅkolaś ca" in kha, ña, ca
2. "puṣpakam iti" in ja
3. "granthilodbhavam iti" in kha
4. "triphalāśarkarāyutam iti" in kha, ña, ca / page 52
and twenty born of phlegm (śleṣman), as well as cough, chronic catarrh, piles, ulcers, and the like—

sanskrit_iast:
hantyanyān yogarajo 'yaṃ yathārkastimiraṃ khalu /
triphalāyāḥ kaṣāyena bhṛṅnarājarasena ca //
meaning:
हन्त्यन्यान् योगरजो ऽयं यथार्कस्तिमिरं खलु /
त्रिफलायाः कषायेन भृङ्नराजरसेन च //
text_mt: this king of formulations truly destroys these and others, just as the sun dispels darkness. / With a decoction of triphalā and the juice of bhṛṅgarāja,

sanskrit_iast:
vraṇaprakṣālanaṅkuryādupadaṃśapraśāntaye /
paṭīladalacūrṇena dāḍimatvagrajo 'tha vā //
meaning:
व्रणप्रक्षालनङ्कुर्यादुपदंशप्रशान्तये /
पटीलदलचूर्णेन दाडिमत्वग्रजो ऽथ वा //
text_mt: one should wash ulcers to alleviate venereal sores (upadaṃśa); / or with powder of leaves of paṭola or powder of pomegranate bark,

sanskrit_iast:
guṇḍayecca gajenāpi(1) triphalācūrṇakena ca /
triphalāyorajoyaṣṭhimārkavotpalamāricaiḥ //
meaning:
गुण्डयेच्च गजेनापि(1) त्रिफलाचूर्णकेन च /
त्रिफलायोरजोयष्ठिमार्कवोत्पलमारिचैः //
text_mt: one should dust [the wound], or with gaja, or with triphalā powder. / With triphalā, iron powder, liquorice, bhṛṅgarāja, blue water-lily, and black pepper,

sanskrit_iast:
samaindhavaiḥ pacettailamabhyaṅgācchardikāpahaṃ /
sakṣīrān mārkavarasān dviprasthamadhukotpalaiḥ //
meaning:
समैन्धवैः पचेत्तैलमभ्यङ्गाच्छर्दिकापहं /
सक्षीरान् मार्कवरसान् द्विप्रस्थमधुकोत्पलैः //
text_mt: along with rock salt, one should cook oil; applied by massage, it cures vomiting. / With juice of bhṛṅgarāja mixed with milk, two prasthas of madhuka and blue water-lily,

sanskrit_iast:
pacettu tailakuḍavaṃ tannasyaṃ palitāpahaṃ /
nimbampaṭolaṃ triphalā guḍūcī svadiraṃ vṛṣaṃ //
meaning:
पचेत्तु तैलकुडवं तन्नस्यं पलितापहं /
निम्बम्पटोलं त्रिफला गुडूची स्वदिरं वृषं //
text_mt: one should cook a kuḍava of oil; used as nasal drops, it cures greying hair. / Neem, paṭola, triphalā, guḍūcī, khadira, and vāsaka,

sanskrit_iast:
bhūnimbapāṭhātriphalāguḍūcīraktacandanaṃ /
yogadvayaṃ jvaraṃ hanti kuṣṭhavisphoṭakādikaṃ //
meaning:
भूनिम्बपाठात्रिफलागुडूचीरक्तचन्दनं /
योगद्वयं ज्वरं हन्ति कुष्ठविस्फोटकादिकं //
text_mt: or bhūnimba, pāṭhā, triphalā, guḍūcī, and red sandalwood— / these two formulations destroy fever, skin disease (kuṣṭha), eruptions, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
paṭolāmṛtabhūnimbavāsāriṣṭakaparpaṭaiḥ /
khadirāntayutaiḥ kvātho visphoṭajvaraśāntikṛt //
meaning:
पटोलामृतभूनिम्बवासारिष्टकपर्पटैः /
खदिरान्तयुतैः क्वाथो विस्फोटज्वरशान्तिकृत् //
text_mt: A decoction of paṭola, amṛtā, bhūnimba, vāsā, ariṣṭaka, and parpaṭa, / ending with khadira, brings about the alleviation of eruptions and fever.

sanskrit_iast:
daśamūlī cchinnaruhā pathyā dāru punarnavā /
jvaravidradhiśotheṣu śigruviśvajitā hitāḥ //
meaning:
दशमूली च्छिन्नरुहा पथ्या दारु पुनर्नवा /
ज्वरविद्रधिशोथेषु शिग्रुविश्वजिता हिताः //
text_mt: Daśamūlī, chinnaruhā, pathyā, devadāru, and punarnavā, / along with śigru and viśvabheṣaja, are beneficial in fever, abscesses, and swellings.

sanskrit_iast:
madhūkaṃ nimbapatrāṇi lepaḥ syadvraṇaśodhanaḥ /
triphalā khadiro dārvī nyagrodhātibalākuśāḥ //
meaning:
मधूकं निम्बपत्राणि लेपः स्यद्व्रणशोधनः /
त्रिफला खदिरो दार्वी न्यग्रोधातिबलाकुशाः //
text_mt: A paste of madhūka and neem leaves cleanses ulcers. / Triphalā, khadira, dārvī, banyan, atibalā, and kuśa grass,

sanskrit_iast:
nimbamūlakapatrāṇāṃ kaṣāyāḥ śodhane hitāḥ /
karañjāriṣṭanirguṇḍīraso hanyādvraṇakramīn //
:n
1 guṇḍayennagajenāpīti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 53
meaning:
निम्बमूलकपत्राणां कषायाः शोधने हिताः /
करञ्जारिष्टनिर्गुण्डीरसो हन्याद्व्रणक्रमीन् //
:न्
1 गुण्डयेन्नगजेनापीति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 53
text_mt:
decoctions of neem root and leaves are beneficial for cleansing. / The juice of karañja, ariṣṭa, and nirguṇḍī destroys maggots in ulcers.
[Notes]
1. "guṇḍayennagajenāpīti" in kha, ña, ca / page 53

sanskrit_iast:
dhātakicandanabalāsamaṅgāmadhukotpalaiḥ /
dārvīmedonvitair lepaḥ samarpirvraṇaropaṇaḥ //
meaning:
धातकिचन्दनबलासमङ्गामधुकोत्पलैः /
दार्वीमेदोन्वितैर् लेपः समर्पिर्व्रणरोपणः //
text_mt: A paste made with dhātakī, sandalwood, balā, samaṅgā, madhuka, blue water-lily, / dārvī, and medā, combined with clarified butter, heals ulcers.

sanskrit_iast:
guggulutriphalāvyoṣasamāṃrśair ghṛtayogataḥ /
nāḍī duṣṭavraṇaṃ śūlambhagandaramukhaṃ haret //
meaning:
गुग्गुलुत्रिफलाव्योषसमांर्शैर् घृतयोगतः /
नाडी दुष्टव्रणं शूलम्भगन्दरमुखं हरेत् //
text_mt: Guggulu, triphalā, and vyoṣa in equal parts, combined with ghee, / will cure sinus tract (nāḍī), malignant ulcers, colic, and fistula-in-ano.

sanskrit_iast:
haritakīṃ mūtrasiddhāṃ satailalavaṇānvitāṃ /
prātaḥ prātaś ca seveta kaphavātāmayāpahāṃ(1) //
meaning:
हरितकीं मूत्रसिद्धां सतैललवणान्वितां /
प्रातः प्रातश् च सेवेत कफवातामयापहां(1) //
text_mt: One should consume every morning harītakī cooked in urine, / combined with oil and salt; it dispels diseases of kapha and vāta.

sanskrit_iast:
trikaṭutriphalākvāthaṃ(2) sakṣāralavaṇaṃ pivet /
kaphavātātmakeṣveva virekaḥ kaphavṛddhinut //
meaning:
त्रिकटुत्रिफलाक्वाथं(2) सक्षारलवणं पिवेत् /
कफवातात्मकेष्वेव विरेकः कफवृद्धिनुत् //
text_mt: One should drink a decoction of trikaṭu and triphalā with alkali and salt; / it is a purgative in conditions of kapha and vāta that removes increases in kapha.

sanskrit_iast:
pappalīpippalīmūlavacācitrakanāgaraiḥ /
kvāthitaṃ vā pivetpeyamāmavātavināśanaṃ //
meaning:
पप्पलीपिप्पलीमूलवचाचित्रकनागरैः /
क्वाथितं वा पिवेत्पेयमामवातविनाशनं //
text_mt: Or one should drink a draught decocted with long pepper, root of long pepper, / vacā, citraka, and dry ginger, which destroys rheumatoid conditions (āmavāta).

sanskrit_iast:
rāsnāṃ guḍucīmeraṇḍadevadārumahauṣadhaṃ /
pivet sarvāṅgike vāte sāme sandhyasthimajjage //
meaning:
रास्नां गुडुचीमेरण्डदेवदारुमहौषधं /
पिवेत् सर्वाङ्गिके वाते सामे सन्ध्यस्थिमज्जगे //
text_mt: One should drink rāsnā, guḍūcī, castor, devadāru, and dry ginger / in vāta affecting all limbs, accompanied by āma, and located in joints, bones, and marrow.

sanskrit_iast:
daśamūlakaśāyaṃ vā piveddhā nāgarāmbhasā /
śuṇṭhīgokṣurakakvāthaḥ prātaḥ prātir niṣevitaḥ //
meaning:
दशमूलकशायं वा पिवेद्धा नागराम्भसा /
शुण्ठीगोक्षुरकक्वाथः प्रातः प्रातिर् निषेवितः //
text_mt: Or one should drink a decoction of daśamūla, or drink it with ginger-water. / A decoction of dry ginger and gokṣura taken every morning

sanskrit_iast:
sāmavātakaṭīśūlapācano rukpraṇāśanaḥ /
samūlapatraśākhāyāḥ prasāraṇyāś ca tailakaṃ //
meaning:
सामवातकटीशूलपाचनो रुक्प्रणाशनः /
समूलपत्रशाखायाः प्रसारण्याश् च तैलकं //
text_mt: digests āmavāta and lumbar colic, and destroys pain. / Oil prepared from the roots, leaves, and branches of prasāraṇī,

sanskrit_iast:
guḍucyāḥ surasaḥ kalkaḥ cūrṇaṃ vā kvāthameva ca /
prabhūtakālamāsevya mucyate vātaśoṇitāt //
meaning:
गुडुच्याः सुरसः कल्कः चूर्णं वा क्वाथमेव च /
प्रभूतकालमासेव्य मुच्यते वातशोणितात् //
text_mt: or the fresh juice, paste, powder, or decoction of guḍūcī, / taken for a long time, frees one from gout (vātaśoṇita).

sanskrit_iast:
pippalī vardhamānaṃ vā sevyaṃ pathyā guḍena vā /
paṭolatriphalātīvrakaṭukāsṛtasādhitaṃ(3) //
meaning:
पिप्पली वर्धमानं वा सेव्यं पथ्या गुडेन वा /
पटोलत्रिफलातीव्रकटुकासृतसाधितं(3) //
text_mt: Or an increasing dose of long pepper should be taken, or pathyā with jaggery. / Prepared with paṭola, triphalā, intense kaṭukā, and asṛt,

pakvaṃ pītvā jayatyāśu sadāhaṃ vātaśoṇitaṃ /

boiled and drunk, it quickly overcomes vātaśoṇita accompanied by burning sensations.

Guggulu with lukewarm or cold water, or with water of guḍūcī and triphalā,

sanskrit_iast:
balāpunar navair aṇḍavṛhatīdvayagokṣuraiḥ /
sahiṅgu lavanaiḥ pītaṃ sadyo vātarujāpahaṃ //
meaning:
बलापुनर् नवैर् अण्डवृहतीद्वयगोक्षुरैः /
सहिङ्गु लवनैः पीतं सद्यो वातरुजापहं //
text_mt: or drunk with balā, punarnavā, castor, the two bṛhatīs, and gokṣura, / along with asafoetida and salts, immediately dispels pain from vāta.

sanskrit_iast:
kārṣikaṃ pippalīmūlaṃ pañcaiva lavaṇāni ca /
pippalī citrakaṃ śuṇṭhī triphalā trivṛtā vacā //
meaning:
कार्षिकं पिप्पलीमूलं पञ्चैव लवणानि च /
पिप्पली चित्रकं शुण्ठी त्रिफला त्रिवृता वचा //
text_mt: A karṣa each of long pepper root, the five salts, / long pepper, citraka, dry ginger, triphalā, trivṛt, and vacā,

sanskrit_iast:
dvau kṣārau śādvalā dantī svarṇakṣīrī viṣāṇikā /
kolapramāṇāṃ guṭikāṃ pivet sauvīrakāyutāṃ //
meaning:
द्वौ क्षारौ शाद्वला दन्ती स्वर्णक्षीरी विषाणिका /
कोलप्रमाणां गुटिकां पिवेत् सौवीरकायुतां //
text_mt: the two alkalis, śādvalā, dantī, svarṇakṣīrī, and viṣāṇikā— / one should drink a pill the size of a jujube berry taken with sauvīraka vinegar.

sanskrit_iast:
śothāvapāke trivṛtā pravṛddhe codarādike /
kṣīraṃ śothaharaṃ dāru varṣābhūrnāgaraiḥ śubham //
meaning:
शोथावपाके त्रिवृता प्रवृद्धे चोदरादिके /
क्षीरं शोथहरं दारु वर्षाभूर्नागरैः शुभम् //
text_mt: Trivṛt is beneficial in the suppurative stage of swelling, and when abdominal enlargement or the like is advanced. / Milk prepared with devadāru, varṣābhū, and dry ginger is auspicious and removes swelling.

sanskrit_iast:
sekas tathārkavarṣābhūnimbakvāthena śothajit /
vyoṣagarbhaṃ palāśasya triguṇe bhasmavāriṇi //
meaning:
सेकस् तथार्कवर्षाभूनिम्बक्वाथेन शोथजित् /
व्योषगर्भं पलाशस्य त्रिगुणे भस्मवारिणि //
text_mt: Likewise, affusion with a decoction of arka, varṣābhū, and neem overcomes swelling. / Clarified butter prepared with vyoṣa inside, cooked in thrice the amount

sanskrit_iast:
sādhitaṃ pivataḥ sarpiḥ patatyarśo na saṃśayaḥ /
viśvaksenāvanirguṇḍīsādhitaṃ cāpi lāvaṇaṃ //
meaning:
साधितं पिवतः सर्पिः पतत्यर्शो न संशयः /
विश्वक्सेनावनिर्गुण्डीसाधितं चापि लावणं //
text_mt: of ash-water of palāśa—for one drinking it, piles fall off without doubt. / Also salt prepared with viśvaksenā and nirguṇḍī,

sanskrit_iast:
viḍaṅgānalasindhūttharāsnāgrakṣāradārubhiḥ /
tailañcaturguṇaṃ siddhaṃ kaṭudravyaṃ jalena vā //
meaning:
विडङ्गानलसिन्धूत्थरास्नाग्रक्षारदारुभिः /
तैलञ्चतुर्गुणं सिद्धं कटुद्रव्यं जलेन वा //
text_mt: or pungent substances with viḍaṅga, citraka, rock salt, rāsnā, agrakṣāra, / and devadāru cooked in four times the amount of oil, or with water,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇḍamālāpahaṃ tailamabhyaṅgāt galagaṇḍanut /
śaṭīkunāgabalayakvāthaḥ kṣīrarase yutam //
meaning:
गण्डमालापहं तैलमभ्यङ्गात् गलगण्डनुत् /
शटीकुनागबलयक्वाथः क्षीररसे युतम् //
text_mt: is an oil that removes cervical adenitis (gaṇḍamālā); through massage, it cures goitre. / A decoction of śaṭī, kunāga, and balā, combined with milk and meat soup,

sanskrit_iast:
payasyāpippalīvāsākalkaṃ siddhaṃ kṣaye hitam /
vacāviḍabhayāśuṇṭhīhiṅgukuṣṭhāgnidīpyakān //
meaning:
पयस्यापिप्पलीवासाकल्कं सिद्धं क्षये हितम् /
वचाविडभयाशुण्ठीहिङ्गुकुष्ठाग्निदीप्यकान् //
text_mt: prepared with a paste of payasyā, long pepper, and vāsā, is beneficial in wasting. / Vacā, black salt, abhayā, dry ginger, asafoetida, kuṣṭha, citraka, and carom seeds,

sanskrit_iast:
dvitriṣaṭcaturekāṃśasaptapañcāśikāḥ kramāt /
cūrṇaṃ pītaṃ hanti gulmaṃ udaraṃ śūlakāsanut //
meaning:
द्वित्रिषट्चतुरेकांशसप्तपञ्चाशिकाः क्रमात् /
चूर्णं पीतं हन्ति गुल्मं उदरं शूलकासनुत् //
text_mt: in two, three, six, four, one, seven, and five parts respectively— / the powder drunk destroys abdominal tumors (gulma) and enlargement, and cures colic and cough.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṭhānikumbhatrikaṭutriphalāgniṣu sādhitam /

mūtreṇa cūrṇaguṭikā gulmaplīhādimardanī //

पाठानिकुम्भत्रिकटुत्रिफलाग्निषु साधितम् /

मूत्रेण चूर्णगुटिका गुल्मप्लीहादिमर्दनी //
text_mt:
Cooked with pāṭhā, nikumbha, trikaṭu, triphalā, and citraka,
[Notes]

a powder or pill taken with urine crushes abdominal tumors (gulma), spleen diseases, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
vāsānimbapaṭīlāni triphalā vātapittanut(1) /
lihyāt kṣaudreṇa viḍaṅgaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛmivināśanam //
meaning:
वासानिम्बपटीलानि त्रिफला वातपित्तनुत्(1) /
लिह्यात् क्षौद्रेण विडङ्गं चूर्णं कृमिविनाशनम् //
text_mt: Vāsā, neem, and paṭola with triphalā remove vāta and pitta. / One should lick viḍaṅga powder with honey to destroy parasites.

sanskrit_iast:
viḍaṅgasaindhavakṣāramūtrenāpi harītakī /
śallakīvadarījambupiyālāmrārjunatvacaḥ //
meaning:
विडङ्गसैन्धवक्षारमूत्रेनापि हरीतकी /
शल्लकीवदरीजम्बुपियालाम्रार्जुनत्वचः //
text_mt: Harītakī with viḍaṅga, rock salt, and alkali, or with urine; / barks of śallakī, vadarī, jambu, piyāla, mango, and arjuna,

sanskrit_iast:
pītāḥ kṣīreṇa madhvaktāḥ pṛthakśīṇitavāraṇāḥ /
vilvāmraghātakīpāṭhāśuṇṭhīmocarasāḥ samāḥ //
meaning:
पीताः क्षीरेण मध्वक्ताः पृथक्शीणितवारणाः /
विल्वाम्रघातकीपाठाशुण्ठीमोचरसाः समाः //
text_mt: drunk individually with milk and smeared with honey, arrest bleeding. / Equal parts of vilva, mango, dhātakī, pāṭhā, dry ginger, and mocārasa,

sanskrit_iast:
pītā rundhantyatīsāraṃ guḍatakreṇa durjayam /
cāṅgerīkoladadhyambunāgarakṣārasaṃyutam //
meaning:
पीता रुन्धन्त्यतीसारं गुडतक्रेण दुर्जयम् /
चाङ्गेरीकोलदध्यम्बुनागरक्षारसंयुतम् //
text_mt: drunk with jaggery and buttermilk, check obstinate diarrhoea. / Combined with cāṅgerī, jujube fruit, curd-water, dry ginger, and alkali,

sanskrit_iast:
ghṛtayukkvāthitaṃ peyaṃ gudaṃbhrase rujāpaham /
viḍaṅgātiviṣāmustaṃ dārupāthākaliṅgakam //
meaning:
घृतयुक्क्वाथितं पेयं गुदंभ्रसे रुजापहम् /
विडङ्गातिविषामुस्तं दारुपाथाकलिङ्गकम् //
text_mt: a decocted potion mixed with ghee relieves pain in prolapse of the rectum. / Viḍaṅga, ativiṣā, mustā, devadāru, pāṭhā, and holarrhena seeds,

sanskrit_iast:
marīcena samāyuktaṃ śothātīsāranāśanam /
śarkarāsindhuśuṇṭhībhiḥ kṛṣṇāmadhuguḍena vā //
meaning:
मरीचेन समायुक्तं शोथातीसारनाशनम् /
शर्करासिन्धुशुण्ठीभिः कृष्णामधुगुडेन वा //
text_mt: combined with black pepper, destroy swellings and diarrhoea. / With sugar, rock salt, and dry ginger, or with long pepper, honey, and jaggery,

sanskrit_iast:
dve dve khādeddharītakyau jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sukhī /
triphalā pippalīyuktā samdhvājyā tathaiva sā //
meaning:
द्वे द्वे खादेद्धरीतक्यौ जीवेद्वर्षशतं सुखी /
त्रिफला पिप्पलीयुक्ता सम्ध्वाज्या तथैव सा //
text_mt: one should eat two harītakī fruits each time; one will live happily for a hundred years. / Likewise triphalā combined with long pepper, honey, and clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast:
cūrnamāmalakaṃ tena surasena tu bhavitam /
madhvājyaśarkarāyuktaṃ liḍhvā strīśaḥ payaḥ pivet //
meaning:
चूर्नमामलकं तेन सुरसेन तु भवितम् /
मध्वाज्यशर्करायुक्तं लिढ्वा स्त्रीशः पयः पिवेत् //
text_mt: Powder of āmalaka macerated with its own fresh juice, / licked with honey, clarified butter, and sugar, makes one master over women; one should then drink milk.

sanskrit_iast:
māsapippaliśālīnāṃ yavagodhūmayos tathā /
cūrṇabhāgaiḥ samāṃśaiś ca pacet pippalīkāṃ śubhāṃ //
meaning:
मासपिप्पलिशालीनां यवगोधूमयोस् तथा /
चूर्णभागैः समांशैश् च पचेत् पिप्पलीकां शुभां //
text_mt: With equal parts of flour of black gram, long pepper, rice, / barley, and wheat, one should prepare a wholesome cake.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ bhakṣayitvā ca pivet śarkarāmadhuraṃ payaḥ /
navaś caṭakavajjambhed daśavārān striyaṃ dhruvam //
meaning:
तां भक्षयित्वा च पिवेत् शर्करामधुरं पयः /
नवश् चटकवज्जम्भेद् दशवारान् स्त्रियं ध्रुवम् //
text_mt: Having eaten it, one should drink milk sweetened with sugar; / like a young sparrow, he will certainly copulate ten times with a woman.

sanskrit_iast:
samaṅgādhātakīpuṣpalodhranīlotpalāni ca /
:n
1 tripalā cāmlapittanuditi kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 56
etat kṣīrena dātavyaṃ strīṇāṃ pradaranaśanaṃ //
meaning:
समङ्गाधातकीपुष्पलोध्रनीलोत्पलानि च /
:न्
1 त्रिपला चाम्लपित्तनुदिति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 56
एतत् क्षीरेन दातव्यं स्त्रीणां प्रदरनशनं //
text_mt:
Samaṅgā, dhātakī flowers, lodhra, and blue water lily—
[Footnote]
1. "Triphalā cures acid dyspepsia" in Kha and Ña.
[Page 56]
this should be administered with milk to women to destroy menorrhagia.

sanskrit_iast:
vījaṅkauraṇṭakañcāpi madhukaṃ śvetacandanaṃ /
padmotpalasya mūlāni madhukaṃ śarkarātilān //
meaning:
वीजङ्कौरण्टकञ्चापि मधुकं श्वेतचन्दनं /
पद्मोत्पलस्य मूलानि मधुकं शर्करातिलान् //
text_mt:
Seeds of kuraṇṭaka, madhuka, white sandalwood,
roots of lotus and blue water lily, licorice, sugar, and sesame seeds

sanskrit_iast:
dravamāṇeṣu garbheṣu garbhasyāpanamuttamaṃ /
devadāru nabhaḥ kuṣṭhaṃ(1) naladaṃ viśvabheṣajaṃ //
meaning:
द्रवमाणेषु गर्भेषु गर्भस्यापनमुत्तमं /
देवदारु नभः कुष्ठं(1) नलदं विश्वभेषजं //
text_mt:
provide the best stabilization of the fetus when the embryo is slipping away.
Devadāru, nabhas, kuṣṭha, spikenard, and dry ginger,

sanskrit_iast:
lepaḥ kāñcikamampaṣṭastailayuktaḥ śirortinut /
vastrapūtaṃ kṣipet koṣṇaṃ mindhūtyaṃ karṇaśūlanut //
meaning:
लेपः काञ्चिकमम्पष्टस्तैलयुक्तः शिरोर्तिनुत् /
वस्त्रपूतं क्षिपेत् कोष्णं मिन्धूत्यं कर्णशूलनुत् //
text_mt:
applied as a paste with fermented sour gruel and ambaṣṭhā, combined with oil, relieves headache.
Warm rock-salt water filtered through cloth and dropped [into the ear] relieves earache.

sanskrit_iast:
laśunārdrakaśigrūṇāṃ kadalyā vā rasaḥpṛthak /
balāśatāvarīrāsnāmṛtāḥ mairīyakeḥ pivet //
meaning:
लशुनार्द्रकशिग्रूणां कदल्या वा रसःपृथक् /
बलाशतावरीरास्नामृताः मैरीयकेः पिवेत् //
text_mt:
The separate juices of garlic, ginger, and śigru, or of banana, [relieve earache].
One should drink balā, śatāvarī, rāsnā, and amṛtā, or with mairīyaka wine;

sanskrit_iast:
triphalāsahitaṃ sarpistimiraghnamanuttamaṃ /
triphalāvyoṣasindhūptyair ghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ pivennaraḥ //
meaning:
त्रिफलासहितं सर्पिस्तिमिरघ्नमनुत्तमं /
त्रिफलाव्योषसिन्धूप्त्यैर् घृतं सिद्धं पिवेन्नरः //
text_mt:
ghee along with triphalā is unsurpassed in destroying cataracts.
A man should drink ghee prepared with triphalā, the three pungents, and rock salt;

sanskrit_iast:
cākṣuṣyambhedanaṃ hṛdyaṃ(2) dīpanaṃ krapharoganut /
nīlotpalasya kiñjalkaṃ gośakṛdrasasaṃyutaṃ //
meaning:
चाक्षुष्यम्भेदनं हृद्यं(2) दीपनं क्रफरोगनुत् /
नीलोत्पलस्य किञ्जल्कं गोशकृद्रससंयुतं //
text_mt:
it is beneficial to the eyes, purgative, pleasing to the heart, digestive, and relieves phlegm disorders.
The filaments of a blue water lily mixed with the juice of cow dung,

sanskrit_iast:
guṭikāñjanametat syāt dinarātryandhayorhitaṃ /
yaṣṭīmadhuvacākṛṣṇāvījānāṃ kuṭajasya ca //
meaning:
गुटिकाञ्जनमेतत् स्यात् दिनरात्र्यन्धयोर्हितं /
यष्टीमधुवचाकृष्णावीजानां कुटजस्य च //
text_mt:
formed into a pill for collyrium, is beneficial for day-blindness and night-blindness.
With a paste of licorice, vacā, black pepper, and seeds of kuṭaja,

sanskrit_iast:
kalkenāloḍya nimbasya kaṣāyo vamanāya saḥ /
snigdhasvinnayavantoyaṃ pradātavyaṃ virecanam //
meaning:
कल्केनालोड्य निम्बस्य कषायो वमनाय सः /
स्निग्धस्विन्नयवन्तोयं प्रदातव्यं विरेचनम् //
text_mt:
stirred into a decoction of neem, [the formulation] serves to induce vomiting.
To one who has been lubricated and sweated, purgative barley-water should be administered.

sanskrit_iast:
anyathā yojitaṃ kuryāt mandāgniṃ gauravāruciṃ /
pathyāsaindhavakṛṣṇānāṃ(3) cūrṇamuṣṇāmbunā pivet //
meaning:
अन्यथा योजितं कुर्यात् मन्दाग्निं गौरवारुचिं /
पथ्यासैन्धवकृष्णानां(3) चूर्णमुष्णाम्बुना पिवेत् //
text_mt:
Applied otherwise, it causes sluggish digestion, heaviness, and loss of appetite.
One should drink the powder of harītakī, rock salt, and pippalī with hot water;

sanskrit_iast:
virekaḥ sarvarogaghnaḥ śreṣṭho nārācasaṃjñakaḥ /
:n
1 kṛṣṇamiti kha..
2 kuṣṭhamiti ña..
3 pathyāsaindhavakuṣṭhānāmiti kha..
:p 57
siddhayogā munibhyo ye ātreyeṇa pradarśitāḥ /
sarvarogaharāḥ sarvayogāgryāḥ suśrutena hi //

caturaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kalpasāgaraḥ

विरेकः सर्वरोगघ्नः श्रेष्ठो नाराचसंज्ञकः /

2 कुष्ठमिति ञ..
3 पथ्यासैन्धवकुष्ठानामिति ख..

सिद्धयोगा मुनिभ्यो ये आत्रेयेण प्रदर्शिताः /
सर्वरोगहराः सर्वयोगाग्र्याः सुश्रुतेन हि //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मृतसञ्जीवनीकरसिद्धयोगो नाम
