:श् अथैकनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
शान्त्यायुर्वेदः
text_mt:
One should worship the superintendent of elephants, the elephant-trainer, and the astrologer.
One should give that drum to the superintendent of elephants, and he should beat it;
sitting on the elephant's haunches, he should sound it with auspicious, deep tones.
Thus in the Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni, the two hundred and ninetieth chapter, entitled “Pacification Rite for Elephants.”
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "kṛtvānyasmin" in mss. kha, ja, and ña]
[Page 79]
Now the two hundred and ninety-first chapter.
The pacification medicine.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanvantarir uvāca
goviprapālanaṃ karyaṃ rajñā gośāntimāvade /
gāvaḥ pavitrā māṅgalyā goṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ //
meaning:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
गोविप्रपालनं कर्यं रज्ञा गोशान्तिमावदे /
गावः पवित्रा माङ्गल्या गोषु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः //
text_mt:
Dhanvantari said:
The protection of cows and Brahmins must be performed by the king. I shall speak of the pacification rite for cows.
Cows are pure and auspicious; the worlds are established in cows.

sanskrit_iast:
śakṛnmūtraṃ paraṃ tāsāmalakṣmīnāśanaṃ paraṃ /
gavāṃ kaṇḍūyanaṃ vāri śṛṅgasyāghaughamardanam //
meaning:
शकृन्मूत्रं परं तासामलक्ष्मीनाशनं परं /
गवां कण्डूयनं वारि शृङ्गस्याघौघमर्दनम् //
text_mt:
Their dung and urine are supreme, supreme destroyers of misfortune.
Scratching cows and their horn-water crush a multitude of sins.

sanskrit_iast:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpaś ca rocanā /
śaḍaṅgaṃ paramaṃ pāne duḥsvapnādyādivāraṇaṃ //
meaning:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पश् च रोचना /
शडङ्गं परमं पाने दुःस्वप्नाद्यादिवारणं //
text_mt:
Cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and yellow pigment (rocanā):
this six-fold substance is supreme for drinking, warding off bad dreams and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
rocanā viṣarakṣoghnī grāsadaḥ svargago gavāṃ /
yadgṛhe duḥkhitā gāvaḥ sa yāti narakannaraḥ //
meaning:
रोचना विषरक्षोघ्नी ग्रासदः स्वर्गगो गवां /
यद्गृहे दुःखिता गावः स याति नरकन्नरः //
text_mt:
Rocanā destroys poison and demons. One who gives fodder to cows goes to heaven.
A man in whose house cows are distressed goes to hell.

sanskrit_iast:
paragogrāsadaḥ svargī gohito brahmalokabhāk /
godānātkīrtanādrakṣāṃ kṛtvā coddharate kulam //
meaning:
परगोग्रासदः स्वर्गी गोहितो ब्रह्मलोकभाक् /
गोदानात्कीर्तनाद्रक्षां कृत्वा चोद्धरते कुलम् //
text_mt:
One who gives mouthfuls of grass to another's cows attains heaven; one who is benevolent to cows attains the world of Brahmā.
By the gift of cows, by praising them, and by providing them protection, one delivers one's family.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāṃ śvāsāt pavitrā bhūḥ sparśanātkilviṣakṣayaḥ /
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam //
meaning:
गवां श्वासात् पवित्रा भूः स्पर्शनात्किल्विषक्षयः /
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् //
text_mt:
The earth is purified by the breath of cows; sins are destroyed by touching them.
Cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and kuśa-grass water—

sanskrit_iast:
ekarātropavāsaś ca śvapākamapi śodhayet /
sarvāśubhavināśāya purācīratamīśvaraiḥ //
meaning:
एकरात्रोपवासश् च श्वपाकमपि शोधयेत् /
सर्वाशुभविनाशाय पुराचीरतमीश्वरैः //
text_mt:
fasting for a single night [and drinking this] purifies even an outcaste.
In ancient times, this was practiced by the lords to destroy all inauspiciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyekañca tryahābhyamtaṃ mahāsāntapanaṃ smṛtaṃ /
sarvakāmapradañcaitat sarvāśubhavimardanam //
meaning:
प्रत्येकञ्च त्र्यहाभ्यम्तं महासान्तपनं स्मृतं /
सर्वकामप्रदञ्चैतत् सर्वाशुभविमर्दनम् //
text_mt:
Consuming each of these for three days is remembered as the Mahāsāntapana penance;
it bestows all desires and crushes all misfortune.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ payasā divasānekaviṃśatiṃ /
nirmalāḥ sarvakāmāptyā syurgagāḥ spur natottamāḥ //
:p 80
meaning:
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतिं /
निर्मलाः सर्वकामाप्त्या स्युर्गगाः स्पुर् नतोत्तमाः //
:प् 80
text_mt:
The Kṛcchrātikṛcchra penance consists of [subsisting solely on] milk for twenty-one days.
Spotless through attaining all desires, cows should be […]
[page 80]

sanskrit_iast:
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pivenmūtraṃ tryahamuṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pivet /
tryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pītvā vāyubhakṣaḥ paraṃ tryaham //
meaning:
त्र्यहमुष्णं पिवेन्मूत्रं त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पिवेत् /
त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पीत्वा वायुभक्षः परं त्र्यहम् //
text_mt: For three days one should drink warm [cow] urine, for three days drink warm ghee; / having drunk warm milk for three days, one subsists on air for the next three days.

sanskrit_iast:
taptakṛcchravrataṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ brahmalokadaṃ /
śītaistu śītakṛcchraṃ syādbrahmoktaṃ brahmalokadaṃ //
meaning:
तप्तकृच्छ्रव्रतं सर्वपापघ्नं ब्रह्मलोकदं /
शीतैस्तु शीतकृच्छ्रं स्याद्ब्रह्मोक्तं ब्रह्मलोकदं //
text_mt: The taptakṛcchra votive observance destroys all sins and bestows the world of Brahmā; / while with cold [ingredients] it is the śītakṛcchra, proclaimed by Brahmā, bestowing the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
gomūtreṇācaretsnānaṃ vṛttiṃ kuryācca gorasaiḥ /
gobhirvrajecca bhuktāsu bhuñjītātha ca govratī //
meaning:
गोमूत्रेणाचरेत्स्नानं वृत्तिं कुर्याच्च गोरसैः /
गोभिर्व्रजेच्च भुक्तासु भुञ्जीताथ च गोव्रती //
text_mt: One should bathe with cow urine and make one's living with cow products; / one observing the cow observance should walk with the cows and eat after they have eaten.

sanskrit_iast:
māsenaikena niṣpāpo golokī svargago bhavet /
vidyāñca gomatīṃ japtvā golokaṃ paramaṃ vrajet //
meaning:
मासेनैकेन निष्पापो गोलोकी स्वर्गगो भवेत् /
विद्याञ्च गोमतीं जप्त्वा गोलोकं परमं व्रजेत् //
text_mt: In one month, freed from sin, he attains Goloka and goes to heaven; / and having recited the Gomatī-vidyā, he goes to supreme Goloka.

sanskrit_iast:
gitair nṛtyair apsarobhirvimāne tatra modate /
gāvaḥ surabhayo nityaṃ gāvo guggulagandhikāḥ //
meaning:
गितैर् नृत्यैर् अप्सरोभिर्विमाने तत्र मोदते /
गावः सुरभयो नित्यं गावो गुग्गुलगन्धिकाः //
text_mt: He rejoices there in an aerial chariot with singing, dancing, and apsarases. / Cows are ever fragrant, cows smell of guggulu;

sanskrit_iast:
gāvaḥ pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ svastyayanaṃ paraṃ /
annameva paraṃ gāvo devānāṃ haviruttamam //
meaning:
गावः प्रतिष्ठा भूतानां गावः स्वस्त्ययनं परं /
अन्नमेव परं गावो देवानां हविरुत्तमम् //
text_mt: cows are the support of beings, cows are the supreme blessing; / cows are the highest food, the supreme oblation of the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
pāvanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kṣaranti ca vadanti ca /
haviṣā mantrapūtena tarpayantyamarāndivi //
meaning:
पावनं सर्वभूतानां क्षरन्ति च वदन्ति च /
हविषा मन्त्रपूतेन तर्पयन्त्यमरान्दिवि //
text_mt: They yield and are spoken of as the purifier of all beings; / with oblation purified by mantra, they satisfy the immortals in heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣīṇāmagnihotreṣu gāvo homeṣu yojitāḥ /
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ śaraṇamuttamaṃ //
meaning:
ऋषीणामग्निहोत्रेषु गावो होमेषु योजिताः /
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां गावः शरणमुत्तमं //
text_mt: In the agnihotras and fire oblations of the sages, cows are employed; / cows are indeed the supreme refuge of all living beings.

sanskrit_iast:
gāvaḥ pavitraṃ paramaṃ gāvo māṅgalyamuttamaṃ /
gāvaḥ svargasya sopānaṃ gāvo dhanyāḥ sanātanāḥ //
meaning:
गावः पवित्रं परमं गावो माङ्गल्यमुत्तमं /
गावः स्वर्गस्य सोपानं गावो धन्याः सनातनाः //
text_mt: Cows are the supreme purifier, cows are the highest auspiciousness; / cows are the stairway to heaven, cows are blessed and eternal.

sanskrit_iast:
namo gobhyaḥ śrīmatībhyaḥ saurabheyībhya eva ca /
namo brahmasutābhyaś ca pavitrābhyo namo namaḥ //
meaning:
नमो गोभ्यः श्रीमतीभ्यः सौरभेयीभ्य एव च /
नमो ब्रह्मसुताभ्यश् च पवित्राभ्यो नमो नमः //
text_mt: Homage to the cows, the auspicious daughters of Surabhi; / homage to the daughters of Brahmā, and homage, homage to the pure ones!

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇāś caiva gāvaś ca kulamekaṃ dvidhā kṛtam /
ekatra mantrāstiṣṭhanti havirekatra tiṣṭhati //
:p 81
meaning:
ब्राह्मणाश् चैव गावश् च कुलमेकं द्विधा कृतम् /
एकत्र मन्त्रास्तिष्ठन्ति हविरेकत्र तिष्ठति //
:प् 81
text_mt:
Brāhmaṇas and cows are one single family made into two: / in one place reside the mantras, and in the other resides the oblation.
[page 81]

sanskrit_iast:
devabrāhmaṇagosādhusādhvībhiḥ sakalaṃ jagat /
dhāryate vai sadā tasmāt sarve pūjyatamā matāḥ //
meaning:
देवब्राह्मणगोसाधुसाध्वीभिः सकलं जगत् /
धार्यते वै सदा तस्मात् सर्वे पूज्यतमा मताः //
text_mt: The entire universe is indeed constantly sustained by gods, brāhmaṇas, cows, virtuous men, and virtuous women; / therefore all are regarded as most worthy of worship.

sanskrit_iast:
pivanti yatra tattīrthaṃ gaṅgādyā gāva eva hi /
gavāṃ māhātmyamuktaṃ hi cikitsāñca tathā śṛṇu //
meaning:
पिवन्ति यत्र तत्तीर्थं गङ्गाद्या गाव एव हि /
गवां माहात्म्यमुक्तं हि चिकित्साञ्च तथा शृणु //
text_mt: The place where cows drink is indeed a sacred ford like the Gaṅgā and the rest. / The greatness of cows has thus been told; now listen to their medical treatment.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgāmayeṣu dhenūnāṃ tailaṃ dadyāt sasaindhavaṃ /
śṛṅgaverabalāmāṃsakalkasiddhaṃ samākṣikaṃ //
meaning:
शृङ्गामयेषु धेनूनां तैलं दद्यात् ससैन्धवं /
शृङ्गवेरबलामांसकल्कसिद्धं समाक्षिकं //
text_mt: In diseases of the horns of cows, one should give oil with rock salt, / prepared with a paste of ginger, balā, and māṃsī, along with honey.

sanskrit_iast:
karṇaśūleṣu sarveṣu mañjiṣṭhāhiṅgusaindhavaiḥ /
siddhaṃ tailaṃ pradātavyaṃ rasonenātha vā punaḥ //
meaning:
कर्णशूलेषु सर्वेषु मञ्जिष्ठाहिङ्गुसैन्धवैः /
सिद्धं तैलं प्रदातव्यं रसोनेनाथ वा पुनः //
text_mt: In all earaches, oil prepared with mañjiṣṭhā, asafoetida, and rock salt / should be administered, or else with garlic.

sanskrit_iast:
bilvamūlamapāmārgandhātakī casapāṭalā /
kuṭajandantamūleṣu lepāttacchūlanāśanaṃ //
meaning:
बिल्वमूलमपामार्गन्धातकी चसपाटला /
कुटजन्दन्तमूलेषु लेपात्तच्छूलनाशनं //
text_mt: Bilva root, apāmārga, dhātakī, and pāṭalā, / [applied] as a paste on the roots of the teeth, destroys their toothache.

sanskrit_iast:
dantaśūlaharair dravyair ghṛtaṃ rāma vipācitaṃ /
mukharogaharaṃ jñeyaṃ jihvārogeṣu saindhavaṃ //
meaning:
दन्तशूलहरैर् द्रव्यैर् घृतं राम विपाचितं /
मुखरोगहरं ज्ञेयं जिह्वारोगेषु सैन्धवं //
text_mt: Ghee cooked with substances that alleviate toothache, O Rāma, / is known to alleviate diseases of the mouth; in tongue diseases, rock salt [is prescribed].

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṅgaveraṃ haridre dve triphalā ca galagrahe /
hṛcchūle vastiśūle ca vātaroge kṣaye tathā //
meaning:
शृङ्गवेरं हरिद्रे द्वे त्रिफला च गलग्रहे /
हृच्छूले वस्तिशूले च वातरोगे क्षये तथा //
text_mt: Ginger, the two turmerics, and triphalā [are prescribed] in throat obstruction; / in heart pain, bladder pain, wind disorders, and consumption,

sanskrit_iast:
triphalā ghṛtamiśrā ca gavāṃ pāne praśasyate /
atīsāre haridre dve pāṭhāñcaiva pradāpayet //
meaning:
त्रिफला घृतमिश्रा च गवां पाने प्रशस्यते /
अतीसारे हरिद्रे द्वे पाठाञ्चैव प्रदापयेत् //
text_mt: triphalā mixed with ghee is recommended as a drink for cows; / in diarrhoea, one should give the two turmerics and pāṭhā.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣu koṣṭharogeṣu tathāśākhāgadeṣu ca /
śṛṅgaverañca bhārgīñca kāse śvāse pradāpayet //
meaning:
सर्वेषु कोष्ठरोगेषु तथाशाखागदेषु च /
शृङ्गवेरञ्च भार्गीञ्च कासे श्वासे प्रदापयेत् //
text_mt: In all diseases of the belly and afflictions of the limbs, / and in cough and shortness of breath, one should give ginger and bhārgī.

sanskrit_iast:
dātavyā bhagnasandhāne priyaṅgurlabaṇānvitā /
tailaṃ vātaharaṃ pitte madhuyaṣṭīvipācitaṃ //
meaning:
दातव्या भग्नसन्धाने प्रियङ्गुर्लबणान्विता /
तैलं वातहरं पित्ते मधुयष्टीविपाचितं //
text_mt: Priyaṅgu combined with salt should be given for uniting fractures; / oil cooked with liquorice alleviates wind, and [ghee cooked with it alleviates] pitta.

sanskrit_iast:
kaphe vyoṣañca samadhu sapuṣṭakarajo 'sraje /
tailājyaṃ haritālañca bhagnakṣatiśṛtandadet //
meaning:
कफे व्योषञ्च समधु सपुष्टकरजो ऽस्रजे /
तैलाज्यं हरितालञ्च भग्नक्षतिशृतन्ददेत् //
text_mt: In [diseases of] phlegm, [one should administer] the three pungents with honey; in [diseases of] the blood, [the same] with karanja seed powder. / One should give oil, ghee, and orpiment, boiled for fractures and wounds.

sanskrit_iast:
māsāstilāḥ sagodhūmāḥ paśukṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā /
:p 82
eṣāṃ piṇḍī salavaṇā vatsānāṃ puṣṭidātviyaṃ //
meaning:
मासास्तिलाः सगोधूमाः पशुक्षीरं घृतं तथा /
:प् 82
एषां पिण्डी सलवणा वत्सानां पुष्टिदात्वियं //
text_mt:
Urad, sesame seeds, with wheat, milk of animals, and ghee—
[p. 82]
A ball of these with salt brings nourishment to calves.

sanskrit_iast:
balapradā viṣāṇāṃ syadgrahanāśāya dhūpakaḥ /
devadāru vacā māṃsī guggulurhiṅgusarṣapāḥ //
meaning:
बलप्रदा विषाणां स्यद्ग्रहनाशाय धूपकः /
देवदारु वचा मांसी गुग्गुलुर्हिङ्गुसर्षपाः //
text_mt: It gives strength to the horns. An incense for destroying evil spirits [is]: / deodar, sweet flag, spikenard, guggulu, asafoetida, and mustard seeds.

sanskrit_iast:
grahādigadanāśāya eṣa dhūpo gavāṃ hitaḥ /
ghaṇṭhā caiva gavāṃ kāryā dhūpenānena bhūpitā //
meaning:
ग्रहादिगदनाशाय एष धूपो गवां हितः /
घण्ठा चैव गवां कार्या धूपेनानेन भूपिता //
text_mt: This incense is beneficial for cows, for destroying evil spirits and other diseases. / And a bell for cows should be made fumigated with this incense.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvagandhātilaiḥ śuklaṃ tena gauḥ kṣīriṇī bhavet /
rasāyanañca pinyākaṃ matto yo dhāryate gṛhe //
meaning:
अश्वगन्धातिलैः शुक्लं तेन गौः क्षीरिणी भवेत् /
रसायनञ्च पिन्याकं मत्तो यो धार्यते गृहे //
text_mt: With aśvagandhā and sesame seeds, [the discharge becomes] white, [and] thereby the cow becomes rich in milk. / And oil-cake is an elixir; it is kept in the house by one who is wise.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavāṃ purīṣe pañcabhyāṃ nityaṃ śāntyai śriyaṃ yajet /
vāsudevañca gandhādyair aparā śāntirucyate //
meaning:
भवां पुरीषे पञ्चभ्यां नित्यं शान्त्यै श्रियं यजेत् /
वासुदेवञ्च गन्धाद्यैर् अपरा शान्तिरुच्यते //
text_mt: One should daily worship Śrī in cow dung on the fifth [lunar day] for appeasement, / and Vāsudeva with perfumes and the like. Another appeasement rite is proclaimed:

sanskrit_iast:
aśvayukśuklapakṣasya pañcadaśyāṃ yajeddhariṃ /
harirudramajaṃ sūryaṃ śriyamagniṃ ghṛtena ca //
meaning:
अश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्यां यजेद्धरिं /
हरिरुद्रमजं सूर्यं श्रियमग्निं घृतेन च //
text_mt: On the fifteenth [tithi] of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, one should worship Hari, / Hari, Rudra, the Unborn [Brahmā], Sūrya, Śrī, and Agni with ghee.

sanskrit_iast:
dadhi samprāśya gāḥ pūjya kāryaṃ vāhnipradakṣiṇaṃ /
vṛṣāṇāṃ yojeyed yuddhaṃ gītavādyaravair vahiḥ //
meaning:
दधि सम्प्राश्य गाः पूज्य कार्यं वाह्निप्रदक्षिणं /
वृषाणां योजेयेद् युद्धं गीतवाद्यरवैर् वहिः //
text_mt: Having consumed curd and worshipped the cows, circumambulation of the fire should be performed. / One should stage a fight of bulls outside, accompanied by the sounds of song and instrumental music.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāntu lavaṇandeyaṃ brāhmaṇānāñca dakṣiṇā /
naimittike mākarādau yajedviṣṇuṃ saha śriyā //
meaning:
गवान्तु लवणन्देयं ब्राह्मणानाञ्च दक्षिणा /
नैमित्तिके माकरादौ यजेद्विष्णुं सह श्रिया //
text_mt: Salt should be given to cows, and a sacrificial fee to brāhmaṇas. / In occasional rites at the entrance of the sun into Capricorn and the like, one should worship Viṣṇu along with Śrī.

sanskrit_iast:
sthaṇḍilebje madhyagate dikṣu keśaragān surān /
subhadrājo raviḥ pūjyo bahurūpo balirvahiḥ //
meaning:
स्थण्डिलेब्जे मध्यगते दिक्षु केशरगान् सुरान् /
सुभद्राजो रविः पूज्यो बहुरूपो बलिर्वहिः //
text_mt: On a bare ground on a lotus placed in the center, and the gods situated on the filaments in the cardinal directions, / the Sun born of Subhadrā is to be worshipped, [and] a multiform oblation [made] outside.

sanskrit_iast:
khaṃ viśvarūpā siddhiś ca ṛddhiḥ śāntiś ca rohiṇī /
digdhenavo hi pūrvādyāḥ kṛśaraiś candra īśvaraḥ //
meaning:
खं विश्वरूपा सिद्धिश् च ऋद्धिः शान्तिश् च रोहिणी /
दिग्धेनवो हि पूर्वाद्याः कृशरैश् चन्द्र ईश्वरः //
text_mt: Kha, Viśvarūpā, Siddhi, Ṛddhi, Śānti, and Rohiṇī / are indeed the cows of the directions, beginning with the east. The Moon, the Lord [Śiva],

sanskrit_iast:
dikpālāḥ padmapatreṣu kumbheṣvagnau ca homayet /
kṣīravṛkṣasya samidhaḥ sarṣapākṣatataṇḍulān //
meaning:
दिक्पालाः पद्मपत्रेषु कुम्भेष्वग्नौ च होमयेत् /
क्षीरवृक्षस्य समिधः सर्षपाक्षततण्डुलान् //
text_mt: and the guardians of the directions [are to be worshipped] with rice boiled with pulses on lotus leaves, jars, and in fire. One should offer into the fire / kindling sticks of milky trees, mustard seeds, and unblemished whole grains of rice.

sanskrit_iast:
śataṃ śataṃ suvarṇañca kāṃsyādikaṃ dvije dadet /
gāvaḥ pūjyā vimoktavyāḥ śāntyai kṣīrādisaṃyutāḥ //
:p 83
meaning:
शतं शतं सुवर्णञ्च कांस्यादिकं द्विजे ददेत् /
गावः पूज्या विमोक्तव्याः शान्त्यै क्षीरादिसंयुताः //
:प् 83
text_mt:
One should give to a twice-born a hundred [pieces of] gold and bronze and other metals. / Cows are to be worshipped and set free, provided with milk and the like, for appeasement.
[p. 83]

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
śālihotraḥ suśrutāya hayāyurvedamuktavān /
pālakāpyo 'ṅgarājāya gajāyurvedamabravīt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śāntyāyurvedo
nāmaikanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dvinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mantraparibhāṣā
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
शालिहोत्रः सुश्रुताय हयायुर्वेदमुक्तवान् /
पालकाप्यो ऽङ्गराजाय गजायुर्वेदमब्रवीत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शान्त्यायुर्वेदो
नामैकनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्विनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मन्त्रपरिभाषा
text_mt:
Agni said: / Śālihotra taught the veterinary science of horses to Suśruta; / Pālakāpya spoke the veterinary science of elephants to the king of Aṅga.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-first chapter, named 'The Veterinary Science of Appeasement', in the Mahāpurāṇa taught by Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-second chapter.
Terminology of Mantras

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
mantravidyāhariṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu /
viṃśatyarṇādhikā mantrā mālāmantrāḥ smṛtā dvija //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
मन्त्रविद्याहरिं वक्ष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शृणु /
विंशत्यर्णाधिका मन्त्रा मालामन्त्राः स्मृता द्विज //
text_mt: Agni said: / I shall declare Hari in the form of mantra-lore, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation; listen: / Mantras containing more than twenty syllables are remembered as mālā-mantras, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
daśākṣarādhikā mantrāstadarvāgvījasaṃjñitāḥ /
vardhakye siddhidā hy ete mālāmantrāstu yauvena //
meaning:
दशाक्षराधिका मन्त्रास्तदर्वाग्वीजसंज्ञिताः /
वर्धक्ये सिद्धिदा ह्य् एते मालामन्त्रास्तु यौवेन //
text_mt: Mantras of more than ten syllables [are also designated thus]; those below that are termed seed-syllables. / These indeed grant accomplishment in old age, but mālā-mantras in youth.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcākṣarādhikā mantrāḥ siddhidāḥ sarvadāpare /
strīpuṃnapuṃsakatvena tridhāḥ syurmantrajātayaḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चाक्षराधिका मन्त्राः सिद्धिदाः सर्वदापरे /
स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकत्वेन त्रिधाः स्युर्मन्त्रजातयः //
text_mt: The other mantras of more than five syllables grant accomplishment at all times. / The classes of mantras are threefold by way of feminine, masculine, and neuter.

sanskrit_iast:
strīmantrā vahnijāyantā namontāś ca napuṃsakāḥ /
śeṣāḥ pumāṃsaste śastā vakṣyoccāṭaviṣeṣu ca(1) //
meaning:
स्त्रीमन्त्रा वह्निजायन्ता नमोन्ताश् च नपुंसकाः /
शेषाः पुमांसस्ते शस्ता वक्ष्योच्चाटविषेषु च(1) //
text_mt: Feminine mantras end with the wife of Agni [Svāhā], and neuter ones end with 'namaḥ'. / The remaining are masculine; they are recommended in eradication of rivals and poisons.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣudrakriyāmayadhvaṃse striyo 'nyatra(2) napuṃsakāḥ /
mantrāvāgneyasaumyākhyau tārādyantārdvayorjapet //
meaning:
क्षुद्रक्रियामयध्वंसे स्त्रियो ऽन्यत्र(2) नपुंसकाः /
मन्त्रावाग्नेयसौम्याख्यौ ताराद्यन्तार्द्वयोर्जपेत् //
text_mt: Feminine [mantras] are [used] in the destruction of petty magical acts and diseases; elsewhere neuter ones [are used]. / Mantras are designated fiery and gentle; one should recite both preceded by the praṇava [and ending with it].

sanskrit_iast:
tārāntyāgniviyatprāyo mantra āgneya iṣyate /
śiṣṭaḥ saumyaḥ praśastau tau karmaṇoḥ krūrasaumyayoḥ //
:n
1 bandhoccāṭavaśeṣu ceti ja..
2 striyo nātreti kha..
:p 84
meaning:
तारान्त्याग्निवियत्प्रायो मन्त्र आग्नेय इष्यते /
शिष्टः सौम्यः प्रशस्तौ तौ कर्मणोः क्रूरसौम्ययोः //
:न्
1 बन्धोच्चाटवशेषु चेति ज..
2 स्त्रियो नात्रेति ख..
:प् 84
text_mt:
A mantra consisting largely of the stars, the ending, fire, and ether is regarded as fiery. / The rest is gentle; those two are recommended respectively in cruel and gentle rites.
[Footnote]
1. 'bandhoccāṭavaśeṣu ca' according to manuscript ja.
2. 'striyo nātra' according to manuscript kha.
[p. 84]

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyamantraḥ saumyaḥ syātprāyaśo 'nte namo 'nvitaḥ /
saumyamantras tathāgneyaḥ phaṭkāreṇāntato yutaḥ //
meaning:
आग्नेयमन्त्रः सौम्यः स्यात्प्रायशो ऽन्ते नमो ऽन्वितः /
सौम्यमन्त्रस् तथाग्नेयः फट्कारेणान्ततो युतः //
text_mt: A fiery mantra becomes gentle, generally, when endowed with 'namaḥ' at the end. / Likewise, a gentle mantra becomes fiery when joined with the syllable 'phaṭ' at the end.

sanskrit_iast:
suptaḥ prabuddhamātro vā mantraḥ siddhiṃ na yacchati /
śvāpakālo mahāvāho jāgaro dakṣiṇāvahaḥ //
meaning:
सुप्तः प्रबुद्धमात्रो वा मन्त्रः सिद्धिं न यच्छति /
श्वापकालो महावाहो जागरो दक्षिणावहः //
text_mt: A sleeping mantra or one that has just awakened does not grant accomplishment. / The time of sleep is the left nostril, O mighty-armed one; the awake state is the flow through the right [nostril].

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyasya manoḥ saumyamantrasyaitadviparyayāt /
prabodhakālaṃ jānīyādubhayorubhayorahaḥ //
meaning:
आग्नेयस्य मनोः सौम्यमन्त्रस्यैतद्विपर्ययात् /
प्रबोधकालं जानीयादुभयोरुभयोरहः //
text_mt: Of a fiery mantra [the waking state is in the right nostril], and of a gentle mantra it is the reverse of this. / One should know the time of awakening of each of the two, day by day.

sanskrit_iast:
duṣṭarkṣarāśividveṣivarṇādīn varjayenmanūn /
rājyalābhopakārāya prārabhyāriḥ svaraḥ kurūn //
meaning:
दुष्टर्क्षराशिविद्वेषिवर्णादीन् वर्जयेन्मनून् /
राज्यलाभोपकाराय प्रारभ्यारिः स्वरः कुरून् //
text_mt:
One should avoid mantras having inauspicious asterisms, zodiacal signs, inimical syllables, and the like.
For the sake of gaining a kingdom, an enemy [letter] beginning with a vowel [destroys] the Kurus.

sanskrit_iast:
gopālakakuṭīṃ prāyāt pūrṇāmityuditā lipiḥ /
nakṣetrekṣakramādyojyā svarāntyau revatīyujau //
meaning:
गोपालककुटीं प्रायात् पूर्णामित्युदिता लिपिः /
नक्षेत्रेक्षक्रमाद्योज्या स्वरान्त्यौ रेवतीयुजौ //
text_mt:
The script is declared [by the mnemonic]: 'He went to the cowherd's hut, which was full.'
One should apply it in the order of asterisms and glances; the last two vowels are joined to Revatī.

sanskrit_iast:
velā guruḥ svarāḥ śoṇaḥ karmaṇaivetibheditāḥ /
lipyarṇā vaśiṣu jñeyā ṣaṣṭheśādīṃś ca yojayet //
meaning:
वेला गुरुः स्वराः शोणः कर्मणैवेतिभेदिताः /
लिप्यर्णा वशिषु ज्ञेया षष्ठेशादींश् च योजयेत् //
text_mt:
The times, the heavy syllables, the vowels, and the red [letters] are distinguished precisely by ritual action;
the letters of the alphabet are to be known among subjugating [factors], and one should apply the lord of the sixth [house] and others.

sanskrit_iast:
lipau catuṣpathasthāyāmākhyavarṇapadāntarāḥ /
siddhāḥ sādhyā dvitīyasthāḥ susiddhā vairiṇaḥ pare //
meaning:
लिपौ चतुष्पथस्थायामाख्यवर्णपदान्तराः /
सिद्धाः साध्या द्वितीयस्थाः सुसिद्धा वैरिणः परे //
text_mt:
When the alphabet is placed in a crossroad [diagram], the letters positioned within one's own name
are 'accomplished' (siddha); those in the second are 'to be accomplished' (sādhya); those [in the third] are 'well-accomplished' (susiddha); the others are enemies (vairin).

sanskrit_iast:
siddhādīn kalpayedevaṃ siddhātyantaguṇair api(1) /
siddhe siddho japāt sādhyo japapūjāhutādinā(2) //
meaning:
सिद्धादीन् कल्पयेदेवं सिद्धात्यन्तगुणैर् अपि(1) /
सिद्धे सिद्धो जपात् साध्यो जपपूजाहुतादिना(2) //
text_mt:
Thus one should determine the accomplished and the rest, even by the extreme qualities of the accomplished:
for an accomplished practitioner, [the mantra] is accomplished through recitation; the 'to-be-accomplished' through recitation, worship, fire oblation, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
susiddho dhyānamātreṇa sādhakaṃ nāśayedariḥ /
duṣṭārṇapracuro yaḥ syānmantraḥ sarvavininditaḥ //
meaning:
सुसिद्धो ध्यानमात्रेण साधकं नाशयेदरिः /
दुष्टार्णप्रचुरो यः स्यान्मन्त्रः सर्वविनिन्दितः //
text_mt:
The 'well-accomplished' [yields success] by mere meditation; the 'enemy' would destroy the practitioner.
A mantra that abounds in inauspicious syllables is condemned in every respect.

sanskrit_iast:
praviśya vidhivaddīkṣāmabhiṣekāvasānikām /
śrutvā tantraṃ guror labdhaṃ sādhayedīpsitaṃ manum //
meaning:
प्रविश्य विधिवद्दीक्षामभिषेकावसानिकाम् /
श्रुत्वा तन्त्रं गुरोर् लब्धं साधयेदीप्सितं मनुम् //
text_mt:
Having undergone initiation according to rule, concluding with consecration by aspersion,
and having heard the Tantra obtained from the guru, one should accomplish the desired mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
dhīro dakṣaḥ śucirbhakto japadhyānāditatparaḥ /
:n
1 siddhadyantadalair apīti ja..
2 japapūrṇāhutādineti kha..
:p 85
siddhastapasvī kuśalastantrajñaḥ satyabhāṣaṇaḥ //
meaning:
धीरो दक्षः शुचिर्भक्तो जपध्यानादितत्परः /
:न्
1 सिद्धद्यन्तदलैर् अपीति ज..
2 जपपूर्णाहुतादिनेति ख..
:प् 85
सिद्धस्तपस्वी कुशलस्तन्त्रज्ञः सत्यभाषणः //
text_mt:
A steadfast, competent, pure, devoted person intent on recitation, meditation, and the like,
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 1 ...]
[Variant reading: 2 ...]
[Page 85]
accomplished, practicing ascetic austerity, skilled, knowing the Tantras, speaking the truth,

sanskrit_iast:
nigrahānugrahe śakto gururityabhidhīyate /
śānto dāntaḥ paṭuścīrṇabrahmacaryo haviṣyabhuk //
meaning:
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तो गुरुरित्यभिधीयते /
शान्तो दान्तः पटुश्चीर्णब्रह्मचर्यो हविष्यभुक् //
text_mt:
capable of punishment and favor—such a one is designated a guru.
Calm, restrained, clever, having observed celibacy, eating sacrificial food,

sanskrit_iast:
kurvannācāryaśuśrūṣāṃ siddhotsāhī sa śiṣyakaḥ /
sa tūpadeśyaḥ putraś ca vinayī vasudas tathā //
meaning:
कुर्वन्नाचार्यशुश्रूषां सिद्धोत्साही स शिष्यकः /
स तूपदेश्यः पुत्रश् च विनयी वसुदस् तथा //
text_mt:
performing service to the teacher, enthusiastic for success—he is a disciple.
He should be instructed, as should a son, one who is humble, and one who offers wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
mantrandadyāt susiddhau tu sahasraṃ deśikaṃ japet /
yadṛcchayā śrutaṃ mantraṃ chalenātha balena vā //
meaning:
मन्त्रन्दद्यात् सुसिद्धौ तु सहस्रं देशिकं जपेत् /
यदृच्छया श्रुतं मन्त्रं छलेनाथ बलेन वा //
text_mt:
When [a mantra] is well-accomplished, he may impart it; but the spiritual teacher should recite it a thousand [times].
A mantra heard by chance, or acquired by trickery or by force,

sanskrit_iast:
patre sthitañca gāthāñca janayedyadyanarthakam /
mantraṃ yaḥ sādhayedekaṃ japahomārcanādibhiḥ //
meaning:
पत्रे स्थितञ्च गाथाञ्च जनयेद्यद्यनर्थकम् /
मन्त्रं यः साधयेदेकं जपहोमार्चनादिभिः //
text_mt:
or written on a leaf, or a metrical song, would produce misfortune.
If one accomplishes a single mantra by recitation, fire oblations, worship, and the like,

sanskrit_iast:
kriyābhirbhūribhistasya sidhyante svalpasādhanāt /
samyaksiddhaikamantrasya nāsādhyamiha kiñcana //
meaning:
क्रियाभिर्भूरिभिस्तस्य सिध्यन्ते स्वल्पसाधनात् /
सम्यक्सिद्धैकमन्त्रस्य नासाध्यमिह किञ्चन //
text_mt:
through numerous ritual acts, [other mantras] will succeed for him with little effort.
For one who has completely accomplished a single mantra, nothing here is unattainable.

sanskrit_iast:
bahumantravataḥ puṃsaḥ kā kathā śiva eva saḥ /
daśalakṣajapādeka varṇo mantraḥ prasidhyati //
meaning:
बहुमन्त्रवतः पुंसः का कथा शिव एव सः /
दशलक्षजपादेक वर्णो मन्त्रः प्रसिध्यति //
text_mt:
What is there to say of a man possessing many mantras? He is Śiva himself.
By a million recitations, a single-syllable mantra is accomplished.

sanskrit_iast:
varṇavṛddhyā japahrāsastenānyeṣāṃ samūhayet /
vījāddvitriguṇānmantrānmālāmantre japakriyā //
meaning:
वर्णवृद्ध्या जपह्रासस्तेनान्येषां समूहयेत् /
वीजाद्द्वित्रिगुणान्मन्त्रान्मालामन्त्रे जपक्रिया //
text_mt:
With an increase in syllables comes a decrease in recitation; by this [rule] one should calculate for others.
From the seed-syllable to mantras doubled or tripled, the act of recitation is [calculated] for a garland-mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
saṅkhyānuktau śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ sahasraṃ vā japādiṣu /
japāddaśāṃśaṃ sarvatra sābhiśekaṃ hutaṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
सङ्ख्यानुक्तौ शतं साष्टं सहस्रं वा जपादिषु /
जपाद्दशांशं सर्वत्र साभिशेकं हुतं विदुः //
text_mt:
When the number is not stated, [it is] one hundred and eight or a thousand in recitation and the like.
Everywhere, an oblation accompanied by consecration by aspersion is known to be one-tenth of the recitation.

sanskrit_iast:
dravyānuktau ghṛtaṃ home japo 'śaktasya sarvataḥ /
mūlamantrāddaśāṃśaḥ syādaṅgādīnāṃ japādikam //
meaning:
द्रव्यानुक्तौ घृतं होमे जपो ऽशक्तस्य सर्वतः /
मूलमन्त्राद्दशांशः स्यादङ्गादीनां जपादिकम् //
text_mt:
When the substance is not stated, ghee is [offered] in the fire oblation; recitation is [prescribed] everywhere for one who is unable.
The recitation and other rites for the limb[-mantras] and the rest should be one-tenth of the root-mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
japātsaśaktimantrasya kāmadā mantradevatāḥ /
sādhakasya bhavet tṛptā dhyānahomārcanādinā //
meaning:
जपात्सशक्तिमन्त्रस्य कामदा मन्त्रदेवताः /
साधकस्य भवेत् तृप्ता ध्यानहोमार्चनादिना //
text_mt:
Through recitation of an empowered mantra, the deities of the mantra grant desires;
they become satisfied with the practitioner through meditation, fire oblation, worship, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
uccairjapādviśiṣṭaḥ syādupāṃśurdaśabhirguṇaiḥ /
jihvājape śataguṇaḥ sahasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ //
:p 86
meaning:
उच्चैर्जपाद्विशिष्टः स्यादुपांशुर्दशभिर्गुणैः /
जिह्वाजपे शतगुणः सहस्रो मानसः स्मृतः //
:प् 86

sanskrit_iast:
prāṅmukho 'vāṅmukho vāpi mantrakarma samārabhet /
praṇavādyāḥ sarvamantrā vāgyato vihitāśanaḥ //
meaning:
प्राङ्मुखो ऽवाङ्मुखो वापि मन्त्रकर्म समारभेत् /
प्रणवाद्याः सर्वमन्त्रा वाग्यतो विहिताशनः //
text_mt:
Facing east or facing north, one should undertake the ritual of the mantra.
All mantras begin with Praṇava (Oṃ), [recited] with restrained speech, eating prescribed food.

sanskrit_iast:
āsīnastu japenmantrāndevatācāryatulyadṛk /
kuṭīviviktā deśāḥ syurdevālayanadīhradāḥ //
meaning:
आसीनस्तु जपेन्मन्त्रान्देवताचार्यतुल्यदृक् /
कुटीविविक्ता देशाः स्युर्देवालयनदीह्रदाः //
text_mt:
Seated, one should recite the mantras, viewing deity and teacher as equal.
The places should be an isolated hut, a temple, a river, or a lake.

sanskrit_iast:
siddhau yavāgūpūpair vā payo bhakṣyaṃ haviṣyakam /
mantrasya devatā tāvat(1) tithivāreṣu vai japet //
meaning:
सिद्धौ यवागूपूपैर् वा पयो भक्ष्यं हविष्यकम् /
मन्त्रस्य देवता तावत्(1) तिथिवारेषु वै जपेत् //
text_mt:
For accomplishment, his food should be sacrificial food—gruel, cakes, or milk.
One should recite the mantra's deity on the [prescribed] lunar days and weekdays,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamīcaturdaśyorgrahaṇādau ca sādhakaḥ /
dasro yamo 'nalo dhātā śaśī rudro gururditiḥ //
meaning:
कृष्णाष्टमीचतुर्दश्योर्ग्रहणादौ च साधकः /
दस्रो यमो ऽनलो धाता शशी रुद्रो गुरुर्दितिः //
text_mt:
on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days of the dark fortnight, and during an eclipse and the like, as a practitioner.
Dasra (Aśvinī), Yama (Bharaṇī), Anala (Kṛttikā), Dhātṛ (Rohiṇī), Śaśin (Mṛgaśīrṣa), Rudra (Ārdrā), Guru (Punarvasu), Diti (Puṣya),

sanskrit_iast:
sarpāḥ pitaro 'tha bhago 'ryamā śotetaradyutiḥ /
tvaṣṭā maruta indrāgnī mitrendrau nirṛtirjalam //
meaning:
सर्पाः पितरो ऽथ भगो ऽर्यमा शोतेतरद्युतिः /
त्वष्टा मरुत इन्द्राग्नी मित्रेन्द्रौ निरृतिर्जलम् //
text_mt:
the Serpents (Āśleṣā), the Ancestors (Maghā), then Bhaga (Pūrvaphālgunī), Aryaman (Uttaraphālgunī), the non-white light (Savitṛ, Hastā),
Tvaṣṭṛ (Citrā), the Maruts (Svātī), Indrāgnī (Viśākhā), Mitra and Indra (Anurādhā and Jyeṣṭhā), Nirṛti (Mūla), the Water (Pūrvāṣāḍhā),

sanskrit_iast:
viśvedevā hṛṣīkeśo vāyavaḥ salilādhipaḥ /
ajaikapādahirvradhnaḥ pūṣāśvinyādidevatāḥ //
meaning:
विश्वेदेवा हृषीकेशो वायवः सलिलाधिपः /
अजैकपादहिर्व्रध्नः पूषाश्विन्यादिदेवताः //
text_mt:
the Viśvedevas (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Hṛṣīkeśa (Śravaṇa), the Vāyus (Śraviṣṭhā/Dhaniṣṭhā), the Lord of Waters (Śatabhiṣaj),
Ajaikapād (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Ahirbudhnya (Uttarabhādrapadā), Pūṣan (Revatī)—these are the deities beginning with Aśvinī.

sanskrit_iast:
agnidasrāvumā nighno nāgaś candro divākaraḥ /
mātṛdurgā diśāmīśaḥ kṛṣṇo vaivasvataḥ śivaḥ //
meaning:
अग्निदस्रावुमा निघ्नो नागश् चन्द्रो दिवाकरः /
मातृदुर्गा दिशामीशः कृष्णो वैवस्वतः शिवः //
text_mt:
Agni, the two Dasras, Umā, Vighnahartṛ (Gaṇeśa), the Nāga, the Moon, the Sun,
the Mothers, Durgā, the Lord of Directions (Yama), Kṛṣṇa, Vaivasvata, Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcadaśyāḥ śaśāṅkastu pitarastithidevatāḥ /
haro durgā gururviṣṇurbrahmā lakṣmīrdhaneśvaraḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चदश्याः शशाङ्कस्तु पितरस्तिथिदेवताः /
हरो दुर्गा गुरुर्विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा लक्ष्मीर्धनेश्वरः //
text_mt:
and for the fifteenth [lunar day], the Moon (Pūrṇimā) or the Ancestors (Amāvāsyā)—these are the deities of the lunar days.
Hara, Durgā, Guru, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Lakṣmī, and the Lord of Wealth (Kubera)—

sanskrit_iast:
ete suryādivāreśā lipinyāso 'tha kathyate /
keśānteṣu ca vṛtteṣu cakṣuṣoḥ śravaṇadvaye //
meaning:
एते सुर्यादिवारेशा लिपिन्यासो ऽथ कथ्यते /
केशान्तेषु च वृत्तेषु चक्षुषोः श्रवणद्वये //
text_mt:
these are the lords of the days beginning with Sunday. Now the ritual deposition of the alphabet is described:
at the edge of the hair, on the rounded regions [of the face], on the two eyes, on the two ears,

sanskrit_iast:
nāsāgaṇḍauṣṭhadantānāṃ dve dve mūrdhasyayoḥ kramāt /
varṇān pañcasuvargānāṃ(2) bāhucaraṇasandhiṣu //
meaning:
नासागण्डौष्ठदन्तानां द्वे द्वे मूर्धस्ययोः क्रमात् /
वर्णान् पञ्चसुवर्गानां(2) बाहुचरणसन्धिषु //
text_mt:
two each on the nose, cheeks, lips, and teeth, in the head and mouth in order;
the letters of the five groups [of consonants] on the joints of the arms and feet,

sanskrit_iast:
pārśvayoḥ pṛṣṭhato nābhau hṛdaye ca kramānnyaset /
:n
1 tareti kha..
2 pañcasvaravargāṇāmiti kha..
:p 87
yādīṃś ca hṛdaye nyasyedeṣāṃ syuḥ saptadhātavaḥ //
meaning:
पार्श्वयोः पृष्ठतो नाभौ हृदये च क्रमान्न्यसेत् /
:न्
1 तरेति ख..
2 पञ्चस्वरवर्गाणामिति ख..
:प् 87
यादींश् च हृदये न्यस्येदेषां स्युः सप्तधातवः //
text_mt:
on the two flanks, behind on the back, at the navel, and at the heart, one should deposit in order.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 1 ...]
[Variant reading: 2 ...]
[Page 87]
One should deposit the letters beginning with ya at the heart; these correspond to the seven bodily tissues:

sanskrit_iast:
tvagasṛṅmāṃsakasnāyumedomajjāśukrāṇi dhātavaḥ /
vasāḥ payo vāsako likhyante caiva lipīśvarāḥ //
meaning:
त्वगसृङ्मांसकस्नायुमेदोमज्जाशुक्राणि धातवः /
वसाः पयो वासको लिख्यन्ते चैव लिपीश्वराः //
text_mt:
skin, blood, flesh, sinew, fat, marrow, and semen are the tissues;
lymph, chyle, and muscle. And the lords of the alphabet are written:

sanskrit_iast:
śrīkaṇṭho 'nantasūkṣmau ca trimūrtiramareśvaraḥ /
agnīśo bhāvabhūtiś ca tithīśaḥ sthānuko haraḥ //
meaning:
श्रीकण्ठो ऽनन्तसूक्ष्मौ च त्रिमूर्तिरमरेश्वरः /
अग्नीशो भावभूतिश् च तिथीशः स्थानुको हरः //
text_mt:
Śrīkaṇṭha, Ananta and Sūkṣma, Trimūrti, Amareśvara,
Agnīśa, Bhāvabhūti, Tithīśa, Sthāṇuka, Hara,

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍīśo bhautikaḥ sadyojātaścānugraheśvaraḥ /
akrūraś ca mahāsenaḥ śaraṇyā devatā amūḥ //
meaning:
दण्डीशो भौतिकः सद्योजातश्चानुग्रहेश्वरः /
अक्रूरश् च महासेनः शरण्या देवता अमूः //
text_mt:
Daṇḍīśa, Bhautika, Sadyojāta, Anugraheśvara,
Akrūra, and Mahāsena—these are the protective deities.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ krodhīśattaṇḍau ca pañcāntakaśivottamau /
tathaiva rudrakūrmau ca trinetrau caturānanaḥ //
meaning:
ततः क्रोधीशत्तण्डौ च पञ्चान्तकशिवोत्तमौ /
तथैव रुद्रकूर्मौ च त्रिनेत्रौ चतुराननः //
text_mt:
Then Krodhīśa and Caṇḍa, Pañcāntaka and Śivottama,
likewise Rudra and Kūrma, Trinetra, and Caturānana,

sanskrit_iast:
ajeśaḥ śarmasoneśau tathā lāṅgalidārukau /
ardhanārīśvaraścomā kāntaścāṣāḍhidaṇḍinau //
meaning:
अजेशः शर्मसोनेशौ तथा लाङ्गलिदारुकौ /
अर्धनारीश्वरश्चोमा कान्तश्चाषाढिदण्डिनौ //
text_mt:
Ajeśa, Śarva and Someśa, likewise Lāṅgalin and Dāruka,
Ardhanārīśvara, Umākānta, Āṣāḍhin and Daṇḍin,

sanskrit_iast:
atrirmonaś ca meṣaś ca lohitaś ca śikhī tathā /
chagalaṇḍadviraṇḍau dvau samahākālavālinau //
meaning:
अत्रिर्मोनश् च मेषश् च लोहितश् च शिखी तथा /
छगलण्डद्विरण्डौ द्वौ समहाकालवालिनौ //
text_mt:
Atri, Mona, Meṣa, Lohita, and Śikhin,
Chagalaṇḍa and Dviraṇḍa, along with Mahākāla and Vālin,

sanskrit_iast:
bhujaṅgaś ca pinākī ca khaḍgīśaś ca vakaḥ punaḥ /
śveto bhṛgurlaguḍīśākṣaś ca sambartakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
भुजङ्गश् च पिनाकी च खड्गीशश् च वकः पुनः /
श्वेतो भृगुर्लगुडीशाक्षश् च सम्बर्तकः स्मृतः //
text_mt:
Bhujaṅga, Pinākin, Khaḍgīśa, and Baka again,
Śveta, Bhṛgu, Laguḍīśa, Akṣa, and Saṃvartaka is remembered.

sanskrit_iast:
rudrātmaśaktān likhyādīn namontān vinyaset kramāt /
aṅgāni vinyasetsarve mantrāḥ sāṅgāstu siddhidāḥ //
meaning:
रुद्रात्मशक्तान् लिख्यादीन् नमोन्तान् विन्यसेत् क्रमात् /
अङ्गानि विन्यसेत्सर्वे मन्त्राः साङ्गास्तु सिद्धिदाः //
text_mt:
One should deposit in order [these deities who are] identical with the powers of Rudra, ending with 'namaḥ', beginning with the vowels.
One should deposit the limb[-mantras]; all mantras endowed with limbs grant accomplishment.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛllekhāvyomasapūrvāṇyetānyaṅgāni vinyaset /
hṛdādīnyaṅgamantrāntair yo japeddhṛdaye namaḥ //
meaning:
हृल्लेखाव्योमसपूर्वाण्येतान्यङ्गानि विन्यसेत् /
हृदादीन्यङ्गमन्त्रान्तैर् यो जपेद्धृदये नमः //
text_mt:
One should deposit these limbs preceded by Hṛllekhā and Vyoman.
One who recites ending with the limb-mantras: 'hṛdayāya namaḥ' at the heart,

sanskrit_iast:
svāhā śirasyatha vaṣaṭśikhāyāṃ kavace c hūṃ /
vauṣat netre 'strāya phaṭasyāt pañcāṅgaṃ netravarjitam //
meaning:
स्वाहा शिरस्यथ वषट्शिखायां कवचे च् हूं /
वौषत् नेत्रे ऽस्त्राय फटस्यात् पञ्चाङ्गं नेत्रवर्जितम् //
text_mt:
'svāhā' at the head, then 'vaṣaṭ' at the crest, and 'hūṃ' on the armor,
'vauṣaṭ' on the eyes, 'astrāya phaṭ' for the weapon; the five-limbed [nyāsa] lacks the eyes.

sanskrit_iast:
niraṅgasyātmanā cāṅgaṃ nyasyemānniyutaṃ japet /
kramābhyāṃ devīṃ vāgīśīṃ yathoktāṃstu tilān hunet //
:p 88
meaning:
निरङ्गस्यात्मना चाङ्गं न्यस्येमान्नियुतं जपेत् /
क्रमाभ्यां देवीं वागीशीं यथोक्तांस्तु तिलान् हुनेत् //
:प् 88
text_mt:
For [a mantra] without limbs, having deposited the limbs with one's self, one should recite these a hundred thousand times.
In both ways, one should sacrifice sesame seeds as prescribed to the goddess Vāgīśī.
[Page 88]

sanskrit_iast:
lipidevī sākṣasūtrakumbhapustakapadmadhṛk /
kavitvādi prayaccheta karmādau siddhaye nyaset /
niṣkavirnirmalaḥ sarve mantrāḥsidhyanti mātṛbhiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mantraparibhāṣā nāma
dvinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha trinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nāgalakṣaṇāni
agnirucāca
meaning:
लिपिदेवी साक्षसूत्रकुम्भपुस्तकपद्मधृक् /
कवित्वादि प्रयच्छेत कर्मादौ सिद्धये न्यसेत् /
निष्कविर्निर्मलः सर्वे मन्त्राःसिध्यन्ति मातृभिः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मन्त्रपरिभाषा नाम
द्विनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रिनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नागलक्षणानि
अग्निरुचाच
text_mt:
Lipidevī holds a rosary, a water-pot, a book, and a lotus;
she bestows poetic skill and the like; one should perform the ritual deposition at the beginning of rites for success.
One becomes free of flaw and stainless; all mantras become accomplished by means of the Mother [syllables].
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-second chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'General Definitions of Mantras'.
Now follows the two hundred and ninety-third chapter.
Characteristics of Serpents.
Agni said:

sanskrit_iast:
nāgādayo 'tha bhāvādidaśasthānāni karma ca /
sūtakaṃ daṣṭaceṣṭeti saptalakṣaṇamucyate //
meaning:
नागादयो ऽथ भावादिदशस्थानानि कर्म च /
सूतकं दष्टचेष्टेति सप्तलक्षणमुच्यते //
text_mt:
The classes of serpents and others, the ten conditions and locations, and the action,
the astrological birth-omen, and the behavior of the bitten—these are declared to be the seven characteristics.

sanskrit_iast:
śeṣavāsukitakṣākhyāḥ karkaṭo 'bjo mahāmbujaḥ /
śaṅkhapālaś ca kulika ity aṣṭaunāgavaryakāḥ //
meaning:
शेषवासुकितक्षाख्याः कर्कटो ऽब्जो महाम्बुजः /
शङ्खपालश् च कुलिक इत्य् अष्टौनागवर्यकाः //
text_mt: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, named Takṣaka, Karkaṭa, Abja, Mahāmbuja, / Śaṅkhapāla, and Kulika—these are the eight chief serpents.

sanskrit_iast:
daśāṣṭapañcatriguṇaśatamūrdhānvitau kramāt /
viprau nṛpo viśau śūdrau dvau dvau nāgeṣu kīrtitau //
meaning:
दशाष्टपञ्चत्रिगुणशतमूर्धान्वितौ क्रमात् /
विप्रौ नृपो विशौ शूद्रौ द्वौ द्वौ नागेषु कीर्तितौ //
text_mt: Endowed with ten, eight, five, and three times a hundred hoods in order, / two are declared brāhmaṇas, one king, two vaiśyas, and two śūdras among serpents.

sanskrit_iast:
tadanvayāḥ pañcaśataṃ tebhyo jātā asaṃkhyakāḥ /
phaṇimaṇḍalirājīlavātapittakaphātmakāḥ //
meaning:
तदन्वयाः पञ्चशतं तेभ्यो जाता असंख्यकाः /
फणिमण्डलिराजीलवातपित्तकफात्मकाः //
text_mt: Their lineage consists of five hundred, and innumerable ones were born from them. / Hooded, circulatory, and striped [snakes] consist of wind, bile, and phlegm [respectively].

sanskrit_iast:
vyantarā doṣamiśrāste sarpāṃ darvīkarāḥ smṛtāḥ /
rathāṅgalāṅgalacchatrasvastikāṅkuśadhāriṇaḥ(1) //
meaning:
व्यन्तरा दोषमिश्रास्ते सर्पां दर्वीकराः स्मृताः /
रथाङ्गलाङ्गलच्छत्रस्वस्तिकाङ्कुशधारिणः(1) //
text_mt: Intermediate [snakes] have mixed humors; hooded snakes are known as darvīkaras, / bearing [the marks of] a chariot-wheel, a plough, an umbrella, a svastika, or an elephant-goad.

sanskrit_iast:
gonasā mandagā dīrghā maṇḍalair vidhaiścitāḥ(2) /
:n
1 rathāṅgalāṅgalatramuṣṭikāṅkuśadhāriṇa iti kha..
2 sthitā iti kha..
:p 89
rājilāścitritāḥ snigdhāstiryagūrdhvañca vājibhiḥ //
meaning:
गोनसा मन्दगा दीर्घा मण्डलैर् विधैश्चिताः(2) /
:न्
1 रथाङ्गलाङ्गलत्रमुष्टिकाङ्कुशधारिण इति ख..
2 स्थिता इति ख..
:प् 89
राजिलाश्चित्रिताः स्निग्धास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वञ्च वाजिभिः //
text_mt:
Gonasas are slow-moving, long, and covered with circles of various kinds.
[Footnote]
1. 'rathāṅgalāṅgalatramuṣṭikāṅkuśadhāriṇaḥ' according to manuscript kha.
2. 'sthitāḥ' according to manuscript kha.
[p. 89]
Rājilas are variegated, glossy, and [marked] horizontally and vertically with stripes.

sanskrit_iast:
vyantarā miśracihnāś ca bhūvarṣāgneyavāyavaḥ /
caturvidhāste ṣaḍviṃśabhedāḥ ṣoḍaśa gonasāḥ //
meaning:
व्यन्तरा मिश्रचिह्नाश् च भूवर्षाग्नेयवायवः /
चतुर्विधास्ते षड्विंशभेदाः षोडश गोनसाः //
text_mt: Intermediate snakes have mixed marks; [they are divided according to] earth, rain, fire, and wind. / They are of four kinds with twenty-six varieties; the gonasas are sixteen [varieties].

sanskrit_iast:
trayodaśa ca rājīlā vyantarā ekaviṃśatiḥ /
ye 'nuktakāle jāyante sarpāste vyantarāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
त्रयोदश च राजीला व्यन्तरा एकविंशतिः /
ये ऽनुक्तकाले जायन्ते सर्पास्ते व्यन्तराः स्मृताः //
text_mt: The rājilas are thirteen, and the intermediate ones are twenty-one. / Snakes that are born at an improper time are remembered as intermediate snakes.

sanskrit_iast:
āṣāḍhāditrimāsaiḥ syādgarbho māṣacatuṣṭaye /
aṇḍkānāṃ śate dve ca catvāriṃśat prasūyate //
meaning:
आषाढादित्रिमासैः स्याद्गर्भो माषचतुष्टये /
अण्ड्कानां शते द्वे च चत्वारिंशत् प्रसूयते //
text_mt: Conception occurs in the three months beginning with Āṣāḍha; in four months [the embryo develops]. / Two hundred and forty eggs are laid.

sanskrit_iast:
sarpā grasanti sūtaughān vinā strīpunnapuṃsakān /
unmīlate 'kṣi saptāhāt kṛṣṇo māsādbhavedvahiḥ //
meaning:
सर्पा ग्रसन्ति सूतौघान् विना स्त्रीपुन्नपुंसकान् /
उन्मीलते ऽक्षि सप्ताहात् कृष्णो मासाद्भवेद्वहिः //
text_mt: The serpents swallow their brood of offspring, except for females, males, and neuters. / The eyes open after seven days; after a month [the snake] becomes dark outside.

sanskrit_iast:
dvādaśāhāt subodhaḥ syāt dantāḥ syuḥ sūryadarśanāt /
dvātriṃśaddinaviṃśatyā catasrasteṣu daṃṣtrikāḥ //
meaning:
द्वादशाहात् सुबोधः स्यात् दन्ताः स्युः सूर्यदर्शनात् /
द्वात्रिंशद्दिनविंशत्या चतस्रस्तेषु दंष्त्रिकाः //
text_mt: From twelve days there is clear awareness; teeth emerge from the sight of the sun. / In thirty-two days or twenty, among them there are four fangs:

sanskrit_iast:
karālī makarī kālarātrī ca yamadūtikā /
etāstāḥ saviṣā daṃṣṭrā vāmadakṣiṇapārśvagāḥ //
meaning:
कराली मकरी कालरात्री च यमदूतिका /
एतास्ताः सविषा दंष्ट्रा वामदक्षिणपार्श्वगाः //
text_mt: Karālī, Makarī, Kālarātrī, and Yamadūtikā. / These are the poisonous fangs situated on the left and right sides.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣanmāsānmucyate kṛttiṃ jovetsaṣṭisamādvayaṃ /
nāgāḥ sūryādivāreśāḥ sapta uktā divā niśi //
meaning:
षन्मासान्मुच्यते कृत्तिं जोवेत्सष्टिसमाद्वयं /
नागाः सूर्यादिवारेशाः सप्त उक्ता दिवा निशि //
text_mt: After six months it sheds its skin; it lives for one hundred and twenty years. / The seven serpents are declared the lords of the days beginning with Sunday, day and night.

sanskrit_iast:
sveṣāṃ ṣaṭ prativāreṣu kulikaḥ sarvasandhiṣu /
śaṅkhena vā mahābjena saha tasyodayo 'thavā //
meaning:
स्वेषां षट् प्रतिवारेषु कुलिकः सर्वसन्धिषु /
शङ्खेन वा महाब्जेन सह तस्योदयो ऽथवा //
text_mt: Kulika [presides] in all junctions, with six [portions] for their own respective days; / or its rising occurs together with Śaṅkha or Mahābja,

sanskrit_iast:
dvayīrvā nāḍikāmantramantrakaṃ(1) kulikodayaḥ /
duṣṭaḥ sa kālaḥ sarvatra sarpadaṃśe viśeṣataḥ(2) //
meaning:
द्वयीर्वा नाडिकामन्त्रमन्त्रकं(1) कुलिकोदयः /
दुष्टः स कालः सर्वत्र सर्पदंशे विशेषतः(2) //
text_mt: or the rising of Kulika lasts for a measure of two nāḍikās. / That time is inauspicious everywhere, especially in snakebites.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛttikā bharaṇī svātī mūlaṃ pūrvatrayāśvanī /
viśākhārdrā maghāśleṣā citrā śravaṇarohiṇī //
meaning:
कृत्तिका भरणी स्वाती मूलं पूर्वत्रयाश्वनी /
विशाखार्द्रा मघाश्लेषा चित्रा श्रवणरोहिणी //
text_mt: Kṛttikā, Bharaṇī, Svātī, Mūla, the three Pūrvas, Aśvinī, / Viśākhā, Ārdrā, Maghā, Āśleṣā, Citrā, Śravaṇā, Rohiṇī,

sanskrit_iast:
hastā mandakujau vārau pañcamī cāṣṭamī tithiḥ /
:n
1 nāḍikāmātrasantrakamiti ña..
2 vinirdiśediti ka.. , kha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 90
ṣaṣṭhī raiktā śivā nindyā pañcamī ca caturdaśī //
meaning:
हस्ता मन्दकुजौ वारौ पञ्चमी चाष्टमी तिथिः /
:न्
1 नाडिकामात्रसन्त्रकमिति ञ..
2 विनिर्दिशेदिति क.. , ख.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 90
षष्ठी रैक्ता शिवा निन्द्या पञ्चमी च चतुर्दशी //
text_mt:
Hastā, the days of Saturn and Mars, the fifth and eighth lunar days,
[Footnote]
1. 'nāḍikāmātrasantrakam' according to manuscript ña.
2. 'vinirdiśet' according to manuscripts ka, kha, ja, and ṭa.
[p. 90]
the sixth, empty, and auspicious [tithis are deemed] reprehensible, as well as the fifth and fourteenth.

sanskrit_iast:
sandhyācatuṣṭayaṃ duṣṭaṃ dagdhayogāś ca rāśayaḥ /
ekadvibahavo daṃśā daṣṭaviddhañca khaṇḍitam //
meaning:
सन्ध्याचतुष्टयं दुष्टं दग्धयोगाश् च राशयः /
एकद्विबहवो दंशा दष्टविद्धञ्च खण्डितम् //
text_mt: The four twilights are inauspicious, as are burnt configurations and zodiacal signs. / The bites are one, two, or many, and [classified as] bitten, pierced, and torn.

sanskrit_iast:
adaṃśamavaguptaṃ(1) syāddaṃśamevaṃ caturvidham /
trayo dvyekakṣatā daṃśā vedanā rudhirolvaṇā //
meaning:
अदंशमवगुप्तं(1) स्याद्दंशमेवं चतुर्विधम् /
त्रयो द्व्येकक्षता दंशा वेदना रुधिरोल्वणा //
text_mt: [The bite] without fang-marks is concealed; thus the bite is of four kinds. / Bites may have three, two, or one puncture, with pain and profuse bleeding.

sanskrit_iast:
naktantvekāṅghrikūrmābhā daṃśāś ca yamacoditāḥ /
dīhīpipīlikāsparśī kaṇṭhaśotharujānvitaḥ(2) //
meaning:
नक्तन्त्वेकाङ्घ्रिकूर्माभा दंशाश् च यमचोदिताः /
दीहीपिपीलिकास्पर्शी कण्ठशोथरुजान्वितः(2) //
text_mt: Bites at night resembling a turtle with one foot are impelled by Yama. / Bites that feel like creeping ants, accompanied by swelling and pain in the throat,

sanskrit_iast:
satodo ranthito daṃśaḥ saviṣo nyastanirviṣaḥ /
devālaye śūnyagṛhe valmīkodyānakoṭare //
meaning:
सतोदो रन्थितो दंशः सविषो न्यस्तनिर्विषः /
देवालये शून्यगृहे वल्मीकोद्यानकोटरे //
text_mt: with pricking pain and hardening, are venomous; the rest are non-venomous. / [A bite inflicted] in a temple, an abandoned house, an anthill, the hollow of a garden [tree],

sanskrit_iast:
rathyāsandhau śmaśāne ca nadyāñca sindhusaṅgame /
dvīpe catuṣpathe saudhe gṛhe 'bje parvatāgrataḥ //
meaning:
रथ्यासन्धौ श्मशाने च नद्याञ्च सिन्धुसङ्गमे /
द्वीपे चतुष्पथे सौधे गृहे ऽब्जे पर्वताग्रतः //
text_mt: at a road junction, in a cremation ground, at a river, at a confluence with the ocean, / on an island, at a crossroads, in a palace, in a house, at a lotus pond, before a mountain,

sanskrit_iast:
vilahadvāre jīrṇakūpe jīrṇaveśmani kuḍyake /
śigruśleṣmātakākṣeṣu jambū ḍumbareṇeṣu ca //
meaning:
विलहद्वारे जीर्णकूपे जीर्णवेश्मनि कुड्यके /
शिग्रुश्लेष्मातकाक्षेषु जम्बू डुम्बरेणेषु च //
text_mt: at the opening of a hole, in an old well, in a ruined house, against a wall, / on a moringa, a śleṣmātaka, an akṣa tree, or among jambū and udumbara trees,

sanskrit_iast:
vaṭe ca jīrṇaprākāre khāsyahṛtkakṣajatruṇi /
tālau śaṅkhe gale mūrdhni civuke nābhipādayoḥ //
meaning:
वटे च जीर्णप्राकारे खास्यहृत्कक्षजत्रुणि /
तालौ शङ्खे गले मूर्ध्नि चिवुके नाभिपादयोः //
text_mt: or on a banyan tree, an old rampart, or on the cavity of the mouth, heart, armpit, collarbone, / palate, temple, throat, head, chin, navel, or feet—

sanskrit_iast:
daṃśo 'śubhaḥ śubho dūtaḥ puṣpahastaḥ suvāk sudhīḥ /
liṅgavarṇasamānaś ca śuklavastro 'malaḥ śuciḥ //
meaning:
दंशो ऽशुभः शुभो दूतः पुष्पहस्तः सुवाक् सुधीः /
लिङ्गवर्णसमानश् च शुक्लवस्त्रो ऽमलः शुचिः //
text_mt: such a bite is inauspicious. An auspicious messenger has flowers in hand, speaks well, is wise, / is equal in gender and caste [to the bitten person], wears white garments, is clean, and is pure.

sanskrit_iast:
apadvāragataḥ śastrī pramādī bhūgatekṣaṇaḥ /
vivarṇavāsāḥ pāśādihasto gadgadavarṇabhāk //
meaning:
अपद्वारगतः शस्त्री प्रमादी भूगतेक्षणः /
विवर्णवासाः पाशादिहस्तो गद्गदवर्णभाक् //
text_mt: One who approaches by the wrong door, carries a weapon, is careless, looks at the ground, / wears discoloured garments, holds a noose or the like, speaks with a stammering voice,

sanskrit_iast:
śuṣkakāṣṭhāśritaḥ khinnastilāktakakarāṃśukaḥ /
ārdravāsāḥ kṛṣṇaraktapuṣpayuktaśiroruhaḥ //
meaning:
शुष्ककाष्ठाश्रितः खिन्नस्तिलाक्तककरांशुकः /
आर्द्रवासाः कृष्णरक्तपुष्पयुक्तशिरोरुहः //
text_mt: leans on dry wood, is depressed, has hands smeared with sesamum, wears rags, / wears wet clothes, has black and red flowers in the hair,

sanskrit_iast:
kucamardī nakhacchedī gudaspṛk pādalekhakaḥ /
:n
1 sadaṃśamavaluptamiti ña..
2 kaṇṭhaśoṣarujāntrita iti ña..
:p 91
keśamuñcī tṛṇacchedī duṣṭā dūtāstathaikaśaḥ //
meaning:
कुचमर्दी नखच्छेदी गुदस्पृक् पादलेखकः /
:न्
1 सदंशमवलुप्तमिति ञ..
2 कण्ठशोषरुजान्त्रित इति ञ..
:प् 91
केशमुञ्ची तृणच्छेदी दुष्टा दूतास्तथैकशः //
text_mt:
presses the breast, cuts nails, touches the anus, scratches the feet,
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: 'with a bite, obscured' in manuscript ña.
2. Variant reading: 'accompanied by dryness and pain in the throat' in manuscript ña. / [Page 91]
pulls hair, or cuts grass—such messengers are evil, one and all.

sanskrit_iast:
iḍānyā vā vaheddvedhā yadi dūtasya cātmanaḥ /
ābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ puṣṭayāsmān vidyāstrīpunnapuṃsakān //
meaning:
इडान्या वा वहेद्द्वेधा यदि दूतस्य चात्मनः /
आभ्यां द्वाभ्यां पुष्टयास्मान् विद्यास्त्रीपुन्नपुंसकान् //
text_mt: Whether the iḍā or the other [nāḍī] flows in two ways, if of the messenger or of oneself, / from both of these, through its strength, one should recognise female, male, or neuter.

sanskrit_iast:
dūtaḥ spṛśati yadgātraṃ tasmin daṃśamudāharet /
dūtāṅghricalanaṃ duṣṭhamutthitirniś calā śubhā //
meaning:
दूतः स्पृशति यद्गात्रं तस्मिन् दंशमुदाहरेत् /
दूताङ्घ्रिचलनं दुष्ठमुत्थितिर्निश् चला शुभा //
text_mt: The limb that the messenger touches, at that limb one should declare the bite. / The movement of the messenger's foot is evil; standing still is auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
jīvapārśve śubho dūto duṣṭo 'nyatra sammāgataḥ /
jīvo gatāgatair duṣṭaḥ śubho dūtanivedane //
meaning:
जीवपार्श्वे शुभो दूतो दुष्टो ऽन्यत्र सम्मागतः /
जीवो गतागतैर् दुष्टः शुभो दूतनिवेदने //
text_mt: A messenger on the living [favourable] side is auspicious; one arriving on the other is evil. / The living breath that comes and goes is inauspicious; it is auspicious during the messenger's report.

sanskrit_iast:
dūtasya vāk praduṣṭā sā pūrvāmajārdhaninditā /
vibhaktaistasya vākyāntairviṣarnirviṣakālatā(?) //
meaning:
दूतस्य वाक् प्रदुष्टा सा पूर्वामजार्धनिन्दिता /
विभक्तैस्तस्य वाक्यान्तैर्विषर्निर्विषकालता(?) //
text_mt: The messenger's speech is corrupted if spoken with the first half censured; / by dividing the ends of his speech, the venomous or non-venomous period [is known].

sanskrit_iast:
ādyaiḥ svaraiś ca kādyaś ca vargair bhinnalipirdvidhā /
svarajo vasumānvargī itikṣepā ca mātṛkā //
meaning:
आद्यैः स्वरैश् च काद्यश् च वर्गैर् भिन्नलिपिर्द्विधा /
स्वरजो वसुमान्वर्गी इतिक्षेपा च मातृका //
text_mt: By the initial vowels and the vargas beginning with ka, the script is twofold. / The vowel-born possesses wealth; the varga-born and its dismissal make up the mātṛkā.

sanskrit_iast:
vātāgnīndrajalātmāno vargeṣu ca catuṣṭayam /
napuṃsakāḥ pañcamāḥ syuḥ svarāḥ śakrāmbuyonayaḥ //
meaning:
वाताग्नीन्द्रजलात्मानो वर्गेषु च चतुष्टयम् /
नपुंसकाः पञ्चमाः स्युः स्वराः शक्राम्बुयोनयः //
text_mt: The four [letters] in the vargas have the nature of wind, fire, Indra, and water; / the fifth [letters] are neuter; the vowels originate from Indra and water.

sanskrit_iast:
duṣṭau dūtasya vākpādau vātāgnī madhyamo hariḥ /
praśastā vāruṇā varṇā atiduṣṭā napuṃsakāḥ //
meaning:
दुष्टौ दूतस्य वाक्पादौ वाताग्नी मध्यमो हरिः /
प्रशस्ता वारुणा वर्णा अतिदुष्टा नपुंसकाः //
text_mt: The speech and feet of the messenger are evil [if belonging to] wind and fire; the middle one is Viṣṇu. / Letters belonging to Varuṇa are praised; neuter letters are extremely evil.

sanskrit_iast:
prasthāne maṅgalaṃ vākyaṃ garjitaṃ meghahastinoḥ /
pradakṣiṇaṃ phale vṛkṣe vāmasya ca rutaṃ jitaṃ //
meaning:
प्रस्थाने मङ्गलं वाक्यं गर्जितं मेघहस्तिनोः /
प्रदक्षिणं फले वृक्षे वामस्य च रुतं जितं //
text_mt: At departure, auspicious speech, the roar of clouds or elephants, / a clockwise circumambulation, a fruitful tree, and a sound on the left bring victory.

sanskrit_iast:
śubhā gītādiśabdāḥ syurīdṛśaṃ syādasiddhaye /
anarthagīrathākrando dakṣiṇe virutaṃ kṣutam //
meaning:
शुभा गीतादिशब्दाः स्युरीदृशं स्यादसिद्धये /
अनर्थगीरथाक्रन्दो दक्षिणे विरुतं क्षुतम् //
text_mt: Auspicious are sounds of singing and the like; the contrary leads to failure: / inauspicious songs, lamentation, a cry on the right, or a sneeze.

sanskrit_iast:
veśyā kṣuto nṛpaḥ kanyā gaurdantī murajadhvajau /
kṣīrājyadadhiśaṅkhāmbu chatraṃ bherī phalaṃ surāḥ //
meaning:
वेश्या क्षुतो नृपः कन्या गौर्दन्ती मुरजध्वजौ /
क्षीराज्यदधिशङ्खाम्बु छत्रं भेरी फलं सुराः //
text_mt: A courtesan, one who sneezed, a king, a maiden, a cow, an elephant, a tabor, a banner, / milk, clarified butter, curds, a conch, water, an umbrella, a kettle-drum, fruit, spirits,

sanskrit_iast:
taṇḍulā hema rupyañca siddhaye 'bhimukhā amī /
sakāṣṭhaḥ sānalaḥ kārurmalināmbarabhāvabhṛt //
:p 92
meaning:
तण्डुला हेम रुप्यञ्च सिद्धये ऽभिमुखा अमी /
सकाष्ठः सानलः कारुर्मलिनाम्बरभावभृत् //
:प् 92
text_mt:
rice grains, gold, and silver—these, met facing forward, lead to success. / One carrying wood, fire, an artisan, one wearing dirty garments,
[Page 92]

sanskrit_iast:
galasthaṭaṅgo gomāyugṛdhrolūkakapardikāḥ /
tailaṃ kapālakārpāsā niṣedhe bhasma naṣṭaye //
meaning:
गलस्थटङ्गो गोमायुगृध्रोलूककपर्दिकाः /
तैलं कपालकार्पासा निषेधे भस्म नष्टये //
text_mt: one with an axe at the neck, a jackal, a vulture, an owl, cowries, / oil, a skull, cotton—[these encountered] upon forbidding lead to destruction, and ashes bring ruin.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣarogāś ca sapta syurdhātordhātvantarāptitaḥ /
viṣadaṃśo lalāṭaṃ yātyatonetraṃ tatau sukham /
āsyācca vacanīnāḍyau dhātūna prāpnoti hi kramāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nāgalakṣaṇadirnāma
trinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha caturnavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
daṣṭacikitsā
meaning:
विषरोगाश् च सप्त स्युर्धातोर्धात्वन्तराप्तितः /
विषदंशो ललाटं यात्यतोनेत्रं ततौ सुखम् /
आस्याच्च वचनीनाड्यौ धातून प्राप्नोति हि क्रमात् //

त्रिनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः

दष्टचिकित्सा
text_mt:
The stages of venom are seven, through its passage from one bodily tissue to another. / The venomous bite travels to the forehead, then to the eye, then to the mouth, / and from the mouth to the vocal channels; thus it reaches the bodily tissues in succession.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and ninety-third chapter, entitled 'Characteristics of Serpents and the Like'.
Now, the two hundred and ninety-fourth chapter.
Treatment of snakebite.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
mantradhyānauṣadhair daṣṭacikitsāṃ pravadāmi te /
oṃ namo bhagavate nīlakaṇṭhāyeti /
japanādviṣahāniḥ syadauṣadhaṃ jīvarakṣaṇaṃ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
मन्त्रध्यानौषधैर् दष्टचिकित्सां प्रवदामि ते /
ओं नमो भगवते नीलकण्ठायेति /
जपनाद्विषहानिः स्यदौषधं जीवरक्षणं //
text_mt: Agni said: / I will explain to you the treatment of snakebite through mantras, meditation, and medicines. / By repeating 'oṃ namo bhagavate nīlakaṇṭhāya', venom is destroyed; medicine protects life.

sanskrit_iast:
sājyaṃ sakṛdrasaṃ peyaṃ dvividhaṃ viṣamucyate /
jaṅgamaṃ sarpabhūṣādi śṛṅgyādi sthāvaraṃ viṣaṃ //
meaning:
साज्यं सकृद्रसं पेयं द्विविधं विषमुच्यते /
जङ्गमं सर्पभूषादि शृङ्ग्यादि स्थावरं विषं //
text_mt: Juice with clarified butter is to be drunk at once. Venom is declared to be of two kinds: / mobile, such as from serpents and insects; and immobile venom, such as from poisonous tubers and plants.

text_mt:
Brahmā accompanied by a calm vowel, red, the deliverer, is Śiva. / This is the name-mantra of Garuda (the son of Vinatā); it is remembered as consisting of sound.
"Oṃ, blaze, O high-minded one, to the heart; to the cat-headed Garuḍa, to the head; to Garuḍa's crest; / O Garuḍa, breaker of venom, piercer, piercer, terrify, terrify, crush, [crush]..."
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: 'tārakaḥ' in manuscript kha.
2. Variant reading: 'to the playful head of Garuḍa' in manuscript kha. / [Page 93]
"...crush, crush, for the armour; unimpeded pacification, vaṃ hūṃ phaṭ for the weapon; / averter of terrifying forms, causing all fear, frighten! Burn everything, burn, reduce to ashes, svāhā to the eyes."
A lotus of the mātṛkā enclosed by the letters of the eight directions of petals and the vowels of the filaments, ending in the seven vargas, / having a pericarp formed by the essence of fire,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā hṛdisthaṃ tanmantrī vāmahastatale smaret /
aṅgaṣṭhādau nyasedvarṇānviyaterbheditāḥ kalāḥ(1) //
meaning:
कृत्वा हृदिस्थं तन्मन्त्री वामहस्ततले स्मरेत् /
अङ्गष्ठादौ न्यसेद्वर्णान्वियतेर्भेदिताः कलाः(1) //
text_mt: having placed it in the heart, the practitioner of mantras should visualise it in the palm of the left hand. / He should deposit the syllables on the thumb and other fingers as divided parts of Garuḍa:

sanskrit_iast:
pītaṃ vajracatuṣkoṇaṃ pārthivaṃ śakradaivataṃ /
vṛttārdhamāpyapadmārdhaṃ śuklaṃ varūṇadaivataṃ //
meaning:
पीतं वज्रचतुष्कोणं पार्थिवं शक्रदैवतं /
वृत्तार्धमाप्यपद्मार्धं शुक्लं वरूणदैवतं //
text_mt: yellow, four-cornered with vajras, earthy, presided over by Śakra; / a half-circle, half a watery lotus, white, presided over by Varuṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
tryastraṃ svastikayuktañca taijasaṃ vahnidaivataṃ /
vṛttaṃ vinduvṛtaṃ vāyudaivataṃ kṛṣṇamālinam //
meaning:
त्र्यस्त्रं स्वस्तिकयुक्तञ्च तैजसं वह्निदैवतं /
वृत्तं विन्दुवृतं वायुदैवतं कृष्णमालिनम् //
text_mt: triangular and furnished with a svastika, fiery, presided over by Agni; / circular, surrounded by a dot, presided over by Vāyu, garlanded in black.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhādyaṅgulīmadhye paryasteṣu svaveśmasu /
suvarṇanāgavāhena veṣṭhiteṣu nyaset kramāt //
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठाद्यङ्गुलीमध्ये पर्यस्तेषु स्ववेश्मसु /
सुवर्णनागवाहेन वेष्ठितेषु न्यसेत् क्रमात् //
text_mt: In the middle of the fingers beginning with the thumb, turned downward in their own abodes, / encircled by the golden mount of snakes (Garuḍa), he should deposit them in order.

sanskrit_iast:
viyateś caturo varṇān sumaṇḍalasamatviṣaḥ /
arūpe ravatanmātre(2) ākāśeśivadevate //
meaning:
वियतेश् चतुरो वर्णान् सुमण्डलसमत्विषः /
अरूपे रवतन्मात्रे(2) आकाशेशिवदेवते //
text_mt: The four syllables of Garuḍa, having splendour equal to the auspicious maṇḍalas; / in formless ether consisting of sound, presided over by Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
kaniṣṭhāmadhyaparvasthe nyasettasyādyamakṣaram /
nāgānāmādivarṇāṃś ca svamaṇḍalagatānnyaset //
meaning:
कनिष्ठामध्यपर्वस्थे न्यसेत्तस्याद्यमक्षरम् /
नागानामादिवर्णांश् च स्वमण्डलगतान्न्यसेत् //
text_mt: situated on the middle joint of the little finger, he should deposit its first syllable; / and he should deposit the initial letters of the serpents situated in their own maṇḍalas.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtādivarṇān vinyasedaṅguṣṭādyantaparvasu /
tanmātrādiguṇābhyarṇānaṅgulīṣu nyasedbudhaḥ //
meaning:
भूतादिवर्णान् विन्यसेदङ्गुष्टाद्यन्तपर्वसु /
तन्मात्रादिगुणाभ्यर्णानङ्गुलीषु न्यसेद्बुधः //
text_mt: He should deposit the letters of the elements on the end joints beginning with the thumb; / the wise one should deposit [the letters] near to the subtle elements and other qualities on the fingers.

sanskrit_iast:
sparśanādevatārkṣeṇa haste hanyādviṣadvayaṃ /
maṇḍalādiṣu tān varṇān viyateḥ kavayo jitān //
meaning:
स्पर्शनादेवतार्क्षेण हस्ते हन्याद्विषद्वयं /
मण्डलादिषु तान् वर्णान् वियतेः कवयो जितान् //
text_mt: Merely by the touch of Garuḍa in the hand, he destroys the two types of venom. / The wise have conquered those syllables of Garuḍa on the maṇḍalas and the rest;

sanskrit_iast:
śreṣṭhadvyaṅgulibhirdehanābhisthāneṣu parvasu /
:n
1 bhedikāstatheti kha..
2 varatanmatre iti kha..
:p 94
ājānutaḥ suvarṇābhamānābhestuhinaprabham //
meaning:
श्रेष्ठद्व्यङ्गुलिभिर्देहनाभिस्थानेषु पर्वसु /
:न्
1 भेदिकास्तथेति ख..
2 वरतन्मत्रे इति ख..
:प् 94
आजानुतः सुवर्णाभमानाभेस्तुहिनप्रभम् //
text_mt:
with the two best fingers, on the joints in the regions of the body and the navel,
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: 'so the dividers' in manuscript kha.
2. Variant reading: 'varatanmātre' in manuscript kha. / [Page 94]
up to the knees having the lustre of gold, up to the navel possessing the brilliance of snow,

sanskrit_iast:
kuṅkumāruṇamākaṇṭhādākeśāntāt sitetaraṃ /
brahmāṇḍavyāpinaṃ tārkṣañcandrākhyaṃ nāgabhūṣaṇam //
meaning:
कुङ्कुमारुणमाकण्ठादाकेशान्तात् सितेतरं /
ब्रह्माण्डव्यापिनं तार्क्षञ्चन्द्राख्यं नागभूषणम् //
text_mt: saffron-red up to the throat, and other than white (black) up to the hair ends; / pervading the universe, named Garuḍa, adorned with serpents,

sanskrit_iast:
nīlogranāśamātmānaṃ mahāpakṣaṃ smaredbudhaḥ /
evantātkṣātmano vākyānmantraḥ syānmantriṇo viṣe //
meaning:
नीलोग्रनाशमात्मानं महापक्षं स्मरेद्बुधः /
एवन्तात्क्षात्मनो वाक्यान्मन्त्रः स्यान्मन्त्रिणो विषे //
text_mt: the wise one should meditate on oneself having a dark, fierce beak and large wings. / Thus, from the utterance of the one whose self is Garuḍa, the mantra belongs to the mantrin against venom.

sanskrit_iast:
suṣṭistārkṣakarasyāntaḥsthitāṅguṣṭhaviṣāpahā /
tārkṣaṃ hastaṃ samudyamya tatpañcāṅgulicālanāt //
meaning:
सुष्टिस्तार्क्षकरस्यान्तःस्थिताङ्गुष्ठविषापहा /
तार्क्षं हस्तं समुद्यम्य तत्पञ्चाङ्गुलिचालनात् //
text_mt: The fist of Garuḍa's hand, with the thumb placed within, removes venom. / Raising Garuḍa's hand, by moving its five fingers,

sanskrit_iast:
kuryādviṣasya stambhādīṃstaduktamadavīṣayā /
ākāśādeṣa bhūvījaḥ pañcārṇādhipatirmanuḥ //
meaning:
कुर्याद्विषस्य स्तम्भादींस्तदुक्तमदवीषया /
आकाशादेष भूवीजः पञ्चार्णाधिपतिर्मनुः //
text_mt: he should effect the arrest and so forth of the venom, as declared, with the purpose of subduing pride. / Originating from space, this is the earth seed; the mantra is the master of five syllables.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃstambhayetiviṣato bhāṣayā stambhyedviṣam /
vyatyastabhūṣayā vījo mantro 'yaṃ sādhusādhitaḥ //
meaning:
संस्तम्भयेतिविषतो भाषया स्तम्भ्येद्विषम् /
व्यत्यस्तभूषया वीजो मन्त्रो ऽयं साधुसाधितः //
text_mt: With the utterance 'Paralyze! Paralyze!', one should immobilize the poison. / When properly mastered, this mantra, whose seed syllable is transposed, is well perfected.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃplavaḥ plāvaya yamaḥ(1) śabdādyaḥ saṃharedviṣaṃ /
daṇḍamutthāpayedeṣa sujaptāmbho 'bhiṣekataḥ //
meaning:
संप्लवः प्लावय यमः(1) शब्दाद्यः संहरेद्विषं /
दण्डमुत्थापयेदेष सुजप्ताम्भो ऽभिषेकतः //
text_mt: Beginning with the words 'deluge, inundate, Yama', it destroys the poison. / It should raise the staff through consecration by aspersion with water over which the recitation has been well performed.

sanskrit_iast:
sujaptaśaṅkhabheryādinisvanaśravaṇena vā /
saṃdahatyeva saṃyukto bhūtejovyatyayāt sthitaḥ //
meaning:
सुजप्तशङ्खभेर्यादिनिस्वनश्रवणेन वा /
संदहत्येव संयुक्तो भूतेजोव्यत्ययात् स्थितः //
text_mt: Or by hearing the sound of conches, kettledrums, and other instruments over which the recitation was well performed; / united [with it], it burns [the poison] away, abiding through the inversion of earth and fire.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūvāyuvyatyayānmantro viṣaṃ saṃkrāmayatyasau /
antastho nijaveśmastho vījāgnīndujalātmabhiḥ //
meaning:
भूवायुव्यत्ययान्मन्त्रो विषं संक्रामयत्यसौ /
अन्तस्थो निजवेश्मस्थो वीजाग्नीन्दुजलात्मभिः //
text_mt: Through the inversion of earth and wind, this mantra transfers the poison, / staying within one's own dwelling, with the natures of the seed syllable, fire, moon, and water.

sanskrit_iast:
etat karma nayenmantrī garuḍākṛtivigrahaḥ /
tārkṣavarṇagehasthastajjapānnāśayedviṣam //
meaning:
एतत् कर्म नयेन्मन्त्री गरुडाकृतिविग्रहः /
तार्क्षवर्णगेहस्थस्तज्जपान्नाशयेद्विषम् //
text_mt: The mantra practitioner, his body having the form of Garuḍa, should carry out this rite. / Abiding in the house of Garuḍa's color, he destroys the poison through the recitation of it.

sanskrit_iast:
jāmudaṇḍīdamuditaṃ svadhāśrīvījalāñchitaṃ /
snānapānātsarvaviṣaṃ jvarātogāpamṛtyujit //
meaning:
जामुदण्डीदमुदितं स्वधाश्रीवीजलाञ्छितं /
स्नानपानात्सर्वविषं ज्वरातोगापमृत्युजित् //
text_mt: This is stated as the Jāmudaṇḍī [mantra], marked with the seed syllables of Svadhā and Śrī. / By bathing in it and drinking it, it overcomes all poisons, fever, and untimely death.

sanskrit_iast:
pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi vidhi svāhā /
:n
1 yaśa iti ña..
:p 95
pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi kṣi kṣi svāhā //
dvāvetau pakṣirāḍmantrau viṣaghnāvabhimantraṇāt
pakṣirājāya vidhmahe pakṣidevāya dhīmahi tatro garuḍa
pracodayāt
vahnisthau pārśvatatpūrvau dantaśrīkau ca daṇḍinau ||
meaning:
पक्षि पक्षि महापक्षि महापक्षि विधि स्वाहा /
:न्
1 यश इति ञ..
:प् 95
पक्षि पक्षि महापक्षि महापक्षि क्षि क्षि स्वाहा //
द्वावेतौ पक्षिराड्मन्त्रौ विषघ्नावभिमन्त्रणात्
पक्षिराजाय विध्महे पक्षिदेवाय धीमहि तत्रो गरुड
प्रचोदयात्
वह्निस्थौ पार्श्वतत्पूर्वौ दन्तश्रीकौ च दण्डिनौ ||
text_mt:
'Pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi vidhi svāhā!'
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript ña: "yaśaḥ".
[Page 95]
'Pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi kṣi kṣi svāhā!'
These two mantras of the king of birds destroy poison through consecration.
'We know the king of birds; we meditate upon the deity of birds; may that Garuḍa inspire us!' / The two standing in fire, beside and before that, having teeth and glory, and holding staffs,

sanskrit_iast:
sakālo lāṅgalī ceti nīlakaṇṭhādyamīritaṃ /
vakṣaḥkaṇṭhaśikhāśvetaṃ nyasetstambhe susaṃskṛtau //
hara hara hṛdayāya namaḥ kapardine ca śirase nīlakaṇṭhāya vai
śikhāṃ kālakūṭaviṣabhakṣaṇāya svāhā
atha varma ca kaṇṭhe netraṃ kṛttivāsāstrinetraṃ pūrvādyair ānanair
yuktaṃ śvetapītāruṇāsitaiḥ
meaning:
सकालो लाङ्गली चेति नीलकण्ठाद्यमीरितं /
वक्षःकण्ठशिखाश्वेतं न्यसेत्स्तम्भे सुसंस्कृतौ //
हर हर हृदयाय नमः कपर्दिने च शिरसे नीलकण्ठाय वै
शिखां कालकूटविषभक्षणाय स्वाहा
अथ वर्म च कण्ठे नेत्रं कृत्तिवासास्त्रिनेत्रं पूर्वाद्यैर् आननैर्
युक्तं श्वेतपीतारुणासितैः
text_mt:
possessing Time, and holding a plow—thus is described that which begins with Nīlakaṇṭha. / White on the chest, throat, and crest, one should place it on the post in good preparation.
'Hara, Hara, homage to the heart! To the one with matted hair, to the head! To the blue-throated one, to the crest! To the devourer of the Kālakūṭa poison, svāhā!'
Then the armor; on the throat, the eye; the three-eyed one clad in animal skins, endowed with faces beginning with the east—white, yellow, reddish, and dark—

sanskrit_iast:
abhayaṃ varadaṃ cāpaṃ vāsukiñca dadhadbhujaiḥ /
yasyoparītapārśvasthagaurīrudro 'sya devatā //
meaning:
अभयं वरदं चापं वासुकिञ्च दधद्भुजैः /
यस्योपरीतपार्श्वस्थगौरीरुद्रो ऽस्य देवता //
text_mt: holding gesture of fearlessness, gesture of granting boons, bow, and Vāsuki in his arms, / above whom, on the side, stands Gaurī—Rudra is his deity.

sanskrit_iast:
pādajānuguhānābhihṛtkaṇṭhānanamūrdhasu /
mantrārṇānnyasya karayoraṅguṣṭhādyaṅgulīṣu ca //
meaning:
पादजानुगुहानाभिहृत्कण्ठाननमूर्धसु /
मन्त्रार्णान्न्यस्य करयोरङ्गुष्ठाद्यङ्गुलीषु च //
text_mt: Having placed the syllables of the mantra upon the feet, knees, genitals, navel, heart, throat, face, and head, / and on the hands, on the fingers beginning with the thumbs,

sanskrit_iast:
tarjanyāditadantāsu sarvamaṅguṣṭhayor nyaset /
dhyātvaivaṃ saṃharet kṣipraṃ vaddhayā śūlamudrayā //
meaning:
तर्जन्यादितदन्तासु सर्वमङ्गुष्ठयोर् न्यसेत् /
ध्यात्वैवं संहरेत् क्षिप्रं वद्धया शूलमुद्रया //
text_mt: on the index fingers and the rest ending with them, one should place everything upon the two thumbs. / Having meditated thus, one should quickly remove [the poison] with the trident ritual gesture bound.

sanskrit_iast:
kaniṣṭhā jyeṣṭhayā vaddhā tiśro 'nyāḥ prasṛterjavāḥ /
viṣanāśe vāmahastamanyasmin dakṣiṇaṃ karaṃ //
oṃ namo bhagavate nīlakaṇṭhāya ciḥ amalakaṇṭhāya ciḥ
sarvajñakaṇṭhāya ciḥ kṣipa oṃ svāhā
amalanīlakaṇṭhāya naikasarvaviṣāpahāya
namaste rudramanyava itisarmārjanādviṣaṃ vinaśyati na sandehaḥ
karṇajāpyā upānahāvā
:p 96
meaning:
कनिष्ठा ज्येष्ठया वद्धा तिश्रो ऽन्याः प्रसृतेर्जवाः /
विषनाशे वामहस्तमन्यस्मिन् दक्षिणं करं //
ओं नमो भगवते नीलकण्ठाय चिः अमलकण्ठाय चिः
सर्वज्ञकण्ठाय चिः क्षिप ओं स्वाहा
अमलनीलकण्ठाय नैकसर्वविषापहाय
नमस्ते रुद्रमन्यव इतिसर्मार्जनाद्विषं विनश्यति न सन्देहः
कर्णजाप्या उपानहावा
:प् 96
text_mt:
The little finger is bound with the thumb, while the other three are extended straight. / In the destruction of poison, [one uses] the left hand; in other [rites], the right hand.
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lord, the blue-throated one, ciḥ! To the stainless-throated one, ciḥ!'
'To the omniscient-throated one, ciḥ! Cast it off, oṃ svāhā!'
'To the stainless, blue-throated one, the remover of manifold and all poisons!'
By wiping with 'Homage to your wrath, Rudra', poison is destroyed without doubt, / or by recitation in the ear, or by shoes.

sanskrit_iast:
yajedrudravidhānena nīlagrīvaṃ maheśvaram /
viṣavyādhivināśaḥ syāt kṛtvā rudravidhānakaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe daṣṭacikitsā nāma
caturṇavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pañcāṅgarudravidhānaṃ
meaning:
यजेद्रुद्रविधानेन नीलग्रीवं महेश्वरम् /
विषव्याधिविनाशः स्यात् कृत्वा रुद्रविधानकं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दष्टचिकित्सा नाम
चतुर्णवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पञ्चाङ्गरुद्रविधानं
text_mt:
One should worship the blue-necked Maheśvara according to the rite of Rudra. / By performing the rite of Rudra, there will be the destruction of poison and diseases.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, entitled 'Treatment of Bites', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now the two hundred and ninety-fifth chapter.
The Fivefold Rite of Rudra

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
vakṣye rudravidhānantu pañcāṅgaṃ sarvadaṃ paraṃ /
hṛdayaṃ śivasaṅkalpaḥ śivaḥ sūktantu pauruṣam //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
वक्ष्ये रुद्रविधानन्तु पञ्चाङ्गं सर्वदं परं /
हृदयं शिवसङ्कल्पः शिवः सूक्तन्तु पौरुषम् //
text_mt: Agni said: / I shall declare the supreme fivefold rite of Rudra that grants everything: / the heart is the Śivasaṅkalpa hymn; the Śiva hymn is the Puruṣasūkta;

sanskrit_iast:
śikhābhyaḥ sambhṛtaṃ sūktamāśuḥ kavacameva ca /
śatarudriyamastrañca rudrasyāṅgāni pañca hi //
meaning:
शिखाभ्यः सम्भृतं सूक्तमाशुः कवचमेव च /
शतरुद्रियमस्त्रञ्च रुद्रस्याङ्गानि पञ्च हि //
text_mt: the hymn Sambhṛta represents the crest; the Āśu hymn is the armor; / and the Śatarudriya is the weapon—these are indeed the five limbs of Rudra.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcāṅgānnyasya taṃ dhyātvā japedrudrāṃstaḥ kramāt /
yajjāgrata iti sūktaṃ yadṛcaṃ mānasaṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चाङ्गान्न्यस्य तं ध्यात्वा जपेद्रुद्रांस्तः क्रमात् /
यज्जाग्रत इति सूक्तं यदृचं मानसं विदुः //
text_mt: Having deposited the five limbs and contemplated him, one should recite the Rudra hymns in due order. / The hymn 'Yajjāgrataḥ', consisting of verses, is known as the mental [hymn].

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣiḥ syācchivamaṅkalpaśchandastriṣṭuvudāhṛtaṃ /
śivaḥ sahasraśīrṣeti tasya nārāyaṇo 'pyṛṣiḥ //
meaning:
ऋषिः स्याच्छिवमङ्कल्पश्छन्दस्त्रिष्टुवुदाहृतं /
शिवः सहस्रशीर्षेति तस्य नारायणो ऽप्यृषिः //
text_mt: The seer is Śivasaṅkalpa, and the meter is declared to be Triṣṭubh. / The Śiva hymn is 'Sahasraśīrṣā'; its seer is Nārāyaṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
devatā puruṣo 'nuṣṭupchando jñeyañca traiṣṭubham /

text_mt:
Kubjikā, Tripurā, Gaurī, Candrikā remove poison. / The Prasāda mantra removes poison and increases life and health; / likewise the solar mantra, the mantra of Vināyaka, and constantly all mantras of Rudra.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Fivefold Rite of Rudra', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter.
Mantras and medicines that remove poison.
Agni said:
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra! Cut, cut the poison!
And to the one with a blazing battle-axe in hand! Homage to the Blessed Pakṣirudra! Raise the bitten one, raise him! Shake the bitten one, shake him! Make him speak, make him speak! Raise the snake-bitten one! Play, play! / Bind, bind! Guard, guard! O excellent Rudra, go, go! Slay, slay! Break, break! Terrify, terrify! With your fist destroy the poison! Ṭha ṭha!
[Footnote]
1. "oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūm" in ms. ña..
2. "oṃ hauṃ haṃ" in ms. ja..
3. "caṇḍikā" in ms. ña.. / p. 99
Verily, by [the grace of] Pakṣirudra, poison is destroyed through chanting this mantra.

text_mt:
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra! Destroy the poison, immobile and mobile, / artificial and natural poison, and secondary poison! Destroy the various poisons! / Destroy the poison of the bitten one! Blow, blow! Subdue, subdue! Vomit, vomit! / Pulling the streams [of rain] from the darkness of clouds, become free of poison! Destroy, destroy! Go, go! / Possess, possess! With the extraction of poison as its nature, ending with the mantra, holding the poison: Oṃ, cast it away! Oṃ, cast it away! Svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ khīṃ saḥ ṭhandrauṃ hrīṃ ṭhaḥ.

:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुरणे विषहृन्मन्त्रौषधं नाम
षन्नवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः

गोनसादिचिकित्सा
अग्निरुचाच
text_mt:
Indrabalā, agnikā, droṇapuṣpī, tulasī, devikā, and sahā: / the three pungents smeared with their juice and powdered, when eaten, dispels poison. / The five parts of śirīṣa gathered on the dark fifth lunar day dispels poison.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter, entitled "Mantras and Medicines that Remove Poison," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter.
Treatment of viper bites and others.
Agni said:

sanskrit_iast:
gonasādicikitsāñca vaśiṣṭha śṛṇu vacmi te /
hrīṃ hrīṃ amalapakṣi svāhā
tāmbūlakhādanānmantrī harenmaṇḍalino viṣaṃ //
meaning:
गोनसादिचिकित्साञ्च वशिष्ठ शृणु वच्मि ते /
ह्रीं ह्रीं अमलपक्षि स्वाहा
ताम्बूलखादनान्मन्त्री हरेन्मण्डलिनो विषं //
text_mt:
Listen, O Vasiṣṭha, I will speak to you of the treatment for viper [bites] and others:
"Hrīṃ hrīṃ to the pure-winged bird, svāhā!"
By chewing betel, the practitioner of mantras removes the poison of the Russell's viper.

sanskrit_iast:
laśunaṃ rāmaṭhaphalaṃ kuṣṭhāgnivyoṣakaṃ viṣe /
snuhīkṣīraṃ gavyaghṛtaṃ pakṣaṃ pītvāhije viṣe //

लशुनं रामठफलं कुष्ठाग्निव्योषकं विषे /
स्नुहीक्षीरं गव्यघृतं पक्षं पीत्वाहिजे विषे //
text_mt: Garlic, asafoetida resin, costus, leadwort, and the three pungents in case of poison; / after drinking spurge milk, cow's ghee, [and] the decoction for poison born of serpents.

sanskrit_iast:
atha rājiladaṣṭe ca peyā kṛṣṇā samaindhavā /
ājyakṣaudraśakṛttoyaṃ purītatyā viṣāpahaṃ //

आज्यक्षौद्रशकृत्तोयं पुरीतत्या विषापहं //
text_mt: Now, when bitten by a striped krait, long pepper with rock salt should be drunk. / Ghee, honey, dung-water, [and] purītati dispel poison.

sanskrit_iast:
sakṛṣṇākhaṇḍadugdhājyaṃ pātavyantena mākṣikaṃ /

सकृष्णाखण्डदुग्धाज्यं पातव्यन्तेन माक्षिकं /

cūrṇitair meṣadugdhāktair dhūpaḥ sarvaviṣāpahaḥ /

romanirguṇḍikākokavarṇair vā laśunaṃ samaṃ //

चूर्णितैर् मेषदुग्धाक्तैर् धूपः सर्वविषापहः /

रोमनिर्गुण्डिकाकोकवर्णैर् वा लशुनं समं //

powdered and moistened with sheep's milk, make an incense that dispels all poisons.
p. 101
Or garlic equal in measure to the hairs of nirguṇḍī and ruddy goose feathers.

मुनिपत्रैः कृतस्वेदं दष्टं काञ्चिकपाचितैः /

satailaṃ mūṣikārtighnaṃ phalinīkusumantathā /
sanāgaraguḍambhakṣyaṃ tadviṣārocakāpahaṃ //

सतैलं मूषिकार्तिघ्नं फलिनीकुसुमन्तथा /

text_mt: mixed with oil, which destroys the affliction from mice. Likewise, the flower of priyaṅgu / eaten with ginger and jaggery dispels the poison and loss of appetite caused by them.

sanskrit_iast:
cikitsā viṃṣatirbhūtā lūtāviṣaharo gaṇaḥ /

text_mt: The treatments are twenty in number. The group that destroys spider venom [consists of]: / padmaka, trumpet flower, costus, Indian valerian, vetiver, sandalwood,

nirguṇḍī śārivā śelu lūtārtaṃ secayejjalaiḥ /
guñjānirguṇḍikaṅkolaparṇaṃ śuṇṭhī niśādvayaṃ //

निर्गुण्डी शारिवा शेलु लूतार्तं सेचयेज्जलैः /

text_mt: nirguṇḍī, Indian sarsaparilla, [and] cordia: one should sprinkle the person afflicted by spider [venom] with their decoction. / Guñjā, nirguṇḍī, piper cubeba leaves, dry ginger, the two turmerics,

sanskrit_iast:
karañjāsthi ca tatpaṅkaiḥ(1) vṛścikārtiharaṃ śṛṇu /

When combined, the four formulations dispel [the sting of] scorpions by smearing and the like.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra! Civi, civi! Cut, cut! Kiri, kiri! Pierce, pierce! With the sword, strike, strike! With the trident, pierce, pierce! With the discus, tear apart, tear apart! Oṃ hrūṃ phaṭ!
Consecrated with this mantra, [the remedy] given cuts down the poison of asses and others.

sanskrit_iast:
triphalośīramustāmbumāṃsīpadmakacandanaṃ /

त्रिफलोशीरमुस्ताम्बुमांसीपद्मकचन्दनं /

text_mt: The three myrobalans, vetiver, nut grass water, spikenard, padmaka, and sandalwood, / taken through drinking and the like with goat's milk, removes the poison of asses and others.

sanskrit_iast:

Alkali, the three pungents, sweet flag, asafoetida, false black pepper, rock salt, Indian valerian,

तेषां वीजन्त्व्या ग्राह्यमिति ब्रह्माब्रवीच्च ताम् /

दश जप्त्वा मन्त्रमिदं नमस्कुर्यात्तदौषधं /
त्वामुद्धराम्यूर्ध्वनेत्रामनेनैव च भक्षयेत् //

ātmanaivābhijānāti raṇe kṛṣṇaparājayaṃ //

auṣadhādau prayoktavyo mantro 'yaṃ sthāvare viṣe //

नमो वैदूर्यमाते तन्न 2 रक्ष मां सर्वविषेभ्यो गौरि गान्धारि
चाण्डालि मातङ्गिनि स्वाहा हरिमाये
औषधादौ प्रयोक्तव्यो मन्त्रो ऽयं स्थावरे विषे //

By this statement of truth, let my antidote be accomplished!"
Homage to the Mother of Lapis Lazuli! Tanna, tanna! Protect me from all poisons, O Gaurī, Gāndhārī, Cāṇḍālī, Mātaṅginī! Svāhā! O Harimāyā!
This mantra is to be employed in medicines and the like in the case of stationary poison.

text_mt:
When a burning sensation remains immediately after eating, [the root of] lotus treated with cold water / should be given to drink with ghee and honey, if poison is present immediately thereafter.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter, entitled “Treatment for Bites of the Large Pit Viper and Others,” in the great Agni Purāṇa.
