Now begins the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter.
The pediatric tantra for subduing demonic seizures in children.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
bālatantraṃ pravakṣyāmi bālādigrahamardanaṃ /
atha jātadine vatsaṃ grahī gṛhṇāti pāpinī //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
बालतन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि बालादिग्रहमर्दनं /
अथ जातदिने वत्सं ग्रही गृह्णाति पापिनी //
text_mt: Agni said: / I shall declare the pediatric tantra that crushes seizures affecting children and others. / Now, on the day of birth, a sinful female seizing spirit seizes the infant.

sanskrit_iast:
gātrodvego nirāhāro nānāgrīvāvivartanaṃ /
tacceṣṭitamidaṃ tasyānmātṝṇāñca balaṃ haret //
meaning:
गात्रोद्वेगो निराहारो नानाग्रीवाविवर्तनं /
तच्चेष्टितमिदं तस्यान्मातॄणाञ्च बलं हरेत् //
text_mt: Agitation of the limbs, refusal of food, and various twistings of the neck / are her symptomatic actions; one should offer a sacrificial offering to the Mothers.

sanskrit_iast:
satsyamāṃsasurābhakṣyagandhasragdhūpadīpakaiḥ /
limpecca dhātakīlodhramañjiṣṭhātālacandanaiḥ //
meaning:
सत्स्यमांससुराभक्ष्यगन्धस्रग्धूपदीपकैः /
लिम्पेच्च धातकीलोध्रमञ्जिष्ठातालचन्दनैः //
text_mt: With fish, meat, liquor, edible offerings, fragrant garlands, incense, and lamps [one should make offerings], / and anoint [the child] with dhātakī, lodhra, mañjiṣṭhā, tāla, and sandalwood.

sanskrit_iast:
mahiṣākṣeṇa dhūpaś ca dvirātre bhauṣaṇī grahī /
tacceṣṭā kāsaniśvāsau gātrasaṅkocanaṃ muhuḥ //
meaning:
महिषाक्षेण धूपश् च द्विरात्रे भौषणी ग्रही /
तच्चेष्टा कासनिश्वासौ गात्रसङ्कोचनं मुहुः //
text_mt: Incense [should be made] with bdellium. On the second night, the seizing spirit is Bhauṣaṇī; / her symptoms are cough, sighs, and constant flexing of the limbs.

sanskrit_iast:
ājamūtrair lipet kṛṣṇāsevyāpāmārgacandanaiḥ /
gośṛṅgadantakeśaiś ca dhūpayet pūrvavadbaliḥ //

आजमूत्रैर् लिपेत् कृष्णासेव्यापामार्गचन्दनैः /
गोशृङ्गदन्तकेशैश् च धूपयेत् पूर्ववद्बलिः //
text_mt: One should anoint [the infant] with goat's urine mixed with pippalī, uśīra, apāmārga, and sandalwood, / fumigate with cow-horn, cow-teeth, and cow-hair, and offer the sacrificial offering as before.

sanskrit_iast:
grahī trirātre ghaṇṭhālī tacceṣṭā krandanaṃ muhuḥ /
jṛmbhaṇaṃ svanitantrāso gātrodvegamarocanaṃ //

ग्रही त्रिरात्रे घण्ठाली तच्चेष्टा क्रन्दनं मुहुः /
जृम्भणं स्वनितन्त्रासो गात्रोद्वेगमरोचनं //
text_mt: On the third night the seizing spirit is Ghaṇṭālī; her symptoms are frequent crying, / yawning, sound-producing terror, agitation of the limbs, and loss of appetite.

nakharājībilvadalair dhūpayecca baliṃ haret //

केशराञ्जनगोहस्तिदन्तं साजपयो लिपेत् /
नखराजीबिल्वदलैर् धूपयेच्च बलिं हरेत् //
text_mt: One should anoint [the infant] with saffron, collyrium, and teeth of cows and elephants mixed with goat's milk; / one should fumigate with tiger-claws and bilva leaves, and offer the sacrificial offering.

sanskrit_iast:
grahī caturthī kākolī gātrodvegaprarocanaṃ /

ग्रही चतुर्थी काकोली गात्रोद्वेगप्ररोचनं /
फेनोद्गारो दिशो दृष्टिः कुल्माषैः सासवैर् बलिः //
text_mt: The fourth seizing spirit is Kākolī; [the symptoms are] agitation of the limbs, vomiting, / spitting of froth, and staring into space. The sacrificial offering is made with boiled coarse grain mixed with liquor.

sanskrit_iast:
gajadantāhinirmokavājimūtrapralepanaṃ /
sarājīnimbapatreṇa dhūtakeśena chūpayet //
meaning:
गजदन्ताहिनिर्मोकवाजिमूत्रप्रलेपनं /
सराजीनिम्बपत्रेण धूतकेशेन छूपयेत् //
text_mt: Anointment is done with elephant tusk, cast snake-skin, and horse urine; / one should fumigate with mustard seed, neem leaves, and washed hair.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsādhikā pañcamī syājjṛmbhāśvāsordhadhāriṇī /
:p 104
muṣṭibandhaś ca tacceṣṭā baliṃ matsyādinā haret //
meaning:
हंसाधिका पञ्चमी स्याज्जृम्भाश्वासोर्धधारिणी /
:प् 104
मुष्टिबन्धश् च तच्चेष्टा बलिं मत्स्यादिना हरेत् //

sanskrit_iast:
meṣaśṛṅgabalālodhraśilātālaiḥ śiśuṃ lipet /
phaṭkārī tu grahī ṣaṣṭhī bhayamohaprarodanaṃ //
meaning:
मेषशृङ्गबलालोध्रशिलातालैः शिशुं लिपेत् /
फट्कारी तु ग्रही षष्ठी भयमोहप्ररोदनं //
text_mt: One should anoint the child with meṣaśṛṅgī, balā, lodhra, realgar, and orpiment. / The sixth seizing spirit is Phaṭkārī, causing fear, stupor, and weeping.

sanskrit_iast:
nirāhāro 'ṅgavikṣepo harenmatsyādinā baliṃ /
rājīguggulukuṣṭhebhadantādyair dhūpalepanaiḥ //
meaning:
निराहारो ऽङ्गविक्षेपो हरेन्मत्स्यादिना बलिं /
राजीगुग्गुलुकुष्ठेभदन्ताद्यैर् धूपलेपनैः //
text_mt: Refusal of food and convulsive twitching of the limbs [occur]; one should offer a sacrificial offering with fish and the like, / along with incense and unguents made with mustard, guggulu, kuṣṭha, elephant tusk, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
saptame muktakeśyārtaḥ pūtigandho vijṛmbhaṇaṃ /
sādaḥ prarodanaṅkāso dhūpo vyāghranakhair lipet //
meaning:
सप्तमे मुक्तकेश्यार्तः पूतिगन्धो विजृम्भणं /
सादः प्ररोदनङ्कासो धूपो व्याघ्रनखैर् लिपेत् //
text_mt: On the seventh [day], afflicted by Muktakeśī, [the child exhibits] foul odor, excessive yawning, / exhaustion, weeping, and cough; fumigation is done with tiger-claws, and one should anoint [the infant].

sanskrit_iast:
vacāgomayagomūtraiḥ śrīdaṇḍī cāṣṭame grahī /
diśo nirīkṣaṇaṃ jihvācālanaṅkāsarodanaṃ //
meaning:
वचागोमयगोमूत्रैः श्रीदण्डी चाष्टमे ग्रही /
दिशो निरीक्षणं जिह्वाचालनङ्कासरोदनं //
text_mt: With sweet flag, cow dung, and cow urine [one makes an unguent]. On the eighth [day] the seizing spirit is Śrīdaṇḍī; / staring in all directions, darting of the tongue, coughing, and weeping [are her signs].

sanskrit_iast:
baliḥ pūrvaiva matsyādyair dhūpalepe ca(1) hiṅgulā /
vacāsiddharthalaśunaiścordhvagrāhī mahāgrahī //
meaning:
बलिः पूर्वैव मत्स्याद्यैर् धूपलेपे च(1) हिङ्गुला /
वचासिद्धर्थलशुनैश्चोर्ध्वग्राही महाग्रही //
text_mt: The sacrificial offering is just as before with fish and the like. For the fumigation and unguent: cinnabar, / sweet flag, white mustard, and garlic. The great seizing spirit is Ūrdhvagrāhī.

sanskrit_iast:
udvejanordhvaniḥśvāsaḥ svamuṣṭidvayakhādanaṃ /
raktacandanakuṣṭhādyair dhūpayellepayecchiśuṃ //
meaning:
उद्वेजनोर्ध्वनिःश्वासः स्वमुष्टिद्वयखादनं /
रक्तचन्दनकुष्ठाद्यैर् धूपयेल्लेपयेच्छिशुं //
text_mt: Agitation, upward sighing, and biting one's own two fists [are the symptoms]; / one should fumigate and anoint the child with red sandalwood, kuṣṭha, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
kapiromanakhair dhūpo daśamī rodanī grahī /
tacceṣṭā rodanaṃ śaśvat sugandho nīlavarṇatā //
meaning:
कपिरोमनखैर् धूपो दशमी रोदनी ग्रही /
तच्चेष्टा रोदनं शश्वत् सुगन्धो नीलवर्णता //
text_mt: Fumigation is done with monkey hair and nails. On the tenth [day] the seizing spirit is Rodanī; / her symptoms are continual weeping, a fragrant scent, and bluish complexion.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūpo nimbena bhūtograrājīsarjarasair lipet /
baliṃ vahirharellājakulmāṣakavakodanam(2) //
meaning:
धूपो निम्बेन भूतोग्रराजीसर्जरसैर् लिपेत् /
बलिं वहिर्हरेल्लाजकुल्माषकवकोदनम्(2) //
text_mt: Fumigation is with neem; one should anoint with bhūtakeśī, ugrā, mustard, and sāla resin. / One should offer the sacrificial offering outside, consisting of parched grain, boiled coarse grain, and curds mixed with rice.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvattrayodaśāhaṃ syādevaṃ dhūpādikā kriyā /
gṛhnāti māsikaṃ vatsaṃ pūtanāsaṅkulī grahī //
meaning:
यावत्त्रयोदशाहं स्यादेवं धूपादिका क्रिया /
गृह्नाति मासिकं वत्सं पूतनासङ्कुली ग्रही //
text_mt: Such rites of fumigation and the rest should continue up to the thirteenth day. / The seizing spirit Pūtanāsaṅkulī seizes the one-month-old infant.

sanskrit_iast:
kākavadrodanaṃ śvāso mūtragandho 'kṣimīlanaṃ /
gomūtrasnapanaṃ tasya godantena ca dhūpanam //
:n
1 dhūpadīpe ceti ṭa..
2 karakodanamiti kha..
:p 105
meaning:
काकवद्रोदनं श्वासो मूत्रगन्धो ऽक्षिमीलनं /
गोमूत्रस्नपनं तस्य गोदन्तेन च धूपनम् //
:न्
1 धूपदीपे चेति ट..
2 करकोदनमिति ख..
:प् 105
text_mt:
Crying like a crow, gasping, the smell of urine, and closing of the eyes [are her signs]; / bathing him in cow urine and fumigating him with cow tooth [is the cure].
[Footnote]
1. “dhūpadīpe ca” in manuscript ṭa.
2. “karakodanam” in manuscript kha.

sanskrit_iast:
pītavastraṃ dadedraktasraggandhau tailadīpakaḥ /
trividhaṃ pāyasammadyaṃ tilamāsañcaturvidham //
meaning:
पीतवस्त्रं ददेद्रक्तस्रग्गन्धौ तैलदीपकः /
त्रिविधं पायसम्मद्यं तिलमासञ्चतुर्विधम् //
text_mt: One should offer yellow cloth, red garlands and scents, an oil lamp, / three kinds of milk-rice, liquor, and sesame with black gram, of four kinds.

sanskrit_iast:
karañjādho yamadiśi saptāhaṃ tair baliṃ haret /
dvimāsikañca mukuṭā vapuḥ śītañca śītalaṃ //
meaning:
करञ्जाधो यमदिशि सप्ताहं तैर् बलिं हरेत् /
द्विमासिकञ्च मुकुटा वपुः शीतञ्च शीतलं //
text_mt: Beneath a karañja tree in the southern quarter, one should present the sacrificial offering with these for seven days. / At two months, [the spirit is] Mukuṭā; the body becomes cold and chilled,

sanskrit_iast:
chardhiḥ syānmukhaśoṣādipuṣpagandhāṃśukāni ca /
apūpamodanaṃ dīpaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ nīrādi dhūpakam //
meaning:
छर्धिः स्यान्मुखशोषादिपुष्पगन्धांशुकानि च /
अपूपमोदनं दीपः कृष्णं नीरादि धूपकम् //
text_mt: there is vomiting, dryness of the mouth and the like, [and one offers] fragrant flowers, garments, / sweet cakes, boiled rice, a lamp, dark-colored water, and incense.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīye gomukhī nidrā savinmūtraprarodanam /
yavāḥ priyaṅguḥ palanaṃ kulmāṣaṃ śākamodanam //
meaning:
तृतीये गोमुखी निद्रा सविन्मूत्रप्ररोदनम् /
यवाः प्रियङ्गुः पलनं कुल्माषं शाकमोदनम् //
text_mt: At the third [month, the spirit is] Gomukhī; [the symptoms are] sleepiness, weeping accompanied by excretion of feces and urine; / [the offerings are] barley, priyaṅgu, meat, boiled coarse grain, vegetables, and boiled rice.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīraṃ pūrve dadenmadhye 'hani dhūpaś ca sarpiṣā /
pañcabhaṅgena tat snānaṃ caturthe piṅgalārtihṛt //
meaning:
क्षीरं पूर्वे ददेन्मध्ये ऽहनि धूपश् च सर्पिषा /
पञ्चभङ्गेन तत् स्नानं चतुर्थे पिङ्गलार्तिहृत् //
text_mt: One should offer milk in the east, and at midday fumigation with clarified butter; / the bath is made with the five broken twigs. In the fourth [month, the spirit is] Piṅgalā, destroying comfort;

sanskrit_iast:
tanuḥ śītā pūtigandhaḥ śoṣaḥ sa mriyate dhruvam /
pañcamī lalanā gātrasādaḥ syānmukhaśoṣaṇaṃ //
meaning:
तनुः शीता पूतिगन्धः शोषः स म्रियते ध्रुवम् /
पञ्चमी ललना गात्रसादः स्यान्मुखशोषणं //
text_mt: the body is cold, has a foul smell, and emaciation occurs; he surely dies. / The fifth is Lalanā; there is exhaustion of the limbs and dryness of the mouth,

sanskrit_iast:
apānaḥ pītavarṇaś ca matsyādyair dakṣiṇe baliḥ /
ṣaṇmāse paṅkajā ceṣṭā rodanaṃ vikṛtaḥ svaraḥ //
meaning:
अपानः पीतवर्णश् च मत्स्याद्यैर् दक्षिणे बलिः /
षण्मासे पङ्कजा चेष्टा रोदनं विकृतः स्वरः //
text_mt: and the downward breath and stool are yellow; one should make a sacrificial offering with fish and the like in the south. / At six months, [the spirit is] Paṅkajā; her symptoms are weeping and an altered voice;

sanskrit_iast:
matsyamāṃsasurābhaktapuṣpagandhādibhirbaliḥ /
saprame tu nirāhārā pūtigandhādidantaruk //
meaning:
मत्स्यमांससुराभक्तपुष्पगन्धादिभिर्बलिः /
सप्रमे तु निराहारा पूतिगन्धादिदन्तरुक् //
text_mt: the sacrificial offering is made with fish, meat, liquor, cooked rice, flowers, scents, and the like. / In the seventh [month, the child is] without appetite, foul-smelling, and suffers tooth pain;

sanskrit_iast:
piṣṭamāṃsasurāmāṃsair baliḥ syādyamunāṣṭame /
visphoṭaśoṣaṇādyaṃ syāt taccikitsānna kārayet //
meaning:
पिष्टमांससुरामांसैर् बलिः स्याद्यमुनाष्टमे /
विस्फोटशोषणाद्यं स्यात् तच्चिकित्सान्न कारयेत् //
text_mt: the sacrificial offering is made with flour cakes, meat, and liquor. In the eighth [month, the spirit is] Yamunā; / pustules, wasting, and other symptoms occur; one should not attempt its treatment.

sanskrit_iast:
navame kumbhakarṇyārto jvarī cchardati pālakam /
rodanaṃ māṃsakulmāṣamadyādyair vaiśvake baliḥ //
meaning:
नवमे कुम्भकर्ण्यार्तो ज्वरी च्छर्दति पालकम् /
रोदनं मांसकुल्माषमद्याद्यैर् वैश्वके बलिः //
text_mt: In the ninth [month], afflicted by Kumbhakarṇī, the infant has fever and vomits milk, / and cries; the sacrificial offering is made in the northwest quarter with meat, boiled coarse grain, liquor, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
daśame tāpasī ceṣṭā nirāhārokṣimīlanam /
ghaṇṭā patākā piṣṭoktā surāmāṃsabaliḥ same //
meaning:
दशमे तापसी चेष्टा निराहारोक्षिमीलनम् /
घण्टा पताका पिष्टोक्ता सुरामांसबलिः समे //
text_mt: In the tenth [month, the spirit is] Tāpasī; the symptoms are refusal of food and closing of the eyes; / a bell, a banner, [an image] made of dough, liquor, and meat constitute the sacrificial offering on level ground.

sanskrit_iast:
rākṣasyekādaśī pīḍā netrādyaṃ na cikitsanam /
:p 106
cañcalā dvādaśe śvāsaḥ trāsādikaviceṣṭitam //
meaning:
राक्षस्येकादशी पीडा नेत्राद्यं न चिकित्सनम् /
:प् 106
चञ्चला द्वादशे श्वासः त्रासादिकविचेष्टितम् //

sanskrit_iast:
baliḥ pūrve 'tha madhyāhne kulmāpādyaistilādibhiḥ /
yātanā tu dvitīye 'bde yātanaṃ rodanādikam //
meaning:
बलिः पूर्वे ऽथ मध्याह्ने कुल्मापाद्यैस्तिलादिभिः /
यातना तु द्वितीये ऽब्दे यातनं रोदनादिकम् //
text_mt: the sacrificial offering is given in the eastern quarter at midday with boiled coarse grain, sesame, and the like. / In the second year, [the spirit is] Yātanā, causing torment, weeping, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
tilamāṃsamadyamāṃsair baliḥ snānādi pūrvavat /
tṛtīye rodanī kampo rodanaṃ raktamūtrakaṃ //
meaning:
तिलमांसमद्यमांसैर् बलिः स्नानादि पूर्ववत् /
तृतीये रोदनी कम्पो रोदनं रक्तमूत्रकं //
text_mt: The sacrificial offering is with sesame, meat, liquor, and flesh; bathing and other rites are as before. / In the third year, [the spirit is] Rodanī; trembling, crying, and bloody urine [are the symptoms].

sanskrit_iast:
guḍaudanaṃ tilāpūpaḥ pratimā tilapiṣṭajā /
tilasnānaṃ pañcapatrair dhūpo rājaphalatvacā //
meaning:
गुडौदनं तिलापूपः प्रतिमा तिलपिष्टजा /
तिलस्नानं पञ्चपत्रैर् धूपो राजफलत्वचा //
text_mt: Boiled rice with jaggery, sesame cakes, an effigy made of sesame paste, / a sesame bath with leaves of five plants, and fumigation with the bark of rājaphala [are prescribed].

sanskrit_iast:
caturthe caṭakāśopho jvaraḥ sarvāṅgasādanam /
matsyamāṃsatilādyaiś ca baliḥ snānañca dhūpanam //
meaning:
चतुर्थे चटकाशोफो ज्वरः सर्वाङ्गसादनम् /
मत्स्यमांसतिलाद्यैश् च बलिः स्नानञ्च धूपनम् //
text_mt: In the fourth [year, the spirit is] Caṭakā; swelling, fever, and exhaustion of all limbs [occur]; / the sacrificial offering is made with fish, meat, sesame, and the like, along with bathing and fumigation.

sanskrit_iast:
cañcalā pañcame 'bde tu jvarastrāso 'ṅgasādanam /
māṃsaudanādyaiś ca balirmeṣaśṛṅgeṇa dhūpanam //
meaning:
चञ्चला पञ्चमे ऽब्दे तु ज्वरस्त्रासो ऽङ्गसादनम् /
मांसौदनाद्यैश् च बलिर्मेषशृङ्गेण धूपनम् //
text_mt: In the fifth year, [the spirit is] Cañcalā; fever, terror, and exhaustion of limbs [occur]; / the sacrificial offering is with meat, boiled rice, and the like, and fumigation is with meṣaśṛṅgī.

sanskrit_iast:
palāśodumbarāśvatthavaṭabilvadalāmbudhṛk /
ṣaṣṭhe 'bde dhāvanīśoṣo vairasyaṃ(1) gātrasādanam //
meaning:
पलाशोदुम्बराश्वत्थवटबिल्वदलाम्बुधृक् /
षष्ठे ऽब्दे धावनीशोषो वैरस्यं(1) गात्रसादनम् //
text_mt: Water infused with leaves of palāśa, udumbara, aśvattha, vaṭa, and bilva should be applied. / In the sixth year, [the spirit is] Dhāvanī; wasting, bad taste in the mouth, and exhaustion of limbs [occur].

sanskrit_iast:
saptāhobhirbaliḥ pūrvair dhupasnānañca bhaṅgakaiḥ(2) /
saptame yamunācchardiravacohāsarodanam //
meaning:
सप्ताहोभिर्बलिः पूर्वैर् धुपस्नानञ्च भङ्गकैः(2) /
सप्तमे यमुनाच्छर्दिरवचोहासरोदनम् //
text_mt: For seven days the sacrificial offerings should be as before, with fumigation and bathing with the five twig-leaves. / In the seventh year, [the spirit is] Yamunā; vomiting, muteness, laughter, and weeping [occur].

sanskrit_iast:
māṃsapādyasamadyādyair baliḥ snānañca dhūpanam /
aṣṭame vā jātavedā nirāhāraṃ prarodanam //
meaning:
मांसपाद्यसमद्याद्यैर् बलिः स्नानञ्च धूपनम् /
अष्टमे वा जातवेदा निराहारं प्ररोदनम् //
text_mt: The sacrificial offering is with meat, milk-rice, liquor, and the like, together with bathing and fumigation. / In the eighth year, [the spirit is] Jātavedā; refusal of food and excessive weeping [occur].

sanskrit_iast:
kṛśarāpūpadadhyādyair baliḥ snānañca dhūpanam /
kālābde navame vāhvorāsphoṭo garjanaṃ bhayam //
meaning:
कृशरापूपदध्याद्यैर् बलिः स्नानञ्च धूपनम् /
कालाब्दे नवमे वाह्वोरास्फोटो गर्जनं भयम् //
text_mt: The sacrificial offering is with kṛśarā, cakes, curd, and the like, along with bathing and fumigation. / In the ninth year of time, [the symptoms are] thrashing of the arms, roaring, and terror.

sanskrit_iast:
baliḥ syāt kṛśarāpūpaśaktukulmāsapāyasaiḥ /
daśame 'bde kalahaṃsī dāho 'ṅgakṛśatā jvaraḥ //
:n
1 vaivarṇyamiti ṭha..
2 bhāgakair iti kha..
:p 107
meaning:
बलिः स्यात् कृशरापूपशक्तुकुल्मासपायसैः /
दशमे ऽब्दे कलहंसी दाहो ऽङ्गकृशता ज्वरः //
:न्
1 वैवर्ण्यमिति ठ..
2 भागकैर् इति ख..
:प् 107
text_mt:
The sacrificial offering should consist of kṛśarā, sweet cakes, roasted grain flour, boiled coarse grain, and milk-rice. / In the tenth year, [the spirit is] Kalahaṃsī; burning sensation, emaciation of limbs, and fever [occur].
[Footnote]
1. “vaivarṇyam” in manuscript ṭha.
2. “bhāgakaiḥ” in manuscript kha.

sanskrit_iast:
paulikāpūpadadhyannaiḥ pañcarātraṃ baliṃ haret /
nimbadhūpakuṣṭhalepa ekādaśamake grahī //
meaning:
पौलिकापूपदध्यन्नैः पञ्चरात्रं बलिं हरेत् /
निम्बधूपकुष्ठलेप एकादशमके ग्रही //
text_mt: For five nights one should offer a sacrificial offering of stuffed pastries, sweet cakes, and curd-rice; / fumigation is with neem, and anointing is with kuṣṭha. In the eleventh [year], the seizing spirit

sanskrit_iast:
devadūtī niṣṭhuravāk balirlepādi pūrvavat /
balikā dvādaśe balirlepādi pūrvavat //
meaning:
देवदूती निष्ठुरवाक् बलिर्लेपादि पूर्ववत् /
बलिका द्वादशे बलिर्लेपादि पूर्ववत् //

text_mt:
The rulers of the days are named Pūtanās; the rulers of the years are the Sukumārikās.
Om, homage to all the Mothers! Consume, consume the affliction of the child! / Split, split, burst, burst, flash, flash, seize, seize, / drag, drag! Thus one of perfected form commands. O Hari, O Hari, / make free from blemish, free from blemish, the girl, the boy, the woman, or the man / from the attack of all seizing spirits!
Homage to Goddess Cāmuṇḍā! Hrūṃ hrūṃ hrīṃ! Dispel, dispel / the evil spirits, hrūṃ! Thus, may the Gṛhyakas depart elsewhere, / [to another] path; Rudra commands!
This mantra is effective for all desires in cases of all seizing spirits of children.
Om, homage to the Blessed Lady Cāmuṇḍā! Release, release the tribute or the young girl!

text_mt:
Take the tribute, take! Conquer, conquer! Abide, abide! / This mantra, which affords protection, is recited everywhere in the offering of tribute: / 'May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Skanda, the Fair One, Gaurī, Lakṣmī, the Gaṇas, and the rest / protect [the child] afflicted with fever, and release the young boy!'
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named the doctrine of children which removes seizing spirits of children.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-ninth chapter:
Mantras and related rites for removing seizing spirits.

veṃ vibhūtīṃ vaiṃ vimalāṃ vomasighātavidyutām //
meaning:
वां दीप्तां वीं तथा सुक्ष्मां वुञ्जयां वूञ्चभाद्रिकां /
वें विभूतीं वैं विमलां वोमसिघातविद्युताम् //
text_mt: Vāṃ Dīptā, Vīṃ Sūkṣmā, Vuṃ Jayā, Vūṃ Bhadrikā, / Veṃ Vibhūti, Vaiṃ Vimalā, Voṃ Amoghā,

sanskrit_iast:
vauṃ sarvatomukhīṃ vaṃ pīṭhaṃ vaḥ prārcya raviṃ yajet /
āvāhya dadyāt pādyādi hṛtṣaḍaṅgena suvrata //
meaning:
वौं सर्वतोमुखीं वं पीठं वः प्रार्च्य रविं यजेत् /
आवाह्य दद्यात् पाद्यादि हृत्षडङ्गेन सुव्रत //
text_mt: Vauṃ Vidyutā, Vaṃ Sarvatomukhī, and the seat Vaḥ; having worshipped these, one should worship the Sun. / Having invoked him, one should offer the foot-washing water and the rest with the heart and six limbs, O you of noble vows!

sanskrit_iast:
khakārau daṇḍinau caṇḍau majjā daśanasaṃyutā /
māṃsadīrghā jaradvāyuhṛdaitat sarvadaṃ raveḥ //
meaning:
खकारौ दण्डिनौ चण्डौ मज्जा दशनसंयुता /
मांसदीर्घा जरद्वायुहृदैतत् सर्वदं रवेः //
text_mt: The two kha-sounds, the staff-bearers, the Caṇḍas, marrow combined with teeth, / flesh, long [vowels], the ancient wind, and the heart: this yields all things for the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
vahnīśarakṣo marutām kikṣu pūjyā hṛdādayaḥ /
svamantraiḥ karṇikāntasthā dikṣvastraṃ purataḥ sadṛk //
meaning:
वह्नीशरक्षो मरुताम् किक्षु पूज्या हृदादयः /
स्वमन्त्रैः कर्णिकान्तस्था दिक्ष्वस्त्रं पुरतः सदृक् //
text_mt: The heart and other limbs are to be worshipped in the directions of Fire, Īśa, Rakṣas, and the Wind, / each with their own mantras, stationed within the pericarp; the weapon is in the cardinal directions, facing in front.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvādidikṣu sampūjyāś candrajñagurubhārgavāḥ /
nasyāñjanādi kurvīta sājamūtrair grahāpahaiḥ //
meaning:
पूर्वादिदिक्षु सम्पूज्याश् चन्द्रज्ञगुरुभार्गवाः /
नस्याञ्जनादि कुर्वीत साजमूत्रैर् ग्रहापहैः //
text_mt: The Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are to be worshipped in the directions beginning with the east. / One should administer errhines, collyrium, and the like, with goat's urine, which dispel seizing spirits.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṭhāpathyāvacāśigrusindhūvyoṣaiḥ pṛthak phalaiḥ /
ajākṣīrāḍhake pakvasarpiḥ sarvagrahān haret //
meaning:
पाठापथ्यावचाशिग्रुसिन्धूव्योषैः पृथक् फलैः /
अजाक्षीराढके पक्वसर्पिः सर्वग्रहान् हरेत् //
text_mt: Ghee cooked with pāṭhā, chebulic myrobalan, sweet flag, drumstick tree, rock salt, and ginger-black pepper-long pepper, with different fruits, / in an āḍhaka measure of goat's milk, removes all seizing spirits.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛścikālīphalīkuṣṭhaṃ lavaṇāni ca śārṅgakam /
apasmāravināśāya tajjalaṃ tvabhibhojayet //
:p 111
meaning:
वृश्चिकालीफलीकुष्ठं लवणानि च शार्ङ्गकम् /
अपस्मारविनाशाय तज्जलं त्वभिभोजयेत् //
:प् 111
text_mt:
Heliotropium, Callicarpa macrophylla, saussurea, salts, and śārṅgaka: / for the destruction of epilepsy, one should administer that water as food.
[Page 111]

sanskrit_iast:
vidārīkuśakāśekṣukvāthajaṃ pāyayet payaḥ /
droṇe sayaṣṭikuṣmāṇḍarase sarpiś ca saṃskṛtau //
meaning:
विदारीकुशकाशेक्षुक्वाथजं पाययेत् पयः /
द्रोणे सयष्टिकुष्माण्डरसे सर्पिश् च संस्कृतौ //
text_mt: One should administer milk boiled with a decoction of vidārī, kuśa grass, kāśa grass, and sugarcane, / or ghee refined in a droṇa of juice of licorice and ash gourd,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcagavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tadvadyogaṃ jvaraharaṃ śṛṇu /
oṃ bhasmāstrāya vidmahe ekadaṃṣṭrāya dhīmahi tanno jvaraḥ
pracodayāt
kṛṣṇoṣaṇaniśārāsnādrākṣātailaṃ guḍaṃ lihet //
meaning:
पञ्चगव्यं घृतं तद्वद्योगं ज्वरहरं शृणु /
ओं भस्मास्त्राय विद्महे एकदंष्ट्राय धीमहि तन्नो ज्वरः
प्रचोदयात्
कृष्णोषणनिशारास्नाद्राक्षातैलं गुडं लिहेत् //

sanskrit_iast:
śvāsavānatha vā bhārgīṃ sayaṣṭimadhusarpiṣā /
pāṭhā tiktā kaṇā bhārgī athavā madhunā lihet //
meaning:
श्वासवानथ वा भार्गीं सयष्टिमधुसर्पिषा /
पाठा तिक्ता कणा भार्गी अथवा मधुना लिहेत् //
text_mt: or one suffering from asthma [should lick] clerodendrum with licorice, honey, and ghee; / or one should lick pāṭhā, picrorhiza, long pepper, and clerodendrum with honey.

sanskrit_iast:
dhātrī viśvasitā kṛṣṇā mustā kharjūramāgadhī /
pivaraśceti hikkāghnaṃ tat trayaṃ madhunā lihet //
meaning:
धात्री विश्वसिता कृष्णा मुस्ता खर्जूरमागधी /
पिवरश्चेति हिक्काघ्नं तत् त्रयं मधुना लिहेत् //
text_mt:
Myrobalan, dry ginger, sugar, long pepper, mustā, date, māgadhī,
and pivara: one should lick these three together with honey to destroy hiccups.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmalī jīramāṇḍūkīniśādhātrīrasaṃ pivet /
vyoṣapadmakatriphalākiḍaṅgadevadāravaḥ /
rāsnācūrṇaṃ samaṃ khaṇḍair jagdhvā kāsaharaṃ dhruvam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe grahahṛnmantrādikaṃ nāma
navanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sūryārcanam
meaning:
कामली जीरमाण्डूकीनिशाधात्रीरसं पिवेत् /
व्योषपद्मकत्रिफलाकिडङ्गदेवदारवः /
रास्नाचूर्णं समं खण्डैर् जग्ध्वा कासहरं ध्रुवम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ग्रहहृन्मन्त्रादिकं नाम
नवनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
सूर्यार्चनम्
text_mt:
One suffering from jaundice should drink the juice of cumin, māṇḍūkī, turmeric, and myrobalan.
Trikatu, padmaka, triphalā, viḍaṅga, devadāru,
and powder of rāsnā eaten in equal parts with sugar definitely relieves cough.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and ninety-ninth chapter, named “Mantras for Relieving Planetary Afflictions and Other Rites.”
Now, the three hundredth chapter.
Worship of the Sun

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
śayyā tu daṇḍisājeśapāvakaś caturānanaḥ /
sarvārthasādhakamidaṃ vījaṃ piṇḍārthamucyate //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
शय्या तु दण्डिसाजेशपावकश् चतुराननः /
सर्वार्थसाधकमिदं वीजं पिण्डार्थमुच्यते //
text_mt:
Agni said:
Śayyā, then Daṇḍin, the fire of Īśa with goats, and the four-faced [Brahmā]—
this seed-syllable, which accomplishes all ends, is stated for the purpose of the piṇḍa.

sanskrit_iast:
svayaṃ dīrghasvarādyañca vījeṣvaṅgāni sarvaśaḥ /
khātaṃ sādhu viṣañcaiva savinduṃ sakalaṃ tathā //
:p 112
meaning:
स्वयं दीर्घस्वराद्यञ्च वीजेष्वङ्गानि सर्वशः /
खातं साधु विषञ्चैव सविन्दुं सकलं तथा //
:प् 112

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇasya pañca vījāni pṛthagdṛṣṭaphalaṃ mahat /
gaṇaṃ jayāya namaḥ ekadaṃṣṭrāya acalakarṇine gajavaktrāya
mahoharahastāya
pañcāṅgaṃ sarvasāmānyaṃ siddhiḥ syāllakṣajāpyateḥ //
gaṇādhipataye gaṇeśvarāya gaṇanāyakāya gaṇakrīḍāya
meaning:
गणस्य पञ्च वीजानि पृथग्दृष्टफलं महत् /
गणं जयाय नमः एकदंष्ट्राय अचलकर्णिने गजवक्त्राय
महोहरहस्ताय
पञ्चाङ्गं सर्वसामान्यं सिद्धिः स्याल्लक्षजाप्यतेः //
गणाधिपतये गणेश्वराय गणनायकाय गणक्रीडाय
text_mt:
There are five seed-syllables of the troop, each having a great visible result:
‘Obeisance to Gaṇa, to Jaya, to Ekadaṃṣṭra, to Acalakarṇin, to Gajavaktra,
to Mahodarahasta.’
This fivefold limb is common to all; success will result from a master reciting one hundred thousand [times].
‘To Gaṇādhipati, to Gaṇeśvara, to Gaṇanāyaka, to Gaṇakrīḍa.’

sanskrit_iast:
digdale pūjayenmūrtīḥ purāvaccāṅgapañcakam /
vakratuṇḍāya ekadaṃṣṭrāya mahodarāya gajavaktrāya
vikaṭāya vighnarājāya dhūmravarṇāya
digvidikṣu yajedetāllokāṃśāṃś caiva mudrayā //
meaning:
दिग्दले पूजयेन्मूर्तीः पुरावच्चाङ्गपञ्चकम् /
वक्रतुण्डाय एकदंष्ट्राय महोदराय गजवक्त्राय
विकटाय विघ्नराजाय धूम्रवर्णाय
दिग्विदिक्षु यजेदेताल्लोकांशांश् चैव मुद्रया //
text_mt:
One should worship the icons on the directional petals, as before, and the group of five limbs:
‘To Vakratuṇḍa, to Ekadaṃṣṭra, to Mahodara, to Gajavaktra,’
‘to Vikaṭa, to Vighnarāja, to Dhūmravarṇa.’
One should worship these and the regents of the worlds in the cardinal and intermediate directions with the ritual gesture.

sanskrit_iast:
madhyamātarjanīmadhyagatāṅguṣṭhau samuṣṭikau /
caturbhujo modakāḍhyo daṇḍapāśāṅkuśānvitaḥ //
meaning:
मध्यमातर्जनीमध्यगताङ्गुष्ठौ समुष्टिकौ /
चतुर्भुजो मोदकाढ्यो दण्डपाशाङ्कुशान्वितः //
text_mt:
The thumbs placed between the middle and forefingers, with both hands clenched in fists.
Four-armed, abundant in sweetmeats, equipped with staff, noose, and goad,

sanskrit_iast:
dantabhakṣadharaṃ raktaṃ sābjaṃ pāśāḍkuśair vṛtam /
pūjayettaṃ caturthyāñca viśeṣenātha nityaśaḥ //
meaning:
दन्तभक्षधरं रक्तं साब्जं पाशाड्कुशैर् वृतम् /
पूजयेत्तं चतुर्थ्याञ्च विशेषेनाथ नित्यशः //
text_mt:
bearing his tusk and food, red, holding a lotus, accompanied by a noose and goad—
one should worship him especially on the fourth [lunar day], and also daily.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetārkamūlena kṛtaṃ sarvāptiḥ syāttilair ghṛtaiḥ /
taṇḍulair dadhimadhvājyaiḥ saubhāgyaṃ vaśyatā bhavet //
meaning:
श्वेतार्कमूलेन कृतं सर्वाप्तिः स्यात्तिलैर् घृतैः /
तण्डुलैर् दधिमध्वाज्यैः सौभाग्यं वश्यता भवेत् //
text_mt:
Made from the root of white arka, it yields all attainments with sesamum and clarified butter;
with rice, curd, honey, and clarified butter, fortune and subjugation will arise.

sanskrit_iast:
ghoṣāsṛkprāṇadhātvardī daṇḍī gārtaṇḍabhairavaḥ /
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ kartā vimbapuṭāvṛtaḥ //
meaning:
घोषासृक्प्राणधात्वर्दी दण्डी गार्तण्डभैरवः /
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां कर्ता विम्बपुटावृतः //
text_mt:
Possessing sound, blood, life, and bodily elements, holding a staff, the fierce solar deity Mārtāṇḍa-Bhairava,
the bestower of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, is enclosed within the solar orb.

sanskrit_iast:
hrasvāḥ syurmūrtaryaḥ pañca dīrghā aṅgāni tasya ca /
sindūrāruṇamīśāne vāmārdhadayitaṃ raviṃ //
meaning:
ह्रस्वाः स्युर्मूर्तर्यः पञ्च दीर्घा अङ्गानि तस्य च /
सिन्दूरारुणमीशाने वामार्धदयितं रविं //
text_mt:
The five icons are short [vowels], and his limbs are the long ones.
In the northeast, the sun is crimson like vermilion, loving his left half.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyādiṣu koṇeṣu kujamandāhiketavaḥ /
snātvā vidhivadādityamārādhyārghyapuraḥsaraṃ //
meaning:
आग्नेयादिषु कोणेषु कुजमन्दाहिकेतवः /
स्नात्वा विधिवदादित्यमाराध्यार्घ्यपुरःसरं //
text_mt:
In the corners beginning with the southeast are Mars, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu.
Having bathed according to the rules and worshipped the sun preceded by a water offering,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtāntamaiśe nirmālyaṃ tejaś caṇḍāya dīpitaṃ /
rocanā kuṅkumaṃ vāri raktagandhākṣatāṅkurāḥ //
:p 113
meaning:
कृतान्तमैशे निर्माल्यं तेजश् चण्डाय दीपितं /
रोचना कुङ्कुमं वारि रक्तगन्धाक्षताङ्कुराः //
:प् 113

sanskrit_iast:
veṇuvījayavāḥśāliśyāmākatilarājikāḥ /
javāpuṣpānvitāṃ datvā pātraiḥ śirasi dhārya tat(1) //
meaning:
वेणुवीजयवाःशालिश्यामाकतिलराजिकाः /
जवापुष्पान्वितां दत्वा पात्रैः शिरसि धार्य तत्(1) //
text_mt:
bamboo seed, barley, rice, millet, sesamum, and mustard,
together with hibiscus flowers—having placed them in vessels and held them on the head,

sanskrit_iast:
jānubhyāmavanīṅgatvā sūryāyārghyaṃ nivedayet /
svavidyāmantritaiḥ kumbhair navabhiḥ prārcya vai grahān //
meaning:
जानुभ्यामवनीङ्गत्वा सूर्यायार्घ्यं निवेदयेत् /
स्वविद्यामन्त्रितैः कुम्भैर् नवभिः प्रार्च्य वै ग्रहान् //
text_mt:
having touched the ground with both knees, one should offer the water offering to the Sun.
Having worshipped the planets with nine pitchers consecrated by their own mantras,

sanskrit_iast:
grahādiśāntaye snānaṃ japtvārkaṃ sarvamāpnuyāt /
saṃgrāmavijayaṃ sāgniṃ vījadoṣaṃ savindukaṃ //
meaning:
ग्रहादिशान्तये स्नानं जप्त्वार्कं सर्वमाप्नुयात् /
संग्रामविजयं साग्निं वीजदोषं सविन्दुकं //
text_mt:
the bath is for pacifying planetary afflictions; having recited [the mantra of] the Sun, one obtains everything:
victory in battle. With Agni, with the seed-syllables, and with the bindu,

sanskrit_iast:
nyasya mūrdhādipādāntaṃ mūlaṃ pūjya tu mudrayā /
svāṅgāni ca yathānyāsamātmānaṃ bhāvayedraviṃ //
meaning:
न्यस्य मूर्धादिपादान्तं मूलं पूज्य तु मुद्रया /
स्वाङ्गानि च यथान्यासमात्मानं भावयेद्रविं //
text_mt:
having performed the ritual deposition from the crown to the feet, and having worshipped the root mantra with the ritual gesture
and one's own limbs according to the ritual deposition, one should meditate on oneself as the Sun.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānañca māraṇastambhe pītagāpyāyane sitam /
ripughātavidhau(2) kṛṣṇaṃ mohayecchakracāpavat //
meaning:
ध्यानञ्च मारणस्तम्भे पीतगाप्यायने सितम् /
रिपुघातविधौ(2) कृष्णं मोहयेच्छक्रचापवत् //
text_mt:
The meditation is yellow in killing and immobilising, white in nourishment,
black in rites for destroying enemies, and one should cause bewilderment like Indra's bow.

sanskrit_iast:
yo 'bhiṣekajapadhyānapūjāhomaparaḥ sadā /
tejasvī hṛjayaḥ śrīmān samudrādau jayaṃ labhet //
meaning:
यो ऽभिषेकजपध्यानपूजाहोमपरः सदा /
तेजस्वी हृजयः श्रीमान् समुद्रादौ जयं लभेत् //
text_mt:
One who is always devoted to consecration by aspersion, recitation, meditation, worship, and fire oblation
becomes radiant, victorious in heart, glorious, and attains victory upon the ocean and elsewhere.

sanskrit_iast:
tāmbūlādāvidaṃ nyasya japtvā dadyāduśīrakaṃ /
nyastuvījena hastena sparśanaṃ tadvaśe smṛtaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sūryārcanaṃ nāma triśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
||
:ś athaikādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānāmantrāḥ
meaning:
ताम्बूलादाविदं न्यस्य जप्त्वा दद्यादुशीरकं /
न्यस्तुवीजेन हस्तेन स्पर्शनं तद्वशे स्मृतं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सूर्यार्चनं नाम त्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
||
:श् अथैकाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानामन्त्राः
text_mt:
Having deposited this [mantra] on betel or the like and recited it, one should give uśīraka;
touching with a hand deposited with the seed-syllable is considered to bring about subjugation.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the three hundredth chapter, named “Worship of the Sun.”
Now, the three hundred and first chapter.
Various Mantras

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
vākkarmapārśvayukśukratokakṛte mato plavaḥ /
hutāntā deśavarṇeyaṃ vidyā mukhyā sarasvatī //
:n
1 dhārya ceti kha..
2 vidyutpātavidhāviti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 114
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
वाक्कर्मपार्श्वयुक्शुक्रतोककृते मतो प्लवः /
हुतान्ता देशवर्णेयं विद्या मुख्या सरस्वती //

text_mt:
Agni said:
Joined with speech and action on both sides, for the sake of the offspring of Śukra, a vessel is considered;
ending with fire, this is the prime vidyā Sarasvatī of the region's letters.
[Notes]
1. ‘dhārya ca’ in manuscript kha.
2. ‘vidyutpātavidhau’ in manuscripts gha, ja, ña, and ṭa.
p. 114

sanskrit_iast:
akṣārāśī varṇalakṣaṃ japet samatimān bhavet /
atriḥ savahnirvāmākṣivindurindrāya hṛtparaḥ //
meaning:
अक्षाराशी वर्णलक्षं जपेत् समतिमान् भवेत् /
अत्रिः सवह्निर्वामाक्षिविन्दुरिन्द्राय हृत्परः //
text_mt:
One should recite one hundred thousand letters continuously; one becomes endowed with good intellect.
Atri with Agni, the left eye, and the bindu; followed by the heart for Indra.

sanskrit_iast:
vajrapadmadharaṃ śakraṃ pītamāvāhya pūjayet /
niyutaṃ homayedājyatilāṃstenābhiṣecayet //
meaning:
वज्रपद्मधरं शक्रं पीतमावाह्य पूजयेत् /
नियुतं होमयेदाज्यतिलांस्तेनाभिषेचयेत् //
text_mt:
Having invoked yellow Indra bearing the thunderbolt and the lotus, one should worship him.
One should offer a million clarified butter and sesamum oblations, and consecrate him with that.

sanskrit_iast:
nṛpādirbhraṣṭarajyādīnrājyaputrādimāpnuyāt /
hṛllekhā śaktidevākhyā doṣāgnirdaṇḍidaṇḍavān //
meaning:
नृपादिर्भ्रष्टरज्यादीन्राज्यपुत्रादिमाप्नुयात् /
हृल्लेखा शक्तिदेवाख्या दोषाग्निर्दण्डिदण्डवान् //
text_mt:
A king or similar person fallen from his kingdom obtains his kingdom, sons, and the like.
The Hṛllekhā is named the Śakti deity; the fire of fault, having a staff and a punisher.

sanskrit_iast:
śivamiṣṭvā japecchaktimaṣṭamyādicaturdaśīṃ /
cakrapāśāṅkuśadharāṃ sābhayāṃ varadāyikāṃ //
meaning:
शिवमिष्ट्वा जपेच्छक्तिमष्टम्यादिचतुर्दशीं /
चक्रपाशाङ्कुशधरां साभयां वरदायिकां //
text_mt:
Having worshipped Śiva, one should recite the Śakti [mantra] from the eighth to the fourteenth [lunar day]—
[meditating on her] bearing a discus, noose, and goad, accompanied by the gesture of fearlessness, and granting boons.

text_mt:
By fire oblation and other rites, one attains good fortune, poetic skill, and becomes master of a city.
“Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ, obeisance to Kāma, who brings welfare to all beings, who enchants all beings, who is blazing forth; bring the heart of all beings into my power! Bring it! Oṃ.”
Through recitation and other practices with this mantra, one can subjugate the entire world.
“Oṃ hrīṃ Cāmuṇḍā, burn so-and-so! Burn! Cook! Cook! Bring [them] into my subjugation! Bring [them]! Ṭha ṭha!”

sanskrit_iast:
vaśīkaraṇakṛnmantraścāmuṇḍāyāḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
phalatrayakaṣāyeṇa varāṅgaṃ kṣālayedvaśe //
meaning:
वशीकरणकृन्मन्त्रश्चामुण्डायाः प्रकीर्तितः /
फलत्रयकषायेण वराङ्गं क्षालयेद्वशे //
text_mt:
This is proclaimed as the subjugation mantra of Cāmuṇḍā.
For subjugation, one should wash the pudendum with a decoction of the three fruits.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvagandhāyavaiḥ strī tu niśākarpūrakādinā /
pippalītaṇḍulānyaṣṭau maricāni ca viṃśatiḥ //
meaning:
अश्वगन्धायवैः स्त्री तु निशाकर्पूरकादिना /
पिप्पलीतण्डुलान्यष्टौ मरिचानि च विंशतिः //
text_mt:
A woman [is subjugated] by aśvagandhā and barley with turmeric, camphor, and other [ingredients],
eight grains of long pepper, and twenty black peppercorns.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛhatīrasalepaś ca vaśe syānmaraṇāntikaṃ /
kaṭīramūlatrikaṭukṣaudralepas tathā bhavet //
meaning:
वृहतीरसलेपश् च वशे स्यान्मरणान्तिकं /
कटीरमूलत्रिकटुक्षौद्रलेपस् तथा भवेत् //
text_mt:
Anointment with the juice of bṛhatī brings about subjugation until death;
likewise, an anointment of the root of kaṭīra, trikatu, and honey will do so.

sanskrit_iast:
himaṃ kapitthakarabhaṃ māgadhī madhukaṃ madhu /
teṣāṃ lepaḥ prayuktastu dampatyoḥ svastimāvahet //
meaning:
हिमं कपित्थकरभं मागधी मधुकं मधु /
तेषां लेपः प्रयुक्तस्तु दम्पत्योः स्वस्तिमावहेत् //
text_mt:
Camphor, wood-apple shoot, long pepper, madhuka, and honey—
anointment of these applied brings welfare to husband and wife.

sanskrit_iast:
saśarkarayonilepāt kadambarasako madhu /
sahadevī mahālakṣmīḥ putrajīvī kṛtāñjaliḥ //
:p 115
meaning:
सशर्करयोनिलेपात् कदम्बरसको मधु /
सहदेवी महालक्ष्मीः पुत्रजीवी कृताञ्जलिः //
:प् 115
text_mt:
By anointment of the vagina with sugar, juice of kadamba, and honey,
sahadevī, mahālakṣmī, putrajīvī, and kṛtāñjali—
p. 115

sanskrit_iast:
etaccūrṇaṃ śiraḥkṣiptaṃ likasya vaśamuttamam /
triphalācandanakvāthaprasthā dvikuḍavam pṛthak //
meaning:
एतच्चूर्णं शिरःक्षिप्तं लिकस्य वशमुत्तमम् /
त्रिफलाचन्दनक्वाथप्रस्था द्विकुडवम् पृथक् //
text_mt:
this powder thrown upon the head yields supreme subjugation of a person.
A prastha of the decoction of triphalā and sandalwood, and two kuḍavas each

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛṅgahemarasandoṣātāvatī cuñcukaṃ madhu /
ghṛtaiḥ pakvā niśā chāyā śuṣkā lipyā tu rañjanī //
meaning:
भृङ्गहेमरसन्दोषातावती चुञ्चुकं मधु /
घृतैः पक्वा निशा छाया शुष्का लिप्या तु रञ्जनी //
text_mt:
of juice of bhṛṅgarāja, gold, juice of nightshade, cuñcuka, and honey,
cooked with clarified butter, dried in the shade of night; this paste is delightful.

sanskrit_iast:
vidārīṃ soccaṭāmāṣacūrṇībhhtāṃ saśarkarāṃ /
gathitāṃ yaḥ vipet kṣīrair nityaṃ strīśatakaṃ vrajet //
meaning:
विदारीं सोच्चटामाषचूर्णीभ्ह्तां सशर्करां /
गथितां यः विपेत् क्षीरैर् नित्यं स्त्रीशतकं व्रजेत् //
text_mt:
One who drinks powder of vidārī, uccaṭā, and black gram, mixed with sugar
and cooked in milk, can continuously visit a hundred women.

sanskrit_iast:
gulmamāṣatilavrīhicūrṇakṣīrasitānvitaṃ /
aśvatthavaṃśadarbhāṇāṃ mūlaṃ vai vaiṣṇavīśniyoḥ //
meaning:
गुल्ममाषतिलव्रीहिचूर्णक्षीरसितान्वितं /
अश्वत्थवंशदर्भाणां मूलं वै वैष्णवीश्नियोः //
text_mt:
Mixed with milk and sugar, the powder of gulma, black gram, sesamum, and rice,
and the root of aśvattha, bamboo, and darbha grass, for Vaiṣṇavī and Śrī.

sanskrit_iast:
mūlaṃ dūrvāśvagandhotthaṃ pivet kṣīraiḥ sutārthinī /
kauntīlakṣmyāḥ śiphā dhātrī vajraṃ loghnaṃ vaṭāṅkuram //
meaning:
मूलं दूर्वाश्वगन्धोत्थं पिवेत् क्षीरैः सुतार्थिनी /
कौन्तीलक्ष्म्याः शिफा धात्री वज्रं लोघ्नं वटाङ्कुरम् //
text_mt:
A woman desiring a son should drink milk with the root derived from dūrvā and aśvagandhā;
the root of kauntī, lakṣmī, myrobalan, vajra, iron-destroyer, and a shoot of the banyan tree.

sanskrit_iast:
ājyakṣīramṛtau peyaṃ putrārthaṃ tridivaṃ striyā /
putrārthinī pivet kṣīraṃ śrīmūlaṃ savaṭāṅkuram //
meaning:
आज्यक्षीरमृतौ पेयं पुत्रार्थं त्रिदिवं स्त्रिया /
पुत्रार्थिनी पिवेत् क्षीरं श्रीमूलं सवटाङ्कुरम् //
text_mt:
It should be drunk by a woman for three days in clarified butter, milk, and nectar for the sake of a son.
A woman desiring a son should drink milk with bilva root and a banyan shoot.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīvaḍāṅkuradevīnāṃ rasaṃ nasye vipecca sā /
śrīpadmamūlamutkṣīramaśvatthottaramūlayuk //
meaning:
श्रीवडाङ्कुरदेवीनां रसं नस्ये विपेच्च सा /
श्रीपद्ममूलमुत्क्षीरमश्वत्थोत्तरमूलयुक् //
text_mt:
She should drink or use as nasal drops the juice of bilva, banyan shoot, and the goddess [plant];
the root of white lotus with milk, joined with the northern root of an aśvattha tree,

sanskrit_iast:
taralaṃ payasā yuktaṃ kārpāsaphalapallvaṃ /
apāmārgasya puṣpāgraṃ navaṃ samahiṣīpayaḥ //
meaning:
तरलं पयसा युक्तं कार्पासफलपल्ल्वं /
अपामार्गस्य पुष्पाग्रं नवं समहिषीपयः //
text_mt:
liquid mixed with milk, cotton fruit sprout,
and fresh tip of an apāmārga flower together with buffalo milk.

sanskrit_iast:
putrārthañcārdhaṣaṭśākair yogāś catvāra īritāḥ /
śarkarotpalapuṣpākṣalodhracandanasārivāḥ //
meaning:
पुत्रार्थञ्चार्धषट्शाकैर् योगाश् चत्वार ईरिताः /
शर्करोत्पलपुष्पाक्षलोध्रचन्दनसारिवाः //
text_mt: And four formulations are declared with three herbs for obtaining a son: / sugar, water-lily flower, bibhītaka, lodhra, sandalwood, and sārivā.

sanskrit_iast:
sravamāṇe striyā garbhe dātavyāstaṇḍulāmbhasā /
lājā yaṣṭisitādrākṣākṣaudrasarpīṃṣi vā lihet //
meaning:
स्रवमाणे स्त्रिया गर्भे दातव्यास्तण्डुलाम्भसा /
लाजा यष्टिसिताद्राक्षाक्षौद्रसर्पींषि वा लिहेत् //
text_mt: When a woman is having a miscarriage, they should be given with rice water. / Or she should lick puffed grain, liquorice, white sugar, grapes, honey, and ghee.

sanskrit_iast:
aṭaruṣakalāṅgulyaḥ kākamācyāḥ śiphā pṛthak /
nābheradhaḥ samālipya prasūte pramadā sukham //
meaning:
अटरुषकलाङ्गुल्यः काकमाच्याः शिफा पृथक् /
नाभेरधः समालिप्य प्रसूते प्रमदा सुखम् //
text_mt: Vāsā, kalāṅguli, and the root of kākamācī applied separately / below the navel, a woman gives birth with ease.

sanskrit_iast:
raktaṃ śuklaṃ jāvāpuṣpaṃ raktaśuklastrutau pivet /

text_mt:
One should drink red [and] white hibiscus flowers during red [or] white vaginal discharge.

Saffron, bṛhatī root, anantamūla, liquorice, tṛṇotpala,

śīryamāṇeṣu keśeṣu sthāpanañca bhavedidam //

शीर्यमाणेषु केशेषु स्थापनञ्च भवेदिदम् //
text_mt: eaten with goat's milk and oil, causes the growth of hair. / And when the hair is falling out, this serves to stabilise it.

A prastha of āmalakī and bhṛṅgarāja juice with oil, and an āḍhaka of milk.
Oṃ, obeisance to the blessed Tryambaka! Calm, calm! Culu, culu! Mili, mili! Bhida, bhida! O Gomāninī, / O bearer of the discus! Hrūṃ phaṭ!
In this village, protect, protect the herd of cows! Make peace, make peace!
Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Mahāsena, declared to be heroic and of great strength,

the destroyer of pestilence, may that lord of the world protect me! / One should deposit these two verses separately as mantras protecting cattle.
Thus ends the three hundred and first chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Various Mantras'.
Now, the three hundred and second chapter.
Worship of the Syllables of the Body.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
yadā janmarkṣagaś candro bhānuḥ saptasarāśigaḥ /
pauṣṇaḥ kālaḥ sa vijñeyastadā grāsaṃ parīkṣayet //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
यदा जन्मर्क्षगश् चन्द्रो भानुः सप्तसराशिगः /
पौष्णः कालः स विज्ञेयस्तदा ग्रासं परीक्षयेत् //
text_mt: Agni said: / When the moon is in the natal asterism and the sun is in the seventh sign, / that is to be known as the time of death; then one should observe the seizure [of death].

sanskrit_iast:

kṛṣṇā ca jihvā saptāhaṃ jīvitaṃ tasya vai bhavet //

कण्टोष्ठौ चलतःस्थानाद्यस्य वक्रा च नासिका /
कृष्णा च जिह्वा सप्ताहं जीवितं तस्य वै भवेत् //
text_mt: He whose throat and lips move from their place, whose nose is twisted, / and whose tongue is black, his life indeed lasts seven days.

sanskrit_iast:

तारो मेषो विषं दन्ती नरो दीर्घो वणा रसः /
क्रूद्धोल्काय महोल्काय वीरोल्काय शिखा भवेत् //
:प् 117
text_mt:
[By combining the codes for] tāra, meṣa, viṣa, dantī, nara, the long [vowel], vaṇā, and rasa: / to Krūddholka, to Maholka, to Vīrolka, [there] should be the crest-mantra,
[Page 117]

kaniṣṭhāditadaṣṭānāmaṅgulīnāñca parvasu //

ह्यल्काय राहसोल्काय वैष्णवोष्टाक्षरो मनुः /
कनिष्ठादितदष्टानामङ्गुलीनाञ्च पर्वसु //
text_mt: to Dyulkā, to Rāhasolka—this is the eight-syllable mantra of Viṣṇu. / On the joints of the eight fingers starting from the little finger,

तर्जन्यान्तारमङ्गुष्ठे लग्ने मध्यमया च तत् //

raktagauradhūmraharijjātarūpāḥ sitāstrayaḥ //
meaning:
तलेङ्गुष्ठे तदुत्तारं वीजोत्तारं ततो न्यसेत् /
रक्तगौरधूम्रहरिज्जातरूपाः सितास्त्रयः //
text_mt: on the palm, on the thumb—having uttered it, one should then deposit the root-seed. / Red, white, smoke-coloured, yellow, golden, and three white:

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ rūpānimān varṇān bhāvabuddhānnyaset kramāt /
hṛdāsyanetramūrdhāṅghritāluguhyakarādiṣu(1) //
meaning:
एवं रूपानिमान् वर्णान् भावबुद्धान्न्यसेत् क्रमात् /
हृदास्यनेत्रमूर्धाङ्घ्रितालुगुह्यकरादिषु(1) //
text_mt: one should sequentially deposit these letters having such forms, mentally conceived, / on the heart, face, eyes, head, feet, palate, genitals, hands, and other [limbs].

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgāni ca nyasedvījānnyasyātha karadehayoḥ /
yathātmani tathā deve nyāsaḥ kāryaḥ karaṃ vinā //
meaning:
अङ्गानि च न्यसेद्वीजान्न्यस्याथ करदेहयोः /
यथात्मनि तथा देवे न्यासः कार्यः करं विना //
text_mt: And one should deposit the limbs, having deposited the seed-syllables on the hands and body. / As in oneself, so too on the deity, the ritual deposition is to be done, except for the hands.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdādisthānagān varṇān gandhapuṣpai samarcayet /
dharmādyagnyādyadharmādi gātre pīṭhe 'mbuje nyaset //
meaning:
हृदादिस्थानगान् वर्णान् गन्धपुष्पै समर्चयेत् /
धर्माद्यग्न्याद्यधर्मादि गात्रे पीठे ऽम्बुजे न्यसेत् //
text_mt: One should worship the letters located in the places such as the heart with perfumes and flowers. / One should deposit dharma and so forth in the south-east and other [directions], and adharma and so forth on the body, on the pedestal, and on the lotus.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra keśarakiñjalkavyāpisūryendudāhināṃ /
maṇḍalantritayantāvad bhedaistatra nyaset kramāt //
meaning:
यत्र केशरकिञ्जल्कव्यापिसूर्येन्दुदाहिनां /
मण्डलन्त्रितयन्तावद् भेदैस्तत्र न्यसेत् क्रमात् //
text_mt: Where the three maṇḍalas of the sun, moon, and fire pervade the filaments and anthers, / one should deposit them in sequence according to the divisions.

sanskrit_iast:
guṇāś ca tantrasatvādyāḥ keśarasthāś ca śaktayaḥ /
vimalotkarṣaṇījñānakriyāyogāś ca vai kramāt //
meaning:
गुणाश् च तन्त्रसत्वाद्याः केशरस्थाश् च शक्तयः /
विमलोत्कर्षणीज्ञानक्रियायोगाश् च वै क्रमात् //
text_mt: And the qualities sattva and so forth according to the Tantra, and the powers situated on the filaments: / Vimalā, Utkarṣiṇī, Jñānā, Kriyā, and Yogā in sequence,

sanskrit_iast:
prahvī satyā tatheśānānugrahā madhyatastataḥ /
yogapīṭhaṃ samabhyarcya samāvahya hariṃ yajet //
meaning:
प्रह्वी सत्या तथेशानानुग्रहा मध्यतस्ततः /
योगपीठं समभ्यर्च्य समावह्य हरिं यजेत् //
text_mt: Prahvī, Satyā, likewise Īśānā, Anugrahā, and then in the centre. / Having worshipped the yogic seat and invoked Hari, one should sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
pādyārghyācamanīyañca pītavastravibhūṣaṇaṃ /
etat pañcopacārañca sarvaṃ mūlena dīyate //
meaning:
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयञ्च पीतवस्त्रविभूषणं /
एतत् पञ्चोपचारञ्च सर्वं मूलेन दीयते //
text_mt: Foot-water, water offering, water for sipping, yellow garment, and ornament— / this fivefold offering, everything is presented with the root mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
vāsudevādayaḥ pūjyāś catvāro dikṣu mūrtayaḥ /
vidikṣu śrīsarasvatyai ratiśāntyai ca pūjayet //
:n
1 hṛdāsyanetramūrdhāṅghrijānuguhyakarādiṣviti kha..
:p 118
meaning:
वासुदेवादयः पूज्याश् चत्वारो दिक्षु मूर्तयः /
विदिक्षु श्रीसरस्वत्यै रतिशान्त्यै च पूजयेत् //
:न्
1 हृदास्यनेत्रमूर्धाङ्घ्रिजानुगुह्यकरादिष्विति ख..
:प् 118
text_mt:
The four forms, Vāsudeva and the others, are to be worshipped in the cardinal directions. / In the intermediate directions, one should worship Śrī, Sarasvatī, Rati, and Śānti.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: hṛdāsyanetramūrdhāṅghrijānuguhyakarādiṣviti kha..] [Page 118]

sanskrit_iast:
śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ muṣalaṃ khaḍgaśārṅgike /
vanamālānvitaṃ dikṣu vidikṣu ca yajet kramāt //
meaning:
शङ्खं चक्रं गदां पद्मं मुषलं खड्गशार्ङ्गिके /
वनमालान्वितं दिक्षु विदिक्षु च यजेत् क्रमात् //
text_mt: Conch, discus, mace, lotus, pestle, sword, bow, / together with the garland of wild flowers, one should worship in the cardinal and intermediate directions in order.

sanskrit_iast:
abhyarcya ca vahistārkṣyaṃ devasya purato 'rcayet /
viśvaksenañca someśaṃ madhye āvaraṇādvahiḥ(1) /
indrādiparicāreṇa pūjya sarvamavāpnuyāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe aṅgākṣarārcanaṃ nāma
dvyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha tryadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pañcākṣarādipūjāmantrāḥ
meaning:
अभ्यर्च्य च वहिस्तार्क्ष्यं देवस्य पुरतो ऽर्चयेत् /
विश्वक्सेनञ्च सोमेशं मध्ये आवरणाद्वहिः(1) /
इन्द्रादिपरिचारेण पूज्य सर्वमवाप्नुयात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अङ्गाक्षरार्चनं नाम
द्व्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्र्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
पञ्चाक्षरादिपूजामन्त्राः
text_mt:
And having worshipped Garuḍa outside, one should worship in front of the deity. / Outside the enclosure, with Viṣvaksena and the Lord of Soma in the middle, / having worshipped with Indra and the other attendants, one attains everything.
Thus ends the three hundred and second chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Worship of the Syllables of the Body'.
Now, the three hundred and third chapter.
The Worship Mantras Beginning with the Five-Syllable Mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
meṣaḥ saṃjñā viṣaṃ sādyamasti dīrghodakaṃ rasaḥ /
etat pañcākṣaraṃ mantraṃ śivadañca śivātmakaṃ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
मेषः संज्ञा विषं साद्यमस्ति दीर्घोदकं रसः /
एतत् पञ्चाक्षरं मन्त्रं शिवदञ्च शिवात्मकं //
text_mt: Agni said: / Meṣa, saṃjñā, viṣa, sādya, asti, the long water [vowel], and rasa: / this five-syllable mantra bestows auspiciousness and is identical with Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
tārakādi samabhyarcya devatvādi samāpnuyāt /
jñānātmakaṃ paraṃ brahma paraṃ buddhiḥ śivo hṛdi //
meaning:
तारकादि समभ्यर्च्य देवत्वादि समाप्नुयात् /
ज्ञानात्मकं परं ब्रह्म परं बुद्धिः शिवो हृदि //
text_mt: Having worshipped with the praṇava and the rest, one attains godhead and other states. / Supreme Brahman consists of knowledge; supreme intelligence is Śiva in the heart.

sanskrit_iast:
tacchaktibhūtaḥ sarveśo bhinno brahmādimūrtibhiḥ /
mantrārṇāḥ pañca bhūtāni tanmantrā viṣayās tathā //
meaning:
तच्छक्तिभूतः सर्वेशो भिन्नो ब्रह्मादिमूर्तिभिः /
मन्त्रार्णाः पञ्च भूतानि तन्मन्त्रा विषयास् तथा //
text_mt: The Lord of all, consisting of that power, is divided into the forms of Brahmā and the others. / The letters of the mantra are the five elements, and their mantras are the sense-objects;

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇādivāyavaḥ pañca jñānakarmendriyāṇi ca /
sarvaṃ pañcākṣaraṃ brahma tadvadaṣṭākṣarāntakaḥ //
meaning:
प्राणादिवायवः पञ्च ज्ञानकर्मेन्द्रियाणि च /
सर्वं पञ्चाक्षरं ब्रह्म तद्वदष्टाक्षरान्तकः //
text_mt: the five winds beginning with prāṇa, and the organs of sense and action. / Everything is the five-syllable Brahman; likewise is that which ends with the eight syllables.

sanskrit_iast:
gavyena prakṣayeddīkṣāsthānaṃ mantreṇa coditaṃ /
tantrasambhūtasambhāvaḥ śivamiṣṭvā vidhānataḥ //
:n
1 madhyeṣu toraṇadvahiriti kha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 119
meaning:
गव्येन प्रक्षयेद्दीक्षास्थानं मन्त्रेण चोदितं /
तन्त्रसम्भूतसम्भावः शिवमिष्ट्वा विधानतः //
:न्
1 मध्येषु तोरणद्वहिरिति ख.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 119
text_mt:
One should sprinkle the place of initiation with products of the cow as prescribed by the mantra. / Having produced the required state through the Tantra, having worshipped Śiva according to the rules,
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: madhyeṣu toraṇadvahiriti kha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca] [Page 119]

sanskrit_iast:
mūlamūrtyaṅgavidyābhistaṇḍulakṣepaṇādikam /
kṛtvā caruñca yat kṣīraṃ punastadvibhajet tridhā //
meaning:
मूलमूर्त्यङ्गविद्याभिस्तण्डुलक्षेपणादिकम् /
कृत्वा चरुञ्च यत् क्षीरं पुनस्तद्विभजेत् त्रिधा //
text_mt: having performed the scattering of rice and other rites with the root, icon, and limb Vidyās, / and [preparing] the caru and the milk, he should divide it again into three parts.

sanskrit_iast:
nivedyaikaṃ paraṃ hutvā saśiṣyo 'nyadbhajedguruḥ /
ācamya sakalīkṛtya dadyāccchiṣyāya deśikaḥ //
meaning:
निवेद्यैकं परं हुत्वा सशिष्यो ऽन्यद्भजेद्गुरुः /
आचम्य सकलीकृत्य दद्याच्च्छिष्याय देशिकः //
text_mt: Having offered one [part], having made oblations with the other, the teacher with the disciple should consume the remaining one. / Having sipped water and performed the nyāsa of parts, the teacher should give to the disciple

sanskrit_iast:
dantakāṣṭhaṃ hṛdā japtaṃ kṣīravṛkṣādisambhavam /
saṃśodhya dantān saṃkṣiptvā prajñālyaitat kṣipedbhuvi //
meaning:
दन्तकाष्ठं हृदा जप्तं क्षीरवृक्षादिसम्भवम् /
संशोध्य दन्तान् संक्षिप्त्वा प्रज्ञाल्यैतत् क्षिपेद्भुवि //
text_mt: a tooth-stick consecrated with the heart-mantra, obtained from a milky tree or the like. / Having cleaned the teeth, cast it down, and washed it, he should throw it onto the ground.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrveṇa saumyavārīśagataṃ śubhamatau śubham /
punastaṃ śiṣyamāyāntaṃ(1) śiśvābandhādirakṣitaṃ //
meaning:
पूर्वेण सौम्यवारीशगतं शुभमतौ शुभम् /
पुनस्तं शिष्यमायान्तं(1) शिश्वाबन्धादिरक्षितं //
text_mt: Fallen to the east, north, or west, it is auspicious; otherwise, it is inauspicious. / Then, making that arriving disciple protected by the protective tie and other means,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā vedyāṃ sahānena svapeddarbhāstare budhaḥ /
suṣuptaṃ vīkṣya taṃ śiṣyaḥ prabhāte śrāvayedguruṃ //
meaning:
कृत्वा वेद्यां सहानेन स्वपेद्दर्भास्तरे बुधः /
सुषुप्तं वीक्ष्य तं शिष्यः प्रभाते श्रावयेद्गुरुं //
text_mt: the wise [teacher] should sleep with him on an altar covered with darbha grass. / Having seen [the dreams] in deep sleep, the disciple should relate them to the teacher at dawn.

sanskrit_iast:
śubhaiḥ siddhipadair bhaktistaiḥ punarmaṇḍalārcanam /
maṇḍalaṃ bhadrakādyuktaṃ pūjayetsarvasiddhidaṃ //
meaning:
शुभैः सिद्धिपदैर् भक्तिस्तैः पुनर्मण्डलार्चनम् /
मण्डलं भद्रकाद्युक्तं पूजयेत्सर्वसिद्धिदं //
text_mt: If [the dreams] are auspicious and grant success, devotion is generated by them; then comes the worship of the maṇḍala. / One should worship the maṇḍala, such as the bhadraka, which grants all attainments.

sanskrit_iast:
snātvācamya mṛdā dehaṃ mantrair ālipya kalpyate /
śivatīrthe naraḥ snāyādaghamarṣaṇapūrvakam //
meaning:
स्नात्वाचम्य मृदा देहं मन्त्रैर् आलिप्य कल्प्यते /
शिवतीर्थे नरः स्नायादघमर्षणपूर्वकम् //
text_mt: Having bathed, sipped water, and smeared the body with clay with mantras, it is prepared. / A person should bathe in a sacred water of Śiva, preceded by the Aghamarṣaṇa rite.

sanskrit_iast:
hastābhiṣekaṃ kṛtvātha prāyāt pūjādikaṃ budhaḥ /
mūlenābjāsanaṃ kuryāttena pūrakakumbhakān //
meaning:
हस्ताभिषेकं कृत्वाथ प्रायात् पूजादिकं बुधः /
मूलेनाब्जासनं कुर्यात्तेन पूरककुम्भकान् //
text_mt: Having then consecrated his hands, the wise one should proceed to worship and other rites. / He should form the lotus seat with the root-mantra, and with it perform inhalation and retention [of breath].

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānaṃ yojayitvordhvaṃ śikhānte dvādaśāṅgule /
saṃśoṣya dagdhvā svatanuṃ plāvayedamṛtena ca //
meaning:
आत्मानं योजयित्वोर्ध्वं शिखान्ते द्वादशाङ्गुले /
संशोष्य दग्ध्वा स्वतनुं प्लावयेदमृतेन च //
text_mt: Having united the self above, at the end of the tuft of hair twelve finger-widths [up], / having dried up and burned his own body, he should flood it with nectar.

sanskrit_iast:
dhmātvā divyaṃ vapustasminnātmānañca punarnayet /
kṛtvevaṃ cātmaśuddhiḥ syādvinyasyārcanamārabhet //
meaning:
ध्मात्वा दिव्यं वपुस्तस्मिन्नात्मानञ्च पुनर्नयेत् /
कृत्वेवं चात्मशुद्धिः स्याद्विन्यस्यार्चनमारभेत् //
text_mt: Having meditated upon a divine body, he should bring the self back into it. / Having thus performed the purification of self, and having deposited [the mantras], he should begin worship.

sanskrit_iast:
kramāt kṛṣṇasitaśyāmaraktapītā nagādayaḥ /
mantrārṇā daṇḍināṅgāni teṣu sarvāstu mūrtayaḥ //
:n
1 śiṣyamācāntamiti ña..
:p 120
meaning:
क्रमात् कृष्णसितश्यामरक्तपीता नगादयः /
मन्त्रार्णा दण्डिनाङ्गानि तेषु सर्वास्तु मूर्तयः //
:न्
1 शिष्यमाचान्तमिति ञ..
:प् 120
text_mt:
Sequentially black, white, dark, red, and yellow are the mountains and other deities; / the syllables of the mantra are the body parts of the staff-bearer, and all forms dwell in them.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: śiṣyamācāntamiti ña..] [Page 120]

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhāntaṃ vinyasyāṅgāni sarvataḥ /
nyasenmantrākṣaraṃ pādaguhyahṛdvaktramūrdhasu //
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठादिकनिष्ठान्तं विन्यस्याङ्गानि सर्वतः /
न्यसेन्मन्त्राक्षरं पादगुह्यहृद्वक्त्रमूर्धसु //
text_mt: Having assigned [the syllables to] the limbs everywhere, from the thumb to the little finger, / one should deposit the syllables of the mantra on the feet, the private parts, the heart, the mouth, and the head.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāpakaṃ nyasya mūrdhādi mūlamaṅgāni vinyaset /
raktapītaśyāmasitān pīṭhapādān svakālajān //
meaning:
व्यापकं न्यस्य मूर्धादि मूलमङ्गानि विन्यसेत् /
रक्तपीतश्यामसितान् पीठपादान् स्वकालजान् //
text_mt: Having performed the pervasive ritual deposition from the head downwards, one should deposit the root [mantra] and the limbs. / The red, yellow, dark, and white legs of the pedestal, born of their respective times,

sanskrit_iast:
svāṅgānmantrair nyasedgātrāṇyadharmādīni dikṣu ca /
tatra padmañca suryādimaṇḍale tritayaṃ guṇān //
meaning:
स्वाङ्गान्मन्त्रैर् न्यसेद्गात्राण्यधर्मादीनि दिक्षु च /
तत्र पद्मञ्च सुर्यादिमण्डले त्रितयं गुणान् //
text_mt: and the members [of the pedestal]—unrighteousness and the rest—he should deposit from his own limbs with mantras in the cardinal directions. / There [on the pedestal he should deposit] the lotus, and in the disc of the sun and the others, the triad of qualities.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvādipatre kāmādyā navakaṃ karṇikopari /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā kramādraudro kālī kalavikāriṇī //
meaning:
पूर्वादिपत्रे कामाद्या नवकं कर्णिकोपरि /
वामा ज्येष्ठा क्रमाद्रौद्रो काली कलविकारिणी //
text_mt: On the petals beginning in the east, the [śaktis] beginning with Vāmā, and a group of nine on the pericarp: / Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and in order Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikāriṇī,

sanskrit_iast:
balavikāriṇī cārtha balapramathanī tathā /
sarvabhūtadamanī ca navamī ca manonmanī //
meaning:
बलविकारिणी चार्थ बलप्रमथनी तथा /
सर्वभूतदमनी च नवमी च मनोन्मनी //
text_mt: and Balavikāriṇī, Balapramathanī, / and Sarvabhūtadamanī, and the ninth, Manonmanī.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetā raktā sitā pītā śyāmā vahninibhāṣitā /
kṛṣṇāruṇāś ca tāḥ śaktīrjvālārūpāḥ smaret kramāt //
meaning:
श्वेता रक्ता सिता पीता श्यामा वह्निनिभाषिता /
कृष्णारुणाश् च ताः शक्तीर्ज्वालारूपाः स्मरेत् क्रमात् //
text_mt: White, red, white, yellow, dark, flame-colored, / black, and reddish-brown—one should visualize those powers in order, in the form of flames.

sanskrit_iast:
anantayogapīṭhāya āvāhyātha hṛdabjataḥ /
sphaṭikābhaṃ caturvāhuṃ phalaśūladharaṃ śivam //
meaning:
अनन्तयोगपीठाय आवाह्याथ हृदब्जतः /
स्फटिकाभं चतुर्वाहुं फलशूलधरं शिवम् //
text_mt: Having invoked [Śiva] for the seat of infinite yoga from the lotus of the heart, / [one should visualize] Śiva, radiant as crystal, four-armed, holding a fruit and a trident,

sanskrit_iast:
sābhayaṃ varadaṃ pañcavadaṃnañca trilocanam /
patreṣu murtayaḥ pañca sthāpyāstatpuruṣādayaḥ //
meaning:
साभयं वरदं पञ्चवदंनञ्च त्रिलोचनम् /
पत्रेषु मुर्तयः पञ्च स्थाप्यास्तत्पुरुषादयः //
text_mt: granting fearlessness and boons, five-faced, and three-eyed. / On the petals, the five icons beginning with Tatpuruṣa are to be placed.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrve tatpuruṣaḥ śveto aghoro 'ṣṭabhujo 'sitāḥ /
caturvāhumukhaḥ pītāḥ sadyojātaś ca paścime //
meaning:
पूर्वे तत्पुरुषः श्वेतो अघोरो ऽष्टभुजो ऽसिताः /
चतुर्वाहुमुखः पीताः सद्योजातश् च पश्चिमे //
text_mt: In the east is Tatpuruṣa, white; Aghora is eight-armed and dark; / Sadyojāta in the west is four-armed, four-faced, and yellow.

sanskrit_iast:
vāmadevaḥ strīvilāsī caturvaktrabhujo 'ruṇaḥ /
saumye pañcāsya īśāne īśānaḥ sarvadaḥ sitaḥ //
meaning:
वामदेवः स्त्रीविलासी चतुर्वक्त्रभुजो ऽरुणः /
सौम्ये पञ्चास्य ईशाने ईशानः सर्वदः सितः //
text_mt: Vāmadeva is sportive with women, four-faced, four-armed, and reddish; / in the north is the five-faced [form], and in the northeast is Īśāna, all-bestowing and white.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭāṅgāni yathānyāyamanantaṃ sūkṣmamarcayet /
siddheśvaraṃ tvekanetraṃ pūrvādau diśa pūjayet //
meaning:
इष्टाङ्गानि यथान्यायमनन्तं सूक्ष्ममर्चयेत् /
सिद्धेश्वरं त्वेकनेत्रं पूर्वादौ दिश पूजयेत् //
text_mt: One should worship the desired limbs according to rule, and Ananta and Sūkṣma; / in the cardinal directions beginning with the east, one should worship Siddheśvara and Ekanetra,

sanskrit_iast:
ekarudraṃ trinetrañca śrīkaṇṭhañca śikhaṇḍinam /
:p 121
aiśānyādividikṣvete vidyeśāḥ kamalāsanāḥ(1) //
meaning:
एकरुद्रं त्रिनेत्रञ्च श्रीकण्ठञ्च शिखण्डिनम् /
:प् 121
ऐशान्यादिविदिक्ष्वेते विद्येशाः कमलासनाः(1) //

sanskrit_iast:
śvetaḥ pītaḥ sito rakto dhūmro rakto 'ruṇaḥ śitaḥ /
śūlāśaniśareśvāsavāhavaś caturānanāḥ //
meaning:
श्वेतः पीतः सितो रक्तो धूम्रो रक्तो ऽरुणः शितः /
शूलाशनिशरेश्वासवाहवश् चतुराननाः //
text_mt: White, yellow, white, red, smoke-colored, red, reddish-brown, and white; / their arms bear a trident, a thunderbolt, and a bow and arrow, and they are four-faced.

sanskrit_iast:
umā vaṇḍeśanandīśau mahākālo gaṇeśvaraḥ /
vṛṣo bhṛṅgariṭiskandānuttarādau prapūjayet //
meaning:
उमा वण्डेशनन्दीशौ महाकालो गणेश्वरः /
वृषो भृङ्गरिटिस्कन्दानुत्तरादौ प्रपूजयेत् //
text_mt: One should worship Umā, Caṇḍeśa and Nandīśa, Mahākāla, Gaṇeśa, / the Bull, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, and Skanda, beginning in the north.

sanskrit_iast:
kuliśaṃ śaktidaṇḍau ca khaḍgapāśadhvajau gadāṃ /
śūlaṃ cakraṃ yajet padmaṃ pūvvādau devamarcya ca //
meaning:
कुलिशं शक्तिदण्डौ च खड्गपाशध्वजौ गदां /
शूलं चक्रं यजेत् पद्मं पूव्वादौ देवमर्च्य च //
text_mt: One should worship the thunderbolt, the spear and the staff, the sword, the noose, the banner, the mace, / the trident, the discus, and the lotus, beginning in the east, having worshipped the god.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'dhivāsitaṃ śiṣyaṃ pāyayedgavyapañcakam /
ācāntaṃ prokṣye netrāntair netre netreṇa bandhayet //
meaning:
ततो ऽधिवासितं शिष्यं पाययेद्गव्यपञ्चकम् /
आचान्तं प्रोक्ष्ये नेत्रान्तैर् नेत्रे नेत्रेण बन्धयेत् //
text_mt: Then one should have the pupil, who has undergone preliminary consecration, drink the five products of the cow. / Having rinsed his mouth and sprinkled him [with water] with the eye [mantras], one should blindfold his eyes with the eye [mantra].

sanskrit_iast:
dvāraṃ praveśayecchipyaṃ maṇḍapasyātha dakṣiṇe /
sāsanādikuśāsīnaṃ tatra saṃśodhayedguruḥ //
meaning:
द्वारं प्रवेशयेच्छिप्यं मण्डपस्याथ दक्षिणे /
सासनादिकुशासीनं तत्र संशोधयेद्गुरुः //
text_mt: He should lead the pupil through the door in the south of the pavilion; / seated there on kuśa grass with a seat and the like, the guru should purify him.

sanskrit_iast:
āditattvāni saṃhṛtya paramārthe layaḥ kramāt /
punarutpādayecchiṣyaṃ sṛṣṭimārgeṇa deśikaḥ //
meaning:
आदितत्त्वानि संहृत्य परमार्थे लयः क्रमात् /
पुनरुत्पादयेच्छिष्यं सृष्टिमार्गेण देशिकः //
text_mt: Having dissolved the primary cosmic principles in order into the supreme reality, / the teacher should generate the pupil again by the process of creation.

sanskrit_iast:
nyāsaṃ śiṣye tataḥ kṛtvā taṃ pradakṣiṇamānayet /
paścimadvāramānīya kṣepayet kusumāñjalim //
meaning:
न्यासं शिष्ये ततः कृत्वा तं प्रदक्षिणमानयेत् /
पश्चिमद्वारमानीय क्षेपयेत् कुसुमाञ्जलिम् //
text_mt: Then, having performed the ritual deposition upon the pupil, he should lead him in a clockwise circumambulation; / having brought him to the western door, he should have him throw a handful of flowers.

sanskrit_iast:
yasmin patanti puṣpāṇi tannāmādyaṃ vinirdiśet /
pārśveyāgabhuvaḥ khāte kuṇḍe sannabhimekhale(2) //
meaning:
यस्मिन् पतन्ति पुष्पाणि तन्नामाद्यं विनिर्दिशेत् /
पार्श्वेयागभुवः खाते कुण्डे सन्नभिमेखले(2) //
text_mt: Upon whatever [deity] the flowers fall, he should assign him that name as the primary one. / In the fire-pit dug beside the sacrificial ground, possessing a proper navel and girdles,

sanskrit_iast:
śivāgniṃ janayitveṣṭvā punaḥ śiṣyeṇa cārcayet /
dhyānenātmanibhaṃ śiṣyaṃ saṃhṛtya pralayaḥ kramāt //
meaning:
शिवाग्निं जनयित्वेष्ट्वा पुनः शिष्येण चार्चयेत् /
ध्यानेनात्मनिभं शिष्यं संहृत्य प्रलयः क्रमात् //
text_mt: having generated the Śiva-fire and sacrificed, he should have him worship again with the pupil. / Having brought the pupil, who resembles oneself, through meditation into gradual dissolution,

sanskrit_iast:
punarutpādya tatpāṇau dadyāddarbhāṃś ca mantritān /
pṛthivyādīni tattvāni juhuyāddhṛdayādibhiḥ //
:n
1 kamalānanā iti ña..
2 sandhādimekhale iti kha..
:p 122
meaning:
पुनरुत्पाद्य तत्पाणौ दद्याद्दर्भांश् च मन्त्रितान् /
पृथिव्यादीनि तत्त्वानि जुहुयाद्धृदयादिभिः //
:न्
1 कमलानना इति ञ..
2 सन्धादिमेखले इति ख..
:प् 122
text_mt:
and having generated him again, he should place consecrated darbha grass in his hand. / He should make oblations of the cosmic principles beginning with earth using the heart and other [mantras].
[Footnote]
1 [Variant] "kamalānanāḥ" according to manuscript ña.
2 [Variant] "sandhādimekhale" according to manuscript kha. / [Page 122]

sanskrit_iast:
ekaikasya śataṃ hutvā vyomamūlena homayet /
hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ kuryādastreṇāṣṭāhutīrhunet //
meaning:
एकैकस्य शतं हुत्वा व्योममूलेन होमयेत् /
हुत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं कुर्यादस्त्रेणाष्टाहुतीर्हुनेत् //
text_mt: Having offered a hundred oblations for each one, he should offer fire oblations with the root [mantra] of ether. / Having made the fire oblations, he should make the full oblation; he should offer eight fire oblations with the weapon [mantra].

sanskrit_iast:
prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhyarthaṃ tataḥ śeṣaṃ samāpayet /
kumbhaṃ samantritaṃ prārcya śiśuṃ pīṭhe 'bhiṣecayet //
meaning:
प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्ध्यर्थं ततः शेषं समापयेत् /
कुम्भं समन्त्रितं प्रार्च्य शिशुं पीठे ऽभिषेचयेत् //
text_mt: An expiation for the sake of complete purity, and then he should finish the remainder. / Having worshipped the jar that has been consecrated with mantras, he should consecrate the youth on the pedestal with aspersion.

sanskrit_iast:
śiṣye tu samayaṃ datvā svarṇādyaiḥ svaguruṃ yajet /
dīkṣā pañcākṣarasyoktā viṣṇvāderevameva hi //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe pañcākṣarādipūjāmantrā nāma
tryadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha caturadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pañcapañcāśadviṣṇunāmāṇi
meaning:
शिष्ये तु समयं दत्वा स्वर्णाद्यैः स्वगुरुं यजेत् /
दीक्षा पञ्चाक्षरस्योक्ता विष्ण्वादेरेवमेव हि //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पञ्चाक्षरादिपूजामन्त्रा नाम
त्र्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुरधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
पञ्चपञ्चाशद्विष्णुनामाणि
text_mt:
Having imparted the rule of conduct to the pupil, he should worship his guru with gold and other gifts. / The initiation of the five-syllable mantra has been spoken; in this very manner is that of Viṣṇu and the other deities.
Thus ends the three hundred and third chapter, entitled “The Worship Mantras of the Five-Syllable [Formula] and Others,” in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and fourth chapter.
The Fifty-Five Names of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
japan vai pañcapañcāśadviṣṇunāmāni yo naraḥ /
mantrajapyādiphalabhāk tīrtheṣvarcādi cākṣayam //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
जपन् वै पञ्चपञ्चाशद्विष्णुनामानि यो नरः /
मन्त्रजप्यादिफलभाक् तीर्थेष्वर्चादि चाक्षयम् //
text_mt:
Agni said:
The man who recites the fifty-five names of Viṣṇu
obtains the fruit of mantra recitation and the rest, and imperishable [merit] from worship and other rites at sacred fords.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkare puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ gayāyāñca gadādharam /
rāghavañcitrakūṭe tu prabhāse daityasūdanam //
meaning:
पुष्करे पुण्डरीकाक्षं गयायाञ्च गदाधरम् /
राघवञ्चित्रकूटे तु प्रभासे दैत्यसूदनम् //
text_mt: [One should know] Puṇḍarīkākṣa at Puṣkara, and Gadādhara at Gayā, / Rāghava at Citrakūṭa, and the Slayer of Daityas at Prabhāsa,

sanskrit_iast:
jayaṃ jayantyāṃ tadvacca jayantaṃ hastināpure /
vārāhaṃ vardhamāne ca kāśmīre cakrapāṇinam //
meaning:
जयं जयन्त्यां तद्वच्च जयन्तं हस्तिनापुरे /
वाराहं वर्धमाने च काश्मीरे चक्रपाणिनम् //
text_mt: Jaya at Jayantī, and likewise Jayanta at Hastināpura, / Vārāha at Vardhamāna, and Cakrapāṇi in Kaśmīr,

sanskrit_iast:
janārdanañca kubjāmre mathurāyāñca keśavam /
kubjāmrake hṛṣīkeśaṃ gaṅgādvāre jaṭādharam //
meaning:
जनार्दनञ्च कुब्जाम्रे मथुरायाञ्च केशवम् /
कुब्जाम्रके हृषीकेशं गङ्गाद्वारे जटाधरम् //
text_mt: Janārdana at Kubjāmra, and Keśava at Mathurā, / Hṛṣīkeśa at Kubjāmraka, and Jaṭādhara at Gaṅgādvāra,

sanskrit_iast:
śālagrāme mahāyogaṃ hariṃ gobardhanācale /
:p 123
piṇḍārake caturvāhuṃ śaṅkhoddhāre ca śaṅkhinam //
meaning:
शालग्रामे महायोगं हरिं गोबर्धनाचले /
:प् 123
पिण्डारके चतुर्वाहुं शङ्खोद्धारे च शङ्खिनम् //
text_mt:
Mahāyoga at Śālagrāma, Hari on Mount Govardhana,
[Page 123]
the Four-Armed at Piṇḍāraka, and the Conch-Bearer at Śaṅkhoddhāra,

sanskrit_iast:
vāmanañca kurukṣetre yamunāyāṃ trivikramam /
viśveśvaraṃ tathā śoṇe kapilaṃ pūrvasāgare //
meaning:
वामनञ्च कुरुक्षेत्रे यमुनायां त्रिविक्रमम् /
विश्वेश्वरं तथा शोणे कपिलं पूर्वसागरे //
text_mt: Vāmana at Kurukṣetra, and Trivikrama on the Yamunā, / Viśveśvara on the Śoṇa, Kapila at the Eastern Ocean,

sanskrit_iast:
viṣṇuṃ mahodadhau vidyādgaṅgāsāgarasaṅgame /
vanamālañca kiṣkindhyāṃ devaṃ raivatakaṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
विष्णुं महोदधौ विद्याद्गङ्गासागरसङ्गमे /
वनमालञ्च किष्किन्ध्यां देवं रैवतकं विदुः //
text_mt: one should know Viṣṇu in the Great Ocean, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, / Vanamālin at Kiṣkindhā, and the god at Raivataka is known [by wise men],

sanskrit_iast:
kāśītaṭe mahāyogaṃ virajāyāṃ ripuñjayam /
viśākhayūpe hy ajitannepāle lokabhāvanam //
meaning:
काशीतटे महायोगं विरजायां रिपुञ्जयम् /
विशाखयूपे ह्य् अजितन्नेपाले लोकभावनम् //
text_mt: Mahāyoga on the bank of Kāśī, Ripuñjaya at Virajā, / Ajita at Viśākhayūpa, and Lokabhāvana in Nepāla.

sanskrit_iast:
dvārakāyāṃ viddhi kṛṣṇaṃ mandare madhusūdanam /
lokākule ripuharaṃ śālagrāme hariṃ smaret //
meaning:
द्वारकायां विद्धि कृष्णं मन्दरे मधुसूदनम् /
लोकाकुले रिपुहरं शालग्रामे हरिं स्मरेत् //
text_mt: Know Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā, Madhusūdana at Mandara, / Ripuhara at Lokākula, and one should remember Hari at Śālagrāma.

sanskrit_iast:
puruṣaṃ pūruṣavaṭe vimale ca jagatprabhuṃ /
anantaṃ saindhavāraṇye daṇḍake śārṅgadhāriṇam //
meaning:
पुरुषं पूरुषवटे विमले च जगत्प्रभुं /
अनन्तं सैन्धवारण्ये दण्डके शार्ङ्गधारिणम् //
text_mt: Puruṣa at Pūruṣavaṭa, and the Lord of the Universe at Vimala, / Ananta in the Saindhava Forest, and the Bow-Holder in Daṇḍaka,

sanskrit_iast:
utpalāvartake śaurīṃ narmadāyāṃ śriyaḥ patiṃ /
dāmodaraṃ raivatake nandāyāṃ jalaśāyinaṃ //
meaning:
उत्पलावर्तके शौरीं नर्मदायां श्रियः पतिं /
दामोदरं रैवतके नन्दायां जलशायिनं //
text_mt: Śauri at Utpalāvartaka, the Husband of Śrī on the Narmadā, / Dāmodara at Raivataka, and the Recliner on the Water at Nandā,

sanskrit_iast:
gopīśvarañca sindhvavdhau māhendre cācyutaṃ viṭuḥ /
sahādrau devadeveśaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ māgadhe vane //
meaning:
गोपीश्वरञ्च सिन्ध्वव्धौ माहेन्द्रे चाच्युतं विटुः /
सहाद्रौ देवदेवेशं वैकुण्ठं मागधे वने //
text_mt: and Gopīśvara in the ocean of the Sindhu, and they know Acyuta at Mahendra, / the Lord of the God of Gods on Mount Sahya, and Vaikuṇṭha in the Māgadha forest,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpaharaṃ vindhye auḍre tu puruṣottamam /
ātmānaṃ hṛdaye viddhi japatāṃ bhuktimuktidam //
meaning:
सर्वपापहरं विन्ध्ये औड्रे तु पुरुषोत्तमम् /
आत्मानं हृदये विद्धि जपतां भुक्तिमुक्तिदम् //
text_mt: the Destroyer of All Sins in the Vindhya, and Puruṣottama in Oḍra; / know the Self in the heart, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation upon those who recite [His names].

sanskrit_iast:
vaṭe vaṭe vaiśravaṇaṃ catvare catvare śivam /
parvate parvate rāmaṃ sarvatra madhusūdanaṃ //
meaning:
वटे वटे वैश्रवणं चत्वरे चत्वरे शिवम् /
पर्वते पर्वते रामं सर्वत्र मधुसूदनं //
text_mt: Vaiśravaṇa under every banyan tree, Śiva at every crossroads, / Rāma on every mountain, and Madhusūdana everywhere;

sanskrit_iast:
naraṃ bhūmau tathā vyomni vaśiṣṭhe garuḍadhvajam /
vāsudevañca sarvatra saṃsmaran bhuktimuktibhāk //
meaning:
नरं भूमौ तथा व्योम्नि वशिष्ठे गरुडध्वजम् /

[Fire oblations] with dūrvā grass are for long life; with lotuses, for fortune; with *udumbara* wood, for sons; / with ghee in a cowshed, for success with cattle; with all milk-trees, for wisdom.
Om kṣauṃ. Obeisance to the Blessed Lord, to Nārasiṃha, who wears a garland of flames, / who has blazing fangs, who has eyes of fire, who slays all demons, / who destroys all evil spirits, who cures all fevers; burn, burn; cook, cook; protect, protect; *hūṃ phaṭ*.

This mantra of Nārasiṃha averts all troubles. / Through recitation and the like it removes sorcery, seizing spirits, pestilence, poisons, and ailments. / With powder and the bile of a frog, it produces paralysis of water and fire.

text_mt:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the mantra that enchants the three worlds, for the attainment of the four goals of life.
Om śrīṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ. Om, obeisance to Puruṣottama, / the counter-image of Puruṣottama, abode of Lakṣmī, agitator of all the world, / cleaver of the hearts of all women, infatuator of the three worlds with passion, / torment, torment the minds of beautiful divine and mortal people; kindle, kindle; wither, wither; slay, slay; / paralyze, paralyze; liquefy, liquefy; attract, attract, O supremely fortunate one, bestower of all good fortune, / bestower of desires; strike, strike such-and-such a person with the discus, with the mace, with the sword, with all […]
[Page 127]
pierce, pierce with arrows; bind, bind with the noose; strike, strike with the elephant goad; quickly, quickly; / why do you wait until my desire is fulfilled? *Hūṃ phaṭ*, obeisance! / Om, O Puruṣottama, infatuator of the three worlds with passion, *hūṃ phaṭ*, obeisance to the heart; draw [them], O one of great might, *hūṃ phaṭ*, to the weapon; O Lord of the three worlds, / strike, strike the minds of all people, tear them open, tear them open, bring them under my control, bring them under my control, *hūṃ phaṭ*, / to the eye; O enchanter of the three worlds, O matchless Hṛṣīkeśa, / attractor of the hearts of all women, come, come, obeisance!

phaṭ! Oṃ, svāhā to the aquatic creature! Sharp as a sword, cleave, cleave! Homage to the sword!

text_mt:
Agni said: / The chest with fire, the southern eye, Daṇḍīḥ, Śrīḥ, the grantor of all success: / “Homage to Mahāśrī, possessing great attainments, shining like great lightning!
Homage to Śrī, O Goddess Vijayā! O Gaurī, possessing great strength, bind, bind, homage! Hūṃ, / O you of great body, lotus in hand, hūṃ phaṭ homage to Śrī! To Śrī phaṭ, to Śrī / homage! To Śrī phaṭ, śrīṃ homage! To Śrī, O bestower of prosperity, homage, / svāhā svāhā, śrī phaṭ!”

sanskrit_iast:
asyāṅgāni navoktāni teṣvekañca samāśrayet /
trilakṣamekalakṣaṃ vā japtvākṣābjaiś ca bhūtidaḥ //
meaning:
अस्याङ्गानि नवोक्तानि तेष्वेकञ्च समाश्रयेत् /
त्रिलक्षमेकलक्षं वा जप्त्वाक्षाब्जैश् च भूतिदः //
text_mt: Her nine limbs have been stated; one should resort to one among them. / Having recited three hundred thousand or one hundred thousand times with rosaries of lotus seeds, one becomes a bestower of prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīgehe viṣṇugehe vā śriyaṃ pūjya dhanaṃ labhet /
ājyāktaistaṇḍulair lakṣaṃ juhuyāt khādirānale //
meaning:
श्रीगेहे विष्णुगेहे वा श्रियं पूज्य धनं लभेत् /
आज्याक्तैस्तण्डुलैर् लक्षं जुहुयात् खादिरानले //
text_mt: Having worshipped Śrī in a temple of Śrī or in a temple of Viṣṇu, one obtains wealth. / One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of grains of rice smeared with ghee into a fire of khadira wood.

sanskrit_iast:

सर्षपाम्भोभिषेकेण नश्यन्ते सकला ग्रहाः //
text_mt: A king becomes subjugated, prosperity increases, and Śrī increases more and more. / By aspersion with mustard water, all planetary afflictions are destroyed.

Lakṣmī and increase of wealth arise from a hundred thousand oblations with bilva. / Then one should contemplate in the heart the four-doored abode of Indra.
[Page 131]

Poison, the beloved of Mahiṣa, fire, Rudra, light, a pair of cranes—
[Page 132]
“Oṃ hrīṃ, O great crusher of Mahiṣa, ṭha ṭha!” is the root mantra. / “Homage to the slayer of Mahiṣa! Whirl, whirl the enemy Mahiṣa, hūṃ phaṭ / ṭha ṭha! Make Mahiṣa neigh, neigh, hūṃ! Slay, slay Mahiṣa, O Goddess, hūṃ / O slayer of Mahiṣa, phaṭ!” / This is declared to be the Durgā-hṛdaya along with its limbs, which accomplishes all ends.

One should worship that Goddess as prescribed, and the pedestal situated in the midst of the limbs.
“Oṃ hrīṃ, O Durgā, O protectress, svāhā”; and “Homage to Durgā, / homage to the fair-complexioned one, / to Āryā, to the golden-hued one, to Kṛttikā, to the grantor of fearlessness, to the maiden, / to the shapely one.”
One should worship these icons situated on the petals in order, with the initial vowels.

Bearing a conch, discus, lotus, trident, and other weapons, of fierce form, / one should invoke her in battle and similar occasions, and worship her for victory by means of swords and the like.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventh chapter, entitled "Worship of Trailokyamohanī, Lakṣmī, and Others," in the Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now, the three hundred and eighth chapter.
Worship of Tvaritā.

text_mt:
Agni said: / I shall now fully declare the limb-mantras of Tvaritā, which bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation:
"Oṃ, homage to the Support Śakti! Oṃ hrīṃ puru puru, homage to the Great Lion!
Homage! Oṃ, homage to the lotus! Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ khecachekṣaḥ!
Strīṃ oṃ hrūṃ kṣaiṃ hrūṃ phaṭ, homage to Tvaritā! Khe ca, homage to the heart! Cache, homage to the head! Chekṣaḥ, homage to the topknot! Kṣastrī, homage to the armor! Strīṃ hrūṃ, homage to the eyes! Hrūṃ khe, phaṭ, homage to the weapon! Oṃ, we know the Tvaritā knowledge; we meditate on the swift knowledge; may the goddess impel us thereto! Homage to Śrīpraṇītā!
Homage to Hrūṅkārā! Oṃ kheca, homage to the heart!
Homage to Khecarī! Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍā! Homage to Chedanī! Homage to Kṣepaṇī! Striyai, homage to Hrūṅkārī! To Kṣemaṅkarī, to Jayā, to Kiṅkara, protect! Oṃ, by the command of Tvaritā, become steadfast, vaṣaṭ!"
Totalā, Tvaritā, Tūrṇā—thus has this mantra been proclaimed.
