अनादि परमं ब्रह्म सत्त्वं नाम तदुच्यते //
text_mt: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: / the beginningless supreme Brahman; it is called neither being nor non-being.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādāntaṃ sarvato 'kṣiśiromukham /
sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati //
meaning:
सर्वतः पाणिपादान्तं सर्वतो ऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् /
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति //
text_mt: With hands and feet on all sides, with eyes, heads, and faces on all sides, / with ears on all sides in the world, it stands encompassing all.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam /
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca //
meaning:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् /
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च //
text_mt: Shining with the virtues of all the senses, yet devoid of all the senses; / unattached, yet supporting all; free of the gunas, yet experiencing the gunas;

sanskrit_iast:
vahirantaś ca bhūtānāmacarañcarameva ca /
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthañcāntike 'pi yat //
meaning:
वहिरन्तश् च भूतानामचरञ्चरमेव च /
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थञ्चान्तिके ऽपि यत् //
text_mt: outside and inside beings, moving and unmoving; / incomprehensible because of its subtlety; both far away and near;

sanskrit_iast:
avibhaktañca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam /
bhūtabhartṛ ca vijñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca //
meaning:
अविभक्तञ्च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् /
भूतभर्तृ च विज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च //
text_mt: undivided among beings, yet standing as if divided; / it should be known as the sustainer of beings, devouring them and generating them.

sanskrit_iast:
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate /
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya dhiṣṭhitaṃ //
meaning:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते /
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य धिष्ठितं //
text_mt: The light even of lights, it is said to be beyond darkness; / knowledge, the object of knowledge, attainable by knowledge, seated in the heart of all.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā /
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare //
meaning:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना /
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे //
text_mt: By meditation, some see the self in the self by the self; / others by the yoga of knowledge, and others by the yoga of action.

sanskrit_iast:
anye tvevamajānanto śrutvānyebhya upāsate /
tepi cāśu tarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ //
meaning:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तो श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते /
तेपि चाशु तरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः //
text_mt: Others, not knowing thus, worship having heard from others; / they too, devoted to hearing, certainly cross beyond death quickly.

sanskrit_iast:
sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca /
pramādamohau tamaso bhavato jñānameva ca //
:p 348
meaning:
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च /
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतो ज्ञानमेव च //
:प् 348
text_mt:
From sattva arises knowledge, and from rajas greed; / negligence and delusion arise from tamas, as does ignorance.
[p. 348]

sanskrit_iast:
guṇā vartanta ity eva yo 'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate /
mānāvamānamitrāritulyastyāgī sa nirguṇaḥ //
meaning:
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्य् एव यो ऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते /
मानावमानमित्रारितुल्यस्त्यागी स निर्गुणः //
text_mt: He who stands firm, thinking only, "The gunas operate," and is not shaken, / equal in honor and dishonor, to friend and foe, renouncing [all undertakings]—he is beyond the gunas.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayaṃ /
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit //
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययं /
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् //
text_mt: They speak of the imperishable Aśvattha tree with its roots above and branches below, / whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; he who knows it is a knower of the Veda.

sanskrit_iast:
dvau bhūtasargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca /
ahiṃsādiḥ kṣamā caiva daivīsampattito nṛṇāṃ //
meaning:
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोके ऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च /
अहिंसादिः क्षमा चैव दैवीसम्पत्तितो नृणां //
text_mt: There are two orders of beings in this world: the divine and the demonic. / Non-violence and the like, and forbearance, belong to men of divine endowment.

sanskrit_iast:
na śaucaṃ nāpi vācāro hy āsurīsampadoddhavaḥ /
narakatvāt krodhalobhakāmastasmāttrayaṃ tyajet //
meaning:
न शौचं नापि वाचारो ह्य् आसुरीसम्पदोद्धवः /
नरकत्वात् क्रोधलोभकामस्तस्मात्त्रयं त्यजेत् //
text_mt: Neither ritual purity nor conduct arises from demonic endowment. / Because they lead to hell, one should abandon the triad of anger, greed, and desire.

sanskrit_iast:
yajñastapas tathā dānaṃ sattvādyaistrividhaṃ smṛtam /
āyuḥ sattvaṃ balārogyasukhāyānnantu sāttvikaṃ //
meaning:
यज्ञस्तपस् तथा दानं सत्त्वाद्यैस्त्रिविधं स्मृतम् /
आयुः सत्त्वं बलारोग्यसुखायान्नन्तु सात्त्विकं //
text_mt: Sacrifice, ascetic austerity, and gift are considered threefold according to sattva and the rest. / Food that promotes longevity, mental strength, physical strength, health, and happiness is sāttvika.

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhaśokāmayāyānnaṃ tīkṣṇarūkṣantu rājasaṃ /
amedhyocchiṣṭapūtyannaṃ tāmasaṃ nīrasādikaṃ //
meaning:
दुःखशोकामयायान्नं तीक्ष्णरूक्षन्तु राजसं /
अमेध्योच्छिष्टपूत्यन्नं तामसं नीरसादिकं //
text_mt: Food that brings suffering, sorrow, and disease, being pungent and dry, is rājasika. / Food that is impure, remnant, foul-smelling, and tasteless is tāmasika.

sanskrit_iast:
yaṣṭavyo vidhinā yajño niṣkāmāya sa sāttvikaḥ /
yajñaḥ phalāya dambhātmī rājasastāmasaḥ kratuḥ //
meaning:
यष्टव्यो विधिना यज्ञो निष्कामाय स सात्त्विकः /
यज्ञः फलाय दम्भात्मी राजसस्तामसः क्रतुः //
text_mt: Sacrifice performed according to rule without desire is sāttvika; / a sacrifice [offered] for reward or out of ostentation is rājasika; [that devoid of faith and rules] is a tāmasika rite.

sanskrit_iast:
śraddhāmantrādividhyuktaṃ tapaḥ śārīramucyate /
devādipūjāhiṃsādi vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate //
meaning:
श्रद्धामन्त्रादिविध्युक्तं तपः शारीरमुच्यते /
देवादिपूजाहिंसादि वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते //
text_mt: Ascetic austerity prescribed by faith, mantras, and the like, [such as] worship of gods and non-violence, is called bodily; / ascetic austerity consisting of speech is said [to be]:

sanskrit_iast:
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ svādhyāyasajjapaḥ /
mānasaṃ cittasaṃśuddhersaunamātsavinigrahaḥ //
meaning:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं स्वाध्यायसज्जपः /
मानसं चित्तसंशुद्धेर्सौनमात्सविनिग्रहः //
text_mt: words causing no agitation, truth, study of the Veda, and good recitation; / mental [austerity is that] of mental purity, silence, and self-restraint.

sanskrit_iast:
sāttvikañca tapo 'kāmaṃ phalādyarthantu rājasaṃ /
tāmasaṃ parapīḍāyai sāttvikaṃ dānamucyate //
meaning:
सात्त्विकञ्च तपो ऽकामं फलाद्यर्थन्तु राजसं /
तामसं परपीडायै सात्त्विकं दानमुच्यते //
text_mt: Ascetic austerity without desire is sāttvika, but that for the sake of fruit and the like is rājasika; / that for hurting others is tāmasika. Sāttvika gift is spoken of [as follows]:

sanskrit_iast:
deśādau caiva dātavyamupakārāya rājasaṃ /
ādeśādāvavajñātaṃ tāmasaṃ dānamīritaṃ //
:p 349
meaning:
देशादौ चैव दातव्यमुपकाराय राजसं /
आदेशादाववज्ञातं तामसं दानमीरितं //
:प् 349
text_mt:
it must be given in an appropriate place and the like; that for return of a favor is rājasika; / a gift given in an improper place and the like, with contempt, is declared tāmasika.
[Page 349]

sanskrit_iast:
oṃtatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
yajñadānādika karma buktimuktipradaṃ nṛṇāṃ //
meaning:
ओंतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः /
यज्ञदानादिक कर्म बुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नृणां //
text_mt: “Oṃ Tat Sat”—this is remembered as the threefold designation of Brahman. / Action such as sacrifice and gifts grants worldly enjoyment and liberation to men.

sanskrit_iast:
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśrañca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ /
bhavatyatyāgināṃ(1) pretya na tu sannyāsināṃ kvacit //
meaning:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रञ्च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलं /
भवत्यत्यागिनां(1) प्रेत्य न तु सन्न्यासिनां क्वचित् //
text_mt: The threefold fruit of action—undesirable, desirable, and mixed— / comes after death to those who have not renounced, but never to renunciants.

sanskrit_iast:
tāmasaḥ karmasaṃyogāt mohātkleśabhayādikāt /
rājasaḥ sāttviko 'kāmāt pañcaite karmahetavaḥ //
meaning:
तामसः कर्मसंयोगात् मोहात्क्लेशभयादिकात् /
राजसः सात्त्विको ऽकामात् पञ्चैते कर्महेतवः //
text_mt: [Renunciation is] tāmasika from connection to actions through delusion, suffering, fear, and the like; / rājasika [from pain], and sāttvika without desire. These five are the causes of action:

sanskrit_iast:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇañca pṛthagvidham /
trividhāś ca pṛthak ceṣṭā daivañcaivātra pañcamaṃ //
meaning:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणञ्च पृथग्विधम् /
त्रिविधाश् च पृथक् चेष्टा दैवञ्चैवात्र पञ्चमं //
text_mt: the seat [of action], likewise the agent, the various organs of action, / the various distinct endeavors, and fate as the fifth here.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaṃ jñānaṃ sāttvikaṃ syāt pṛthag jñānantu rājasaṃ /
atattvārthantāmasaṃ syāt karmākāmāya sāttvikaṃ //
meaning:
एकं ज्ञानं सात्त्विकं स्यात् पृथग् ज्ञानन्तु राजसं /
अतत्त्वार्थन्तामसं स्यात् कर्माकामाय सात्त्विकं //
text_mt: Knowledge [seeing one reality] is sāttvika, but knowledge [seeing] distinction is rājasika; / that devoid of truth is tāmasika. Action without desire is sāttvika;

sanskrit_iast:
kāmāya rājasaṃ karma mohāt karma tu tāmasaṃ /
sīdhyasiddhyoḥ samaḥ kartā sāttviko rājaso 'tyapi //
meaning:
कामाय राजसं कर्म मोहात् कर्म तु तामसं /
सीध्यसिद्ध्योः समः कर्ता सात्त्विको राजसो ऽत्यपि //
text_mt: action for desire is rājasika, while action out of delusion is tāmasika. / The agent who is impartial in success and failure is sāttvika; [passionate] is rājasika;

sanskrit_iast:
śaṭho 'lasastāmasaḥ syāt kāryādidhīś ca sāttvikī /
kāryārthaṃ sā rājasī syādviparītā tu tāmasī //
meaning:
शठो ऽलसस्तामसः स्यात् कार्यादिधीश् च सात्त्विकी /
कार्यार्थं सा राजसी स्याद्विपरीता तु तामसी //
text_mt: crooked and lazy is tāmasika. The intellect discerning duty and non-duty is sāttvika; / that [interpreting duty] for self-interest is rājasika, while that inverted is tāmasika.

sanskrit_iast:
manodhṛtiḥ sāttvikī syāt prītikāmeti rājasī /
tāmasī tu praśokādau mukhaṃ sattvāttadantagaṃ //
meaning:
मनोधृतिः सात्त्विकी स्यात् प्रीतिकामेति राजसी /
तामसी तु प्रशोकादौ मुखं सत्त्वात्तदन्तगं //
text_mt: Resolve of the mind is sāttvika; that pursuing pleasure and desire is rājasika; / but that [persisting] in grief and the like is tāmasika. Happiness arising from sattva reaches its end [in bliss];

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaṃ tadrājasañcāgre ante duḥkhantu tāmasaṃ /
ataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidantataṃ //
meaning:
सुखं तद्राजसञ्चाग्रे अन्ते दुःखन्तु तामसं /
अतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदन्ततं //
text_mt: that pleasure is rājasika [like nectar] at first, but tāmasika brings suffering at the end. / From him is the activity of beings, by whom all this is pervaded;

sanskrit_iast:
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya viṣṇuṃ siddhiñca vindati /
karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā //
:n
1 bhavatyayogināmiti kha..
:p 350
meaning:
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य विष्णुं सिद्धिञ्च विन्दति /
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा //
:न्
1 भवत्ययोगिनामिति ख..
:प् 350
text_mt:
by worshiping Viṣṇu through one's own duty, one attains perfection— / by action, mind, and speech in all states at all times.
[...]
[Variant: 'bhavatyayoginām' in manuscript kha.] / [Page 350]

sanskrit_iast:
brahmādistambhaparyantaṃ jagadviṣṇuñca vetti yaḥ /
siddhimāpnoti bhagavadbhakto bhāgavato dhruvaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gītāsāro nāmāśītyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikāśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yamagītā
meaning:
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्भपर्यन्तं जगद्विष्णुञ्च वेत्ति यः /
सिद्धिमाप्नोति भगवद्भक्तो भागवतो ध्रुवं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गीतासारो नामाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
यमगीता
text_mt:
He who knows the universe from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass as Viṣṇu, / devoted to the Lord, a devotee of the Bhagavat, surely attains perfection.
Thus ends the three hundred and eightieth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled “The Essence of the Gītā.”
Now the three hundred and eighty-first chapter.
The Song of Yama.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
yamagītāṃ pravakṣyāmi uktā yā nāciketase /
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ bhuktyai muktyai mokṣārthināṃ satāṃ //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
यमगीतां प्रवक्ष्यामि उक्ता या नाचिकेतसे /
पठतां शृण्वतां भुक्त्यै मुक्त्यै मोक्षार्थिनां सतां //
text_mt: Agni said: / I shall declare the Song of Yama, which was spoken to Naciketas, / for the worldly enjoyment and liberation of good people who read and listen, who seek liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
yama uvāca
āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaparidhānagṛhādikam /
vāñchatyaho 'timohena susthiraṃ svayamasthiraḥ //
meaning:
यम उवाच
आसनं शयनं यानपरिधानगृहादिकम् /
वाञ्छत्यहो ऽतिमोहेन सुस्थिरं स्वयमस्थिरः //
text_mt: Yama said: / Alas, through extreme delusion, [man], himself unstable, desires / a seat, bed, vehicle, garments, houses, and the like to be permanently stable.

sanskrit_iast:
bhogeṣu śaktiḥ satataṃ tathaivātmāvalokanaṃ /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyānāṃ kapilodgītameva hi //
meaning:
भोगेषु शक्तिः सततं तथैवात्मावलोकनं /
श्रेयः परं मनुष्यानां कपिलोद्गीतमेव हि //
text_mt: Constant attachment to sense objects, and likewise the vision of the Self, / is the supreme good for men: thus indeed was sung by Kapila.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ nirmasatvamasaṅgatā /
śreyaḥ param manuṣyānāṃ gītaṃ pañcaśikhena hi //
meaning:
सर्वत्र समदर्शित्वं निर्मसत्वमसङ्गता /
श्रेयः परम् मनुष्यानां गीतं पञ्चशिखेन हि //
text_mt: Impartiality everywhere, freedom from egoism, detachment— / this is the supreme good for men: indeed it was sung by Pañcaśikha.

sanskrit_iast:
āgarbhajanmabālyādivayo 'vasthādivedanaṃ /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇām gaṅgāviṣṇupragītakaṃ //
meaning:
आगर्भजन्मबाल्यादिवयो ऽवस्थादिवेदनं /
श्रेयः परं मनुष्याणाम् गङ्गाविष्णुप्रगीतकं //
text_mt: Knowledge of the stages of life such as conception, birth, childhood, and the like / is the supreme good for men: [so] was proclaimed by Gaṅgā and Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
ādhyātmikādiduḥkhānāmādyantādipratikriyā /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manṣyāṇāṃ janakodgītameva ca //
meaning:
आध्यात्मिकादिदुःखानामाद्यन्तादिप्रतिक्रिया /
श्रेयः परं मन्ष्याणां जनकोद्गीतमेव च //
text_mt: Remedy from beginning to end for the sufferings beginning with the spiritual / is the supreme good for men: indeed it was sung by Janaka.

sanskrit_iast:
abhinnayorbhedakaraḥ pratyayo yaḥ parātmanaḥ /
tacchāntiparamaṃ śreyo brahmodgītamudāhṛtaṃ //
:p 351
meaning:
अभिन्नयोर्भेदकरः प्रत्ययो यः परात्मनः /
तच्छान्तिपरमं श्रेयो ब्रह्मोद्गीतमुदाहृतं //
:प् 351
text_mt:
The cognition of difference between the Supreme Self and [individual soul] which are non-different— / the pacification of that is supreme good: [thus] was uttered what was sung by Brahmā.
[Page 351]

sanskrit_iast:
kartavyamiti yatkarma ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitaṃ /
kurute śreyase saṅgān jaigīṣavyeṇa gīyate //
meaning:
कर्तव्यमिति यत्कर्म ऋग्यजुःसामसंज्ञितं /
कुरुते श्रेयसे सङ्गान् जैगीषव्येण गीयते //
text_mt: Whatever rite known as Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman is performed as a duty / for the sake of the highest good through attachment, is sung by Jaigīṣavya.

sanskrit_iast:
hāniḥ sarvavidhitsānāmātmanaḥ sukhahaitukī /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ devalodgītamīritaṃ //
meaning:
हानिः सर्वविधित्सानामात्मनः सुखहैतुकी /
श्रेयः परं मनुष्याणां देवलोद्गीतमीरितं //
text_mt: Abandonment of all desires, causing the happiness of the Self, / is the supreme good for men: it was declared as sung by Devala.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmatyāgāttu vijñānaṃ sukhaṃ brahma paraṃ padaṃ /
kāmināṃ na hi vijñānaṃ sanakodgītameva tat //
meaning:
कामत्यागात्तु विज्ञानं सुखं ब्रह्म परं पदं /
कामिनां न हि विज्ञानं सनकोद्गीतमेव तत् //
text_mt: From renunciation of desire comes experiential knowledge, bliss, and Brahman, the supreme abode; / for those full of desire, experiential knowledge does not arise: that indeed was sung by Sanaka.

sanskrit_iast:
pravṛttañca nivṛttañca kāryaṃ karmaparo 'bravīt /
śreyasāṃ śreya etaddhi naiṣkarmyaṃ brahma taddhariḥ //
meaning:
प्रवृत्तञ्च निवृत्तञ्च कार्यं कर्मपरो ऽब्रवीत् /
श्रेयसां श्रेय एतद्धि नैष्कर्म्यं ब्रह्म तद्धरिः //
text_mt: He who is devoted to action has spoken of the duty of active engagement and renunciation; / this indeed is the best of all goods: actionless Brahman, that is Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
pumāṃścādhigatajñāno bhedaṃ nāpnoti sattamaḥ /
brahmaṇā viṣṇusaṃjñena parameṇāvyayena ca //
meaning:
पुमांश्चाधिगतज्ञानो भेदं नाप्नोति सत्तमः /
ब्रह्मणा विष्णुसंज्ञेन परमेणाव्ययेन च //
text_mt: And the man who has attained knowledge, the best of good men, finds no difference / with Brahman, named Viṣṇu, supreme and imperishable.

sanskrit_iast:
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ saubhāgyaṃ rūpamuttamam /
tapasā labhyate sarvaṃ manasā yadyadicchati //
meaning:
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं सौभाग्यं रूपमुत्तमम् /
तपसा लभ्यते सर्वं मनसा यद्यदिच्छति //
text_mt: Knowledge, experiential knowledge, faith, good fortune, and supreme beauty— / everything whatever one desires in mind is obtained through ascetic austerity.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsti viṣṇusamandhyeyaṃ tapo nānaśanātparaṃ /
nāstyārogyasamaṃ dhanyaṃ nāsti gaṅgāsamā sarit //
meaning:
नास्ति विष्णुसमन्ध्येयं तपो नानशनात्परं /
नास्त्यारोग्यसमं धन्यं नास्ति गङ्गासमा सरित् //
text_mt: There is no object of meditation equal to Viṣṇu; there is no ascetic austerity higher than fasting; / there is no fortune equal to health; there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
na so 'sti bāndhavaḥ kaścidviṣṇuṃ muktvā jagadguruṃ /
adhaścordhaṃ hariścāgre dehendriyamanomukhe //
meaning:
न सो ऽस्ति बान्धवः कश्चिद्विष्णुं मुक्त्वा जगद्गुरुं /
अधश्चोर्धं हरिश्चाग्रे देहेन्द्रियमनोमुखे //
text_mt: There is no relative whatsoever except Viṣṇu, the teacher of the universe; / Hari is below and above, in front, in the body, senses, mind, and mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
ityevaṃ saṃsmaran prāṇān yastyajetsa harirbhavet /
yattad brahma yataḥ sarvaṃ yatsarvaṃ tasya saṃsthitam //
meaning:
इत्येवं संस्मरन् प्राणान् यस्त्यजेत्स हरिर्भवेत् /
यत्तद् ब्रह्म यतः सर्वं यत्सर्वं तस्य संस्थितम् //
text_mt: Remembering thus, whoever relinquishes his vital breaths becomes Hari. / That which is Brahman, from which everything arises, which is all, [in it] his universe is established;

sanskrit_iast:
agrāhyakamanirdeśyaṃ supratiṣṭhañca yatparaṃ /
parāparasvarūpeṇa viṣṇuḥ sarvahṛdi sthitaḥ //
meaning:
अग्राह्यकमनिर्देश्यं सुप्रतिष्ठञ्च यत्परं /
परापरस्वरूपेण विष्णुः सर्वहृदि स्थितः //
text_mt: which cannot be grasped, cannot be designated, firmly established, and supreme— / in the form of both higher and lower, Viṣṇu resides in the heart of all.

sanskrit_iast:
yajñeśaṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ kecidicchanti tatparaṃ /
kecidviṣṇuṃ haraṃ kecit kecid brahmāṇamīśvaraṃ //
meaning:
यज्ञेशं यज्ञपुरुषं केचिदिच्छन्ति तत्परं /
केचिद्विष्णुं हरं केचित् केचिद् ब्रह्माणमीश्वरं //
text_mt: Some desire that supreme [deity] as the Lord of sacrifice, the Spirit of sacrifice; / some as Viṣṇu, some as Hara, some as Brahmā the Lord;

sanskrit_iast:
indrādināmabhiḥ kecit sūryaṃ somañca kālakam /
:p 352
brahmādistambhaparyantaṃ jagadviṣṇuṃ vadanti ca //
meaning:
इन्द्रादिनामभिः केचित् सूर्यं सोमञ्च कालकम् /
:प् 352
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्भपर्यन्तं जगद्विष्णुं वदन्ति च //

sanskrit_iast:
sa viṣṇuḥ paramaṃ brahma yato nāvartate punaḥ /
suvarṇādimahādānapuṇyatīrthāvagāhanaiḥ //
meaning:
स विष्णुः परमं ब्रह्म यतो नावर्तते पुनः /
सुवर्णादिमहादानपुण्यतीर्थावगाहनैः //
text_mt: That Viṣṇu is the supreme Brahman, from which one does not return again. / By great gifts such as gold, ablutions in sacred fords,

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānair vrataiḥ pūjayā ca dharmaśrutyā tadāpnuyāt /
ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ rathameva tu //
meaning:
ध्यानैर् व्रतैः पूजया च धर्मश्रुत्या तदाप्नुयात् /
आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु //
text_mt: meditations, votive observances, worship, and listening to the sacred law, one attains that. / Know the Self as the chariot-rider, and the body as the chariot;

sanskrit_iast:
buddhintu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca /
indrayāṇi hayānāhurviṣayāṃśceṣugocarān //
meaning:
बुद्धिन्तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च /
इन्द्रयाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांश्चेषुगोचरान् //
text_mt: know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins. / The senses are called the horses, and sense objects are their pasture.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ /
yastvavijñānavān bhavatyayuktena manasā sadā //
meaning:
आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः /
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान् भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा //
text_mt: The wise call [the Self] joined with the senses and the mind the enjoyer. / But whoever is devoid of experiential knowledge, with mind always undisciplined,

sanskrit_iast:
na satpadamavāpnoti saṃsārañcādhigacchati /
yastu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā //
meaning:
न सत्पदमवाप्नोति संसारञ्चाधिगच्छति /
यस्तु विज्ञानवान् भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा //
text_mt: does not attain the good realm, and goes into worldly existence. / But whoever possesses experiential knowledge, with mind always disciplined,

sanskrit_iast:
sa tatpadamavāpnoti yasmādbhūyo na jāyate /
vijñānasārathiryastu manaḥpragrahavānnaraḥ //
meaning:
स तत्पदमवाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते /
विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनःप्रग्रहवान्नरः //
text_mt: attains that state from which he is not born again. / The man who has experiential knowledge as his charioteer, who holds the reins of the mind,

sanskrit_iast:
so 'dhvānaṃ paramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam /
indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ //
meaning:
सो ऽध्वानं परमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् /
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्य् अर्था अर्थेभ्यश् च परं मनः //
text_mt: reaches the end of the road, that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / For higher than the senses are the objects, and higher than the objects is the mind;

sanskrit_iast:
manasastu parā buddhiḥ buddherātmā mahān paraḥ /
mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ //
meaning:
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिः बुद्धेरात्मा महान् परः /
महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः //
text_mt: higher than the mind is the intellect, higher than the intellect is the Great Self; / higher than the Great is the Unmanifest, higher than the Unmanifest is the Spirit (Puruṣa).

sanskrit_iast:
puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ /
eṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhātmā na prakāśate //
meaning:
पुरुषान्न परं किञ्चित् सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः /
एषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढात्मा न प्रकाशते //
text_mt: Higher than Puruṣa there is nothing; that is the goal, that is the supreme destination. / Hidden in all these beings, the Self does not shine forth.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛśyate tvagryayā budhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ /
yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñaḥ tadyacchejjñānamātmani //
meaning:
दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः /
यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञः तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञानमात्मनि //
text_mt: But it is seen by subtle intellect, / sharp, by those who perceive what is subtle. / A wise man should restrain speech in the mind; he should restrain that in knowledge, in the self;

sanskrit_iast:
jñānamātmani mahati niyacchecchānta ātmani /
jñātvā brahmātmanoryogaṃ yamādyair brahma sadbhavet //
:p 353
meaning:
ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि /
ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मात्मनोर्योगं यमाद्यैर् ब्रह्म सद्भवेत् //
:प् 353
text_mt:
He should restrain knowledge in the great self, and that in the tranquil self. / Having known the union of brahman and the self by means of restraints and the rest, one becomes the true brahman.
[Page 353]

sanskrit_iast:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau /
yamāś ca niyamāḥ pañca śaucaṃ santoṣasattapaḥ //
meaning:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ /
यमाश् च नियमाः पञ्च शौचं सन्तोषसत्तपः //
text_mt: Non-injury, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession: / these are the restraints; and the five observances are ritual purity, contentment, true ascetic austerity,

sanskrit_iast:
svādhyāyeśvarapūjā ca āsanaṃ padmakādikaṃ /
prāṇāyāmo vāyujayaḥ pratyāhāraḥ svanigrahaḥ //
meaning:
स्वाध्यायेश्वरपूजा च आसनं पद्मकादिकं /
प्राणायामो वायुजयः प्रत्याहारः स्वनिग्रहः //
text_mt: Vedic study, and worship of God. Posture is the lotus posture and the like. / Breath control is the mastery of breath. Sensory withdrawal is self-restraint.

sanskrit_iast:
śubhe hy ekatra viṣaye cetaso yat pradhāraṇaṃ /
niś calatvāttu dhīmadbhirdhāraṇā dvija kathyate //
meaning:
शुभे ह्य् एकत्र विषये चेतसो यत् प्रधारणं /
निश् चलत्वात्तु धीमद्भिर्धारणा द्विज कथ्यते //
text_mt: The holding of the mind firmly upon a single auspicious object, / because of immobility, is called concentration by the wise, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
paunaḥpunyena tatraiva viṣayeṣveva dhāraṇā /
dhyānaṃ smṛtaṃ samādhistu ahaṃ brahmātmasaṃsthitiḥ //
meaning:
पौनःपुन्येन तत्रैव विषयेष्वेव धारणा /
ध्यानं स्मृतं समाधिस्तु अहं ब्रह्मात्मसंस्थितिः //
text_mt: Holding [the mind] repeatedly on that very object / is remembered as meditation. Concentration, however, is the state of the self as “I am brahman.”

sanskrit_iast:
ghaṭadhvaṃsādyathākāśamabhinnaṃ nabhasā bhavet /
mukto jīvo brahmaṇaivaṃ sadbrahma brahma vai bhavet //
meaning:
घटध्वंसाद्यथाकाशमभिन्नं नभसा भवेत् /
मुक्तो जीवो ब्रह्मणैवं सद्ब्रह्म ब्रह्म वै भवेत् //
text_mt: Just as space becomes identical with the sky upon the destruction of a jar, / even so the liberated individual soul, being brahman, becomes the true brahman indeed.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānaṃ manyate brahma jīvo jñānena nānyathā /
jīvo hy ajñānatatkāryamuktaḥ syādajarāmaraḥ //
meaning:
आत्मानं मन्यते ब्रह्म जीवो ज्ञानेन नान्यथा /
जीवो ह्य् अज्ञानतत्कार्यमुक्तः स्यादजरामरः //
text_mt: The individual soul considers itself as brahman through knowledge, not otherwise; / for freed from ignorance and its effects, the individual soul becomes ageless and immortal.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
vaśiṣṭha yamagītoktā paṭhatāṃ bhuktimuktidā /
ātyantiko layaḥ prokto vedāntabrahmadhīmayaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yamagītā nāmaikāśītyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 354
:ś atha dvyaśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
āgneyapurāṇamāhātmyaṃ
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
वशिष्ठ यमगीतोक्ता पठतां भुक्तिमुक्तिदा /
आत्यन्तिको लयः प्रोक्तो वेदान्तब्रह्मधीमयः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यमगीता नामैकाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 354
:श् अथ द्व्यशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
आग्नेयपुराणमाहात्म्यं
text_mt:
Agni said: / O Vasiṣṭha, this Yama’s Song has been spoken, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation to those who recite it. / Absolute dissolution has been explained, consisting of the realization of brahman through Vedānta.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the three hundred and eighty-first chapter, named “The Song of Yama.”
[Page 354]
Now the three hundred and eighty-second chapter:
The Greatness of the Agni Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
agnir uvāca
āgneyaṃ brahmarūpante purāṇaṃ kathataṃ mayā /
saprapañcaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ vidyādvayamayaṃ mahat //
meaning:
अग्निर् उवाच
आग्नेयं ब्रह्मरूपन्ते पुराणं कथतं मया /
सप्रपञ्चं निष्प्रपञ्चं विद्याद्वयमयं महत् //
text_mt: Agni said: / This Purāṇa of Agni, whose form is brahman, has been spoken to you by me, / both with the manifest world and beyond it, consisting of the two knowledges, great.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvākhyā vidyā viṣṇurjagajjaniḥ /
chandaḥ śikṣā vyākaraṇaṃ nighaṇṭujyotirākhyakāḥ //
meaning:
ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वाख्या विद्या विष्णुर्जगज्जनिः /
छन्दः शिक्षा व्याकरणं निघण्टुज्योतिराख्यकाः //
text_mt: The knowledge known as the Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Atharva [Vedas] is Viṣṇu, the origin of the world; / [and] those known as metrics, phonetics, grammar, lexicon, astronomy,

sanskrit_iast:
niruktadharmaśāstrādi mīmāṃsānyāyavistarāḥ /
āyurvedapurāṇākhyā dhanurgandharvavistarāḥ //
meaning:
निरुक्तधर्मशास्त्रादि मीमांसान्यायविस्तराः /
आयुर्वेदपुराणाख्या धनुर्गन्धर्वविस्तराः //
text_mt: Etymology, the legal treatises and the like, the expositions of Mīmāṃsā and Nyāya, / the expositions known as medicine, the Purāṇas, archery, and music,

sanskrit_iast:
vidyā saivārthaśāstrākhyā devāntānyā harirmahān /
ityeṣā cāparā vidyā parividyākṣaraṃ paraṃ //
meaning:
विद्या सैवार्थशास्त्राख्या देवान्तान्या हरिर्महान् /
इत्येषा चापरा विद्या परिविद्याक्षरं परं //
text_mt: And that knowledge known as statecraft—the other, supreme Hari extends unto the gods. / This is the lower knowledge; the higher knowledge is the supreme, imperishable [brahman].

sanskrit_iast:
yasya bhāvo 'khilaṃ viṣṇustasya no bādhate kaliḥ /
aniṣṭvā tu mahāyajñānakṛtvāpi pitṛsvadhāṃ //
meaning:
यस्य भावो ऽखिलं विष्णुस्तस्य नो बाधते कलिः /
अनिष्ट्वा तु महायज्ञानकृत्वापि पितृस्वधां //
text_mt: He whose conviction is that all is Viṣṇu is not oppressed by the Kali age. / Even without having performed the great sacrifices, and without making the ancestral offerings,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇamabhyarcayanbhaktyā nainaso bhājanaṃ bhavet /
sarvakāraṇamatyantaṃ viṣṇuṃ dhyāyanna sīdati //
meaning:
कृष्णमभ्यर्चयन्भक्त्या नैनसो भाजनं भवेत् /
सर्वकारणमत्यन्तं विष्णुं ध्यायन्न सीदति //
text_mt: One who worships Kṛṣṇa with devotion does not become a receptacle of sin. / Meditating on Viṣṇu, the ultimate cause of all, he does not sink down.

sanskrit_iast:
anyatantrādidoṣottho viṣayākṛṣṭamānasaḥ /
kṛtvāpi pāpaṃ govindaṃ dhyāyanpāpaiḥ pramucyate //
meaning:
अन्यतन्त्रादिदोषोत्थो विषयाकृष्टमानसः /
कृत्वापि पापं गोविन्दं ध्यायन्पापैः प्रमुच्यते //
text_mt: A person whose mind is seduced by sense objects, born from the fault of other systems and the like, / even having committed sin, is freed from sins by meditating on Govinda.

sanskrit_iast:
taddhyānaṃ yatra govindaḥ sa kathā yatra keśavaḥ /
tat karma yattadarthīyaṃ kimanyair bahubhāṣitaiḥ //
meaning:
तद्ध्यानं यत्र गोविन्दः स कथा यत्र केशवः /
तत् कर्म यत्तदर्थीयं किमन्यैर् बहुभाषितैः //
text_mt: That is meditation wherein is Govinda; that is a tale wherein is Keśava; / that is action which is performed for his sake. What is the use of other extensive talk?

sanskrit_iast:
na tat pitā tu putrāya na śiṣyāya gururdvija /
paramārthaṃ paraṃ brūyādyadetatte mayoditaṃ //
meaning:
न तत् पिता तु पुत्राय न शिष्याय गुरुर्द्विज /
परमार्थं परं ब्रूयाद्यदेतत्ते मयोदितं //
text_mt: Neither a father to his son, nor a guru to his disciple, O twice-born, / would declare that supreme reality which has been proclaimed to you by me.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsāre bhramatā labhyaṃ putradāradhanaṃ vasu /
:p 355
suhṛdaś ca tathaivānye nopadeśo dvijedṛśaḥ //
meaning:
संसारे भ्रमता लभ्यं पुत्रदारधनं वसु /
:प् 355
सुहृदश् च तथैवान्ये नोपदेशो द्विजेदृशः //
text_mt:
Sons, wives, riches, and property may be obtained by one wandering in saṃsāra,
[Page 355]
And likewise other friends; but such teaching as this is not [attained], O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ putradārair mitrair vā kiṃ mitrakṣetravāndhavaiḥ /
upadeśaḥ paro vandhurīdṛśo yo vimuktaye //
meaning:
किं पुत्रदारैर् मित्रैर् वा किं मित्रक्षेत्रवान्धवैः /
उपदेशः परो वन्धुरीदृशो यो विमुक्तये //
text_mt: What is the use of sons, wives, or friends? What is the use of friends, lands, and relatives? / Such teaching as leads to liberation is the supreme kin.

sanskrit_iast:
dvividho bhūtamārgīyaṃ daiva āsura eva ca /
viṣṇubhaktiparo daivo viparītas tathāsuraḥ //
meaning:
द्विविधो भूतमार्गीयं दैव आसुर एव च /
विष्णुभक्तिपरो दैवो विपरीतस् तथासुरः //
text_mt: The path of living beings is twofold: divine and demonic. / The divine is devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu; the demonic is the opposite of that.

sanskrit_iast:
etat pavitramārogyaṃ dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanaṃ /
sukhaprītikaraṃ nṝṇāṃ mokṣakṛdyattaveritaṃ //
meaning:
एतत् पवित्रमारोग्यं धन्यं दुःस्वप्ननाशनं /
सुखप्रीतिकरं नॄणां मोक्षकृद्यत्तवेरितं //
text_mt: This which has been told to you is purifying, health-giving, auspicious, destroying bad dreams, / granting happiness and affection to men, and bringing about liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
yeṣāṃ gṛheṣu likhitamāgneyaṃ hi purāṇakaṃ /
pustakaṃ sthāsyati sadā tatra neśurupadravāḥ //
meaning:
येषां गृहेषु लिखितमाग्नेयं हि पुराणकं /
पुस्तकं स्थास्यति सदा तत्र नेशुरुपद्रवाः //
text_mt: In whosever homes this Purāṇa of Agni shall abide / as a written book, calamities can never rule there.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ tīrthair gopradānair vā kiṃ yajñaiḥ kimupoṣitaiḥ /
āgneyaṃ ye hi śṛṇvanti ahanyahani mānavāḥ //
meaning:
किं तीर्थैर् गोप्रदानैर् वा किं यज्ञैः किमुपोषितैः /
आग्नेयं ये हि शृण्वन्ति अहन्यहनि मानवाः //
text_mt: What need is there of sacred fords, or gifts of cows, or sacrifices, or fasts, / for those men who hear the Agni Purāṇa day after day?

sanskrit_iast:
ye dadāti tilaprasthaṃ suvarṇasya ca māṣakaṃ /
śṛṇoti ślokamekañca āgneyasya tadāpnuyāt //
meaning:
ये ददाति तिलप्रस्थं सुवर्णस्य च माषकं /
शृणोति श्लोकमेकञ्च आग्नेयस्य तदाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: Whoever gives a prastha of sesame and a māṣa of gold, / and hears even a single verse of the Agni Purāṇa, attains that [fruit].

sanskrit_iast:
adhyāyapaṭhanañcāsya gopradānād viśiṣyate /
ahorātrakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śrotumicchoḥ praṇaśyati //
meaning:
अध्यायपठनञ्चास्य गोप्रदानाद् विशिष्यते /
अहोरात्रकृतं पापं श्रोतुमिच्छोः प्रणश्यति //
text_mt: The recitation of a chapter of this excels the gift of a cow. / The sin committed day and night is destroyed for one who desires to hear it.

sanskrit_iast:
kapilānāṃ śate datte yad bhavejjyeṣṭhapuṣkare /
tadāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ hi paṭhitvā phalamāpnuyāt //
meaning:
कपिलानां शते दत्ते यद् भवेज्ज्येष्ठपुष्करे /
तदाग्नेयं पुराणं हि पठित्वा फलमाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: Whatever [fruit] there is when a hundred tawny cows are given at Jyeṣṭhapuṣkara, / he obtains that very fruit having read the Agni Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
pravṛttañca nivṛttañca dharmaṃ vidyādvayātmakaṃ /
āgneyasya purāṇasya śāstrasyāsya samaṃ na hi //
meaning:
प्रवृत्तञ्च निवृत्तञ्च धर्मं विद्याद्वयात्मकं /
आग्नेयस्य पुराणस्य शास्त्रस्यास्य समं न हि //
text_mt: Regarding duty characterized by worldly engagement and cessation, consisting of the two knowledges, / there is indeed nothing equal to this treatise, the Agni Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
paṭhannāgneyakaṃ nityaṃ śṛṇvan vāpi purāṇakaṃ /
bhakto vaśiṣṭha manujaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
meaning:
पठन्नाग्नेयकं नित्यं शृण्वन् वापि पुराणकं /
भक्तो वशिष्ठ मनुजः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते //
text_mt: Constantly reciting or hearing the Agni Purāṇa, / a devoted man, O Vasiṣṭha, is freed from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
nopasargā na cānarthā na caurāribhayaṃ gṛhe /
tasman syād yatra cāgneyapurāṇasya hi pustakaṃ //
:p 356
meaning:
नोपसर्गा न चानर्था न चौरारिभयं गृहे /
तस्मन् स्याद् यत्र चाग्नेयपुराणस्य हि पुस्तकं //
:प् 356
text_mt:
There are no afflictions, no misfortunes, and no fear of thieves or enemies in the house / of that person where the book of the Agni Purāṇa is kept.
[Page 356]

sanskrit_iast:
na garbhahāriṇībhītirna ca bālagrahā gṛhe /
yatrāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ syānna piśācādikaṃ bhayaṃ //
meaning:
न गर्भहारिणीभीतिर्न च बालग्रहा गृहे /
यत्राग्नेयं पुराणं स्यान्न पिशाचादिकं भयं //
text_mt: There is no fear of child-snatching spirits, nor seizing spirits of children in the house / where the Agni Purāṇa is; there is no fear of piśācas and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṇvanvipro vedavit syāt kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
ṛddhiṃ prāpnoti vaiśyaś ca śūdraścārogyamṛcchati //
meaning:
शृण्वन्विप्रो वेदवित् स्यात् क्षत्रियः पृथिवीपतिः /
ऋद्धिं प्राप्नोति वैश्यश् च शूद्रश्चारोग्यमृच्छति //
text_mt: Hearing it, a brahmin becomes a knower of the Veda; a kṣatriya, a ruler of the earth; / a vaiśya attains prosperity; and a śūdra attains freedom from illness.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ paṭhetśṛṇuyānnityaṃ samadṛgviṣṇumānasaḥ /
brahmāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ sattatra naśyantyupadravāḥ //
meaning:
यः पठेत्शृणुयान्नित्यं समदृग्विष्णुमानसः /
ब्रह्माग्नेयं पुराणं सत्तत्र नश्यन्त्युपद्रवाः //
text_mt: Whoever, with mind impartial and fixed on Viṣṇu, recites or hears daily / this true Purāṇa of Agni and Brahmā, in that place calamities perish,

sanskrit_iast:
divyāntarīkṣabhaumādyā duḥsvapnādyabhicārakāḥ /
yaccānyadduritaṃ kiñcittatsarvaṃ hanti keśavaḥ //
meaning:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमाद्या दुःस्वप्नाद्यभिचारकाः /
यच्चान्यद्दुरितं किञ्चित्तत्सर्वं हन्ति केशवः //
text_mt: Celestial, atmospheric, terrestrial, and the like, bad dreams, malevolent sorceries, / and whatever other misfortune there may be: Keśava destroys all that.

sanskrit_iast:
paṭhataḥ śṛṇvataḥ puṃsaḥ pustakaṃ yajato mahat /
āgneyaṃ śrīpurāṇaṃ hi hemante yaḥ śṛṇoti vai //
meaning:
पठतः शृण्वतः पुंसः पुस्तकं यजतो महत् /
आग्नेयं श्रीपुराणं हि हेमन्ते यः शृणोति वै //
text_mt: For the man who recites, hears, and worships this great book, / the auspicious Purāṇa of Agni—whoever hears it in early winter,

sanskrit_iast:
prapūjya gandhapuṣpādhyair agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet /
śiśire puṇḍarīkasya vasante cāśvamedhajam //
meaning:
प्रपूज्य गन्धपुष्पाध्यैर् अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् /
शिशिरे पुण्डरीकस्य वसन्ते चाश्वमेधजम् //
text_mt: Having worshipped it with fragrances, flowers, and the like, obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice; / in late winter, [the fruit] of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice; and in spring, that born of an Aśvamedha;

sanskrit_iast:
grīṣme tu vājapeyasya rājasūyasya varṣati /
gosahasrasya śaradi phalaṃ tatpaṭhato hy ṛtau //
meaning:
ग्रीष्मे तु वाजपेयस्य राजसूयस्य वर्षति /
गोसहस्रस्य शरदि फलं तत्पठतो ह्य् ऋतौ //
text_mt: In summer, that of a Vājapeya; in the rainy season, that of a Rājasūya; / in autumn, the fruit of a thousand cows for one who reads it in that season.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyaṃ hi purāṇaṃ yo bhaktyāgre paṭhete hareḥ /
so 'rcayecca vasiṣṭheha jñānayajñena keśavam //
meaning:
आग्नेयं हि पुराणं यो भक्त्याग्रे पठेते हरेः /
सो ऽर्चयेच्च वसिष्ठेह ज्ञानयज्ञेन केशवम् //
text_mt: Whoever recites the Agni Purāṇa with devotion before Hari, / he worships Keśava here, O Vasiṣṭha, with a sacrifice of knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāgneyapurāṇasya pustakaṃ tasya vai jayaḥ /
likhitaṃ pūjitaṃ gehe bhuktirmuktiḥ kare 'sti hi //
meaning:
यस्याग्नेयपुराणस्य पुस्तकं तस्य वै जयः /
लिखितं पूजितं गेहे भुक्तिर्मुक्तिः करे ऽस्ति हि //
text_mt: He who has the book of the Agni Purāṇa indeed has victory; / when it is copied and worshipped in his house, worldly enjoyment and liberation are in his hand.

sanskrit_iast:
iti kālāgnirūpeṇa gītaṃ me hariṇā purā /
āgneyaṃ hi purāṇaṃ vai brahmavidyādvayāspadam /
vidyādvayaṃ vasiṣṭhedaṃ bhaktebhyaḥ kathayiṣyasi //
meaning:
इति कालाग्निरूपेण गीतं मे हरिणा पुरा /
आग्नेयं हि पुराणं वै ब्रह्मविद्याद्वयास्पदम् /
विद्याद्वयं वसिष्ठेदं भक्तेभ्यः कथयिष्यसि //
text_mt: Thus was sung to me formerly by Hari in the form of the Fire of Time, / the Agni Purāṇa, the abode of the two knowledges of brahman. / You shall declare these two knowledges, O Vasiṣṭha, to the devotees.

sanskrit_iast:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
vyāsāgneyapurāṇaṃ te rūpaṃ vidyādvayātmakaṃ /
kathitaṃ brahmaṇo viṣṇoragninā kathitaṃ yathā //
:p 357
meaning:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
व्यासाग्नेयपुराणं ते रूपं विद्याद्वयात्मकं /
कथितं ब्रह्मणो विष्णोरग्निना कथितं यथा //
:प् 357
text_mt:
Vasiṣṭha said: / O Vyāsa, the form of the Agni Purāṇa, consisting of the two knowledges / of the brahman that is Viṣṇu, has been spoken to you just as it was spoken by Agni.
[Page 357]

sanskrit_iast:
sārdhaṃ devaiś ca munibhirmahyaṃ sarvāthadarśakaṃ /
purāṇamagninā gautamāgneyaṃ brahmasanmitaṃ //
meaning:
सार्धं देवैश् च मुनिभिर्मह्यं सर्वाथदर्शकं /
पुराणमग्निना गौतमाग्नेयं ब्रह्मसन्मितं //
text_mt: Together with the gods and sages, the Purāṇa showing all aims was proclaimed to me / by Agni, equal to the true brahman, O descendant of Gotama.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyāddhyāsa likhedvā lekhayedapi /
śrāvayetpāṭhayedvāpi pūjayeddhārayedapi //
meaning:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्ध्यास लिखेद्वा लेखयेदपि /
श्रावयेत्पाठयेद्वापि पूजयेद्धारयेदपि //
text_mt: Whoever recites, hears, meditates on it, writes it or has it written, / causes it to be heard or causes it to be recited, worships it or keeps it,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāprakāmo divaṃ vrajet /
lekhayitvā purāṇaṃ yo dadyādviprebhya uttamaṃ //
meaning:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्राप्रकामो दिवं व्रजेत् /
लेखयित्वा पुराणं यो दद्याद्विप्रेभ्य उत्तमं //
text_mt: Freed from all sins, having attained his desires, goes to heaven. / Having had this excellent Purāṇa transcribed, whoever gives it to brahmins

sanskrit_iast:
sa brahmalokamāpnoti kulānāṃ śatamuddharet /
ekaṃ ślokaṃ paṭhedyastu pāpapaṅkādvimucyate //
meaning:
स ब्रह्मलोकमाप्नोति कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् /
एकं श्लोकं पठेद्यस्तु पापपङ्काद्विमुच्यते //
text_mt: He attains the realm of Brahmā and redeems a hundred families. / And one who recites even a single verse is freed from the mire of sin.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādvyāsa sadā śrāvyaṃ śiṣyebhyaḥ sarvadarśanaṃ /
śukādyair munibhiḥ sardhaṃ śrotukāmaiḥ purāṇakaṃ //
meaning:
तस्माद्व्यास सदा श्राव्यं शिष्येभ्यः सर्वदर्शनं /
शुकाद्यैर् मुनिभिः सर्धं श्रोतुकामैः पुराणकं //
text_mt: Therefore, O Vyāsa, this Purāṇa containing all viewpoints should always be recited to disciples / along with sages like Śuka and others who desire to hear it.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyaṃ paṭhitaṃ dhyātaṃ śubhaṃ syād bhuktimuktidaṃ /
agnaye tu namastasmai yena gītaṃ purānakaṃ //
meaning:
आग्नेयं पठितं ध्यातं शुभं स्याद् भुक्तिमुक्तिदं /
अग्नये तु नमस्तस्मै येन गीतं पुरानकं //
text_mt: The Agni Purāṇa, when recited and meditated upon, brings auspiciousness and bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Reverence unto that Agni by whom this Purāṇa was sung!

sanskrit_iast:
vyāsa uvāca
vasiṣṭhena purā gītaṃ sūtaitatte mayoditaṃ /
parāvidyāparāvidyāsvarūpaṃ paramaṃ padam //
meaning:
व्यास उवाच
वसिष्ठेन पुरा गीतं सूतैतत्ते मयोदितं /
पराविद्यापराविद्यास्वरूपं परमं पदम् //
text_mt: Vyāsa said: / Formerly sung by Vasiṣṭha, this which is the highest state, / embodying higher knowledge and lower knowledge, has been told to you by me, O Sūta.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyaṃ durlabhaṃ rūpaṃ prāpyate bhāgyasaṃyutaiḥ /
dhyāyanto brahma cāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ harimāgatāḥ //
meaning:
आग्नेयं दुर्लभं रूपं प्राप्यते भाग्यसंयुतैः /
ध्यायन्तो ब्रह्म चाग्नेयं पुराणं हरिमागताः //
text_mt: The form of the Agni Purāṇa, difficult to obtain, is acquired by the fortunate. / Meditating upon the Agni Purāṇa as Brahman, they have attained Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyārthinas tathā vidyāṃ rājyaṃ rājyārthino gatāḥ /
aputrāḥ putriṇaḥ santi nāśrayā āśrayaṃ gatāḥ //
meaning:
विद्यार्थिनस् तथा विद्यां राज्यं राज्यार्थिनो गताः /
अपुत्राः पुत्रिणः सन्ति नाश्रया आश्रयं गताः //
text_mt: Those seeking knowledge attain knowledge; those seeking kingship attain kingship; / the childless become possessors of children; the shelterless attain shelter;

sanskrit_iast:
saubhāgyārthī ca saubhāgyaṃ mokṣaṃ mokṣārthino gatāḥ /
likhanto lekhayantaś ca niṣpāpaś ca śriyaṃ gatāḥ //
meaning:
सौभाग्यार्थी च सौभाग्यं मोक्षं मोक्षार्थिनो गताः /
लिखन्तो लेखयन्तश् च निष्पापश् च श्रियं गताः //
text_mt: the seeker of good fortune attains good fortune; those seeking liberation attain liberation. / Those who write it or cause it to be written, become sinless and attain prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
śukapailamukhaiḥ sūta āgneyantu purāṇakaṃ /
rūpaṃ cintaya yātāsi bhuktiṃ muktiṃ na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
शुकपैलमुखैः सूत आग्नेयन्तु पुराणकं /
रूपं चिन्तय यातासि भुक्तिं मुक्तिं न संशयः //
text_mt: O Sūta, together with prominent sages like Śuka and Paila, / meditate upon the form of the Agni Purāṇa; you will attain worldly enjoyment and liberation, there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
śrāvaya tvañca śiṣyebhyo bhaktebhyaś ca purāṇakam /
:p 358
sūta uvāca
vyāsa prasādādāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ śrutamādarāt //
meaning:
श्रावय त्वञ्च शिष्येभ्यो भक्तेभ्यश् च पुराणकम् /
:प् 358
सूत उवाच
व्यास प्रसादादाग्नेयं पुराणं श्रुतमादरात् //
text_mt:
And you, recite this Purāṇa to disciples and devotees.
[p. 358]
Sūta said: / By the grace of Vyāsa, the Agni Purāṇa has been heard with reverence.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyaṃ brahmarūpaṃ hi munayaḥ śaunakādayaḥ /
bhavanto naimiṣāraṇye yajanto harimīśvaraṃ //
meaning:
आग्नेयं ब्रह्मरूपं हि मुनयः शौनकादयः /
भवन्तो नैमिषारण्ये यजन्तो हरिमीश्वरं //
text_mt: The Agni Purāṇa is indeed the very form of Brahman, O sages headed by Śaunaka! / You, abiding in the Naimiṣa forest, worshipping Hari the Lord,

sanskrit_iast:
tiṣṭhantaḥ śraddhayā yuktāstasmādvaḥ samudīritam /
agninā proktamāgneyaṃ purāṇaṃ vedasammitaṃ //
meaning:
तिष्ठन्तः श्रद्धया युक्तास्तस्माद्वः समुदीरितम् /
अग्निना प्रोक्तमाग्नेयं पुराणं वेदसम्मितं //
text_mt: remaining endowed with faith—therefore it has been declared to you: / the Agni Purāṇa, spoken by Agni, equal to the Vedas,

sanskrit_iast:
brahmavidyādvayopetaṃ bhuktidaṃ muktidaṃ mahat /
nāsmātparataraḥ sāro nāsmātparataraḥ suhṛt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मविद्याद्वयोपेतं भुक्तिदं मुक्तिदं महत् /
नास्मात्परतरः सारो नास्मात्परतरः सुहृत् //
text_mt: accompanied by both kinds of knowledge of Brahman, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation, great. / There is no essence higher than this; there is no friend higher than this.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsmātparataro grantho nāsmātparataro gatiḥ /
nāsmātparataraṃ śāstraṃ nāsmātparatarā śrutiḥ //
meaning:
नास्मात्परतरो ग्रन्थो नास्मात्परतरो गतिः /
नास्मात्परतरं शास्त्रं नास्मात्परतरा श्रुतिः //
text_mt: There is no text higher than this; there is no refuge higher than this. / There is no treatise higher than this; there is no revealed scripture higher than this.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsmātparataraṃ jñānaṃ nāsmātparatarā smṛtiḥ /
nāsmātparo hy āgamo 'sti nāsmādvidyā parāsti hi //
meaning:
नास्मात्परतरं ज्ञानं नास्मात्परतरा स्मृतिः /
नास्मात्परो ह्य् आगमो ऽस्ति नास्माद्विद्या परास्ति हि //
text_mt: There is no knowledge higher than this; there is no remembered tradition higher than this. / There is indeed no Āgama higher than this, nor is there any higher knowledge than this.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsmātparaḥ syātsiddhanto nāsmātparamamaṅgalam /
nāsmātparo 'sti vedāntaḥ purāṇaṃ paramantvidaṃ //
meaning:
नास्मात्परः स्यात्सिद्धन्तो नास्मात्परममङ्गलम् /
नास्मात्परो ऽस्ति वेदान्तः पुराणं परमन्त्विदं //
text_mt: There can be no established doctrine higher than this; there is no highest auspiciousness [apart from it]. / There is no Vedānta higher than this; this Purāṇa is indeed supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsmātparataraṃ bhūmau vidyate vastu durlabham /
āgneye hi purāṇe 'smin sarvavidyāḥ pradarśitāḥ //
meaning:
नास्मात्परतरं भूमौ विद्यते वस्तु दुर्लभम् /
आग्नेये हि पुराणे ऽस्मिन् सर्वविद्याः प्रदर्शिताः //
text_mt: There exists on earth no rare object higher than this. / For in this Agni Purāṇa, all sciences have been shown.

sanskrit_iast:
sarve matsyāvatārādyā gītā rāmāyaṇantviha /
harivaṃśo bhāratañca nava sargāḥ pradarśitāḥ //
meaning:
सर्वे मत्स्यावताराद्या गीता रामायणन्त्विह /
हरिवंशो भारतञ्च नव सर्गाः प्रदर्शिताः //
text_mt: All [incarnations] beginning with the fish incarnation have been sung, and here the Rāmāyaṇa, / the Harivaṃśa and the Mahābhārata, and the nine creations have been shown.

sanskrit_iast:
āgamo vaiṣṇavo gītaḥ pūjādīkṣāpratiṣṭhayā /
pavitrārohaṇādīni pratimālakṣaṇādikaṃ //
meaning:
आगमो वैष्णवो गीतः पूजादीक्षाप्रतिष्ठया /
पवित्रारोहणादीनि प्रतिमालक्षणादिकं //
text_mt: The Vaiṣṇava Āgama has been sung, with worship, initiation, and consecration, / rites such as investiture with the sacred thread, and the characteristics of images and the like,

sanskrit_iast:
prāsādalakṣaṇādyañca mantrā vai bhuktimuktidāḥ /
śaivāgamastadarthaś ca śākteyaḥ saura eva ca //
meaning:
प्रासादलक्षणाद्यञ्च मन्त्रा वै भुक्तिमुक्तिदाः /
शैवागमस्तदर्थश् च शाक्तेयः सौर एव च //
text_mt: the characteristics of temples and so forth, and the mantras that bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation; / the Śaiva Āgama and its meaning, as well as the Śākta and the Saura [traditions],

sanskrit_iast:
maṇḍalāni ca vāstuś ca mantāṇi vividhāni ca /
pratisargaścānugīto brahmāṇḍaparimaṇḍalaṃ //
:p 359
meaning:
मण्डलानि च वास्तुश् च मन्ताणि विविधानि च /
प्रतिसर्गश्चानुगीतो ब्रह्माण्डपरिमण्डलं //
:प् 359
text_mt:
the maṇḍalas, site architecture, various mantras, / and secondary creation have been sung, [as well as] the circumference of the cosmic egg.
[p. 359]

sanskrit_iast:
gīto bhuvanakoṣaś ca dvīpavarṣādinimnagāḥ /
gayāgaṅgāprayāgādi tīrthamāhātmyamīritaṃ //
meaning:
गीतो भुवनकोषश् च द्वीपवर्षादिनिम्नगाः /
गयागङ्गाप्रयागादि तीर्थमाहात्म्यमीरितं //
text_mt: The description of the earth has been sung, the continents, regions, and rivers; / the greatness of sacred fords such as Gayā, the Gaṅgā, and Prayāga has been declared;

sanskrit_iast:
jyotiś cakraṃ jyotiṣādi gīto yuddhajayārṇavaḥ /
manvantarādayo gītāḥ dharmā varṇādikasya ca //
meaning:
ज्योतिश् चक्रं ज्योतिषादि गीतो युद्धजयार्णवः /
मन्वन्तरादयो गीताः धर्मा वर्णादिकस्य च //
text_mt: the wheel of the heavenly bodies, astrology and astronomy, and the Yuddhajayārṇava have been sung; / the cosmic eras of Manus and the rest have been sung, and the duties of the castes and life-stages;

sanskrit_iast:
aśaucaṃ dravyaśuddhiś ca prāyaścittaṃ pradarśitaṃ /
rājadharmā dānadharmā vratāni vividhāni ca //
meaning:
अशौचं द्रव्यशुद्धिश् च प्रायश्चित्तं प्रदर्शितं /
राजधर्मा दानधर्मा व्रतानि विविधानि च //
text_mt: ritual impurity, purification of substances, and expiation have been shown; / the duties of kings, the duties regarding gifts, and various votive observances;

sanskrit_iast:
vyavahārāḥ śāntayaś ca ṛgvedādividhānakaṃ /
sūryavaṃśaḥ somavaṃśo dhanurvedaś ca vaidyakaṃ //
meaning:
व्यवहाराः शान्तयश् च ऋग्वेदादिविधानकं /
सूर्यवंशः सोमवंशो धनुर्वेदश् च वैद्यकं //

text_mt:
Among the ten exemplar manuscripts of the Agni Purāṇa marked with ‘ka’ and subsequent letters, in nine exemplar manuscripts the text concludes with the chapter on the greatness of the Purāṇa following the Yamagītā chapter. In the manuscript marked ‘ga’, however, following the Yamagītā chapter, there are thirty-three additional chapters beginning with the section on creation. Because these said chapters are absent in nine exemplar manuscripts, their authenticity is doubtful. Even granting authenticity, since only one manuscript, that marked ‘ga’, is available—which is defective with missing letters in various places—I was unable to print these additional chapters here. Nevertheless, for the purpose of making this known, a few additional chapters found only in the manuscript marked ‘ga’ have been emended to the best of my ability and printed in the form of an appendix. Because the manuscript marked ‘ga’ has missing letters and is corrupt, faulty readings exist in many places of this appendix.

Having become Brahmā, Narasiṃha sets forth in the creation of the world.
I shall tell that to you; listen to me, O Bharadvāja.
The Lord named Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds,
having arisen, is carried […].
[...]
1 This reading cannot be emended due to the loss of letters in the manuscript. [page 362]
By his own measure, his lifespan is traditionally held to be one hundred years.
And Viṣṇu is Time, by whom his lifespan is calculated,
as well as that of other beings, moving and unmoving,
and of all [elements] beginning with earth, soil, and oceans, O best of beings.
Eighteen nimeṣas are declared to be one kāṣṭhā;
thirty kāṣṭhās are a kalā; thirty kalās should be known as a muhūrta.
A human day and night is traditionally taught to consist of that number of muhūrtas.
That many days and nights make a month consisting of two fortnights.

text_mt:
Six of those months make an ayana; there are two ayanas: southern and northern.
The southern ayana is night for the gods, and the northern is day.
Two ayanas are declared to be a year for mortals;
a month of human beings is taught to be a day and night for the ancestors.
A human year is traditionally held to be a day and night for the Vasus and other gods.
Hear from me the division of those [ages] designated as Kṛta, Tretā, and so on,
by thousands of divine years: four, [three, two, and one], into twelve.
Four, three, two, and one, respectively, in the Kṛta and following [yugas],
thousands of divine years in the yugas, the knowers of the past say.
Measured by that many hundreds, the dawn preceding each is named there.
And the twilight following it is equal to that; it indeed comes after the yuga.
The period of time that exists between dawn and twilight, O twice-born,
is to be known as a yuga, designated as Kṛta, Tretā, and so on.

Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali: this is the four-yuga cycle.
A thousand of them is called a day of Brahmā, O twice-born.
[page 363]
In a day of Brahmā, O sage, there are fourteen Manus.
Their auspicious measurement made by time is [as follows]:
the Seven Sages, the gods, Śakra, the Manu, and his sons, the kings,
are created at one time and destroyed as before.
Seventy-one cycles of four yugas are enumerated
as a manvantara, the time of a Manu, and of Śakra and the others as well, O twice-born.
Eight hundred and fifty-two thousand by divine count, [O Sūta,]
and fifty-one other [years], and seven others, O sage,
and twenty thousand—this time is traditionally stated with an excess.
Thus should a day of Brahmā be known; it is proclaimed as this.

text_mt:
Thus ends the first chapter, named the Section on Creation, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the second chapter.
Sūta said:
Here, while the god was asleep, a lotus arose from his navel.
In that lotus, O fortunate one, he who is versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
Brahmā was born; he was addressed by him: "Create creatures, O high-minded one!"
Having spoken thus, the lord Nārāyaṇa vanished.
Thinking of the god Viṣṇu, who had gone after saying, "So be it,"
Brahmā remained; he did not comprehend at all any cause for the universe.
Then great anger arose in that great-souled Brahmā.
From that, Rudra was born upon his lap, originating from his wrath.
Crying, he was addressed by that Brahmā of unmanifest birth:
When told, "Give me a name," he gave him [the name] Rudra.
He too was told by him: "Create this world again!"

Endowed with ascetic austerity, he repeatedly created in the exhausted waters.
[Page 365]
When he was immersed in the waters, however, another Prajāpati
Brahmā, the lord of beings, created standing to his right, and another
Dakṣa, who stood to his left, and then he brought forth his wife.
With her he engendered the lord Manu Svāyambhuva.
From him the creation of living beings was effected thus by Brahmā.
In this way the creation has been related by me to you, O best of sages,
of the Lord of the universe as he created. What further do you wish to hear?
Bharadvāja said:
"This has been narrated in brief by you to me, O Lomaharṣaṇa.
Speak again in detail of the primary creation, O high-minded one!"
Sūta said:
"At the end of this cosmic egg, the lord awakened from night-sleep;
then Brahmā, filled with the quality of sattva, looked upon the empty world.

text_mt:
Nārāyaṇa is to be worshipped by the highest, the first-born even of the ancients,
the blessed one whose nature is Brahman, beginningless, the source of all.
[…] this verse regarding Nārāyaṇa,
the god whose form is Brahman, the imperishable source of the world:
'The waters are called nārāḥ; the waters are indeed the offspring of Nara.
That was his primary resting place (ayana); therefore he is called Nārāyaṇa.'
As he was contemplating creation, as previously at the beginnings of the kalpas,
there arose for him, devoid of growth, [a creation] full of delusion:
darkness (tamas), delusion (moha), great delusion (mahāmoha), and that named blinding darkness (tāmisra and andhatāmisra)—
five kinds of ignorance arose of that great-souled one before all else.
[Note]
1. Due to missing characters in the exemplar, this reading cannot be emended.
2. This reading is corrupt.
[Page 366]
The creation established in five ways, as he meditated, lacking conscious awareness,
is to be known as the primary creation (mukhya-sarga) by the discerning who understand creation.

text_mt:
Again, as he was meditating upon another, superior creation,
the transverse stream (tiryak-śrotas) arose; […] it is recorded as the transverse stream.
They are well known as animals and the like; they follow the wrong path.
Thinking that creation of the transverse stream to be incapable of fulfilling the purpose, the four-faced one [meditated again].
The third [creation], the upward stream (ūrdhva-śrotas), moved above the earthly realm.
From that arose the gods who move upward, born along with the creation.
When the Prajāpati was not satisfied with that creation, then he paused,
considering those born from the primary creation to be ineffective.
Then as he was reflecting, O brāhmaṇa, that [creation] is remembered as the downward stream (arvāk-śrotas).
Human beings, born thus as the downward stream, are considered capable of achieving the purpose.
They possess illumination, but are born with darkness and have an excess of rajas;
therefore they endure sorrow and are continually active.
Thus these creations have been recounted to you, O best of sages.

text_mt:
The first is the creation of Mahat; the second is that of the subtle elements (tanmātras).
The third is the transformational (vaikārika) creation, known as that of the sense organs.
The fourth is the primary creation (mukhya-sarga); […] the immovables are recorded.
The fifth is that called the transverse stream (tiryak-śrotas), the animal species.
Then the sixth is that of the upward streams; the seventh is the creation of the gods.
Then the best, of the downward stream, is the seventh [or eighth], the human creation.
The eighth is the supportive creation (anugraha-sarga); it is both sāttvika and tāmasa."
The ninth is the creation of Rudra. These are the nine creations of Prajāpati.
[Page 367]
These five are secondary creations; the primary creations are traditionally remembered, O dear one.
Both the primary and the secondary creations are the root causes of the world.
They are the creation arising from Brahmā as he creates, which have been related by me.
Then, entering with his potency, the supreme modification, he created everything—

text_mt:
Nārāyaṇa, possessing one form that dissolves everything, the sole lord of the universe, through the forms of Brahmā and the others.
Thus ends the second chapter, named the Topic of Creation, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the third chapter.
The Topic of Creation
Bharadvāja said:
The ninefold creation arose from Brahmā, who is born of the Unmanifest.
How did it multiply, O Sūta? Tell me this now.
Sūta said:
First created by Brahmā, following Rudra, were those rich in ascetic austerity:
Sanaka and the others, who were created, as well as Marīci and the others:
Marīci, Atri, and likewise Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu,
and Pulastya of great splendour, Pracetas, and Bhṛgu,
and Nārada as the tenth, and Vasiṣṭha of great brilliance.
Sanaka and the others were established in the duty called cessation;
[Page 368]
Marīci and the others in the duty called engagement; the sage Nārada solely in liberation.

text_mt:
He who was born from the limb of the Prajāpati, named Dakṣa—
through the lineage of his daughters' sons, this entire universe of moving and unmoving beings,
the gods, the Dānavas, the Gandharvas, serpents, and birds,
all supremely righteous, were born of Dakṣa’s daughters.
The four classes of beings, both unmoving and moving,
multiplied, and so did those originating from the creation of the Manus.
The great sages, Marīci and the others, were the makers of the creation of the Manus,
as were the highly fortunate Vasiṣṭha and the others, born from the mind of Brahmā.
In these creations, that Supreme Self creates beings, beginning with the ether, through Time;
and then he, the Infinite One, in the form of kings and in the form of sages, creates [...].
Thus ends the third chapter, named the Topic of Creation, in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the fourth chapter.
The Topic of Creation
Bharadvāja said:
Tell me in detail, O highly intelligent one, of the creation of Rudra;

and how again Marīci and the others brought forth the secondary creation.
[Page 369]
How did Vasiṣṭha become the son of Mitra and Varuṇa,
having previously been born from the mind of Brahmā, O one of great destiny?
Sūta said:
I shall declare the creation of Rudra and his production, O good one;
and hear in detail as I declare the secondary creation of the sages.
At the beginning of the kalpa, as he was meditating upon a son equal to himself,
there appeared from the body of the Lord a youth of blue and red colour,
having the form of the Lord who is half-female, fierce, with an immense body,
illuminating all the cardinal and intermediate directions with his splendour.
Seeing him blazing with splendour, Prajāpati replied:
"Divide yourself today at my command, O highly intelligent one!"
Being thus addressed by Brahmā, the glorious Rudra there
then separated his female nature and his male nature.

text_mt:
He divided the male nature into eleven parts.
I will tell you their names; hear them from me, O best of the twice-born:
Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Kapālin, and Rudra,
Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, and Aparājita,
Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin, and likewise Raivata—
these are declared to be the eleven Rudras, lords of the three worlds.
And in the same way Rudra divided femininity tenfold and singly;
she remained standing as his wife in manifold forms.
When formerly he performed terrifying ascetic austerity lying on his back in the water,
then that lord, the mighty Rudra, created there,
by the power of ascetic austerity, O best of Brahmins, various beings:
[Page 370]
piśācas, foul creatures, and those with faces like lions, camels, and makaras,
others headed by vetālas, and thousands of others.

Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapus, Śānti, Siddhi, and Kīrti—thirteen.

Sambhūti, Anubhūyā, Smṛti, Prīti, and Kṣamā,
and Sannati, Satyā, Ūrjā, and Khyāti, O best of the twice-born;
and Svāhā is to be known as the tenth, and Svadhā is recorded as the eleventh.
And these were given by Dakṣa to the purified sages.
And those who were the sons of Marīci and the others, them I tell unto you:
Marīci's wife Sambhūti gave birth to the sage Kaśyapa.
And Smṛti, wife of Aṅgiras, brought forth daughters:
Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, and Anumati.
Likewise, Anasūyā bore sinless sons to Atri:
Soma, Durvāsas, and the yogin Dattātreya.
In Prīti, the wife of Pulastya, was born his son Dādāni;
his son indeed was Viśravas, whose sons were Rāvaṇa and others.

for whose destruction in the worlds Viṣṇu, in the ocean of milk,
besought by the gods headed by Brahmā, took an incarnation here.
Kardama, Ambarīṣa, and Sahiṣṇu—a triad of sons
Kṣamā, the wife of Pulastya Prajāpati, bore.
[Page 372]
And Kratu's wife Satvatī gave birth to the Vālakhilyas,
those sixty thousand sages of vital fluid drawn upward,
of the size of a thumb-joint, blazing with the splendour of the sun.
Then from Pracetas, in Satyā, three sons of true resolve
were born; and their sons and grandsons were hundreds and thousands.
And in Ūrjā seven sons were born to Vasiṣṭha:
Rajas, Ūrdhvabāhu, Śaraṇa, and Anagha […]
Surūpa, and Śukra—these all became the seven sages.
From Bhṛgu and Khyāti was born Lakṣmī, the wife of Viṣṇu.

Likewise, Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ were born as two sons of Bhṛgu through Khyāti.
Āyati and Niyati were the very lovely daughters of Meru;
they were the wives of Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ. From the two [couples] were born two sons:
Prāṇa and Mṛkaṇḍu; Mārkaṇḍeya was the son of Mṛkaṇḍu,
by whom death was conquered long ago, O Brahmin, through Nārāyaṇa.
From him Devaśiras was born; Prāṇa also had a son
renowned as Dyutimān; Sañjaya was his son.
From them, O fortunate one, the lineage of Bhṛgu attained wide expansion.
And he who was named Agni, the eldest son of Brahmā,
from him Svāhā bore three sons of noble energy, O twice-born ones:
Pāvaka, Pavamāna, and Śuci who consumes water.
I shall relate their descendants, declared to be forty-six in number;

text_mt:
these are spoken of in many ways, along with the father and the three grandsons;
thus, through their lineage, forty-nine are proclaimed.
The ancestors created by Brahmā, whom I have explained to you,
from them Svadhā bore two daughters: Menā and Dhāriṇī.
Dakṣa, who had formerly been commanded by the Self-born to create offspring:
hear from me, O best of men, how he created living beings.
Formerly Dakṣa created beings by his mind, O sage:
gods, sages, along with Gandharvas, Asuras, and serpents.
When, as he created, creatures did not multiply,
then the sage, the lord of creatures, reflected for the sake of creation.
Desiring to create various creatures by sexual reproduction,
[he took] Asiknī, the daughter of the lord of creatures Vīraṇa.
Dakṣa created sixty daughters upon Vīriṇī—so runs our tradition;

he gave ten to Dharma and thirteen to Kaśyapa,
twenty-seven to Soma, four to Ariṣṭanemi,
two to Bahuputra, and two to Aṅgiras,
and two to the wise Kṛśāśva; hear from me their offspring.
Viśvā bore the Viśvedevas, and Sādhyā bore the Sādhyas;
the Maruts were born of Marutvatī, and the Vasus are traditionally considered [born] of Vasu.
The Bhānu gods were born of Bhānu, and the Muhūrtajas were born of Muhūrtā;
Ghoṣa was born of Lambā, and the Jāmijas were born of Jāmī;

Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa—these are proclaimed as the eight Vasus.
Their sons and grandsons were hundreds and thousands;
the Sādhyas are also said to be numerous, and their sons were in the thousands.
Aditi, Diti, Danu, Ariṣṭā, Surasā,
Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhā, Khasā, Irā,
Kadrū, and Muni, O knower of righteousness—hear from me their offspring.

text_mt:
and many other powerful Daityas, sons of Diti.
From Ariṣṭā the Gandharvas were born […],
and from Surasā arose many hosts of Vidyādharas.
The sage Kaśyapa begot cattle upon Surabhi.
From Vinatā, however, two sons were born, renowned as Garuḍa and Aruṇa.
[page 375]
Garuḍa, out of affection, became the mount of Viṣṇu,
the God of gods of boundless splendor; and Aruṇa became the charioteer of the Sun.
Six sons were born from Tāmrā by Kaśyapa; learn of them from me:
horses, camels, donkeys, elephants, gavayas, and deer.
Likewise, in Krodhā were born beasts of vicious species;
Irā [bore] the species of trees, creeping plants, vines, grasses, and horses as offspring.
Khasā, however, [bore] the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; Muni [bore] the Apsarases;
and Kadru's sons were the great serpents, biting snakes of ferocious venom.

text_mt:
Those who are proclaimed as the twenty-seven wives of Soma, devoted to sacred vows—
their sons, O twice-born one, were beings of great strength, beginning with Budha.
Sixteen were the offspring of the wives of Ariṣṭanemi here.
Of the wise Bahuputra, lightning and others were born in Tāmrā.
The sons of Pratyaṅgiras were the foremost sages honored by sages;
and the divine sage Kṛśāśva's sons were the divine weapons.
These indeed are born again at the end of a thousand yugas.
These are proclaimed as the descendants of Kaśyapa, stationary and moving.
Through their sons, grandsons, and descendants, the creation of Prajāpati multiplied,
for the god Nārasiṃha the wise, who is firmly established.
These manifestations, O brāhmaṇa, have been proclaimed to you by me.
The progeny of the daughters of Dakṣa has been narrated to you by me.
Whoever, endowed with faith, remembers these, will obtain fame and lineage.

text_mt:
Primary creation and secondary creation have been spoken to you by me in brief, for the purpose of the expansion of creation.
[page 376]
Those men who, devoted to Viṣṇu, always recite this, O twice-born ones,
become spotless.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Section on Creation," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now the fifth chapter:
The account of Vasiṣṭha being the son of Mitra and Varuṇa.
Sūta said:
The creation of the world by Viṣṇu, the Great-souled, has been told to you by me, O twice-born one,
as well as how gods, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and others were brought forth.
Regarding that which was asked of me by you previously in the presence of the sages—
namely, how Vasiṣṭha came to be the son of Mitra and Varuṇa—
that sacred ancient narrative I shall tell.
Listen with an attentive mind, O Bharadvāja, to what is uttered by me.
A knower of the truth of all duty and purpose, the best of all who know,
one who has reached the further shore of all branches of knowledge, was the Prajāpati named Dakṣa.

text_mt:
By him thirteen auspicious daughters were given to Kaśyapa.
I shall speak their names; learn them from me now:
Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kāṣṭhā, Muhūrtā, Siṃhikā, O sage,
Srutā, Kroṣṭā, Surabhi, Vinatā, Surasā, […]
Kadru, Surasā, and also Yātudevī remembered as Śunī—
these were the daughters of Dakṣa; he gave them to Kaśyapa.
[page 377]
The eldest and most eminent among them was named Aditi.
Aditi gave birth to twelve sons possessing brilliance equal to fire.
I shall speak their names; listen, O best of the twice-born,
by whom this daytime and night constantly proceeds in succession:
Bharga, Aṃśu, Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa,
Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, and Vivasvat, O one of great intellect,
Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, then Indra, and Viṣṇu is remembered as the twelfth.

text_mt:
These indeed are the twelve Ādityas; they rain […] and they shine.
Her middle son was named Varuṇa;
known as a World Protector, he is proclaimed in the western quarter.
In the western quarter of the western ocean shines
the glorious mountain named Asta, made of gold,
with peaks made of all manner of gems, accompanied by mineral cascades.
Endowed [with them], that mountain shines, composed of various jewels and auspicious,
with deep caves and resounding with lions and tigers,
frequented by gods and Gandharvas in various secluded regions.
When the sun has set behind it, the world is filled with darkness.
Upon its peak is a most divine, auspicious [city] made of gold,
delightful, constructed by Viśvakarman with jeweled pillars,
a city named Sukhāvatī, abundant with means of enjoyment.

Therein, the Āditya Varuṇa, blazing with his own splendor,
protects all these worlds, appointed personally by Brahmā.
[p. 378]
Being attended upon by Gandharvas and likewise by hosts of Apsarases,
his body radiant with celestial scents, adorned with divine ornaments,
Varuṇa once went together with Mitra to the forest,
in Kurukṣetra, to an auspicious forest constantly frequented by Brahmanical sages,
endowed with various flowers and fruits, filled with various […]
where the hermitages of ascetics with upward-drawn semen are seen.
Having resorted to that sacred ford, which possessed abundant flowers, fruits, and water,
wearing bark garments and black antelope skins, they practiced supreme ascetic austerity.
There, in a certain region of the forest, was a clear and auspicious lake,
crowded with many shrubs and creepers, frequented by various birds,
covered with groves of various trees, and adorned with a lotus pond,

the semen divided into parts in the lotus, […].
That semen fell in three parts: into a lotus, onto the dry ground, and into the water.
In the lotus, Vasiṣṭha was born, O best of sages;
on the dry ground Agastya was born, and in the water the Matsya of great luster.

text_mt:
Agastya in a water jar, and Matsya in the water.
Both of them on that ground practiced still more fierce ascetic austerity.
[Notes]
1 This reading is corrupt.
2 This reading is not correct.
3 This verse cannot be emended due to defects in the manuscript.
[p. 380]
Having attained his desire through ascetic austerity, [he reached] the supreme, eternal light.
As the two foremost of gods were practicing ascetic austerity, Brahmā approached and said:
“O gods Mitra and Varuṇa, endowed with sons, of great splendor,
may there be supreme Vaiṣṇava perfection for both of you again.
Now, remain in your own sphere of authority as witnesses of the world.”
Having spoken thus, Brahmā vanished, and the two remained in their own offices.
Thus has been recounted to you, O Brahmin, the great-souled Vasiṣṭha's
and the wise Agastya's being sons of Mitra and Varuṇa.
This ancient narrative that bestows male progeny destroys sins.
Having heard it, a king together with his ministers and sons is freed from sin.

text_mt:
And whatever people, observing pure vows, hear this desiring sons,
they obtain sons without delay; there is no doubt in this.
And whoever constantly recites this during offerings to gods and ancestors, O best of the twice-born,
his gods and ancestors depart satisfied as they please.
And that human being who recites this daily upon rising in the morning
obtains very great sons and goes to the heavenly world.
The excellent [narrative] spoken of old by those devoted to the Veda has been recounted by me.
Whoever will recite or always hears it,
he, purified, swiftly goes to the superior realm.
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the glorious Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Account of Vasiṣṭha’s Being the Son of Mitra and Varuṇa'.
[Page 381]
Now, the sixth chapter:
The Episode of Mārkaṇḍeya.
Bharadvāja said:
How was death conquered by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya?
Tell this to me, O Sūta; [it was spoken] by you long ago.

text_mt:
Listen from me to this great narrative, O Bharadvāja;
let all the sages listen, I tell what occurred in the past:
In the immensely sacred Kurukṣetra, at the seat of Vyāsa in the excellent hermitage,
the best of sages, the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, was seated there,
having bathed and performed his recitation, surrounded by sage-disciples,
knower of the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, expert in all scriptures.
Having bowed down properly, the exceedingly righteous Śuka,
referring to this very matter, asked him with folded hands
concerning the very matter about which we have been questioned here by you in the presence of the sages,
by you, a devotee of Narasiṃha and dweller at the sacred ford.
Śuka said:
How was death defeated by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya?
Tell this to me, father; I wish to hear it from you now.
Vyāsa said:
How death was conquered by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya,

in that manner I shall tell you; listen with concentration, dear child.
Let these sages also listen to what is now being spoken by me,
[Page 382]
and let the queens also hear this sublime, great narrative:
From Bhṛgu, through Khyāti, a son named Mṛkaṇḍu was indeed born,
and of the great-souled Mṛkaṇḍu, there was a wife named Sumitrā,
knower of dharma, devoted to dharma, intent on service to her husband.
To him, upon her, was born the son Mārkaṇḍeya of great intellect,
the grandson of Bhṛgu, highly fortunate, […] of great intellect.
The beloved boy grew up, his father having performed the rites for him there.
Indeed, as soon as he was born, an astrologer stated:
'In his twelfth year, the son will be afflicted by death.'
Hearing that, his mother and father both became grief-stricken,
their hearts overcome with sorrow as they gazed upon that highly intelligent one.

text_mt:
Nevertheless, his wise, intelligent father then diligently performed
every rite in due time; [and] he was sent to the house of his teacher.
[…] devoted to serving the teacher,
having mastered the Vedas and scriptures, he returned to his holy home.
Having bowed down at the feet of his mother and father with humility,
the wise Mārkaṇḍeya, possessing great splendour, dwelt in that house.
Beholding that great-souled one and his extraordinary faith,
both his mother and father were greatly distressed there, O Śuka.
Seeing the two of them overwhelmed with grief, Mārkaṇḍeya of great splendour
[Footnote:]

2 This reading is incorrect. / [Page 383]
spoke these words at that time: “Why is there such sorrow
that you feel, O mother, together with my wise father?
You ought to tell the cause of the sorrow to me who am asking.”

text_mt:
Thus addressed by her son, the great-souled [boy's] mother
recounted all that which the astrologer had said.
Having heard that, he, very resolute, spoke again to his mother and father:
“O mother, together with my father, not even the slightest grief should be felt by you.
I will avert death […] by ascetic austerity; there is no doubt of this.
And I will perform great ascetic austerity so that I attain a long lifespan.”
Having said this, comforting his parents […],
he went to the forest filled with various sages.
There he saw his grandfather comfortably seated together with the sages,
the righteous Bhṛgu, [saw] the highly intelligent Mārkaṇḍeya.
Then Bhṛgu said to the fortunate child Mārkaṇḍeya:
“Why have you come, my son? Is it well with your father,
with your mother, and with your relatives? What is the reason for your coming?”

text_mt:
Being thus addressed by the great-souled sage,
Mārkaṇḍeya then told him all the words of the astrologer.
Having heard the words of his grandson, Bhṛgu spoke to him again:
“Such is your thought, O one of great intellect! What action do you wish to perform?”
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
“I desire now to conquer death, which snatches away living beings.
[Footnote:]
1 This reading is corrupted by manuscript defect. / [Page 384]
Through your instruction, O Guru, tell us the means for that.”
The Guru said:
“Without having worshipped Nārāyaṇa with the mind through ascetic austerity, O son,
who could conquer death? Therefore worship him with ascetic austerity!
Him, the [unborn] Viṣṇu, Acyuta, Puruṣottama,
who loves his devotees, the highest of the gods—go to him for refuge with devotion!
The sage Nārada formerly went to him alone for refuge
through great ascetic austerity, O child—to the sorrowless Nārāyaṇa.

text_mt:
By his grace, O fortunate one, Nārada, the son of Brahmā,
having conquered old age and death, lives happily with a long life.
Who except that lotus-eyed Nārasiṃha, Janārdana,
affectionate toward his devotees, could ward off the army of death?
Therefore, constantly take refuge in Viṣṇu, the creator of the world, the victorious lord of Śrī,
Govinda, the lord of cattle, the god!
If you always worship the unborn god Nārasiṃha,
O child, you will conquer death together with his army; there is no doubt of this.”
Vyāsa said:
Being thus addressed by his grandfather Bhṛgu,
Mārkaṇḍeya of great splendour then spoke with humility to his grandfather:
“O father, you have spoken with certainty that only Viṣṇu is to be worshipped,
and that the Blessed Lord, when worshipped, will take away my death.
How, in this matter, should the worship of Acyuta be performed by me, O Guru,
